href="#s-memorize" aria-label="Link to this section"> Memorizing saves a report exactly as it is on the screen (the dates choice, the filters, the sort order, the columns and the layout) under a name of your own, so you can open it again with one click, share it, and have it e-mailed on a schedule. The Memorize report window with the Name, Group, Share with other users, Send automatically and Email to boxes Fields Field What to enter Name The name of the memorized report. It starts as the report's title. Group A group to file it under, for example Month-end or Weekly. Groups sort the list. Share with other users Tick it to list the report for everyone. Each user can open it only if they may open the report itself. Send automatically No , Daily , Weekly or Monthly . Email to The e-mail address the scheduled report goes to. Step by step: memorize a report Set the report up: filters, sorting, columns and layout. Choose the period in Dates as the last step (see the tip below). Click Memorize . Change the Name if you wish and type a Group . Tick Share with other users if others should have it. To have it e-mailed, choose Daily , Weekly or Monthly in Send automatically and type the address in Email to . Click Save . The program says Report memorized. and shows the report again. It is now in Memorized Reports and in the Report Center. Tip A period chosen from the Dates list moves with the calendar: a report memorized on This month always shows the current month. Dates in From and To are remembered as they are. After you press Refresh , the From and To dates on the screen are sent with the report and stay fixed. To memorize a moving period, choose it from Dates after setting the other filters, and click Memorize without pressing Refresh again. Scheduled e-mail A memorized report with Send automatically set is e-mailed as a spreadsheet file (CSV) attached to a message whose subject is its name and the company name. The e-mails are sent by a program on the server, tools/send_scheduled_reports.php , which your administrator runs once a day (for example with Windows Task Scheduler). On each run: a daily report goes out once a day, a weekly report when a week has passed since the last sending, and a monthly report when a month has passed; a new scheduled report goes out at the next run; the report runs with the access of the user who memorized it, and is skipped if that user's account is no longer active or has lost access to the report; the time of the last sending is shown in the Schedule column of Memorized Reports, and each sending (or failure) is recorded in the audit trail. Note Nothing is sent when Email to is empty, or when the administrator has not set the sender up on the server. The attached file has the report's standard columns and all its rows, whatever layout was used on the screen.

href="#sec-modify-report" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Modify Report panel, which works like the Modify Report window of QuickBooks, changes how a report looks and what it prints: which columns (the report's own and fields from the records behind each row), which rows, the heading and the foot, the fonts, how the figures are written, and the printed page. It is on every report. It needs the special permission Can design report layouts (Administrators always have it). A modified report can be used just for now, or saved as a layout, shared with the other users and made the one the report opens with. Click Modify Report in the title bar of any report. The panel opens between the filter bar and the report. Click Modify Report again to close it. While a saved layout is in use, the button reads Modify Report: followed by the layout's name. The Income Statement with the Modify Report panel open on the Columns tab, and the buttons that take a row out shown at the start of each row The panel has eight tabs: Columns , Rows , Heading , Fonts & look , Figures , Footer , Page and Layouts . Two kinds of change work differently: Fonts, sizes, colours, shading, lines, the words of the heading and the foot, and which heading lines show, change on the report as you pick them. So do showing or hiding a column, its width, its alignment and its heading, for the columns already on the report. Changes to what is printed (moving columns, the rows, the figures, the page) wait. The note Some changes show once you press "Show it this way". appears; click Show it this way to see them. The buttons at the foot of the panel: Show it this way redraws the report with every choice on the panel. Nothing is saved yet, but the report as shown can be printed, exported, e-mailed and memorized. Back to the plain report opens the report without any layout, keeping its dates and filters. The Columns tab The tab lists every column the report can print: first the report's own columns, then the related fields , the fields of the records its rows come from. A row of the Sales by Customer Detail report, for example, comes from a transaction and from a customer, so the memo, the class, the site or the status of the transaction, and the phone, the e-mail, the terms or the credit limit of the customer, can all be added to the report with a tick. The field says which record it comes from: Memo from the transaction , Phone from the customer . The Columns tab of the Trial Balance with the Print tick, the heading, the width, the alignment and the move buttons of each column, and the account fields listed under the report's own columns Column What it does Handle Drag the dotted handle at the start of a row to move the column. Print Tick to print the column, untick to leave it out. Column The column's standard name. (extra) marks a column the report offers but prints only when ticked; from the transaction , from the customer , from the supplier , from the item , from the account or from the fixed asset marks a related field. Heading printed Type the words to print over the column. Empty keeps the standard heading. Width Auto (fits the text), Narrow , Medium or Wide . Lines up Auto , Left , Middle or Right . Move To the start, up one, down one, to the end. Above the list, Find a column or field narrows the list as you type (for example "phone"), and a link per kind of record, such as Transaction fields (16) or Customer fields (14) , scrolls to that group. Under the list, Print all its own columns ticks every column of the report itself, Back to the standard columns undoes every change on this tab, and Take out the added fields unticks every related field at once. The line beside the buttons counts the columns that print and how many of them are added fields. Any column can be moved, the Date or the Name column included, and an added field can be dragged among the report's own columns, renamed, widened and lined up like any other. The Columns tab of Sales by Customer Detail scrolled to the customer fields, with Memo from the transaction and Phone from the customer ticked The related fields on offer: Record Fields Transaction Transaction type, date and number, Name (customer, supplier or payee), Reference number, Memo, Class, Site, Terms, Due date, Ship date, Status, Transaction total, Entered by, Entered on, Approved by. Customer Customer name, Company name, Contact person, Phone, Mobile, Email, Billing address, TIN, Terms, Customer type, Sales rep, Price level, Credit limit, Balance owed today. Supplier Supplier name, Company name, Contact person, Phone, Fax, Email, Address, TIN, Terms, Our account number with them, Credit limit, Balance owed today. Item Item code, Item name, Barcode, Sales description, Purchase description, Category, Item type, Unit, Tax code, Item status, Cost, Average cost, Sales price, Reorder point, Maximum stock, Preferred supplier, On hand today (all sites), Asset value today, Retail value today, Gross profit per unit (price less average cost), Gross profit % per unit, Markup % on average cost. The cost and profit fields are offered only to users who may view costs. A report that everybody can shape column by column is the Customized Inventory Report . Account Account number, Account name, Account type, Category, Parent account, Description, Bank account number. Fixed asset Asset number, Asset, Category, Location, Serial number, Date acquired, Cost, Status. Which records a report offers depends on what its rows point at: a report whose numbers open a transaction offers the transaction's fields and those of its customer or supplier; a report whose names open a customer, a supplier, an item or an account offers that record's fields; the asset reports offer the asset's. Group headings, subtotals and totals have no record behind them, so their cells in an added column stay empty. Sales by Customer Detail with the Memo of each transaction and the customer's Phone added as the last two columns Note The fields are looked up only when they print, and only for the rows on the report, so a report without added fields is as fast as it was. Cost and Average cost appear only for users with View costs and margins , and Bank account number only for users who may see bank balances. Added fields go into the spreadsheet export, into the scheduled e-mail of a memorized report, and into a saved layout, and the report can be sorted by them like by any column. Tip: To make a collections list from the Open Invoices report, add Phone and Email from the customer and Memo from the transaction , drag them next to the customer's name, and save the result as a layout called "Collections list". The Rows tab The Rows tab with Which rows, the zero rows, Only rows containing, the row limit, the subtotal and total ticks, and the rows taken out Field What it does Which rows Every row , or Only the group headings, subtotals and totals for a summary. A report without groups says so under the box. Rows whose figures are all zero Show them or Leave them out . Only rows containing Prints only the detail rows that contain the text typed, in any column. Capitals do not matter. At most this many rows (0 = all of them) Stops after that many detail rows. Subtotal rows Untick to leave the subtotals out. Grand total row Untick to leave the grand total out. Rows taken out one by one: while the panel is open, a small button with a crossed-out eye appears at the start of each row of the report. Click it to take that row out; the row is greyed out until you click Show it this way . The taken-out rows are listed on the right, each with Put back ; Put them all back returns them all. When none is taken out, the list says None taken out. A row is recognised by the words in its first columns, so it stays out whenever the report is run. Note Leaving rows out changes what prints, not the figures: every total is still the total of the whole report. A line above the report (not printed) says how many rows are taken out or left out. The Heading tab The Heading tab with the title, the lines under it, the position of the heading and the parts shown in it Field What it does Report title A title of your own. Empty keeps the report's name. Line under the title One line under the title, for example "For the board meeting". More lines under the title Extra lines, one per line of the box, up to eight. The heading sits On the left , In the middle or On the right . Title in capital letters Prints the title in capitals. Company name Shows the company name. Company address Shows the address from the company settings. Company TIN Shows the TIN from the company settings. Company logo Shows the company logo. Dates and filters line The line with the dates and filters under the title. "Prepared on ..." line under the heading A line with the date, the time and the name of the person running the report, under the dates line. Off as delivered. A line under the heading A rule between the heading and the table. A note under a box says when it cannot show anything yet: No address in the company settings yet , No TIN in the company settings yet , No logo uploaded yet , or Not ticked for this report under Company, Security & Closing Date . The company details and the logo, and the reports the logo prints on, are set in Company, Security & Closing Date . The Fonts & look tab The Fonts & look tab with the settings of the heading, the column headings and the rows THE HEADING Font : one of Standard (Segoe UI), Arial, Calibri, Tahoma, Verdana, Century Gothic, Times New Roman, Georgia, Cambria, Garamond, Bookman Old Style, Courier New or Consolas. Nothing is downloaded: if a computer does not have the font, the browser uses a similar one. Title size : Small , Normal , Large or Extra large . Company name size : Small , Normal or Large . Colour : Black , Dark grey , Blue or Green . THE COLUMN HEADINGS Font and Size ( Small , Normal , Large ). Shading : None , Light grey , Dark, white letters or Blue, white letters . Line up : Over their figures (text left, amounts right) , All on the left or All in the middle . In bold , In capital letters , and Long headings may take two lines . THE ROWS Font and Size ( Small , Normal , Large ). Row height : Normal , Tight (more rows to a page) or Roomy . The grand total : Line above, double line below , A line above , In bold only or Shaded band . Shade every other row , Lines between the columns , A border round the table and Shade the group headings . The Figures tab The Figures tab with the negative figures, zero figures, decimals, scale, currency sign and thousands separator Field Choices Negative figures With a minus sign -1,234.00 , In brackets (1,234.00) , In red -1,234.00 or In red brackets (1,234.00) . Zero figures Show 0.00 , Leave the cell empty or Show a dash . Decimal places on money Two (1,234.56) or None (1,235) . Show the money figures As they are (1,234,567.00) , In thousands (1,235) or In millions (1.2) . The heading then says "amounts in thousands" or "amounts in millions". Currency sign None , On the totals or On every amount . The sign is ₱, from the system settings. Thousands separator (1,234) Untick to print 1234 instead of 1,234. The Footer tab The Footer tab with the foot text, its position, the Printed line, page numbers and the signature lines Field What it does Text at the foot of the report Your own text, for example "Confidential: for internal use only". Up to eight lines. The foot text sits On the left , In the middle or On the right . A line above the foot A rule between the table (or the signature lines) and the foot text. "Printed on ... by ..." line The line with the date, time and name of the person who printed the report. Page numbers on the printed pages "Page 1 of 3" at the foot of each page (Chrome and Edge). Signature lines at the foot Prints signature lines under the report. Caption under each signature line One caption per line, up to four. As delivered: Prepared by, Checked by, Approved by. Names printed above the captions The names to print above the lines, in the same order as the captions. Example For a trial balance to be signed, tick Signature lines at the foot , keep the three captions, and type the names of the bookkeeper, the chief accountant and the owner, one per line, in Names printed above the captions . The Page tab The Page tab with the paper, the printed page, the margins and the title on every page Field Choices Paper The printer's own , A4 (210 x 297 mm) , Letter (8.5 x 11 in) , Long / Folio (8.5 x 13 in) or Legal (8.5 x 14 in) . Printed page Upright (portrait) or Sideways (landscape) . Margins Narrow (6 mm) , Normal (12 mm) or Wide (20 mm) . Report title at the top of every printed page From the second printed page on, in the top margin (Chrome and Edge). These settings are for the printed page only. Click Print / PDF above the report to see them. The Layouts tab The Layouts tab with the Save this layout button and the Every saved layout link Open a saved layout lists Standard (no layout) and every layout of this report that is yours or shared, marked (opens by default) and shared where they apply. Choosing one opens the report in it. When there is none, the tab says No layout saved for this report yet. Save this layout opens the window described below. Delete followed by the layout's name deletes the layout that is open. It appears for the layout's owner and for administrators. Every saved layout opens Saved Report Layouts .

t: Saving, sharing and deleting a layout
x: href="#s-saving-sharing-and-deleting-a-layout" aria-label="Link to this section"> A layout keeps everything set on the Modify Report panel's tabs, the added fields included, so the report can be opened the same way again, by you or by everyone. The Save this layout window with the name, the default tick and the sharing tick Field What it does Name The layout's name, for example "Trial Balance for the bank". Replace "..." instead of adding another Shown when the layout that is open is yours, and ticked: saving updates it. Untick to save a new layout. Open this report with this layout from now on Makes it the layout the report opens with. Let the other users use it too Shares it. Users who cannot design reports can then choose it from their Layouts button. Step by step: save a layout Open the report and click Modify Report . Make your changes on the tabs. There is no need to click Show it this way first: everything on the panel is saved, including changes not shown yet. Open the Layouts tab and click Save this layout . Type a Name . Tick Open this report with this layout from now on and Let the other users use it too as needed. Click Save the layout . The report opens in the new layout, with the message Layout "Trial Balance for the bank" saved. It is on the Modify Report panel of that report. Default and shared layouts A layout marked as the default opens whenever the report is opened by someone who can see it: only you for a private layout, everyone for a shared one. A report has one default at a time. Making a layout the default takes the mark off the report's other layouts that you can see. To see the report without its default layout, click Back to the plain report on the Modify Report panel, choose Standard under Layouts , or choose Standard (no layout) on the Layouts tab. A layout can be changed only by its owner, and deleted by its owner or an administrator. To adapt someone else's layout, open it, change it and save it under a new name. Important Making one of your private layouts the default also takes the mark off a shared layout that was the default for everyone, and nobody else sees your private layout. Everyone else then gets the plain report. Keep the default on a shared layout when others rely on it. Step by step: delete a layout Open the report in the layout (Layouts tab > Open a saved layout ). Click Delete followed by the layout's name. Click Delete it to confirm. The report itself is not changed. The program says Layout deleted. Layouts can also be deleted on the Saved Report Layouts page. Message What it means Give the layout a name. The Name box is empty. That layout belongs to another user, so it cannot be changed here. Save it under a new name instead. Untick Replace and save a new layout. Saving a report layout needs the "Can design report layouts" permission. An administrator can give it to your role. Your role lacks the permission.

href="#s-good-to-know-about-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> Columns with costs and margins appear only for users with the special permission View costs and margins . Reports based on sites show only the sites you may see. Some reports print a note under the title, for example the Accounts Receivable Graph's "A few customers owing a large share of the total indicates concentration risk." Saving a layout also needs access to the Saved Report Layouts page, and memorizing needs access to the Memorized Reports page. Ask your administrator if the buttons are missing.

href="#pg-home-memorized" aria-label="Link to this section"> Memorized Reports lists the reports you memorized and those other users shared, with their schedules. Use it to open them, check when a scheduled report was last sent, and remove the ones no longer needed. Where to find it: Home > Memorized Reports. The Memorized Reports list with two reports in the groups Month-end and Weekly The columns Column What it shows Group The group given when memorizing. The list is sorted by group, then name. Name The memorized report's name. Click it to open the report. If you may not open the report, the name is not a link and no access is shown beside it. Report The report it is based on, for example Income Statement. Shared Yes when it is shared with the other users. Schedule For a scheduled report: how often, the address and the time it was last sent. Owner The username of the person who memorized it. Remove Deletes the memorized report. Shown to its owner and to administrators. Step by step: open a memorized report Open Home > Memorized Reports . Click the report's Name . It opens with its memorized dates, filters and layout. Step by step: remove a memorized report Click Remove on its line. Click OK to confirm Remove this memorized report? The program says Memorized report removed. The removal is recorded in the audit trail. Step by step: change a memorized report A memorized report cannot be edited in place. To change it: Open it from the list. Change the dates, filters or layout. Memorize it again, under the same name if you wish. Remove the old one. Good to know To memorize a report, open the report and click Memorize (see Working with reports ). Scheduled reports are e-mailed by tools/send_scheduled_reports.php , which your administrator runs daily; the page says so above the list. When the list is empty it says No memorized reports yet.

href="#pg-home-report_layouts" aria-label="Link to this section"> Saved Report Layouts lists every report layout that is yours or shared with you, for all reports at once, so they can be kept tidy: opened, made the default, or deleted. Layouts are made on the report itself, with the Modify Report button. Where to find it: Home > Saved Report Layouts, or Every saved layout on the Layouts tab of the Modify Report panel. The Saved Report Layouts list with the layout Trial Balance for the bank, its Make default button and the delete button The columns Column What it shows Report The report the layout belongs to. Click it to open the report in this layout. Layout The layout's name, with its own report title under it when it has one. Columns How many of the report's columns it prints, for example 4 of 4 shown , or standard . Owner Who saved it, marked shared when others may use it. (default) opens by default when the report opens with this layout. Buttons Button What it does Make default Makes this layout the one its report opens with. Shown to users who may design reports, on layouts that are not the default yet. Delete (bin icon) Deletes the layout after you confirm. Shown to its owner and to administrators. Step by step: make a layout the default Click Make default on its line. The program says, for example, "Trial Balance for the bank" now opens by default. Any other default layout of that report that you can see loses its mark. Step by step: delete a layout Click the bin button on its line. Click OK to confirm Delete the layout followed by its name. The program says Layout deleted. The report itself is not changed. When no layout is saved, the list says No layouts saved yet. Open a report and press Modify Report. Good to know To change a layout, open it from the Report column, click Modify Report , make the changes and save it with Replace ticked (see Working with reports ). There is no button to take the default mark off without choosing another default; to stop a layout opening by default, make another layout the default, or delete it.

href="#pg-coa-accounts" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Chart of Accounts is the list of every account the books use: cash and bank accounts, receivables, inventory, payables, equity, income and expenses. Here you add accounts, group them under main accounts, give them their account type, mark the ones that keep a subsidiary ledger, and open the ledger or the register of any account. Where to find it: Financial > Chart of Accounts The Chart of Accounts: 1000 Cash with the total of its eight sub-accounts, the sub-accounts under it, and the accounts of the types Cash and Loans Receivable The accounts are shown in five cards, Assets , Liabilities , Equity , Incomes and Expenses . Each card is in code order, and every main account is followed by its sub-accounts. A sub-account is indented under its main account with an arrow, for example 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking under 1000 Cash, and a main account says under its name how many sub-accounts it has. Accounts that the modules need, such as 1100 Accounts Receivable, 1200 Inventory and 2000 Accounts Payable, carry the word system in grey. Tick Include inactive accounts above the list to show the accounts you have made inactive; they appear greyed out. The columns Column What it shows Code The account code. The list is sorted by it. Name The account name. Click it to open the General Ledger of this account. Type The account type: a built-in type (see the table below), or a type of your own (see Account Types ) with the built-in type it behaves as under it in grey, for example Cash over Bank . Normal Debit or Credit : the side that increases the account. With SL Yes when the account keeps a subsidiary ledger. Balance The balance of the account on its normal side, for all dates. A main account with sub-accounts shows, in bold, the total of its own balance and the balances of its sub-accounts (on a phone it is labelled Total with sub-accounts ). A negative balance is shown in brackets. Links Edit , Register and Delete , for the users allowed to use them. A main account shows the total of its sub-accounts. In the demo company, 1000 Cash shows 1,469,480.61 : the total of its eight sub-accounts, among them 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking with 577,084.14 and 1020 Cash in Bank - BPI Savings with 800,000.00. 1000 Cash has no balance of its own; when a main account has one, its own balance is shown under the total as own and the amount. Inactive sub-accounts count in the total even while they are hidden. The financial statements show the same totals (see Balance Sheet ). Bank balances show as ••• to a user who has neither the special permission View bank balances outside Banking nor access to Use Register . The total of a main account with Bank sub-accounts is hidden the same way. Account types The account type decides where the account appears on the statements and which forms offer it. The program has the fifteen built-in types below; the category and the normal balance follow from the type. You can add types of your own, such as Cash or Loans Receivable , under Account Types : each one behaves as one of the built-in types, is a classification of its own on the Balance Sheet and the Income Statement, and is linked to a section of the Statement of Cash Flows. Built-in type Category Normal balance Section on the statements Statement of Cash Flows (to start with) Bank Asset Debit Current Assets Cash and cash equivalents Accounts Receivable Asset Debit Current Assets Operating activities Other Current Asset Asset Debit Current Assets Operating activities Fixed Asset Asset Debit Fixed Assets Investing activities Other Asset Asset Debit Other Assets Investing activities Accounts Payable Liability Credit Current Liabilities Operating activities Credit Card Liability Credit Current Liabilities Operating activities Other Current Liability Liability Credit Current Liabilities Operating activities Long Term Liability Liability Credit Long-term Liabilities Financing activities Equity Equity Credit Equity Financing activities Income Income Credit Income Net income Other Income Income Credit Other Income Net income Cost of Goods Sold Expense Debit Cost of Goods Sold Net income Expense Expense Debit Expenses Net income Other Expense Expense Debit Other Expenses Net income Some types also change what the forms allow. A type of your own does the same as the built-in type it behaves as: an account of the type Cash that behaves as Bank is offered wherever a Bank account is. Bank accounts are the ones offered on Write Checks , Make Deposits , the cash account of a Cash Voucher and Reconcile . Create cash funds such as a petty cash fund or a revolving fund as Bank accounts too, so they can be paid out of and reconciled. Credit Card accounts can be chosen on Write Checks and Transfer Funds. Other Current Asset accounts can be chosen in Transfer Funds and as the Deposit to account of a sales receipt. A journal entry line to an Accounts Receivable account needs a customer, and a line to an Accounts Payable account needs a vendor. The New account form, with what the chosen type does and where its accounts are shown Fields Field What to enter / what it means Account type A built-in type from the table above, or a type of your own, listed with the built-in type it behaves as, for example Cash (Bank) . The box under the code and name says what the type does and where its accounts are shown on the Balance Sheet or the Income Statement and on the Statement of Cash Flows. A new account starts as Expense ; when you choose a main account in Sub-account of before touching the type, the new account takes the type of that main account. Code Up to 20 characters. Every account needs its own code. Name Up to 120 characters. Sub-account of Leave blank for a main account, or choose the main account it belongs under. Only main accounts are listed, and the main account must be of the same category (an asset under an asset, an expense under an expense). On the financial statements a sub-account is shown under its main account, in the classification of the main account's type, and the main account shows the total of its sub-accounts. Normal balance From type takes the normal balance of the type. Choose Debit or Credit only for a contra account (see below). Active Untick to stop offering the account on forms. It keeps its history and still shows on reports. With SL (keeps a subsidiary ledger) Tick when you want a listing of the names (customers, suppliers, employees, other names) that transacted this account. See "With SL" below. Bank account no. (bank accounts) The bank's account number, for your reference. Description A note about what the account is for. The form reminds you: "Contra accounts (accumulated depreciation, sales returns, drawings) use the opposite normal balance of their type." For example, 1525 Accumulated Depreciation - Machinery is a Fixed Asset account with a Credit normal balance, so it reduces the fixed assets on the Balance Sheet. Editing account 1009 Cash on Hand - Accounting Office, of the type Cash, which behaves as Bank Step by step To add an account: Open Financial > Chart of Accounts . Click New account . Choose the Account type . Type the Code and the Name . If the account belongs under another one, choose it in Sub-account of . The new account takes the type of that main account unless you chose a type yourself. Leave Normal balance at From type unless this is a contra account. Tick With SL if you want the account to keep a subsidiary ledger. For a bank account, type the Bank account no. Click Save account , or Save account & New to save it and start another one straight away. To change an account: Click Edit on the account's line. Change what you need. The title of the form shows the code, for example "Edit account 1000". Click Save account . To make an account inactive: Click Edit on the account's line. Untick Active . Click Save account . To delete an account: Find the account. A Delete link appears only on an account that is not a system account, whose balance is zero and that has no sub-accounts. Click Delete and confirm "Delete this account?". To open an account's register: click Register on its line. The link appears for Bank, Credit Card, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Other Current Asset and Other Current Liability accounts. See Use Register . To export the list: click Export . The file chart_of_accounts.csv holds, for every account shown and in the order of the list, the code, name, type, the built-in type it behaves as, category, normal balance, parent, With SL, balance, the total with sub-accounts (for a main account that has sub-accounts) and the active flag. Export needs the print/export permission on this page. Buttons New account: opens a blank account form. Shown only to users with the special permission to change the Chart of Accounts. Account types: opens Account Types . The account form has the same button. Export: downloads the list as a spreadsheet file. Module default accounts: opens Module Default Accounts . With SL: keeping a subsidiary ledger An account marked With SL keeps a listing of the names that transacted it, like a subsidiary ledger of advances to employees, deposits from customers or loans from officers. While the box is ticked: every journal entry, cash voucher and check that posts to the account must name a customer, supplier, employee or other name. On a journal entry or cash voucher the name is chosen on the line; on a check, the payee of the check counts for every line. saving without a name is refused with a message that names the account, for example "The account 1400 - Prepaid Expenses is marked "With SL", so the line posting to it needs a name: choose a customer, supplier, employee or other name." the Subsidiary Ledger and the Schedule of Accounts list the account and its names. The rule applies to entries saved after the box is ticked. Entries made earlier keep whatever name they had. What it records Adding or changing an account posts nothing. Every change is written to the audit trail. Good to know "Enter the account code and name." Both are required. "Another account uses this code." Choose a different code. "A sub-account must be under a parent account of the same category." Choose a parent of the same category, or change the type. "System accounts used by the modules cannot be made inactive." Accounts with the system tag must stay active. "This account has transactions; it cannot be moved to a different category." You can change the type within the same category (for example from Expense to Other Expense), but not from an expense to an asset once entries have been posted. "This account has sub-accounts of its category; it cannot be moved to another category." A main account keeps its category while it has sub-accounts. "This account is one the modules post to: it can only take a type that behaves as Accounts Receivable." An account with the system word keeps its built-in type. It can still take a type of your own that behaves as the same built-in type, for example 1050 Undeposited Funds a type that behaves as Other Current Asset. "This account is in use. Make it inactive instead of deleting it." An account cannot be deleted while it has ledger entries or transaction lines, is a module default account, has sub-accounts, or is used on an item. Make it inactive instead. Without the special permission to change the Chart of Accounts, the list is read-only and the New account , Edit and Delete links do not appear.

href="#s-coa-import" aria-label="Link to this section"> A whole chart of accounts, or a part of it, can be brought in from a file instead of being typed account by account. The file is a CSV file or an Excel workbook (its first worksheet), with one line per account. Nothing is saved when the file is read: every line is shown first in a review form, where a line with a problem is in red with its reason, any cell can be corrected and any line removed. The accounts are saved when no line is in red, every one of them or none. Where to find it: Financial > Chart of Accounts > Import (beside New account ). It needs the Create right on Chart of Accounts and the special permission to change the Chart of Accounts; updating the accounts already on the chart also needs the Edit right. Import the chart of accounts: the lines under review, two of them in red with their reasons The columns of the file The first line of the file names the columns, in any order. The names below are read, and so are the headings of the chart's own Export (Code, Name, Type, Normal balance, Parent, With SL, Active) and the usual other words (Account Code, Account Title, Account Type, Parent Code, Sub-account of, Remarks ...). Download the CSV template on the page has the columns and a few example accounts. Column What it holds code The account code (required), at most 20 characters, used by no other account. name The name of the account (required), at most 120 characters. type The account type (required), as Account Types lists it: Bank, Accounts Receivable, Other Current Asset, Fixed Asset, Accounts Payable, Equity, Income, Expense ... or a type of your own. The usual other words are read too (Current Asset, Revenue, Cost of Sales, Capital ...), and the review says how each was read. parent Sub-account of: the code (or the name) of the main account it is under, on the chart or in the same file, of the same category. Blank for a main account. One level of sub-accounts, as on the account form. normal_balance Debit or Credit (Dr and Cr are read too). Blank: the normal balance of the type. A contra account, such as an allowance or accumulated depreciation, takes the other one. with_sl Yes when the account keeps a subsidiary ledger of names; blank: No. is_active Yes or No; blank: Yes. description, bank_account_no Optional. They are under ... on each line of the review. Step by step Click Import on the Chart of Accounts, choose the file and click Read the file for review . Choose what to do with an account whose code is already on the chart: Update it from the file (its name, type, main account and the other cells of its line; a blank cell keeps what is saved) or Leave it as it is (the line is shown but not saved). Read the lines. Each line says what it will do: a new account, an account of the chart that will be updated (and what of it), the same as on the chart, or left as it is. A line in red has its reason under it and the cell it names outlined in red. Correct a cell by typing in it or choosing from its list: the line is checked again at once. Remove a line with x ( Put back the last brings it back), or remove every line in red at once. Click Save N accounts . The main accounts are saved first, then their sub-accounts, so a sub-account may come before its main account in the file. What is checked The code, the name and the type are there; the same code is not on two lines of the file; the type is one of Account Types and is switched on. A main account named on a line is on the chart or in the file; it is a main account itself (not a sub-account); it is of the same category; an account with sub-accounts is not made a sub-account. A sub-account whose main account is a line in red waits for that line. The rules of the account form for an account of the chart: an account the modules post to (marked system ) keeps a type that behaves as its built-in type and stays active; an account with transactions or with sub-accounts keeps its category. Normal balance is Debit or Credit; With SL and Active are Yes or No. Every account added or updated is written to the audit trail, with the name of the file. The import posts nothing: balances are entered as opening balances or journal entries.

href="#pg-coa-account_types" aria-label="Link to this section"> Account Types lists the account types: the fifteen built-in ones and the types you add yourself, such as Cash or Loans Receivable . Each type is a classification of its own on the Balance Sheet and the Income Statement (a heading, its accounts and a total), and each balance sheet type is linked to a section of the Statement of Cash Flows, so the cash flow statement always ties to the cash accounts. Where to find it: Financial > Account Types, or the Account types button on the Chart of Accounts and on the account form. Account Types: the types of each category, with the types Cash and Loans Receivable among the built-in ones A type of your own behaves as one of the built-in types. The built-in type decides everything the program does with the accounts: their category and normal balance, the group they are shown in (Current Assets, Fixed Assets, Expenses ...) and which forms offer them. An account of the type Cash that behaves as Bank is offered on Write Checks, Make Deposits, the cash vouchers, the teller cash and Reconcile, exactly like a Bank account. Your type adds its own name, its place on the statements and its section of the Statement of Cash Flows. The list The types are shown in five cards, Assets , Liabilities , Equity , Income and Expenses , in the order they take on the statements. Column What it shows Type The name of the type and its description. The fifteen built-in types carry the word built-in in grey; a type you made inactive carries inactive . Behaves as The built-in type it behaves as ( itself for a built-in type). Shown under The group of the statement its heading is shown in, for example Current Assets. Cash flow section Cash and cash equivalents , Operating , Investing or Financing . Income and expense types show Net income : they reach the Statement of Cash Flows through the net income. Accounts How many accounts are of the type. Open / Edit Opens the type: Open for a built-in type, Edit for one of yours. The card On the Statement of Cash Flows beside the list shows which types are in each section. In the demo company, Cash and Bank are the cash and cash equivalents, and Loans Receivable is an operating activity with Accounts Receivable and the other current assets and liabilities. A new account type named Loans Receivable, behaving as Other Current Asset, an operating activity Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name Up to 60 characters, for example Loans Receivable . Two types cannot have the same name. A built-in type keeps its name. Behaves as The built-in type the accounts of this type behave as. The line under it says what the program does with them. It cannot be changed on a built-in type, or on a type that accounts use: move the accounts to another type first. On the Statement of Cash Flows For an asset, liability or equity type: Cash and cash equivalents (its accounts make the cash at the beginning and at the end of the statement), Operating activities , Investing activities or Financing activities (the change in its accounts is shown in that section). It starts at the section of the built-in type (see the table under Account types ). An income or expense type has no choice: it is part of the net income. Order The order among the types that behave as the same built-in type, lower first. The built-in types are numbered 10, 20 ... 150, so a type of yours with the order 5 comes before the built-in type it behaves as: Cash (5) before Bank (10). Description A note about what the type is for, shown under its name in the list. Active Untick to stop offering the type when an account is added or changed. The accounts already of the type keep it. Built-in types are always active. The box at the bottom of the form shows where the type will be, for example "Balance Sheet: Assets > Current Assets > Loans Receivable (its accounts and a total). Statement of Cash Flows: Operating activities." The type Loans Receivable with its five accounts, and the asset accounts of other types that can be given it The accounts of a type An open type has two more cards: Accounts of this type lists its accounts. Tick some, choose another type in Move the ticked accounts to and click Move . Give accounts this type lists the accounts of the same category that are of another type, each with its present type. Type part of a code or name in the search box to narrow the list. Ticking a main account ticks its sub-accounts too; untick any you want to leave. Click Give them the type and the type's name. An account that takes a type of another built-in type behaves as that built-in type from then on: for example an Other Current Asset account given the type Cash (which behaves as Bank) is then offered wherever money is paid or received. Its entries do not change. Accounts the modules post to (with the word system on the Chart of Accounts) are offered only for a type that behaves as their own built-in type. You can also choose the type of one account on its form in the Chart of Accounts . Step by step To add a type, for example Loans Receivable: Open Financial > Account Types and click New account type . Type the Name : Loans Receivable. In Behaves as , choose Other Current Asset . Leave On the Statement of Cash Flows at Operating activities . Type an Order (5 puts it before the other current assets) and a Description if you like. Click Save account type . The message "Account type added. Give it its accounts below." appears and the type stays open. To give accounts a type: Open the type ( Edit on its line). In Give accounts this type , tick the accounts, for example 1210 Loans Receivable - Current, 1211 Loans Receivable - Past Due and the others of the loan portfolio. Click Give them the type Loans Receivable . The message says how many accounts are now of the type. To make a Cash classification of the cash on hand, the cash in banks and the cash funds: add a type named Cash that behaves as Bank , with Cash and cash equivalents on the Statement of Cash Flows, then give it 1000 Cash (its sub-accounts are ticked with it) and any other cash account. The Balance Sheet then shows the heading Cash with these accounts and Total Cash , and the Statement of Cash Flows ends with the same total. To move accounts to another type: open the type they are of, tick them under Accounts of this type , choose the other type in Move the ticked accounts to and click Move . Only types of the same category are offered. To change a type: open it, change what you need and click Save account type . The statements follow at once; no entry changes. To delete a type: open a type of yours that no account uses and click Delete this type , then confirm. A type with accounts must give them to another type first. How the statements show the types Balance Sheet and Income Statement: inside the group of its built-in type (Current Assets, Fixed Assets, Expenses ...), every type has a heading with its name, its accounts and the line Total and the type's name. Where a group holds only one built-in type and none of yours, the group's own heading is enough and the type heading is left out, for example Fixed Assets. Main accounts and sub-accounts: a sub-account is shown under its main account, in the classification of the main account's type. On the Balance Sheet and the Income Statement a main account with sub-accounts is a heading followed by its sub-accounts, a line for its own entries when it has any, and its total. The Balance Sheet Summary and the Income Statement Summary show the main accounts only, each with its total. Statement of Cash Flows: the accounts of the types in Cash and cash equivalents give the cash at the beginning and at the end of the period. The change in every other balance sheet account is shown in the section of its type, under the type's heading with the line Net change in and the type's name. Each account is counted once, so the cash at the end of the period equals the total of the cash accounts on the Balance Sheet. What it records Adding or changing a type and giving accounts a type post nothing and change no amount. Every change is written to the audit trail; giving an account a type is written as a change of that account. Good to know "There is already an account type named "Cash"." Names are compared without regard to capitals. "Choose the section of the Statement of Cash Flows the accounts of this type belong to." An asset, liability or equity type needs its section. "5 account(s) are of this type. Move them to another type first." A type with accounts cannot be deleted, and the built-in type it behaves as cannot change. "The account 1100 is one the modules post to: it can only take a type that behaves as Accounts Receivable." Such accounts keep their built-in type. A sub-account keeps the category of its main account, and an account with entries keeps its category, so types are given within one category. Adding, changing and deleting types needs the special permission Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts ; giving accounts a type also needs Edit on the Chart of Accounts. Users without it see the list only. Import Data accepts the name of any type, built-in or yours, in the account type column of the accounts file.

href="#pg-coa-classes" aria-label="Link to this section"> Classes split the books your own way: by branch, department, project or product line. Every transaction form has a Class box, the class is copied to every ledger line the transaction posts, and the financial reports can be filtered by class or shown with one column per class. You name the classes yourself and can rename them at any time. Where to find it: Financial > Class List The Class List with Head Office, Makati Store and Cebu Store, and the New class form on the right The columns Column What it shows Class name The name shown on forms and reports. Description Your note about the class. Order The position of the class in drop-down lists (lowest first). Entries How many transactions carry this class. Net income (FY) Income less expenses posted with this class in the current fiscal year. Shown only to users who may open Income Statement by Class . Active Yes or No . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Class name Up to 80 characters, for example Main Branch, Piggery or Meat Shop. Two classes cannot share a name. Order in lists A whole number. Classes are listed from the lowest number up, then by name. Description An optional note, up to 255 characters. Active (offered on transaction forms) Untick to stop offering the class on new transactions. It stays on the transactions that already have it and in the report filters. Editing the Head Office class Step by step To add a class: Open Financial > Class List . In the New class panel, type the Class name . Type the Order in lists and a Description if you want them. Click Save class , or Save class & New to add another one straight away. To rename or change a class: Click Edit on the class's line. The panel becomes Edit class . Change the name, order, description or Active box. Click Save class . Click Cancel to go back to a blank form without saving. To delete a class: click Delete on its line and confirm. The link appears only on a class that no transaction carries. Buttons Income Statement by Class , Balance Sheet by Class , Trial Balance by Class and Cash Flows by Class (the Statement of Cash Flows by Class) open the reports that show the classes side by side. What it records Nothing is posted. The class you choose on a transaction is copied to its ledger lines when the transaction is saved. Good to know "Renaming a class changes its name everywhere, including past transactions and reports." Reports always show the current name. "Another class already has this name." Choose a different name. "Cebu Store is already used on transactions, so it cannot be deleted. Make it inactive instead." Any use counts, including a line of a journal entry or a POS terminal's default class. When you save a transaction with the Class box empty, the program asks first: No class selected , "This transaction has no class. It will be saved as Unclassified and will not appear under any class on the class reports." Click Choose a class to go back to the box, or Continue saving . The question is not asked while no class exists yet. On journal entries and cash vouchers each line can carry its own class. The class at the top of the form fills the class of every line that has an account.

href="#pg-coa-names" aria-label="Link to this section"> This list holds the people and bodies that are paid or tracked without being a customer or a supplier: employees (cash advances, reimbursements), owners, government offices and the like. The names appear in the Paid to and SL lists of cash vouchers, in the Name list of journal entries and in the Pay to the order of list of checks, next to the customers and suppliers. Where to find it: Financial > Employees & Other Names Employees & Other Names on the All tab Three tabs filter the list: All , Employees and Other names . The Employees tab The Other names tab, with Barangay Treasurer The columns Column What it shows Name The name as it appears in the pickers. Type Employee or Other name . Employee no. The employee number, if any. Position The position, or the relationship for other names. Phone The phone number. Active Yes or No . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Person or organization already on file On a new name only. When the person is already in the program (a member, customer or supplier), choose it here: the name becomes one more role of that party. Left at Not on file: a new party made from this name , the name gets a party of its own, unless it looks like one on file: then saving stops with the possible matches, and you choose the party or tick This is a different person or organization . See The party on member, customer, supplier and other-name forms . Type Employee or Other name . On the Employees or Other names tab it starts with that type. Name Required, up to 120 characters. The same name cannot be entered twice with the same type. Employee no. Optional, for employees. Position / relationship For example Cashier, or "Permits and clearances". Phone Optional. TIN The tax identification number, if any. Address Optional. Notes Optional. Active Untick to leave the name out of the pickers. It stays on the documents that already have it. Editing an other name Step by step To add a name: Open Financial > Employees & Other Names . In the New name panel, choose the Type . Type the Name and the other details you have. Click Save name , or Save name & New to add another one. To change a name: click Edit on its line, change the details in the Edit name panel, and click Save name . To delete a name: click Delete on its line and confirm. The link appears only on names that no transaction carries. Buttons Cash Voucher opens the Cash Voucher page. Good to know "This name is already on the list." A name of the same type already exists. "Ella Ramos is already used on transactions, so it cannot be deleted. Make it inactive instead." In the pickers, employees are listed as "Ella Ramos (Employee)" and other names as "Barangay Treasurer (Other name)", so you can tell them from a customer or supplier with the same name. Adding a name here does not give that person a login. Users are managed in User Accounts .

href="#pg-coa-memorized_txns" aria-label="Link to this section"> A memorized transaction is a saved copy of a transaction you enter again and again: the monthly rent check, a standing invoice, the payroll journal entry. It keeps the names, accounts, items and amounts; the date and the document number are given each time it is entered. You can enter it from the list whenever you need it, get a reminder when it is due, or let the program enter it on its due date. Where to find it: Financial > Memorized Transactions. The Home page also shows Memorized transactions due with an Open button when a reminder is due (see Home Dashboard ). The Memorized Transactions list with a bill and a check that are overdue The columns Column What it shows Name and type The name you gave it, with its type (Invoice, Bill, Check, Journal Entry, Inventory Adjustment and so on) and its notes underneath. Name on the transaction The customer, supplier or payee of the saved copy. Amount The total of the saved copy. Schedule How it is entered: Automatically , Reminder , When needed or, for an adjustment or a batch of invoices, Loaded when needed (the full wording shows when you point at it), with the frequency under it, for example "Every month" or "Every 2 weeks". Next due The next due date, with Due or Overdue under it when a reminder is due. Entered How many times it was entered, for example "3 of 12 times" when a number is set, with the date of the last entry under it. Lines with a reminder due are marked with a coloured edge. Inactive ones are greyed out. When you use groups, each group has its own heading line. Memorizing a transaction You add to this list in two ways, for users who may create memorized transactions: From the form, before saving: Memorize Transaction beside the save buttons of every transaction form (see Memorize Transaction and Load Memorized Transaction ), and Memorize Adjustment on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . Item receipts, batches of invoices and inventory adjustments are memorized this way. From a saved transaction: the Memorize button on the saved (not voided) invoices, sales receipts, estimates, sales orders, statement charges, credit memos, bills, supplier debit memos, purchase orders, checks, journal entries and cash vouchers. Load Memorized Transaction on a new form fills the form from one of them. On this list, the Open button (open on the form) does the same: it opens a new form of its kind filled from it. The list with memorized adjustments and an invoice memorized from the form: the Open button on every line The Memorize dialog of a bill Field What to enter / what it means Name it Starts as the name on the transaction and its type, for example "Accounting Partners & Co. Bill". Required. Group (optional) A heading to group related entries, for example "Month-end". How it is entered Enter it automatically , Remind me when it is due or Don't remind me (I enter it from the list) . Every A number and a unit: Day(s) , Week(s) , Month(s) , Quarter(s) or Year(s) . Next due The date of the next entry. It starts one month after the transaction's date. Remind (days before) How many days before the due date the reminder starts (0 to 90). Number remaining (blank = no limit) How many more times it should be entered, for example 11 for the rest of a one-year lease. Notes Shown under the name on the list. The three ways of entering: Enter it automatically: the program records the entry on its due date, the first time anyone opens the system that day, and shows "Memorized transaction "..." was entered automatically for 09/03/2026." If several due dates were missed, it catches up one date at a time, each entry with its own date. Remind me when it is due: from the set number of days before the due date, the line shows Due (or Overdue once the date has passed) and the Home page lists it. You enter it with Enter now . Don't remind me (I enter it from the list): it waits on the list until you enter it. Step by step To memorize a transaction: Open the saved transaction, for example a bill from Accounting Partners & Co. Click Memorize . Check Name it and choose a Group if you use groups. Choose How it is entered . Set Every , for example 1 Month(s) , and the Next due date. Set Remind (days before) and Number remaining if needed. Click Memorize . The message "Memorized as "...". It is on the Memorized Transactions list." confirms it. To enter a memorized transaction now: Open Financial > Memorized Transactions . Click Enter now on its line. The dialog Enter a memorized transaction opens. Check the Date of the entry . It starts at the next due date. Leave Move the schedule on to the next due date ticked if this entry is the one that was due. Untick it for an extra entry that should not move the schedule. Click Enter it . The document is recorded straight away and opens so you can check it. To change the schedule: Click the pencil button on the line. In the Edit form at the top, change the Name , Group (optional) , How it is entered , Every , Next due , Remind (days before) , Number remaining (blank = no limit) , Stop after , Active or Notes . Click Save . To take one off the list: click the trash button and confirm "Take "..." off the memorized list? The transactions already entered from it are not touched." Buttons New journal entry opens a blank Make Journal Entries form. Enter now is shown on active lines to users who may create memorized transactions. It is green when the line is due. Open opens a new form filled from the line, to change and save. A batch of invoices and an inventory adjustment are always used this way (their figures are revised each time), so they have no Enter now ; their button is green when they are due. What it records Entering a memorized transaction saves an ordinary transaction of its type, with a new number and the date you chose, and posts it exactly as if you had typed it. An invoice or bill gets its due date from its terms. After the entry, Last entered , Entered and Number remaining are updated and Next due moves on by the frequency. Each entry is noted in the audit trail. Good to know The saved copy does not change when you edit the original transaction later. To change the amounts, memorize the corrected transaction again and delete the old line. When Number remaining reaches zero, or the next due date falls after Stop after , the memorized transaction becomes inactive and is no longer entered or reminded. An automatic entry that cannot be recorded (for example because its date is on or before the closing date, or a default account is missing) is switched to Remind me when it is due and the reason is written to the audit trail. Enter it by hand once the problem is fixed. Opening balance entries and voided transactions cannot be memorized. The transactions entered from the list are ordinary transactions: change, void or delete them on their own pages.

href="#pg-coa-budgets" aria-label="Link to this section"> A budget holds the amounts you plan for each account, month by month, for one fiscal year. A budget is for the income statement or for the balance sheet, and can be limited to one class. The Income Statement vs Budget and Balance Sheet vs Budget reports put the actual figures beside it and show the difference. Where to find it: Financial > Set Up Budgets. The same page, for sales forecasts per customer, is Customers > Set Up Forecast (see Set Up Forecast ). Set Up Budgets with no budget yet The columns Column What it shows Name The budget's name. Click it to enter the amounts. What it budgets Income statement (profit and loss) or Balance sheet . Fiscal year The year, or the months it covers when the fiscal year does not start in January. Class The class the budget is for, if any. Yearly total The sum of all its monthly amounts. Notes Your notes. Each line has an Amounts button and a delete (trash) button. The New budget form Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name For example "Budget 2027". Required. What it budgets Income statement (profit and loss) lists the Income, Other Income, Cost of Goods Sold, Expense and Other Expense accounts. Balance sheet lists the asset, liability and equity accounts. Fiscal year The year the budget is for. The months follow the fiscal year set in Company, Security & Closing Date ; the form says in which month it starts. Class (optional) Leave blank for the whole company, or choose a class to budget one branch or department. The actual figures are then only those of that class. Notes Optional. Start from last year's actual figures Fills the grid with the actual figures of the year before, so you adjust them instead of typing everything. The amounts grid After Create , the budget opens in its amounts grid. Each active account of the budget's kind has a row, grouped by account type, with a box for each of the twelve months and a Year total. The Total row at the bottom adds up each month. Fill a row: type an amount, click in any box of a row, then click Across . Every month of that row gets the amount. Yearly total: type a yearly amount, click in a row, then click Spread . The amount is divided evenly over the twelve months; the last month takes the centavos left over. Notes: change the budget's notes. Enter income and expense amounts as positive figures. For a balance sheet budget, enter the balance you expect at the end of each month, also as positive figures for assets, liabilities and equity. Step by step To create a budget: Open Financial > Set Up Budgets . Click New budget . Type the Name , choose What it budgets and type the Fiscal year . Choose a Class if the budget is for one class. Tick Start from last year's actual figures if you want the grid filled for you. Click Create . The grid opens with the message "Budget 2027 created. Enter the monthly amounts below." Type or change the monthly amounts. Click Save the amounts . The message says how many monthly amounts were saved. To change the amounts later: click the budget's name or Amounts , change the figures and click Save the amounts . To compare with the actual figures: on the grid click Compare with actual , or open the report from Income statement vs budget on the list. To delete a budget: click the trash button on its line and confirm "Delete "..." and its amounts?". What it records A budget posts nothing to the books. It is only compared with the ledger by the budget reports. Good to know "There is already a budget called "Budget 2027" for 2027." Two budgets of the same kind and year cannot share a name. "Enter the fiscal year." The year must be between 2000 and 2100. When Start from last year's actual figures is ticked, the copied figures are only shown on the grid ("Last year's actual figures were copied in. Change what you need and press Save."). They are kept only after you click Save the amounts . Empty boxes and zeros are not saved. The Compare with actual button opens the report on the newest budget of that kind. If you have several budgets, choose the one you want in the report's Budget box.

href="#pg-coa-journal" aria-label="Link to this section"> A journal entry posts debits and credits directly to the accounts you choose. Routine activity posts automatically from invoices, bills, payments and the POS, so you use journal entries for what no other form records: opening balances, accruals, reclassifications, corrections and closing entries. Where to find it: Financial > Make Journal Entries opens the list of journal entries. The Home page quick action Make Journal Entries opens a blank entry. The Journal Entries list The list shows the journal entries and opening balance entries of a date range (from 90 days back to 30 days ahead when it opens). Use From , To , Status ( Posted or Void ), Class and Search (number, name or memo), then click Filter . Click a number to open the entry. Export downloads the list. A new journal entry Fields Field What to enter / what it means Date The date the entry posts on. Entry no. Leave blank to get the next number (the grey text shows it, for example JE-00005). Type your own number only if you need one. Reference An outside reference, for example a document number. Memo What the entry is for. It is used as the memo of every line that has none. Class The class of the whole entry. It fills the class of every line. Opening balance entry Tick for the entry that brings in your opening balances. It is then labelled Opening Balance instead of Journal Entry. Explanation Shown only when you change a saved entry: why the entry is changed (at least 10 characters). The approver reads it, and it is kept with the change in the audit trail. The lines: Column What to enter / what it means Account Type part of the account name to find it, for example "rent" for 6010 Rent Expense. Debit The debit amount of the line. Credit The credit amount of the line. A line has a debit or a credit, not both. Memo The description of the line. Name A customer, supplier, employee or other name. Required on Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable and With SL accounts. Class The class of the line. Change it only when this line belongs to another class. Under the lines, Totals shows the debits and the credits, and Difference shows what is still out of balance. Add line adds a row; the red X removes one. Step by step To make a journal entry: Open Financial > Make Journal Entries and click New journal entry . Check the Date . Type a Reference and a Memo . Choose the Class if you use classes. On the first line, choose the Account and type the Debit . On the next line, choose the account and type the Credit . Add more lines if needed, until Difference shows 0.00. Choose a Name on every line that needs one. Click Save entry , or Save entry & New to start another one. Example To accrue September rent of ₱85,000.00 that will be billed in October, debit 6010 Rent Expense ₱85,000.00 and credit 2200 Accrued Expenses ₱85,000.00, with the memo "Accrued rent, September". To enter opening balances: Start a new journal entry dated the day before you begin using the system. Tick Opening balance entry . Debit each asset account with its balance and credit each liability and equity account with its balance. Save when Difference is 0.00. In the demo company, OB-0001 debits 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking ₱2,500,000.00 and the other cash accounts, and credits 3000 Owner's Capital ₱3,320,000.00. To change a journal entry: a saved entry is changed only with the approval of a second, authorized user (a user with the Approve right on Make Journal Entries). Open the entry from the list. Click Edit (needs approval) . Change the lines or the header. Type the Explanation : why the entry is changed. If the approver is with you, open Supervisor approval and let them type their user name and password (or an approval code); the change is made at once. Otherwise leave it empty. Click Save the change . Without an approver at the desk the change waits on Journal Entry Changes , and the entry stays as it is until it is approved. An entry with a change waiting shows a yellow notice with Review the change , and an entry that was changed lists its changes under Changes made to this entry . To print a journal entry: open it and click Print , then click Print above the page. See the print format below. To void or delete a journal entry: open it, click Void or Delete , type the reason and confirm. Voiding keeps the entry with no effect on the ledger; deleting removes it, and a full copy stays in the audit trail. To memorize a journal entry: open it and click Memorize (see Memorized Transactions ). A saved opening balance entry, with the general ledger entries it created The saved entry shows the date, number, status, memo, class and who entered it, the lines as you entered them, and General ledger entries created automatically with the total debits and credits. A ledger line that was cleared in a bank reconciliation is marked cleared . Buttons Edit , Print , Memorize , Void , Delete : see the procedures above. Each appears only when you have the permission. History opens the Transaction History of the entry. Back to list returns to the Journal Entries list. Journal list (on the form) goes back to the list without saving. The print format The printed journal entry has the company name, address and TIN (and the logo, when the administrator has switched it on for this document), the title JOURNAL ENTRY or OPENING BALANCE , the number and the date. Under it are the memo, reference, site and class, then a table with Account , Description , Name , Class , Debit and Credit , the two totals, and the signature lines Prepared by (the user who entered it), Checked by and Approved by . A line without its own class prints the class of the entry. The printed opening balance entry What it records Each line posts to its account exactly as entered: a debit line debits the account, a credit line credits it. The name and the class of the line go with it to the ledger, so a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable with the name ABC Trading Corp. changes that customer's balance. An opening balance entry posts the same way; only its label differs. Good to know "A journal entry needs at least two lines." "Debits (85,000.00) must equal credits (80,000.00)." The totals must agree to the centavo. "Choose an account for every journal line." A line with an amount needs an account. "A journal line cannot have both a debit and a credit." Split it into two lines. "Lines posted to Accounts Receivable need a customer name." and "Lines posted to Accounts Payable need a vendor name." Choose the name on that line. A journal entry to Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable changes the customer's or supplier's balance, but it is not an invoice or a bill: it does not appear in Receive Payments or Pay Bills . Use those modules for sales and purchases. A journal entry never changes item quantities, even when it posts to 1200 Inventory. Use Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand for stock. "The books are closed through 06/28/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date." Only users with the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled can post on or before the closing date, or change an entry that was cleared in a bank reconciliation. A voided entry cannot be edited. When the Class at the top is empty but every line that has an account carries its own class, the program saves without asking about the class. Journal entry numbers (JE-) are shared with other entries the program makes itself, such as bank service charges, interest earned and cash over and short, so the numbers on this list may skip.

href="#pg-coa-je_edits" aria-label="Link to this section"> The changes to saved journal entries (and opening balance entries) that wait for approval, and the ones decided. A change is made only when a second user approves it: the maker asks, with the explanation; the checker compares and approves or rejects. Where to find it: Financial > Journal Entry Changes, or Journal entry changes on the journal entry form. Users without the Approve right on Make Journal Entries see their own requests. The list has the tabs Waiting for approval , Approved , Rejected , Withdrawn and All , with who asked and when, the entry, the explanation, the status and who decided. Click Review (or Open ) to see one change. Reviewing a change The change shows the entry, who asked, when and why, and Before and after : the entry as it is now and the entry as proposed, line by line, with the values the change alters highlighted. A change of the date, number, reference, memo, class or line of business is listed above the lines. Approve and apply saves the entry with the proposed lines at once, through the same checks as a new entry (balanced debits and credits, the closing date), with the explanation as the reason in the audit trail. Reject leaves the entry as it is. Type the reason in Remarks first: the user who asked reads it. Withdraw the request (the user who asked, while it waits) takes the change back. Good to know A change is approved by someone other than the user who asked for it, with the Approve right on Make Journal Entries (System Administration > Page Access). "The journal entry was changed since this request was made." The entry changed after the request: reject it and ask again on the entry as it is now. A newer change to the same entry replaces the one waiting (it is marked Replaced by a later request ). Every request, approval, rejection and withdrawal is in the audit trail.

href="#pg-coa-default_accounts" aria-label="Link to this section"> Each module posts to a set of default accounts: the receivable, the payable, the tax accounts, the inventory and cost of sales, the clearing accounts of the POS and so on. They are set up before any transaction is recorded. Items, tax codes, payment methods and fixed asset categories can carry their own accounts; the defaults are used when they do not. Where to find it: Financial > Module Default Accounts, or the Module default accounts button on the Chart of Accounts. Module Default Accounts for the demo company Fields Default What it is used for Accounts Receivable Debited by invoices, statement charges and finance charges; credited by payments and credit memos. Creditable Withholding Tax Debited with the income tax (1% / 2%) a customer withholds on a payment. Creditable VAT Withheld Debited with the VAT (5%) a government customer withholds on a payment: a VAT credit (2550Q Item 16). Default Sales Income Credited by sales lines whose item has no income account. Finance Charge Income Credited by assessed finance charges. Output Tax Credited with VAT on sales when the tax code has no output tax account. Reimbursable Expense Income Credited when billable costs are added to an invoice. Sales Discounts Debited with early-payment discounts given on customer payments. Sales Returns and Allowances Debited by credit memo lines. Undeposited Funds Debited by payments and sales receipts waiting to be deposited; credited by Make Deposits. Accounts Payable Credited by bills; debited by bill payments and supplier debit memos. Default Purchases / Expense Debited by purchase lines whose non-stock item has no expense account. Input Tax Debited with VAT on purchases when the tax code has no input tax account. Purchase Discounts Credited with early-payment discounts taken in Pay Bills. Withholding Tax Payable (Expanded) Credited with the income tax (1% / 2%) withheld from suppliers in Pay Bills, until it is remitted (0619-E, 1601-EQ). VAT Withheld Payable Credited with the VAT (5%) withheld from suppliers in Pay Bills, until it is remitted (1600-VT). Advances to Suppliers Debited by advances paid to suppliers; credited when they are applied to bills. Cost of Goods Sold Debited with the cost of stock sold, when the item has no cost of sales account. Inventory Adjustment (Shrinkage) The other side of inventory adjustments and physical counts. Inventory Asset The stock account of items that have no asset account of their own. Processing / Disassembly Variance The variance of processing orders. Item Group Price Variance The group price of the item groups sold less the prices of their items, for the groups without a price variance account of their own. Processing Labor & Overhead Absorbed Credited with labor and overhead added to processing orders. Card Clearing POS card and other non-cash tenders whose payment method has no clearing account. Cash on Hand (Register) POS cash sales of a terminal that has no cash account of its own. Cash Over and Short The difference found when a POS shift is closed. E-wallet Clearing POS e-wallet tenders whose payment method has no clearing account. Bank / Merchant Charges Merchant fees on card settlements in Make Deposits, and the suggested service charge account in Reconcile. Interest Income The suggested interest account in Reconcile. Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets The gain or loss when a fixed asset is disposed of. Opening Balance Equity The other side of opening balances brought in with items and fixed assets. Retained Earnings Holds the net income of earlier fiscal years on the Trial Balance and the Balance Sheet. Step by step To change a default account: Open Financial > Module Default Accounts . In the card of the module, choose the new account in the drop-down beside the label. Change any other defaults you need. Click Save default accounts . The message says how many defaults were changed. Good to know Changing a default affects only transactions saved from then on. Saved transactions keep what they posted, until they are edited and saved again. Only active accounts are offered. A default cannot be cleared back to — not set — once it is set. The boxes are greyed out, with the note "You need the "Chart of Accounts changes" permission to edit these.", for users who lack the edit permission on this page or the special permission Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts .
