A customer's usual taxes ( Taxes this customer withholds on its record) are ticked when its invoice is ticked. The box works even before the invoice is ticked: its tax base already shows the open balance net of VAT, and ticking a tax ticks the invoice. The withholding taxes of an invoice: WT on Goods 1% ticked Example (a government buyer): the City Government of Makati pays an invoice of ₱100,688.00 (₱89,900.00 plus ₱10,788.00 VAT) and withholds 5% VAT (₱4,495.00) and 1% income tax (₱899.00) on the ₱89,900.00. Tick WT on VAT and WT on Goods on the invoice: Payment becomes ₱95,294.00, the check received. The two kinds are kept apart, as the BIR requires: the 1% / 2% income tax withheld is debited to 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax (a credit against the company's income tax), the 5% VAT withheld to 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld (a VAT credit, 2550Q Item 16, listed in the Creditable VAT Withheld Schedule ). Neither is input VAT. A payment saved before the taxes were kept by type keeps its withholding as it was. A payment with the 5% VAT and 1% income tax the customer withheld To give the early-payment discount: Enter the payment date. If it is within the discount days of the invoice's terms (for example "2% 10 Net 30"), the Disc. avail. column shows the discount and the Discount box shows it in grey. Type the discount in Discount . It is not filled in for you. Apply the rest as the payment. Example Cebu Tech Hub pays INV-00006 of ₱96,718.72 within 10 days on terms 2% 10 Net 30. The discount is ₱1,934.37, and the payment ₱94,784.35. To apply available credits (unapplied payments or credit memos): Choose the customer. The Available credits card lists each credit with its date, memo and available amount. Click Apply available credits to spread all the credits over the open invoices, the ticked ones first, then the oldest; or type an amount in Apply now on a credit; or type an amount in the Credits column of an invoice. Add a payment if money was also received, or leave Amount received blank to apply only the credits. Click Save payment . The message says how much credit was applied ("Credits applied." when no money was received). To refund an overpayment: Record the payment with the full amount received. The part not applied stays as a credit: "Overpayment of … is kept as a credit for this customer." Tick Refund any overpayment before saving to go straight to the refund form, or later click Refund on the payment. See Create Credit Memos/Refunds . To change a payment, open it from the Payments list and click Edit . The customer cannot be changed. Payments taken at the POS are changed from the POS module. The list of customer payments Payments list opens the list of customer payments. Its Status filter offers Has unapplied credit , Fully applied and Void , and the Open column shows the unused part of each payment. What it records Account Debit Credit Deposit to (1050 Undeposited Funds) Amount received 4060 Sales Discounts Discounts 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax Income tax withheld (1% / 2%) 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld VAT withheld (5%) 1100 Accounts Receivable Total of the above For the ABC Trading Corp. example: debit Undeposited Funds ₱100,000.00 and Creditable Withholding Tax ₱1,500.00, credit Accounts Receivable ₱101,500.00. The invoices paid become Partial or Paid. Applying a credit moves no money and records no ledger entry: the credit memo or earlier payment already reduced Accounts Receivable. It only links the credit to the invoice, so both show as settled. Good to know The payments applied can never be more than the amount received. The Unapplied figure turns red, a message explains, and the save buttons are disabled until you correct it or click Auto-apply amount . Messages you may see: "Choose a customer.", "The amount received cannot be negative.", "The amount applied to INV-… is more than its open balance (…).", "You applied … but received only …. Lower the payments on the invoices, or correct the amount received.", "Credit … has only … available.", "Enter the amount received or choose credits to apply." and "The credits chosen (…) are more than the open invoices can take. Lower the credit amounts by …". Pending invoices are not listed; mark them final first. Credits recorded on a job are not listed when you receive a payment from the customer. Open the job's credit memo and click Apply credit to invoices instead. A payment included in a bank deposit cannot be voided or deleted until it is removed from the deposit. Voiding a payment removes its applications, so its invoices are open again. Money in Undeposited Funds reaches the bank account with Make Deposits .

href="#pg-cust-credit_memos" aria-label="Link to this section"> A credit memo reduces what a customer owes: for goods returned, a price correction or an allowance. The credit can be kept for later, applied to an invoice at once, or paid back as a refund. This page also records refunds of overpayments. Where to find it: Customers > Create Credit Memos/Refunds. Also Credit memo in the Customer Center, and Create Credit Memos/Refunds under Quick actions on the Home dashboard. The list of credit memos and refunds The list shows credit memos and customer refunds together, with a Type column. The Open column shows the credit still available. A refund queued for printing shows "to print" beside its status until it is printed. A new credit memo Fields The common fields are explained under Working with sales forms, earlier in this chapter. The credit memo adds: Field What to enter / what it means Reference For example the invoice the goods were sold on. Inventory site The site of the sale. Return goods to stock Ticked by default: stocked items come back into inventory. Return to site Where returned goods go. Same as inventory site by default. On a new credit memo, the What to do with this credit card asks: Field What to enter / what it means Credit Keep as available credit , Apply to an invoice now or Give a refund . Invoice With Apply: the open invoice to reduce. Choose the customer first so the list fills. Step by step To record returned goods: Click New . Choose the Customer:Job . The page reloads for the customer. Leave Return goods to stock ticked if the goods can be sold again, and choose Return to site if they go to another site. Untick it for defective goods that will not return to stock. Enter the items, quantities and rates returned, with the same tax code as the sale. Type a Memo such as "Returned 2 defective keyboards". In Credit , choose what to do with it: Keep as available credit : the customer uses it on a later payment. Apply to an invoice now : choose the Invoice ; the credit reduces it by up to its open balance. Give a refund : after saving, the refund form opens ("Now record how the refund was paid."). Click Save . A saved credit memo with its unapplied credit To apply a kept credit later, open the credit memo and click Apply credit to invoices . Receive Payments opens with all the customer's available credits spread over the open invoices; change the amounts if needed and click Save payment . See Receive Payments . To refund a credit memo or an overpayment: Open the credit memo or payment and click Refund (shown while it has unapplied credit). The page "Refund Credit Memo CM-00001" shows the customer and the available credit. Fill in: Date . Pay from account : the bank account the refund is paid from. Required. Refund method : cash, check and so on. Amount : the available credit by default; you may refund less. Memo : "Refund of Credit Memo CM-00001" by default. Class , when classes are set up. Queue a refund check for printing : tick if a check will be printed. Click Record refund . The program shows "Refund recorded." and opens the refund. The refund takes the next check number and prints as a REFUND VOUCHER with the payee, address, TIN, amount in words, the account paid from, the ledger lines and signature lines including Received by . The printed credit memo What it records A credit memo is the reverse of a sale. Each line is debited to 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances (whatever item it is), its tax is debited to the output tax account, and the total is credited to 1100 Accounts Receivable. With Return goods to stock ticked, stocked items come back into the site at the current average cost: debit Inventory, credit Cost of Goods Sold. Example CM-00001 credits Metro School Supplies for 2 keyboards returned to stock. Account Debit Credit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances ₱1,898.10 2100 Output Tax ₱227.77 1200 Inventory ₱1,233.33 5000 Cost of Goods Sold ₱1,233.33 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱2,125.87 A refund pays the credit back: Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable Refund amount Pay from account (bank) Refund amount The credit memo's status is Open while it has unapplied credit and Closed when it is fully applied or refunded. Good to know Refund messages: "The refund must be more than zero and no more than the available credit (…)." and "Choose the account the refund is paid from." A refund above your role's "Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval" needs supervisor approval ("refund above your amount limit"). Voiding or deleting a refund above that amount needs approval too. Refunds cannot be edited: "Refunds cannot be edited. Void it and record a new one." A credit memo that was refunded cannot be voided until the refund is voided: "It has been refunded (…). Void the refund first." Voiding a credit memo that was applied removes the application and reopens the invoice. The What to do with this credit card only appears on a new credit memo. Discount and price limits are not checked on credit memos.

href="#s-customer-and-receivables-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> These reports show who owes what, how old the amounts are and how customers pay. They share the report tools explained in Working with reports : Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize , and clicking a figure or number to open what is behind it. All of them are in the sidebar under Customers > Reports , in the group "Customer and Receivables Reports", and in Home > Report Center . Where a report has a Customer filter, choosing a customer also includes its jobs. The aging reports sort each open amount by the number of days past its due date at the As of date: Current (not yet due, and all unapplied credits), 1 - 30 , 31 - 60 , 61 - 90 and > 90 days past due. Pending invoices are never included.

href="#pg-rpt-ar_aging_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> Shows, for each customer and job, how much is owed and how long it has been overdue. Use it to see at a glance who to call first. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > A/R Aging Summary. Also the "overdue document(s)" link under Accounts Receivable on the Home dashboard. The A/R Aging Summary as of 09/27/2026 Filters: As of and Customer . Each row is a customer or job with its open amounts in the five aging columns and the Total . Unapplied payments and credits are included as negative Current amounts, so Metro School Supplies shows -₱2,625.87 in Current. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ). Above the table the report checks itself against the ledger: "Accounts Receivable per ledger: 253,913.11 — agrees with the aging total." If it says the ledger "differs from the aging total", something was posted to Accounts Receivable without a customer document, usually a journal entry; look for it in the General Ledger. Click a customer to open the A/R Aging Detail for that customer.

href="#pg-rpt-ar_aging_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every open document grouped by aging period, so you can see exactly which invoices are late. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > A/R Aging Detail The A/R Aging Detail as of 09/27/2026 Filters: As of and Customer . The groups are Current, 1 - 30 days past due, 31 - 60, 61 - 90 and > 90, each with its total. The columns are Type , Date , Num (click to open), Customer , Terms , Due date , Days past due and Open balance . The report keeps its own order and cannot be re-sorted. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-customer_balance_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> Shows the Accounts Receivable balance of every customer and job at a date, straight from the ledger. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Customer Balance Summary The report can also be narrowed by Customer , Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ). The Customer Balance Summary as of 09/27/2026 Filter: As of . Columns: Customer:Job and Balance . Only customers with a balance are listed. When every entry to Accounts Receivable names a customer, the total equals the Accounts Receivable account on the Balance Sheet at the same date. Click a name for its Customer Balance Detail.

href="#pg-rpt-customer_balance_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every transaction that changed each customer's balance, with a running balance. Use it to answer "how did we arrive at this balance?". Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Customer Balance Detail, or Balance detail in the Customer Center. The Customer Balance Detail as of 09/27/2026 Filters: As of and Customer . For each customer and job: Type , Date , Num , Memo , Amount (charges positive, payments and credits negative) and the running Balance , then a total. A payment shows the full amount taken off the balance, including any discount and withholding: PMT-00001 shows -₱101,500.00. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-open_invoices" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every unpaid invoice, statement charge and finance charge, and every unapplied payment or credit memo, grouped by customer. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Open Invoices The Open Invoices report as of 09/27/2026 Filters: As of and Customer . Columns: Type , Date , Num , Terms , Due date , Days past due and Open balance , with a total per customer. Unapplied credits appear as "Unapplied Customer Payment" or "Unapplied Credit Memo" with a negative amount. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ). Tip Unapplied credits next to open invoices of the same customer can be applied to them in Receive Payments , with or without new money.

href="#pg-rpt-collections" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists only the overdue documents, with the customer's contact person, phone and email, ready for collection calls. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Collections Report The Collections Report as of 09/27/2026 Filters: As of and Customer . Each customer heading shows the Contact , Phone (phone and mobile) and the email in the Num / email column. Under it: Type , Date , Num / email (the document number), Due date , Days overdue and Amount due , with a total per customer. Documents not yet due and unapplied credits are left out. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-avg_days_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> Shows how many days, on average, each customer takes to pay an invoice in full. Use it to review credit terms and credit limits. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Average Days to Pay Summary The Average Days to Pay Summary for this fiscal year Filters: Dates (this fiscal year by default), From , To and Customer . Columns: Customer , Invoices paid and Average days to pay , and an OVERALL AVERAGE row. Only invoices fully paid during the period count; the days run from the invoice date to the date of the payment or credit that finished paying it. Statement and finance charges are not included. Click a customer for the detail. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-avg_days_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the paid invoices behind the average, one by one. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Average Days to Pay The Average Days to Pay detail for this fiscal year Filters: Dates , From , To and Customer . For each customer: Invoice , Invoice date , Amount , Paid in full (the date) and Days to pay , then "Average for" the customer, and the overall average at the bottom. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-ar_graph" aria-label="Link to this section"> Pictures the receivables: a bar chart of the amounts by aging period and a pie chart of the share owed by each customer. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Accounts Receivable Graph The report can also be narrowed by Customer type and Member type (see Filters on related records ). The Accounts Receivable Graph as of 09/27/2026 Filter: As of . Receivables by aging period shows one bar per period; click a figure to open the A/R Aging Detail. Share of total owed by customer shows the five largest customers and "All others". The table lists every customer (jobs counted with their customer) with Owed and % of total . As the report notes, "A few customers owing a large share of the total indicates concentration risk." In the demo company, ABC Trading Corp. alone owes 70.2%.

href="#pg-rpt-unbilled_costs" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the costs marked billable to a customer or job in Enter Bills or Write Checks that have not been added to an invoice yet, so no reimbursable expense is forgotten. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Unbilled Cost by Job The report can also be narrowed by Customer type , Member type and Vendor (see Filters on related records ). The Unbilled Cost by Job report Filter: Customer . For each customer or job: Type (Bill or Check), Date , Num , Vendor , Account / item , Memo and Amount , with totals. To bill them, start an invoice for the customer; the costs appear in its Billable time and costs for this customer card (see Create Invoices ). Once invoiced, a cost leaves this report.

href="#pg-rpt-txn_list_customer" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every customer transaction in a period, grouped by customer and job. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Transaction List by Customer, or Transaction list in the Customer Center. The Transaction List by Customer for September 2026 Filters: Dates , From , To , Customer , Type (one kind of transaction) and Include estimates and sales orders (unticked, only posting documents are listed). href="#pg-rpt-item_price_list" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the selling price of every active item, and its price at every active price level. href="#pg-rpt-income_customer_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> What each customer's purchases earned in a period: the sales of the items sold to the customer less what those items cost, that is the income, or the loss when the cost is higher. Use it to see which customers are worth the most to the business, and which ones are sold to at a loss. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Income by Customer Summary Income by Customer Summary with the sales, cost of sales, income and margin of each customer Filters: Dates (this month as delivered), From , To , Sales rep , Class and Site . One line per customer or job, and Walk-in / cash sales for counter sales without a customer: The report can also be narrowed by Customer type , Member type , Item , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Sort by puts the customers in the order of Qty sold , Sales , Cost of sales , Income / (loss) or Margin % , Increasing or Decreasing : for example Income / (loss) , Decreasing lists the most profitable customers first and the losses last. Default order lists them by name (see Sorting ). Income by Customer Summary sorted by Income / (loss), decreasing Column Meaning Transactions How many invoices, sales receipts, POS sales, credit memos and returns the customer had. Qty sold The quantity of items, less what came back. Sales The sales of those items, net of VAT and discounts, less credit memos and returns. Cost of sales What the items cost when they were sold (their average cost at that moment). Income / (loss) Sales less cost of sales. A negative figure is a loss and its line is marked with a red edge. Margin % Income as a share of the sales. Cost, income and margin are shown only to users who may view costs. Services and other items that are not stocked have no cost, so all their sales are income. Click a customer for the Income by Customer Detail of the same period.

href="#pg-rpt-income_customer_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> The same figures line by line: every item sold to each customer in the period, with what it earned. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Income by Customer Detail Income by Customer Detail: the items sold to each customer with their cost and income Filters: Dates , From , To , Customer , Item , Sales rep , Class and Site . For each customer a heading line, then one line per item sold: Type , Date , Num (click to open the transaction), Item (click for the Inventory Center), Qty , Sales price , Sales , Cost of sales , Income / (loss) and Margin % , and a total per customer. Returns and credit memos are negative lines; a line sold below cost is marked with a red edge. The report can also be narrowed by Customer type , Member type , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). Tip Sort out a loss by opening the transaction from Num : a price typed too low, a discount above the limit, or an item whose cost went up after its price was set. Set Item Prices and Levels can price items from their cost plus a markup.

href="#pg-rpt-sales_item_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every sale of each item in a period. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Sales by Item Detail Sales by Item Detail for September 2026 Filters: Dates , From , To , Customer , Item and Class . href="#pg-rpt-sales_item_group" aria-label="Link to this section"> The item groups sold, counted as groups and not as the items in them, so you can see which groups sell the most. Sales in every module count: invoices, sales receipts, statement charges and POS sales, less credit memos and POS returns. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Sales by Item Group. Column Meaning Item group name The group (click it to open its form). Qty The number of groups sold. Group price The average price of one group: the total over the quantity. Total What the groups sold for, before tax. Click it to see the transactions. Sort by puts the groups in the order of Qty or Total , Increasing or Decreasing ; with the item details or the transactions shown, they move with their group. Default order lists the groups by code (see Sorting ). The Totals line adds up the quantities and totals. Consolidated price , Price variance , Tax and Transactions can be added with Modify Report . With Show the individual item details ticked, each group is followed by its items (quantity, price and amount) and its price variance, then a total for the group; with Show the transactions , by each invoice, sales receipt and POS sale it was sold on. Sales by Item Group with the individual item details The report reads the groups recorded while Track Item Group Sales transactions was ticked; when it is cleared, the report says so.

Only inventory and assembly items are counted. For each site: Site / item , Qty sold , Sales and Cost of sales , with site totals. href="#pg-rpt-sales_inv_movement" aria-label="Link to this section"> The quantity sold worked out from the stock: what each item had at the start, what was delivered, what was withdrawn and what is left at the end. The difference is what the sales took out, valued at the average selling price of the period. Use it to check the sales against the inventory, for example for a store that counts its stock at the end of the day. Where to find it: Customers > Reports > Sales Report Through Inventory Movement. It is given to the roles that may open Sales by Item Summary. Sales Report Through Inventory Movement: beginning inventory, delivery, withdrawals, ending inventory, sales quantity, average price and total sales Filters: Dates with a From date and time and a To date and time (this month as delivered), Item , Site , Class , Category , Cashier , Shift and Exclude zero sales . The times let a business open 24 hours see the sales, deliveries, withdrawals and ending inventory of each shift (for example 12:01 AM - 8:00 AM, 8:01 AM - 2:00 PM and 2:01 PM - 12:00 AM), and so the cash sales and the stock each cashier is answerable for; Shift fills in the time a POS shift was opened and closed. See Dates with times, cashier and shift . Tick Exclude zero sales to leave out the items with no sales in the period (of the cashier, when one is chosen). Column Meaning Item description The inventory part or assembly. The Item code can be added with Modify Report . Beg. inventory The ending inventory of the day before the From date. Delivery (in) What came in during the period: Write Checks and Cash Vouchers with inventory (positive or negative), Receive Items, Receive Items and Enter Bills, Transfer Inventory to the site, Adjust Quantity (positive), Build Assemblies (the assembled items) and Disassemble / Process Items (the outputs). Invoices, batch invoices, sales receipts and POS sales are not included. Withdrawals (out) What went out other than by sales: Transfer Inventory from the site, Adjust Quantity (negative), Build Assemblies (the component items), Disassemble / Process Items (the inputs consumed) and Supplier Debit Memos. Invoices, batch invoices, sales receipts and POS sales are not included. Ending inventory The ending inventory of the To date. Sales (qty) Beg. inventory + Delivery - Withdrawals - Ending inventory : the quantity the invoices, batch invoices, sales receipts and POS sales took out of stock, less credit memos and POS returns that restock. Ave. price The average price per unit of those invoices, batch invoices, sales receipts and POS sales: their amount over the quantity sold. Total sales Sales (qty) × Ave. price , which equals the total amount of the invoices, batch invoices, sales receipts and POS sales of the item. Click it for Sales by Item Detail . The TOTAL line adds up the quantities and the total sales; its Ave. price is the total sales over the total quantity sold. Only transactions dated within the range count, and voided ones are left out. Click a beginning, delivery, withdrawal, ending or sales figure to see its source transactions in Inventory Movement Transactions . Example Cheese sticks: 10 at the start, 5 delivered, 2 withdrawn and 8 left at the end, so 5 were sold. The invoices and POS sales of the period sold them for ₱75.00, an average of ₱15.00, so Total sales is 5 × ₱15.00 = ₱75.00. Sales of one cashier Choose a Cashier (the users who entered sales documents or worked a POS shift) to see that cashier's share; the site becomes the outlet the cashier worked at. Sales (qty) , Ave. price and Total sales are then those of the sales documents the cashier entered, and a Sold by other cashiers column shows the rest of the quantity sold, so Sales (qty) + Sold by other cashiers is still Beg. inventory + Delivery - Withdrawals - Ending inventory . The stock columns stay those of the site, as stock does not belong to a cashier. The report for one cashier, with the quantity sold by the other cashiers With a Shift chosen, the report covers that shift alone, at its terminal's site: the beginning inventory when it opened, the sales rung up during it, and the ending inventory when it closed. The report for one POS shift with Exclude zero sales ticked: only the items sold during the shift

href="#pg-rpt-pending_sales" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the invoices and sales receipts saved as pending, which have not yet posted. href="#pg-rpt-open_so_customer" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists what is still to be delivered on open sales orders, customer by customer. For each customer: Date , Num , Ship date (the expected ship date of the order), Item , Ordered , Invoiced , Backordered (still to deliver) and Open amount (backordered quantity times the rate, less the line discount, before VAT). href="#pg-rpt-open_so_item" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists, for each item, the quantity still committed on open sales orders, beside the quantity on hand and on purchase orders.
