Site box All sites (as delivered), or one site. With a site chosen, the whole page is that site's: see Looking at one site below. Item The item name/code (click it) and the display name. On hand Quantity in stock. A negative quantity is shown in red. On SO Quantity still to be delivered on open sales orders. Avail. On hand less On SO: what you can still promise. On PO Quantity still to be received on open purchase orders. Reorder The reorder point. It is highlighted when the stock is at or below it. The item list narrowed to the items containing "lap" as it is typed The item details on the right The top card shows the code and name, the type, barcode, unit and preferred vendor, the total On hand in large figures, and: Sales price , Average cost , Value (the remaining value of the item's movements; with a site chosen, the site's quantity × the average cost), Reorder point (and the build point of an assembly), On sales order and On purchase order . Average cost and value are shown only to users who may view costs. Below it: Quantity by site: the quantity at each active site. Open orders: the open sales orders and purchase orders for the item, with the quantity still open and the due or ship date. Click a document to open it. Bill of materials: for an assembly, its components and the quantity of each per unit. Transaction history: the movements of the item, newest first: Date , Transaction (click to open it), Site , Qty (negative when goods went out), Unit cost , Value , Avg after (the average cost after the movement) and On hand after (the total for all sites after the movement). The cost columns are shown only to users who may view costs. The heading says how many movements are shown of how many there are. Two dates and Latest 100 , Latest 500 or All , then Show , choose which ones. On hand after counts every movement from the item's very first one, in the order they happened: by date, and on one date the stock received (bills, item receipts, returns, adjustments up) before the stock used or sold that day (processing orders, builds and transfers, then sales and adjustments down), whatever order they were typed in. A bill and a processing order of the same day read as bought, then processed. The last line is Opening balance (0, before the first movement) or, when older movements are not shown, Balance before the first date shown, with how many earlier movements there are and a Show all link. The first line shown always starts from that balance. A line with no quantity changes only the value: Value adjustment on an adjustment, Below-zero stock settled at this cost under a receipt (see Stock below zero ). When the quantity on hand differs from the total of the movements, a yellow note says by how much and points to Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data . Since version 53 this is put right by itself the next time the item moves, and the average cost never uses the quantity in that note: it always divides the value by the quantity of the movements. Looking at one site Choose a site in the Site box (the list refreshes at once) and everything on the page counts that site alone. A strip at the top says Showing Makati Store only: the quantities, open orders and transaction history below are this site's , with Show all sites to go back. The Inventory Center for LAP-001 with the Makati Store chosen: the strip at the top, the site's quantity, and its movements with the column Makati Store after In the list, On hand , On SO , Avail. and On PO are the site's figures, and the count under the search box names the site. In the detail card, the large figure reads On hand at Makati Store , with the company-wide quantity under it ("11 at all sites"), and Value here , On sales order and On purchase order are the site's. Quantity by site shows the chosen site's row, with an All sites link in its heading. Without a site, every site's row is listed, each a link that filters the page to that site, and an All sites total closes the table. Open orders at Makati Store lists only the sales orders and purchase orders for that site. Transaction history at Makati Store lists only the movements at that site, and its last column, Makati Store after , is that site's own quantity after each movement, counted from the first movement at the site (the newest line shows what the site holds now; a figure below zero is in red). The Site column is left out, since every line is the same site. With no movement at the site, the table says No movements at Makati Store. Transaction history at one site: the bill of 10/01 first at 71.48, then the processing orders of that day The site is kept while you click from item to item, so a store can be gone through item by item. Buttons Button What it does New inventory item Opens a blank inventory part form in the Item List . New assembly Opens a blank inventory assembly form. Edit item Opens the item's form. Purchase order Starts a new purchase order to the item's preferred vendor. Adjust Opens Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand with the item's row highlighted. Transfer Starts a new Transfer Inventory with the item on the first line. Build For an assembly: opens Build Assemblies on it. Disassemble or Process / break down Opens Disassemble / Process Items with the item as the input. An assembly loads its bill of materials; another item loads the first active formula that uses it as an input. Valuation detail Opens the Inventory Valuation Detail report for the item. Average cost changes Opens the Average Cost Changes report for the item, all dates: every transaction that moved its average cost and why. Each button appears only when you may use the page it opens. Step by step: check an item before promising it to a customer Open Inventory > Inventory Center . Type part of the code or name (for example LAP ) in Search / scan barcode and press Enter. If the goods must come from one store, pick that site in the site box. Read Avail. : that is what you can still sell without breaking an earlier promise. Click the item code and look at Open orders to see when more is expected on a purchase order. Tip If Avail. is short at one site but there is stock at another, click Transfer to move it.

href="#pg-inv-items" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Item List holds every item you buy or sell. Each line of an invoice, bill, receipt or POS sale uses one of these items, and the item decides the accounts the line posts to, its tax code and, for stocked goods, the stock it moves. Where to find it: Inventory > Item List. The Item List with the All tab open, showing services, inventory parts, a non-inventory part, an assembly and other charges The Item List narrowed as "mou" is typed in the search box: three items of 131

href="#s-the-item-types" aria-label="Link to this section"> When you create an item you choose its type . The type cannot be changed afterwards, so choose with care. Type Use it for Demo example Service Work you charge or pay for: labor, installation, repairs SRV-INSTALL Installation and Setup Inventory part Goods you buy, keep in stock and sell; quantity and value are tracked per site LAP-001 Laptop 14-inch i5 16GB Non-inventory part Goods bought or sold without keeping stock, such as special orders or supplies NI-TONER Toner Cartridge (special order) Inventory assembly A stocked item you build from other items, with a bill of materials SET-OFFICE Office Monitor Set Other charge Fees and charges: delivery, late payment, reimbursable expenses DEL-FEE Delivery Fee Subtotal A line that adds up the lines above it on a sales form SUBTOTAL Subtotal Group Several items entered with one code; each member is put on the form GRP-WFH Work-from-Home Bundle Discount A percentage or fixed amount taken off the line above it DISC-10 10% Discount Payment Money received on the document itself, such as a down payment DOWNPMT Down Payment Received The last tab, Sales tax items , is not an item type. It lists the tax codes (for example VAT12, NT and EX) with their Rate , Output tax account , Input tax account and Active status. Tax codes are managed under Financial > Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists (the Manage tax codes link under the table; see Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists ), and each item carries its own tax code. How the special types behave on a sales form Subtotal: shows on screen the total of the lines above it, up to the previous subtotal. Its own amount is zero and it posts nothing. It prints on the document without a quantity. Group: a group is sold on one line: the group, how many, and its Group price (see Item groups: group price and price variance ). When the document is saved, the line becomes the items of the group, each at its own price (so stock, cost of sales and the sales of each item are recorded), and one price variance line for the difference between the group price and the prices of its items, posted to the group's Price variance GL account . The document can then be shown and edited by item group or by item details. On a purchase form the members come in at their cost. Discount: a percentage discount (for example DISC-10, 10%) takes that percentage of the amount of the line directly above it; a fixed discount (DISC-AMT, ₱100.00) takes off the amount in its Fixed discount amount (you can type another amount on the line). The discount line posts as a negative amount to the item's Discount account (4060 Sales Discounts in the demo), so it is recorded as a debit there. Payment: records money received on the document itself. The line reduces the document total and posts as a debit to 1050 Undeposited Funds, to be deposited later in Make Deposits . A payment line carries no tax. Important Put a percentage discount directly under the line it discounts. Placed under a Subtotal line, it does not take the percentage of the subtotal. The POS register sells services, inventory parts, non-inventory parts, assemblies, other charges and item groups; subtotal, discount and payment items are not offered there.

href="#s-the-list" aria-label="Link to this section"> Part of the page What it does Tabs All or one item type, plus Sales tax items . Search box Type part of a code, display name, barcode, category, preferred supplier or description. The list narrows with every letter you type, with no button to press; several words must all be found ("cab hdmi"). The count at the right says how many items match ("3 of 131 item(s)"), and "No item matches what you typed." shows when none does. Enter opens the first item that matches. The × in the box clears it. Category box All categories , (no category) , or one category; the list changes as soon as you choose. The item counts of the Category List open the Item List with this box set. Include inactive Tick it to list inactive items too; they are shown in grey. The list changes at once. Code Click it to open the item. Name , Type , Category , Unit The display name, type, category and unit (the base unit of the item's U/M set). Price The sales price; for a percentage discount, the percentage. Cost , Avg cost The purchase cost and, for tracked items, the average cost. Shown only to users who may view costs. On hand For tracked items, the total quantity at all sites; negative quantities are shown in red. Tax , Pref. vendor The item's tax code and preferred vendor. Buttons New item: a menu of the nine types; pick one to open a blank form of that type. Category List: opens the Category List , where categories are added, renamed and deleted. Import items: adds or updates items of every type from a CSV file, read for review first (see Importing items ). It is shown when you may create items; the new-item form has it too. Export: downloads the items of the tab (narrowed by the words in the search box) as a CSV file (type, code, name, description, unit, price, on hand, and cost and average cost for users who may view costs). It needs the Print/Export permission, and the export is recorded in the audit trail. Importing items (Import items) Items of every type, inventory parts, non-inventory parts, services, inventory assemblies, other charges, groups, discounts, subtotals and payments, can be brought in from a CSV file, one row per item: for example the stock list of the former system. A code already on the Item List is updated with the columns of the file only; a new code is added. Where to find it: Import items on the Item List and on a new item's form. It needs the Create right on the Item List; a row that updates an item already on the list needs the Edit right too, and an opening quantity the Create right on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand. Import items: rows of several types read for review, with the opening quantity of an inventory part Download the CSV template gives every column with a sample row of each type; The columns on the page explains each one. The main ones are Item name / code (required, unique), Display name (needed for a new item), Type (blank = Inventory part), Category (added to the Category List when it is new), Unit , Cost , Sales price and Opening qty ; the accounts, tax code, preferred supplier, price levels, reorder points, the components of assemblies and groups (CODE x quantity; CODE x quantity) and the site and date of the opening quantity are under … on each row. Click Read the file for review . Every row is checked as it would be saved, for example ""Gadget" is not an item type. Use one of: ..." or a component that is not on the list or earlier in the file; correct the cells or remove the row, click Check again , then Upload . All the rows are saved, or none if one still has a problem. The opening quantity of new inventory parts and assemblies is posted as one inventory adjustment against Opening Balance Equity.

href="#s-the-item-form" aria-label="Link to this section"> The form changes with the type. These pictures show the new-item form of each type. New inventory part form with the Purchase information, Sales information, Inventory information and Price levels sections New inventory assembly form with the Build point field and the Bill of materials table New service form New non-inventory part form New other charge form New subtotal form, with only the first section New group form with the Items in this group table New discount form with the Discount % and Fixed discount amount fields and the Discount account New payment form, with only the sales description An existing item opens with its code in the title, for example Item: LAB-ASM , and the same sections as its type. Form of the service item LAB-ASM Assembly Labor (per set), which uses the Time (hour) U/M set Fields: first section (every type) Field What to enter Item name / code The short code people type or scan, up to 40 characters, for example LAP-001. Required and unique. Display name The name shown on lists and documents, up to 120 characters. Required. Barcode Inventory parts, assemblies and non-inventory parts only. The code printed on the product; the POS register and the Inventory Center find the item by it. It must be unique. Unit of measure (U/M set) The set of units the item is counted in (see U/M Set List ). Leave it empty for a single unit. Sales unit With a U/M set: the unit sales documents start in. Base unit follows the set's own choice. Purchase unit With a U/M set: the unit purchase documents start in. Unit Without a U/M set: the name of the unit, for example pc or kg. Hidden when a set is chosen. Category The item category, used to group reports such as POS Sales by Category . Categories are kept under Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists . Active Untick it to stop using the item. Inactive items are not offered on new documents but stay on old ones. An inventory part or assembly can be made inactive only when it has no balance: nothing on hand at any site and no value left. While it has one, Active stays ticked and cannot be unticked, and the line under it says "Has a balance: it can be made inactive once it is at zero." Services, non-inventory parts and the other types can be made inactive at any time. When a U/M set is chosen, the note under the fields reminds you that stock, costs and reports stay in the base unit of the set; the Manage U/M sets link opens the U/M Set List. Fields: Purchase information Service, inventory part, non-inventory part, other charge and inventory assembly. Field What to enter Purchase description The text used on purchase documents. Not on assemblies. Cost The usual purchase cost per base unit. It fills the rate on purchase forms. For a service or other charge used in a bill of materials or a processing order, it is the standard cost charged for it. Shown only to users who may view costs. Standard cost (info) Assemblies only: a cost for your information. The real cost of an assembly comes from its builds. Cost of goods sold account Inventory parts and assemblies: the account debited when the item is sold. Default 5000 Cost of Goods Sold. Expense / purchase account Other types: the account debited when the item is bought. Leave it on Default to use the module default (6110 Purchases - Non-inventory in the demo). Preferred vendor The usual supplier. Used by the Inventory Center's Purchase order button and the stock status reports. Fields: Sales information Every type except subtotal. Field What to enter Sales description The text put on sales documents. Sales price The standard selling price per base unit, before VAT. Not on payments; on a group it is the Group price (see Item groups: group price and price variance ). Discount % (0 = fixed amount) Discounts only: the percentage taken off the line above. Leave 0 for a fixed amount. Fixed discount amount Discounts only: the amount taken off when the percentage is 0. Income account The account credited when the item is sold. Default 4000 Sales. On a discount this field is Discount account (default 4060 Sales Discounts). Tax code The tax code of the item, for example VAT12 (12%). None means no tax. Fields: Inventory information Inventory parts and assemblies only. Field What to enter Inventory asset account The asset account that holds the value of the stock. Default 1200 Inventory. Reorder point (min) When the total on hand falls to this quantity, the item is flagged for reordering. 0 means no reorder point. Maximum stock The quantity you want after reordering. The stock status reports suggest ordering up to it. Build point Assemblies only: when stock falls to this quantity, the stock status reports suggest a build. On hand , Average cost On an existing item: the total quantity and the average cost, for information. Quantity on hand , Total value , As of , Site On a new inventory part only: the opening stock (optional). It is posted as an inventory adjustment against Opening Balance Equity at that site and date. Fields: Bill of materials (assemblies) and Items in this group (groups) Column What to enter Item A component: an inventory part, assembly, service, other charge or non-inventory part. Qty How many of it go into one unit of the assembly, or into one group. Avg / std cost , Total Assemblies, for users who may view costs: the average cost (stocked items) or cost (others) of the component and the cost for the quantity. Click Add component for another line and the red cross to remove one. For an assembly, Total component cost shows the cost of one unit at today's costs. Put labor (such as LAB-ASM Assembly Labor) and overhead on the bill of materials as service or other charge items: they are charged at their Cost when you build. Item groups: group price and price variance A group, such as a burger meal or a work-from-home set, is sold at a price of its own, which may differ from the sum of the prices of its items. The form of a group has, under Category : Field What it means Group price The price of one group. It is the price followed on estimates, sales orders, sales receipts, invoices and POS sales when Adopt the Group Price in the Item Group is ticked (System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date > Inventory and POS). Consolidated price The sum of the individual prices of the items in the group (each item's sales price times its quantity in the group). It follows the items as you change them. Price variance Group price less Consolidated price : negative when the group is sold for less than its items. Price variance GL account Where the price variance of each group sold is recorded. Blank uses the module default account Item Group Price Variance (4070, an income account). The Items in this group table shows the Price and Amount of each item, and the sum of the individual prices under it. Tax code of the price variance (under Sales information) is the tax of the variance line; blank uses the tax code most items of the group have. The form of a group: group price, consolidated price, price variance and its GL account, and the items with their prices When a group is sold, its items are recorded at their own prices and the variance goes to the variance account. For example, GRP-WFH Work-from-Home Bundle has a laptop (39,990.00), a mouse (599.00) and a backpack (899.00): a consolidated price of 41,488.00. With a group price of 40,000.00, two bundles sold record sales of 79,980.00, 1,198.00 and 1,798.00 on the three items and a price variance of -2,976.00 (a debit to Item Group Price Variance), so the invoice is 80,000.00 before VAT. Sold as a group at the foot of the form shows the groups sold this month and this fiscal year and their sales, with a link to Sales by Item Group . Fields: Price levels Shown for inventory parts, assemblies, non-inventory parts, services and other charges when price levels exist. There is one box for each active price level, ten as delivered ( Wholesale −5%, VIP −10%, Retail Plus +5% and Price Level 4 to Price Level 10 at 0%), five to a row. Beside each level name you see its percentage and the price it gives on the sales price, for example -5% = 854.05 . The figure follows the sales price as you type it. Leave a box empty to use the level's percentage. Type a figure to fix the item's price on that level, whatever the percentage. Customers who have a price level get these prices on invoices, sales receipts and at the POS. Levels are renamed and their percentages changed with Rename price levels on Set Item Prices and Levels or under Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists (both linked at the bottom of the section). To set many items at once, use Set Item Prices and Levels. Buttons Save item: saves and keeps the item open. Save item & New: saves and opens a blank form of the same type. Cancel and Back to list: return to the list without saving. Inventory Center: on a saved inventory part or assembly, opens it in the Inventory Center. Step by step: create an inventory part Open Inventory > Item List and click New item > Inventory part . Type the Item name / code (for example BAG-002 ) and the Display name . Type or scan the Barcode if the product has one. Choose the Unit of measure (U/M set) or type the Unit , and the Category . Under Purchase information , type the Cost and pick the Preferred vendor . Leave the Cost of goods sold account as it is unless your accountant asks otherwise. Under Sales information , type the Sales price and choose the Tax code (VAT12 for VAT-able goods). Under Inventory information , type the Reorder point (min) and Maximum stock . If the goods are already on your shelves, type the opening Quantity on hand and its Total value , the As of date and the Site . Fill the Price levels boxes only for levels that need a fixed price. Click Save item . The message "Item saved." appears. Step by step: create an assembly Click New item > Inventory assembly . Fill the first section, the sales price, tax code, reorder point, maximum stock and Build point . Under Bill of materials , pick the first component in Item and type its Qty per assembly. Click Add component for each other component, including labor as a service item. Check Total component cost , then click Save item . Build the stock with Build Assemblies . An assembly has no opening quantity on its form. For assemblies you already had before you started, use Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand with Quantity and total value , so they come in with a value. Step by step: create a group, discount, subtotal or payment item Click New item and pick Group , Discount , Subtotal or Payment . Type the Item name / code and Display name . For a group, add the member items and their quantities under Items in this group , then type the Group price and choose the Price variance GL account (or leave the module default). For a discount, type either the Discount % (0 = fixed amount) or the Fixed discount amount , and check the Discount account . Type a Sales description (it is printed on the documents). Click Save item . Step by step: change or retire an item Click the item's Code on the list (tick Include inactive to find an inactive one). Change the fields and click Save item . Changes apply to new documents; saved documents keep their own figures. To retire the item, untick Active and save. Items cannot be deleted, because documents still refer to them. Important An inventory part or assembly that still has stock or a value cannot be made inactive. Sell it, transfer it, or adjust it to zero with Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand first; then Active can be unticked. Saving it inactive anyway is refused with, for example, "BAG-001 still has 16 on hand (Main Warehouse, Makati Store, Cebu Store) and a value of 8,000.00. Only an inventory item with no balance can be made inactive: sell, transfer or adjust it to zero first." The same rule applies to an is_active column of Import from CSV . An inventory part with stock: Active ticked and locked, with the reason under it What it records Saving an item posts nothing, except the opening balance of a new inventory part. That is posted as an inventory adjustment dated As of at the chosen Site : Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory Total value 3900 Opening Balance Equity Total value Example A new item BAG-002 with Quantity on hand 20 and Total value ₱10,000.00 comes in as 20 units at ₱500.00 each. If you leave Total value at 0, the units come in at no cost; type the value. Good to know "Enter the item code and name." Both fields are required. "Another item already uses this code." or "Another item already uses this barcode." Codes and barcodes are unique. "Add at least one component." An assembly or group needs at least one line. "An item cannot be a component of itself." "This item was already entered in units of its present U/M set, so the set cannot be changed. Add the units you need to that set instead." Users without the Edit permission on the Item List see the form with every field greyed out. Every change is kept in the audit trail with the values before and after. The Home dashboard shows Items at or below reorder point , with the number of negative stock records under it; that line opens Inventory Stock Status by Item .

href="#pg-inv-categories" aria-label="Link to this section"> Categories group the items: Computers, Accessories, Frozen Products, Meat. An item's category is chosen on its form, and the categories filter the Item List, Set Item Prices and Levels, the Item Price List and the inventory reports, and make the groups of POS Sales by Category. The Category List is where they are added, renamed and deleted. Where to find it: Inventory > Lists > Category List. Also the Category List button of the Item List. The Category List with the number of items, the active items, the quantity on hand and the value of each category, and the New category form The list Column What it shows Category The name. The search box above the list narrows it as you type. Items How many items are in the category, active or not. Click the number to open the Item List with only those items. Active How many of them are active. On hand The quantity on hand of its inventory parts and assemblies, at all sites. Value That quantity at average cost. Shown only to users who may view costs. The line (no category) at the foot counts the items that have none; its number opens them in the Item List so they can be given one. Add or rename a category To add one, type the Category name in New category and click Add category (or Add category & New to add another straight away). The message Category "Frozen Products" added. appears. To rename one, click Rename on its line, type the new name and click Save the name . Every item in the category shows the new name at once, on every page and report. Spaces at the ends of the name are removed and runs of spaces become one. Two categories cannot have the same name, whatever the capitals: the program says There is already a category called "...". To put the two together, delete one and move its items to the other. Renaming a category: its line is marked in the list and the form on the right holds its name Delete a category Click Delete on the category's line. A Delete panel opens on the right. If items are in the category, choose in Move its items to where they go: another category, which merges the two, or No category . A category without items needs no choice. Click Delete the category and confirm. The message says where the items went, for example Category "Supplies" deleted. Its 4 item(s) are now in "Accessories". Keep it closes the panel without deleting. Deleting the Accessories category: its items are moved to another category first Note Only the category of the items changes: their prices, costs, stock and history stay as they are. Adding needs the Create right on this page, renaming the Edit right and deleting the Delete right; every change is kept in the audit trail. The categories can also be added and renamed on the Item categories tab of Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists , which points here for deleting.

href="#pg-inv-sites" aria-label="Link to this section"> A site is a place where you keep stock. Set up one for each warehouse, store, stockroom and delivery van, and one for damaged goods. Where to find it: Inventory > Inventory Site List. The Inventory Site List with five sites and the New site form The table on the left lists the sites: Code , Name , Type , Address , Items (how many items have stock there), Units (the total quantity there), POS (how many POS terminals sell from it) and an Edit link. The form on the right adds a new site, or changes the one you clicked Edit on. Editing the site WH Main Warehouse Fields Field What to enter Code A short code, up to 20 characters, for example WH. It is saved in capitals and must be unique. Name The site name, for example Main Warehouse. Type Warehouse , Retail store , Stockroom , Delivery van , Damaged goods or Other . Active Untick it to stop using the site. Address The site's address (optional). Step by step: add a site Open Inventory > Inventory Site List . Type the Code and Name , choose the Type and type the Address . Click Save site (or Save site & New to add another). The message "Site saved." appears. To change a site, click Edit on its row, change the fields and click Save site . Buttons Transfer inventory: opens a new Transfer Inventory . Quantity on Hand by Site: opens the report with one column per site. Good to know "Another site uses this code." "This site still holds stock. Transfer it out before making the site inactive." Sites cannot be deleted. The first active site of the type Damaged goods receives the goods returned at the POS that cannot be resold (see POS Receipts, Returns & Voids ). Each POS terminal sells from one site, chosen in POS Terminals .

href="#pg-inv-uom" aria-label="Link to this section"> A U/M set (unit of measure set) lets you buy, sell and count one item in several units: by the piece and by the box, by the kilo and by the sack. Each set has one base unit , the unit stock is counted and costed in, and any number of other units with the number of base units each contains. Where to find it: Inventory > U/M Set List. The Manage U/M sets link on the item form also opens it. The U/M Set List with five sets and the New U/M set form The note at the top explains the rule: a document line can be entered in any unit of the item's set; the quantity is multiplied by the number of base units the unit contains and the price divided by it, so a case of 12 at ₱1,200.00 is stored as 12 pieces at ₱100.00 each. Stock, costs and reports are always kept in the base unit. The list shows each Set , its Kind , Base unit , Units and the number of Items using it, with an Edit link. Inactive sets are marked inactive . Editing the set Length (m): base unit m, with cm = 0.01 m and roll = 100 m Fields Field What to enter Set name A name that is unique, for example Length (m). Kind Count , Weight , Volume , Length , Area , Time or Other . It only groups the list. Base unit The unit stock is kept in, for example m or pc. Active Untick it to stop offering the set on new items. Unit Another unit of the set, for example roll. Description Its name, for example Roll of 100 m. Left blank, the unit code is used. = how many (base unit) How many base units one of it contains, for example 100. It can be less than 1 (1 cm = 0.01 m). Unit sales documents start in The unit code sales lines start in. Blank means the base unit. Unit purchases start in The unit code purchase lines start in. Blank means the base unit. An item can override the two starting units with its own Sales unit and Purchase unit . Step by step: create a U/M set Open Inventory > U/M Set List . Type the Set name , choose the Kind and type the Base unit (for example pc ). On the first line, type the Unit (for example box ), its Description and how many base units it holds (for example 50 ). Click Add unit for each other unit. Type the units that sales and purchases should start in, or leave them blank for the base unit. Click Save U/M set . The message "U/M set saved." appears. Open each item that uses the set in the Item List and choose the set in Unit of measure (U/M set) . To change a set, click Edit on its row. Remove a unit with the red cross, then save. Good to know "Enter the set name and the base unit." and "Another U/M set already uses this name." "Every unit needs how many ... it contains (a number greater than zero)." "The unit ... is the base unit; it is already on the list." and "The unit ... is listed twice." "The unit ... is used on n record(s) and cannot be removed. Keep it on the list." A unit used on documents or chosen as an item's sales or purchase unit stays. Renaming the base unit renames the unit of every item in the set. On the POS register, an item whose set has more than one unit gets a U/M box on its cart line.

href="#pg-inv-formulas" aria-label="Link to this section"> A processing formula is a reusable recipe for turning one or more inputs into several outputs: taking an item apart, opening a box to sell the contents one by one, or processing raw material into a main product and by-products. It says what goes in, what comes out and how the cost is shared, for one batch . A processing order multiplies the formula by the number of batches you run. Where to find it: Inventory > Processing Formulas (Multi-Output BOM). The Formulas and Processing formulas buttons on the processing pages open it too. The Processing Formulas list with three active formulas The list The list shows the Code , Name , process Type , Allocation method, Inputs (per batch) , Outputs (per batch) (by-products and scrap are marked), the number of Orders that used it and its Status . Choose Active formulas , Inactive formulas or All formulas in the box above the table. Run: starts a new processing order with the formula loaded. New formula: opens a blank formula. New from assembly BOM: pick an assembly in the box beside it and click the button. The new formula is filled from its bill of materials: code UNB- plus the assembly code, type Disassembly / Unbuild , method Relative standard cost , the assembly as input and its stocked components as outputs. Processing orders: opens the list of processing orders. Note You do not need a formula to take an assembly apart: a processing order can load any assembly's bill of materials directly. A blank New Processing Formula form Fields Field What to enter Code Up to 30 characters, saved in capitals, unique. Name What the formula does, for example Break bulk: USB 32GB box of 50. Process type Disassembly / Unbuild , De-kitting / Break-bulk or Co-product / By-product . Usual processing site The site orders start on. Any leaves it to the person running it. Cost allocation method How the cost is shared among the outputs (see the table below). The help text under the box explains the method chosen. Description / instructions Notes for the people doing the work. Active Untick it to stop the formula being chosen for new orders. Inputs per batch: the Item consumed (an inventory part, assembly, non-inventory part, service or other charge), a Description and the Qty per batch. Est. cost is filled when you check the allocation. Additional costs per batch (optional): labor, machine time or overhead added to the cost. Account credited starts on the module default account for absorbed processing costs (5200 Direct Labor Absorbed in the demo); type a Description and the Amount per batch. Outputs per batch: the Item produced (inventory parts and assemblies only), a Description , the Role ( Co-product (main) , By-product or Scrap / waste ), the Qty per batch and the Basis . Share , Est. cost and Unit cost are filled when you check the allocation. The cost allocation methods By-products and scrap are valued first, at their Basis (a value per unit; scrap is usually 0). The rest of the cost goes to the co-products by the method: Method How the co-products share the cost Basis on a co-product Relative sales value In proportion to quantity × selling price Price per unit; blank uses the sales price Relative standard cost In proportion to quantity × standard cost Cost per unit; blank uses the item cost Physical units Every unit produced carries the same cost Not used Weight / measure In proportion to quantity × weight or volume per unit Weight per unit (required) Fixed percentages Each gets its percentage; they must add up to 100 The percentage Current average cost (difference to variance) Each is valued at its average cost; the difference goes to the variance account Value per unit; blank uses the average cost Manual amounts (difference to variance) Each gets the amount you give; the difference goes to the variance account Total cost of the line per batch With the first five methods the outputs always carry the whole cost. The last two value the outputs and post any difference from the cost to the processing variance account. The formula BRK-USB50: one USB-032-BX50 box in, 50 USB-032 out, shared by physical units Step by step: create a formula Click New formula . Type the Code and Name , choose the Process type , the Usual processing site and the Cost allocation method . Under Inputs per batch , choose each item and its Qty . Click Add input for more. Under Additional costs per batch (optional) , enter the labor or overhead, or leave the line empty. Under Outputs per batch , choose each item, its Role and Qty , and a Basis where the method needs one. Click Add output for more. Click Check allocation . The shares and costs are worked out with today's costs, and a blue box gives the total cost per batch, the by-products and scrap, the amount allocated and, for the variance methods, the variance. Click Save formula (or Save & New ). The message "Formula ... saved." appears. Buttons on a saved formula Run this formula: starts a processing order with it. Deactivate or Activate: a deactivated formula "stays on past orders but cannot be chosen for new ones". Delete: only for a formula never used on an order; you must type a reason, and a full copy is kept in the audit trail. Yield analysis: for a used formula, opens the Processing Yield Analysis report on it. Formula list: back to the list. A formula already used shows "Used on n processing order(s). Changes apply to new orders only; posted orders keep their own lines." Good to know "Add at least one input item (what is being processed or taken apart)." and "Add at least one output item (what the process produces)." "... cannot be an output. Outputs must be inventory or assembly items so their quantity and value can be tracked." "... is both an input and an output. Use an inventory adjustment for rework of the same item." and "The same output item is listed twice. Combine the lines." "Mark at least one output as a co-product (main product)." The five sharing methods need one. "The co-product percentages must add up to 100% ..." and "Enter the weight or measure per unit (basis) for ...". "By-product and scrap values (...) are more than the total cost to allocate (...). Lower their values per unit." "Formula ... is used on n processing order(s). Deactivate it instead."

href="#pg-inv-transfers" aria-label="Link to this section"> Use Transfer Inventory to move stock from one site to another, for example from the Main Warehouse to the Makati Store. The quantities move; the total value of your inventory does not change. Where to find it: Inventory > Transfer Inventory (opens the list; click New transfer ). Also the Transfer button of the Inventory Center, Transfer inventory on the Inventory Site List, and the Home dashboard Quick actions . The Inventory Transfers list The list The list shows the transfers dated from 90 days ago to 30 days ahead. Change From and To , choose a Status ( Posted or Void ) or Class , or type in Search (number, name or memo), then click Filter . The columns are Date , No. (click to open), From site and To site (where the goods left and where they arrived), Reference , Memo , Class , Quantity (the total quantity moved), Status and By . Export downloads the list as a CSV file with the same columns. Note A transfer has no amount, so the list shows the quantity moved instead of a total. A new transfer form with three empty lines Fields Field What to enter Date The date of the move. From site The site the goods leave. To site The site receiving them. Memo A note, for example Stock for store. Class The class, if you use classes. Item An inventory part or assembly. On hand at source Filled in when you choose the item: the quantity at the From site. Qty to move The quantity to move. Step by step: move stock to a store Open Inventory > Transfer Inventory and click New transfer . Check the Date , choose the From site (for example Main Warehouse) and the To site (Makati Store). On each line choose the Item , check On hand at source and type the Qty to move . Click Add line , Add 5 lines or Add 10 lines for more lines; the square plus button at the end of a line inserts one above it. Click Record transfer (or Record transfer & New ). The message "Transfer recorded. Quantities moved without changing total inventory value." appears and the transfer opens. If the From site does not have enough, the program first asks "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance. Do you want to continue?": Yes records it, No goes back to the transfer. The saved transfer IT-00003: 2 SET-OFFICE moved for the Makati store display Step by step: print, void or delete a transfer Open the transfer from the list. Click Print for the printout, which names the From site and the To site in its heading and lists the items and quantities with a Total quantity line and signature lines. Click Print again on the printout page to send it to the printer. To undo the transfer, click Void , type the reason and click Void transaction . The document stays, marked VOID, and the goods go back. Delete removes it; its full content stays in the audit trail. Printout of the transfer IT-00003 Edit a transfer A posted transfer has an Edit button (for users with the edit permission on Transfer Inventory). Edit Inventory Transfer shows the transfer as it was entered: Date , From site , To site , Memo , Class , the lines, and Reason for the change . An inventory transfer with its Edit button Edit Inventory Transfer Open the transfer from the Transfers list and click Edit . Change the quantities, the items, the sites or the date. On hand at source counts what this transfer itself took from the site it moved from, so the stock you see is what you can move. Type the Reason for the change and click Save changes . When you save, the stock moves again: the quantities the transfer moved go back to the site they left, then the new lines leave the From site and arrive at the To site , at average cost. The before and after, with the reason, go to the audit trail. A move that would take a site below zero asks first, as on a new transfer. A voided transfer cannot be edited, and transfers dated on or before the closing date are protected. What it records No journal entry: the goods leave one site and arrive at the other with the same value, and both sides use the item's inventory asset account. Each item goes out of the From site at its average cost and comes into the To site at that same cost. Good to know "Choose two different sites." "You are not allowed to move stock to that site." The To site list shows every active site, but you can finish the transfer only to a site you may use. "Not enough stock of ... at the source site (...)." This appears only when Allow selling or moving stock below zero (with warning) is switched off. "Enter at least one item and quantity." The saved transfer shows From site and To site in its header and a Total quantity under its lines; it has no rate or amount columns. The item's history in the Inventory Center and the Inventory Valuation Detail show the movement out of one site and into the other. A saved transfer can be corrected with Edit (see above), or voided and recorded again.

href="#pg-inv-adjust" aria-label="Link to this section"> Use this page to correct the quantity or the value of stock: goods damaged, lost, stolen, spoiled or used as samples, stock found, a write-down to net realizable value, or a cost correction. Every adjustment needs a reason, is posted to the books, and is recorded in the audit trail with your name. Where to find it: Inventory > Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand (opens a new adjustment). Also the Adjust button of the Inventory Center (which opens it with that item on the first line) and the Home dashboard Quick actions . Per Item or Per Batch The bar at the top, Adjustment option , offers two ways of entering the same adjustment: Per Item Adjustment is the QuickBooks layout: you pick the items to adjust on lines, one by one or several at once, and see the quantity on hand, the new quantity and the difference of each. Use it for a few items, a damaged carton, a sample. Per Batch Adjustment lists every stocked item of the site in one long grid; you type the new figures of the ones that changed. Use it after counting a whole site. Click either one. The program remembers your choice and opens the page that way next time. Both post the same kind of transaction, with the same reasons and the same entries. The page as it first opens: Per Item Adjustment with three empty lines A new Per Item Adjustment: the option bar, the header, and the lines with BAG-001 down 2 and MOU-001 counted at 18 Per Item Adjustment: the header Field What to enter Adjustment type Quantity , Total value or Quantity and total value . The lines show the quantity columns, the value columns, or both, as you change it. The value types are offered only to users who may view costs. Adjustment date The date of the adjustment. Reference no. A reference, for example an incident report number. Adjustment account The account that takes the gain or loss. Default 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage. Inventory site The site whose stock you are adjusting. Changing it updates the Qty on hand of every line. Customer:Job Optional: the customer or job the adjustment is for (goods used on a job, samples for a customer). It is carried onto the ledger lines for job costing. Class The class of the adjustment, if you use classes. A line without a class of its own gets it. Reason (required) The reasons on the list (as delivered: Count difference , Damage , Theft / loss , Spoilage / expiry , Samples / promotional use , Found stock , Write-down to net realizable value , Cost correction ) or Other (then Describe it). Edit reasons beside the label changes the list (see below). Per Item Adjustment: the lines Column What it means Item Type part of the code or name and pick the item. An item can be on one line only; a second line with it is marked red and refused on saving. Description The item's display name. Qty on hand What the chosen site holds now, in the U/M of the line. New quantity Type the quantity the site should have. The difference fills in by itself. Qty difference Or type the change itself, for example -2 for two units damaged, 5 for five found. The new quantity fills in by itself. U/M The unit the quantities are typed in, when the item has a U/M set (pieces, boxes, cases). The program converts to the base unit. Current value Value types: the value of the item at all sites. New value Value types: the value the item should have at all sites after the adjustment. With Quantity and total value , typing the New quantity fills it in with the value the new quantity gives at the average cost (shown in grey italics); type over it to set a value of your own. Net adjustment What the line changes the value of the stock by: the quantity change at the average cost, plus any value change. Negative figures (in brackets) are losses. Shown to users who may view costs. Class The class of this line, when it differs from the one at the top. The cross at the end of a line removes it; the square plus button beside it inserts an empty line above it. Add line , Add 5 lines and Add 10 lines add empty lines at the end. Find & Select Items... opens a list of every active inventory part and assembly with its quantity at the site. Type in the search box to narrow it, tick Only items in stock at the site if you want, tick the items (the box in the heading ticks every item shown) and click Add the selected items . Each one gets a line. Items already on a line cannot be ticked again. Set Qty to Zero makes the New quantity of every line 0, for writing off everything on the lines. Categories with Add their items puts every active item of the ticked categories on the lines at once (the items already on a line are left as they are), to adjust whole categories. Click the Categories box, tick one category or several, then click Add their items . Find & Select Items has a Categories box as well: tick one or more to list only their items. Find & Select Items: the items matching "cab" with their quantity at the site, one of them ticked Under the lines are the Memo and two figures that change as you type: Total value of adjustment (the quantity differences at average cost plus any value changes; negative for a loss; shown to users who may view costs) and Number of item adjustments (the lines that change something). The buttons: Save & Close posts the adjustment and opens it; Save & New posts it and opens a fresh form with the same option, type and site; Clear empties the form after asking. An adjustment that would leave an item below zero at the site asks "Saving the transaction will lead the inventory to a negative balance. Do you want to continue?" first, in both adjustment options: Yes posts it, No goes back to the lines. Per Batch Adjustment The boxes at the top, Adjustment type , Site and Categories , choose what the grid shows; changing them reloads the page. Categories is a list of check boxes: click it and tick one category, or two or more, then click Show (or just close the list). The grid lists only the items of the ticked categories, so they can be counted and adjusted together. Tick all and Clear work on the whole list, and with many categories a search box at the top finds one by name. With nothing ticked the box reads All categories and the grid lists every item. The button shows the ticked categories ("Accessories, Computers", or "Accessories, Cables and 2 more categories"), and Post adjustment & New opens the next grid with the same categories ticked. The header has the same Adjustment date , Reference no. , Adjustment account , Reason , Memo and Class as above. Per Batch Adjustment: the Categories list with two categories ticked Per Batch Adjustment at the Main Warehouse, with the Qty at site of each item The grid lists every active inventory part and assembly. The first two columns are the item name/code and the display name. Column Meaning Qty at site The quantity now at the chosen site. New qty Type the quantity the site should have. Leave it blank to leave the item alone. Change The difference, worked out as you type. Total qty Value types: the quantity at all sites. Current value Value types: the value at all sites (total qty × average cost). New value Value types: type the value the item should have at all sites after the adjustment. With Quantity and total value , that is the value with the new quantity: typing the New qty fills it in at the average cost (grey italics) until you type a value of your own. Net adjustment What the row changes the value of the stock by (users who may view costs). Under the grid, Total value of adjustment and Number of item adjustments add up as you type. Click Post adjustment (or Post adjustment & New ). Per Batch Adjustment of the Accessories category with Quantity and total value: MOU-001 counted one less, its new value worked out and its net adjustment Edit reasons The reasons offered in the Reason box are a list the company keeps. Users who may edit adjustments see Edit reasons beside the box. Click Edit reasons . The box Reasons for adjustments lists them. Change the wording of a reason, put the list in order with the up and down arrows, take a reason off with the cross, or click Add a reason and type it. Click Save the reasons . The Reason box offers the new list at once; nothing typed on the adjustment is lost. Other (described in words) is always offered last and cannot be taken off. A reason can be at most 60 characters, and the same reason cannot be on the list twice. Adjustments already saved keep the reason they were saved with. Each change is recorded in the audit trail. Reasons for adjustments: the list with Repacked added Memorize Adjustment and Load Memorized Adjustment An adjustment made again and again (the weekly spoilage of the same items, a monthly sample allocation) can be kept as a pro-forma and loaded the next time, to revise the figures and post. Fill in the adjustment as usual (Per Item or Per Batch): the items, their new quantity or difference, the reason, the memo. Click Memorize Adjustment (beside the save buttons). Type a name in Name it , a Group if you use groups, and choose the Reminder : Don't remind me (I load it when needed) , or Remind me when it is due with how often and the next due date. Click Memorize Adjustment in the box. The message "Memorized as "...". Load it with "Load Memorized Adjustment" and revise the figures for the next adjustment. Nothing was posted." appears and the form stays as it was, ready to be posted too. The Memorize Adjustment box To use it: click Load Memorized Adjustment in the title bar, then Load on its line. The form opens in the option it was memorized in (Per Item or Per Batch) with its site, type, account, reason, memo and lines; change what differs and save. A Per Item pro-forma can also be shown in the Per Batch grid: a difference becomes the new quantity. A memorized adjustment is never posted on its own: on the Memorized Transactions list it has Open (open on the form) instead of Enter now . Load Memorized Adjustment: the memorized adjustments with their site and number of items Step by step: write off damaged goods (Per Item) Open Inventory > Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand and click Per Item Adjustment . Leave Adjustment type on Quantity and choose the Inventory site , for example Main Warehouse. Choose the Reason , for example Damage , and type a Memo such as water leak . On the first line pick the item, for example BAG-001, and type -2 in Qty difference . New quantity shows what will be left. If the Supervisor approval box opens, ask a supervisor to type their username and password in it (or a one-time approval code). Click Save & Close . The message "1 item adjustment(s) posted and logged with your name and the reason." appears and the adjustment opens. Step by step: write an item down to a new value Choose Adjustment type Total value . Choose the reason Write-down to net realizable value (or Cost correction ). Pick the item on a line (Per Item) or find its row (Per Batch), and type the total value it should have in New value , for all sites together. Save. The quantity stays; the average cost becomes the new value divided by the quantity. Step by step: bring in stock with its value Use Quantity and total value when both the count and the worth change, for example assemblies you had before you started using the program. Choose Adjustment type Quantity and total value and the site. Choose the Reason and type a Memo . For the item, type the new quantity for this site and the New value the item should have in total once the new quantity is in. Save. The quantity changes first, at the average cost, and the value is then set to exactly the New value you typed. The average cost becomes the new value divided by the item's total quantity. Example Suppose SET-OFFICE Office Monitor Set has 2 units at the Main Warehouse and nowhere else, worth ₱30,000.00. You count 5 and agree they are worth ₱70,000.00 in all. Type the new quantity 5 and New value 70000 . After posting, the item has 5 units worth ₱70,000.00 (₱14,000.00 each): Inventory is debited ₱40,000.00 and the adjustment account credited ₱40,000.00. Edit an adjustment A posted adjustment has an Edit button (for users with the edit permission on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand). Edit Inventory Adjustment opens it on lines, as a Per Item Adjustment, whichever way it was entered, with its Adjustment type , date, reference, account, site, Customer:Job, class, Reason and memo, and a box Why it is being changed . An inventory adjustment with its Edit button Edit Inventory Adjustment: Qty on hand without the adjustment, its difference and new quantity Qty on hand and Current value are what the site had without this adjustment, so New quantity , Qty difference and New value read as they did when it was entered: an adjustment that took 2 damaged bags off shows Qty difference -2 and the new quantity it left. Open the adjustment from the Adjustments list and click Edit . Change the difference or the new quantity (the other follows), the new value, the U/M or the class of a line; add or remove lines with Find & Select Items or the x . Keep or change the Reason , type Why it is being changed , and click Save changes . Saving takes the adjustment off the books, works the lines out again against the stock without it, and posts it again in the same step, under the same number. The before and after, with the reason, go to the audit trail. An adjustment above your amount limit needs supervisor approval, as a new one does. The adjustments list Click Adjustments list to see the saved adjustments. The list works like the transfers list (filters From , To , Status , Class , Search ; New adjustment and Export buttons). Click a number to open an adjustment; from there you can Edit , Print , Void or Delete it. The Inventory Adjustments list with a damage adjustment and a physical count What it records A decrease takes the goods out at average cost: Account Debit Credit 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage ₱1,000.00 1200 Inventory ₱1,000.00 This is the entry of ADJ-00001 (2 BAG-001 at ₱500.00). An increase posts the reverse, at the current average cost. Each ledger line carries the class of its line (or of the adjustment) and the Customer:Job chosen at the top. A value change debits Inventory and credits the adjustment account when the value goes up, and the reverse when it goes down. Good to know "Put at least one item on the adjustment before memorizing it." (Memorize Adjustment with no lines) "Choose or describe the reason for the adjustment." "No changes entered. Type the new quantity or value for the items to adjust." (Per Batch) or "No changes entered. Choose the items and type their new quantity (or the difference)." (Per Item). "BAG-001 is on two lines. Keep it on one line." (Per Item) "You are not allowed to adjust stock at that site." A supervisor must approve when the adjustment is worth more than your Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval (the value is estimated at average cost). A user with the Approve permission on this page approves their own. The value of an item is kept for all sites together, so a value adjustment changes the average cost everywhere. A saved adjustment can be corrected with Edit (see above), or voided and posted again. Giving one person both this page and Physical Inventory Count (with create or edit rights) is flagged as a segregation-of-duties conflict when roles and users are saved.

href="#pg-inv-build" aria-label="Link to this section"> Building turns components into finished assemblies: the component quantities go down, the assembly quantity goes up, and the component cost (plus any labor on the bill of materials) becomes the value of the assembly. When components are short, you can save the build as pending and complete it when the parts arrive. Where to find it: Inventory > Build Assemblies (opens the Assembly Builds list; click Build assemblies ). Also the Build button of the Inventory Center and the Home dashboard Quick actions . The Assembly Builds list with a pending and a completed build The list works like the transfers list; its Status filter offers Completed , Pending and Void . Note The Total column of this list is not used for builds and shows 0.00. The value of a build is in the item's history and in the Inventory Valuation Detail . The Build Assemblies form for 1 SET-OFFICE at the Main Warehouse Fields Field What to enter Assembly item The assembly to build. Build at site Where the components are taken from and the assembly is put. Quantity to build How many assemblies. Date The build date. Memo A note, for example Weekly build. Class The class, if you use classes. Changing the assembly, site or quantity reloads the page. The line On hand at site shows how many of the assembly the site has, and its build point. The table lists the bill of materials: Component , Description , Per unit , Needed (per unit × quantity) and On hand at site ( n/a for labor and other items without stock). A component that is short is shown in red with short . Step by step: build assemblies Open Inventory > Build Assemblies and click Build assemblies . Choose the Assembly item and the Build at site , and type the Quantity to build . Check that no line says short . Click Build (or Build & New ). The message "Assembly built." appears. Step by step: save a pending build and complete it later When a component is short, the page says "Some components are short. You can save the build as pending ; it is non-posting and can be completed when the parts arrive." Click Save as pending build . The message "Build saved as pending. It will not affect inventory until completed." appears. When the parts are in, open the build from the list (or from the Pending Builds report). In the box at the bottom, "This build is pending. When the missing components arrive, complete it here.", check the Build date and click Complete build . If parts are still missing, the message "Still short of components: ..." lists them. The pending build BLD-00002 with the Complete build box The saved build shows the assembly and each component with its quantity. Print gives a printout of the build, Void undoes it and Delete removes it (with a reason). Printout of the build BLD-00002 Buttons Builds list: the list of builds. Pending Builds: the Pending Builds report. Disassemble (unbuild): opens a processing order that takes the assembly apart (see Disassemble / Process Items ). Edit a build A build has an Edit button (for users with the edit permission on Build Assemblies). Edit Build Assembly shows the Assembly item , Build at site , Quantity to build , Date , Memo , Class , the components and Reason for the change . A build with its Edit button Edit Build Assembly The components follow the quantity: with the same assembly they are the quantities per unit recorded on this build; when another assembly is chosen they come from its bill of materials. On hand at site counts what this build itself used, so the components you see are what you can build with. A completed build: Save changes posts it again (the components it used go back to the site, the new quantities are taken and the assembly is added at their cost). When the components are short for the new quantity it says so and cannot be saved. A pending build: Save changes (still pending) keeps it pending (nothing moves in stock), and Save and complete the build completes it when the components are there. The before and after, with the reason, go to the audit trail. What it records Stocked components are issued at their average cost; labor and other non-stock components are charged at their Cost and credited to their expense account. The assembly receives the total. Building one SET-OFFICE (MON-024, KEY-001, MOU-001, CAB-HDMI and LAB-ASM at ₱150.00): Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory (SET-OFFICE) ₱7,706.67 1200 Inventory (the four stocked parts) ₱7,556.67 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed (LAB-ASM) ₱150.00 There is no gain or loss. A pending build posts nothing. Good to know "Choose the assembly and a quantity greater than zero." and "This assembly has no bill of materials." "There are not enough components at this site. Save the build as pending, or transfer / receive the components first." A build never issues parts that are short. A pending build keeps the component quantities it was saved with, even if the bill of materials changes later. A saved build can be corrected with Edit (see above), or voided and built again. A pending build is also completed with Complete build on the build itself.

href="#pg-inv-process" aria-label="Link to this section"> A processing order takes items out of stock, puts the resulting items in, and spreads the cost over them. Use it to: take an assembly or a finished item apart (disassembly or unbuild), for example a trade-in PC broken into parts; break a box or kit into single units for separate sale (de-kitting or break-bulk), for example a box of 50 flash drives; process raw material into several products (co-products and by-products), with labor and overhead added. Where to find it: Inventory > Disassemble / Process Items (opens the Processing Orders list). Also the Run buttons of the formulas, the Disassemble or Process / break down button of the Inventory Center, the Disassemble (unbuild) button of Build Assemblies and the Home dashboard Quick actions . The Processing Orders list with disassembly, co-product and break-bulk orders The list The list shows the orders from 90 days ago to 30 days ahead: Date , No. , Type , Formula , Site , Inputs , Outputs , Variance qty (the input quantity less the output quantity), Total cost (users who may view costs), Status ( Completed , Pending or Void ) and By . Filter by From , To , Type , Status and Search (number, item, formula or memo). The buttons are New processing order , Formulas , Register (the Processing & Disassembly Register ) and Export . A new processing order form Fields: the top of the form Field What to enter Process type Disassembly / Unbuild , De-kitting / Break-bulk or Co-product / By-product . The help text explains it. Load lines from A formula ( Formula: ... ) or an assembly's bill of materials ( Unbuild assembly (bill of materials): ... ). Leave — none: enter the lines below — to type the lines yourself. Batches / units How many batches of the formula, or how many assemblies to take apart. Date The processing date. Processing site (inputs) The site the inputs are taken from. Receive outputs at The site the outputs go to. Same site when left empty. Reference no. Your reference. The number the order will get is shown beside it, for example No. PRC-00006. Cost allocation method How the cost is shared (see the methods under Processing Formulas ). Variance account (difference) Shown for the two variance methods: the account for the difference. — default — uses the module default (5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage in the demo). Memo , Class A note and the class. Fields: the three grids Inputs (consumed): Item , Description , Planned (the quantity the formula or bill of materials called for), Qty (the actual quantity used), On hand at site (in red when short), Est. unit cost and Est. cost . The Total inputs row adds up the quantities as you type. Stocked items are issued at their average cost; services and non-stock items are charged at their standard cost. Additional processing costs (optional): Account credited , Description and Amount , for labor, machine time or overhead. The account is credited, that is, the cost is absorbed into the outputs. Outputs (produced): Item , Description , Role , Planned , Qty (the actual quantity produced), Basis , Share of cost , Allocated cost and Unit cost . The Running total row adds up the quantities and the allocated cost. Under it, Variance qty (inputs less outputs) is the total input quantity less the total output quantity, worked out as you type: in red when less came out than went in (a loss in processing, such as trimmings or evaporation), in green when more came out. After a preview the next row compares the allocated cost with the Total cost to allocate . You may type an Allocated cost or a Unit cost on an output: entering one works out the other from the quantity. Typing a cost on a co-product switches the method to Manual amounts , so the figures you entered are the ones posted and any difference goes to the variance account. On a by-product or scrap line, the unit cost you type is its value per unit. Step by step: run a formula Open Inventory > Processing Formulas (Multi-Output BOM) and click Run on the formula (or choose it in Load lines from ). Type the number of Batches / units and click Load lines . The lines are filled from the formula, multiplied by the batches, and the allocation is shown at once. Check the Processing site (inputs) and Receive outputs at . Change the output Qty to what was really produced, if it differs from Planned . The difference shows as the yield. Click Preview allocation to see the Cost allocation preview : input materials, additional costs, total cost to allocate, by-products and scrap, allocated to outputs and, for the variance methods, Variance posted (loss / (gain)) . The preview uses today's average costs; posting uses the average cost at the time of posting. Click Save and post (or Save & New ). The message "... posted: inputs issued, outputs received at their allocated cost." appears. Step by step: take an assembly apart without a formula Click New processing order . In Load lines from , choose Unbuild assembly (bill of materials): SET-OFFICE ... and type the number of assemblies in Batches / units . Click Load lines . The assembly becomes the input and its stocked components the outputs; labor on the bill of materials is not recovered. The method is set to Relative standard cost . Check the lines and click Save and post . Step by step: save a pending order and complete it When an input is short, Save and post gives "Not enough stock at the processing site: ... Save the order as pending, or transfer or receive the items first." An order dated before today is also checked on its own date: it may not take stock that only came in later, nor so much that the site would go below zero on a later date, for example "CARCASS (need 96.67, have 71.48 on 10/01/2026 without going below zero on a later date; the rest came in after it)". Date the order on or after the bill that brought the stock in. Click Save as pending . The order is saved, does not affect inventory or the books, and shows its amounts as estimates. When the inputs are in, open the order. In the box "When the inputs are available at the processing site, complete the order here.", check the Processing date and click Complete and post . The pending processing order PRC-00005: 2 TRD-PC taken apart into RAM, SSD and scrap The saved order The page shows the order's details (date, number, status, type, method, formula × batches, sites, reference, memo, who entered and approved it), the Inputs (consumed) , the Additional processing costs , and the Outputs (produced) and cost allocation with the Yield of each output (actual against planned, red when below 100%). The inputs grid ends with a Total inputs line (quantity and cost), the outputs grid with a Total outputs line (quantity, the allocation percentages, which add up to 100%, and the cost allocated), then a Variance qty line, the input quantity less the output quantity, and a Variance line: the inputs and additional costs less the outputs. The variance is 0.00 when the whole cost was allocated, and is highlighted when it is not, for example with the Current average cost or Manual amounts method, where the difference is posted to the variance account. A completed order also shows the General ledger entries created automatically . The Quantity summary box gives the Input quantity , the Output quantity and the Variance qty (inputs less outputs) ; when the lines use different units of measure (boxes in, pieces out) it says so, since the quantities are added as entered. The Cost summary box gives input materials, additional costs, total cost, by-products and scrap, co-products and variance. Each input shows its Unit cost and Cost . Example A meat shop cuts 5.02 kg of pork into 2.3 kg of Pork Humba and 2.7 kg of Pork Menudo. Total inputs 5.02, total outputs 5, so the Variance qty (inputs less outputs) is 0.02 kg: the trimmings lost in cutting. The cost of the 5.02 kg is still spread over the two outputs. Its buttons: Edit: changes the order (not on a voided one). Saving a posted order posts it again. Run again: a new order with the same formula, batches and site. Print: the PROCESSING ORDER printout. The inputs table gives each input's Qty , Unit cost and Cost ; the Total inputs and Total outputs lines close the grids, and a small table at the right gives Inputs , Outputs , Variance (inputs less outputs) and Variance qty (inputs less outputs) , followed by the Prepared by, Processed by and Checked / approved by lines. Users who may not view costs get the quantities only, with the variance qty. Void: keeps the document but takes the outputs back out of stock and returns the inputs. Delete: removes it; its full content stays in the audit trail. History , Back to list . Printout of the processing order PRC-00005, marked PENDING What it records The inputs and additional costs are credited; the outputs are debited with their allocated cost. When PRC-00005 is completed (2 TRD-PC at ₱3,000.00 and ₱300.00 of labor, shared by relative sales value after the scrap): Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory (4 RAM-8GB) ₱3,131.69 1200 Inventory (2 SSD-512) ₱3,048.31 1200 Inventory (8 SCRAP-KG by-product) ₱120.00 1200 Inventory (2 TRD-PC) ₱6,000.00 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed ₱300.00 With Current average cost or Manual amounts , a difference between the cost and the outputs' values is posted to the variance account: a debit when the outputs are worth less (a loss), a credit when they are worth more (a gain). Good to know A supervisor must approve an order whose total cost is more than your Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval . "Every input needs an item and a quantity greater than zero." and "Outputs must be inventory or assembly items." An order is not posted while an input has no unit cost or average unit cost, or a co-product or by-product would be received at no cost: "The processing order cannot be posted with no unit cost: the input PORK-LOIN has no unit cost or average unit cost, and the outputs PORK-CHOP, PORK-WASTE would be received at no cost. ..." The input shows no unit cost in red in Est. unit cost , and the output's Unit cost box is outlined in red. Enter the unit cost of the input on its item form or receive it at its cost first, and give every co-product and by-product a share of the cost (scrap may stay at zero). Save as pending still works, and Complete and post is checked the same way. The check can be switched off with Block posting processing orders with no unit cost in Company, Security & Closing Date . "This order cannot be voided: its outputs were already used, and stock would go below zero for ..." appears when the outputs were sold or used and negative stock is not allowed. When it is allowed, the void goes ahead with the warning "Its outputs were already used; stock is now negative for .... Record the missing receipt or adjustment." "A voided processing order cannot be edited." The costs of a pending order are estimates at today's average costs. How processing orders move the average cost A processing order is often where an item's average cost changes most, because it does two things at once: it takes the inputs out at their average cost, and it puts the outputs in at their share of that cost. Five things decide what it does to the averages. The inputs go out at the average of all sites. Whatever the input's average is when the order is saved passes into the outputs. If the input's average is wrong, every output inherits it: a carcass at an overstated ₱462.69 instead of ₱225.00 makes every cut about twice as dear. Each output takes its share of the cost. The share follows the Allocation method of the order or its formula: with Physical units or Weight / measure every kilo gets the same unit cost, trimmings as much as the chops; with Relative sales value the dearer cuts take more; with Fixed percentages the shares never change. When the input cost, the shares or the yields change from one order to the next, the unit cost of an output changes with them, and so does its average. A formula with relative sales value or fixed percentages keeps the unit costs steadier. With Current average cost (difference to variance) the outputs come in at their own average, which then does not move at all; the difference goes to the processing variance account. Outputs received while they are below zero. When the counter sells cuts before the processing order is entered, the cuts go below zero at their last average. The order then settles that shortfall at its own unit cost and charges the difference to cost of goods sold (see Stock below zero ). Before version 53 the difference stayed on the few units left and could multiply the average. Inputs used before the bill is entered. The same happens to the input: processed before the supplier's bill is in, it goes below zero, and the bill settles the shortfall. Entering the bill first, or on the same date (the stock received is counted first on each date), keeps the cuts at the bill's cost. Back-dated and edited orders. A saved order is costed at the averages of the moment it is saved, not of its date, and saving an old order again issues its inputs at today's average. Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data works every cost out again in date order. The Average Cost Changes report lists each of these as it happened, with the average before and after; tick Processing, disassembly and builds only to see the processing orders alone. Note Version 53 fixes a fault that made averages jump after processing orders.
