Click Void transaction . The sale is kept, marked VOID, its entries are removed from the ledger and the goods go back to stock. Tip Void sales before the shift is closed, so the Z-reading and the drawer count include the void. What it records A return is a POS Return . With goods that can be resold, returning one MOU-001 Wireless Mouse (₱599.00 plus ₱71.88 VAT, refunded in cash): Account Debit Credit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances ₱599.00 2100 Output Tax ₱71.88 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers ₱670.88 1200 Inventory ₱350.00 5000 Cost of Goods Sold ₱350.00 The goods come back at the item's current average cost: to the terminal's site when they can be resold, or to the first active site of the type Damaged goods (Damaged Goods in the demo) when they cannot. With no damaged-goods site, goods that cannot be resold are not put back in stock and cost of goods sold is not reversed. A refund by card or e-wallet credits that method's clearing account instead of cash. A cash refund lowers the shift's expected cash. Voiding a sale or a return removes everything it posted. Every void and refund appears in the POS Void and Refund Log . Good to know "Open a shift on your terminal before processing returns." "Choose a completed sale to return." Voided and suspended sales cannot be returned. "You cannot return more than was sold of ...". "Enter the quantities being returned." and "Enter the reason for the return." Every return and every void needs a supervisor, even for small amounts. Returning needs the Create permission on this page; voiding needs Delete/Void. For an account customer you can also give a credit memo in the Customers module (see Create Credit Memos/Refunds ).

href="#pg-pos-approval_codes" aria-label="Link to this section"> Approval Codes lets a supervisor approve from anywhere. Instead of walking to the counter and typing their password, the supervisor generates a one-time code here (on their own phone or computer, logged in as themselves), reads it out to the cashier or clerk, and the cashier types it in the Approval code tab of the Supervisor approval box. The code stands for the supervisor's username and password: the approval is recorded under the supervisor's name, the code works once, and an unused code expires on its own. The page also keeps the list of every code and what became of it. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Approval Codes. The page is given to the roles that may approve at the POS Register (and to administrators); the Create right on it is what allows generating codes. The Approval Codes page just after a code was generated: the code card, the Generate form and the list Generate an approval code Field What it does What it is for (optional) A note kept with the code and shown in the list, for example "Price override for a bulk buyer". For which user Any user , or one user: then only that user can use the code. On which page Any page where I may approve , or one page (POS Register as delivered): then the code works only on that page. The list offers the pages that show a Supervisor approval box: the register, receipts and shifts, invoices, sales receipts, estimates, sales orders, credit memos, batch invoices, checks, cash vouchers, pay bills, inventory adjustments, physical counts, processing orders and asset maintenance. Valid for 1 hour , 4 hours , 12 hours , 1 day (as delivered), 3 days or 7 days . Click Generate code . The message Approval code XXXX-XXXX generated. It can be used once, until (date and time). appears, and the code is shown large in a card at the top left, with who and what it is for and Copy , which puts it on the clipboard for a message to the cashier. A code has eight letters and digits in two groups of four, such as AC7K-9MXT, made only of characters that are not mistaken for one another (no 0 and O, 1 and I, 5 and S, 8 and B, 2 and Z), so it can be read out over the phone. Important Give the code only to the person who needs it. Whoever types it gets your approval, under your name, for one transaction on the page you chose. Limit a code to one user and one page when you can, and keep Valid for short. The list The four counters, Open , Used , Expired and Cancelled , show how many codes are in each state; click one to show only those, and again to show all. The filters Generated from / To (the last 30 days as delivered) and My codes only narrow the list, and Show applies them. Each line shows: Column What it shows Code The code. A code another user generated and already used is shown with its second half hidden. State Open (usable, with "until" and its expiry), Used , Expired or Cancelled . Generated When, and by whom. For The user it was limited to (or "any user") and the page (or "any page"). Purpose The note typed when it was generated. Used For a used code: when, by whom, on what (for example "15.00% discount on LAP-001") and a link to the transaction it approved. A cancelled code shows when it was cancelled; an expired one says "never used". Cancel on an open code's line (for its issuer, and for users with the Edit or Delete right on the page) asks "Cancel this code? It can no longer be used." and then says The code was cancelled. It can no longer be used. The Approval Codes page with the counters, the filters and the list of codes How a code is checked When a code is typed in a Supervisor approval box, the program checks, in this order, that the code exists, that it is still open (not used, expired or cancelled), that it was not limited to another user or another page, that the person using it is not the supervisor who generated it, that the supervisor is still an active user, and that the supervisor's role may Approve on that page. Then the code is marked used and the transaction is saved with the supervisor as Approved by . If the save fails for another reason (a missing field, say), the code is handed back and stays open for the next try. Every code generated, used, refused or cancelled is in the Audit Trail , with the audit actions Approval code issued , Approval code used , Approval failed and Approval code cancelled . Note Users who may open the page but have no Create right on it see the list and the note You can see the codes but not generate them . A code can never be used by the supervisor who generated it ("You cannot approve your own transaction with a code you generated."), and a supervisor who loses the Approve right makes their open codes useless ("... is not allowed to approve on this page, so their code cannot be used here.").

href="#pg-pos-terminals" aria-label="Link to this section"> A terminal is one selling counter. Set up one for each counter, phone or tablet that sells, with the site it sells from, the cash account of its drawer, its receipt numbering, its default class and the users who work it. Where to find it: Point of Sale > POS Terminals. The POS Terminals page with Makati Counter 1 and Cebu Counter 1, and the New terminal form The table lists the terminals: Code , Name , Site , Cash account , Class , Next receipt (the number the next sale will get), Users ("any user with POS access" when nobody is assigned) and an Edit link. Inactive terminals are shown in grey. Editing the terminal POS-01 Makati Counter 1 Fields Field What to enter Code A short code, up to 20 characters, for example POS-01. Saved in capitals, unique. Name The counter's name, for example Makati Counter 1. It is printed on the receipts and readings. Inventory site (stock is sold from here) The site whose stock the counter sells. Cash on hand account The cash account of the drawer: cash sales are debited to it, and over and short are posted to it. Default 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers. Receipt prefix The start of the receipt numbers, for example MK1-. Default OR-. Default class of sales The class the counter's sales start with. Active Untick it to stop the counter being used. Users assigned to this terminal The users who work the counter. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) to pick several. Step by step: set up a counter Open Point of Sale > POS Terminals . Type the Code and Name , choose the Inventory site and the Cash on hand account . Type the Receipt prefix and choose the Default class of sales . Pick the cashiers and supervisors in Users assigned to this terminal . Click Save terminal (or Save terminal & New ). The message "Terminal saved." appears. To change a terminal, click Edit on its row. Good to know "Enter the code, name, site and cash account." and "Another terminal uses this code." Receipt numbers are the prefix followed by an eight-digit number, one sequence per terminal: MK1-00000001, MK1-00000002 .... "Receipt numbers are sequential per terminal and cannot be reset here." Charges, returns and payments on account take the next number too. Someone assigned to one or more terminals can use only those terminals. Someone not assigned to any terminal can use every active terminal at the sites they may use, including terminals that list other users. The Administrator can use every terminal. A user limited to some sites (see User Accounts ) sees only the terminals at those sites. Terminals cannot be deleted; untick Active instead.

href="#s-point-of-sale-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The POS reports are under Point of Sale > Reports . They use the common report tools ( Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize , and clicking a figure to see its detail), explained in Working with reports . Most of them can be narrowed to a Site , Terminal and Cashier . Unless a report says otherwise, voided and suspended sales are left out and returns are deducted. Cost and margin columns are shown only to users who may view costs.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_txn" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every receipt with the items sold on it: one heading line per receipt, then one line per item. Use it to check a day's receipts one by one. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Transaction No. (detail). POS Sales by Transaction No. (detail) for today, with the receipts MK1-00000007 and MK1-00000008 Filters: Dates (default Today ), Site , Terminal and Cashier . The receipt line shows the Transaction no. / item (the receipt number; click it to open the sale), Time , Cashier , Terminal , Customer ( Walk-in when none), Payment (the payment methods used), Discount , Net sales , VAT , Receipt total , Cost and Margin . Each item line shows its Qty , U/M , Price , Discount , Net sales , Cost and Margin . Returns are marked "(return)" and shown as negatives.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_item" aria-label="Link to this section"> Counter sales less returns, net of VAT, for each item. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Item. POS Sales by Item for today Filters: Dates (default Today ), Site , Terminal and Cashier . Columns: Item , Receipts (how many receipts sold it), Qty , Discounts , Net sales , Cost and Margin (net sales less cost). The report can also be narrowed by Item , Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ).

href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_category" aria-label="Link to this section"> The same figures for each item category; items without a category are under (uncategorized) . Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Category. The report can also be narrowed by Category , Item type and Preferred supplier (see Filters on related records ). POS Sales by Category for today, with Accessories and Bundles

t: POS Sales by Cashier & Payment Method
x: href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_cashier" aria-label="Link to this section"> One report for two questions: how much each cashier sold, and how the money came in. Each cashier has a heading line with their sales figures, and under it one line per payment method they took, so a cashier's cash, card, GCash and Maya totals can be matched with the drawer and the providers' reports. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Cashier & Payment Method. POS Sales by Cashier & Payment Method for today: a cashier's line with the payment methods under it Filters: Dates (default Today ), Site , Terminal and Cashier . The cashier's line shows Receipts , Qty , Discounts , Net sales (ex VAT) , Cost , Margin , Voids (how many of their sales were voided in the period) and Tendered (incl. VAT) , the money they took in. Each payment line under it shows the method's name, its Type (Cash, Card, E-wallet, Bank transfer, Gift voucher, Check or Other), the number of Receipts it was used on and the amount Tendered (incl. VAT) . Sales charged to a customer's account are on the line Charged to customer accounts (type On account ). Refunds are deducted from the method chosen for the refund. When more than one cashier sold, a last group, All cashiers, by payment method , adds the same payment lines up for the whole counter, and the TOTAL line closes the report. Tip Compare a cashier's voids with the others'. Many voids from one cashier are worth a look in the POS Void and Refund Log . To match a till, read the Tendered figure of the cashier's Cash line against the cash counted at the Z-reading.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_hour" aria-label="Link to this section"> Net sales for each hour of the day, with a bar chart. Use it to plan staff for the busy hours. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Hour. POS Sales by Hour, with the TOTAL of the Transactions, Net sales and Average sale columns Filters: Dates (default This month ), Site , Terminal and Cashier . Columns: Hour (for example 14:00–14:59), Transactions , Net sales (net of VAT, returns deducted) and Average sale . The TOTAL row adds up the Transactions and the Net sales , and its Average sale is the total net sales divided by all the transactions.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_daily_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> One line per day and terminal. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Daily Sales Summary. POS Daily Sales Summary for September 2026 Filters: Dates (default This month ), Terminal , Cashier and Class . Class keeps the sales of one class (the class of the terminal, or the one the cashier chose on the sale); Unclassified keeps the sales without a class. Columns: Date , Terminal , Sales (number of sales), Returns and Voids (totals, VAT included), Net sales , VAT and Total (sales less returns).

href="#pg-rpt-pos_readings" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every X- and Z-reading taken in a period, with its figures. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > X- and Z-Reading Summary. X- and Z-Reading Summary for September 2026 with an X-reading and Z-reading #1 Filters: Dates (the business date; default This month ) and Terminal . Columns: Date , Reading (X, or Z with its number; click it to print the reading again), Terminal , Receipts (first to last), Gross , Discounts , Returns , Voids , Net , VAT , Expected cash , Counted , Over/(short) and By . Use it to check that every business day has its Z-reading and to follow the cash differences.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_discount_log" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every discounted line sold at a counter, with who gave it and who approved it. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Discount Log. POS Discount Log with a 5% discount on LAP-001 Filters: Dates (default This month ), Terminal and User . Columns: Time , Receipt (click to open), Terminal , Cashier , Item , Qty , Price , Disc % , Discount and Approved by (empty when the discount was within the cashier's limit). Charge sales made at a counter are included.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_void_log" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every void, delete and refund done in the Point of Sale, taken from the audit trail. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Void and Refund Log. POS Void and Refund Log with a void and a refund approved by the supervisor Filters: Dates (default This month ), Terminal and User . Columns: Time , Action ( Void , Delete or Refund ), Receipt (click to open), Terminal , Cashier (the user who did it), Amount , Reason and Approved by . As the note says, every void and refund requires a supervisor.

href="#pg-rpt-pos_sales_item_group" aria-label="Link to this section"> The item groups sold at the POS, counted as groups: how many of each group were sold, at what group price, and for how much. POS returns are taken off. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > POS Sales by Item Group. It is given to the roles that may open POS Sales by Item. POS Sales by Item Group Filters: Dates (default Today ), Terminal , Site , Cashier and Item group . Columns: Item group name , Qty (groups sold), Group price and Total (before VAT), with a Totals line. Tick Show the individual item details to list under each group its items, with their quantities, prices and amounts, and the price variance; Show the transactions lists the receipts. Click a total to see its receipts. Sort by orders the groups by Qty or Total , Increasing or Decreasing (see Sorting ). POS Sales by Item Group with the individual item details

href="#pg-rpt-pos_ending_inventory" aria-label="Link to this section"> The quantity on hand of every item at a cashier's outlet at the end of the cashier's shift, to be counted and signed when the stock is turned over to the next cashier. It prints on the POS roll printer as well as on a page. Where to find it: Point of Sale > Reports > Ending Inventory - POS Cashier. Also the Ending inventory button of a shift in Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings (and the box icon on each line of the shift list), which opens it for that shift. It is given to the roles that may open the X- and Z-Reading Summary, and to the cashiers, who print their own. Ending Inventory - POS Cashier for a closed shift, report type A: item code and total Filters: Dates with a From date and time and a To date and time , Item , Site , Class , Category , Cashier , Shift , Report type and Exclude inventory with zero balance . Filter What it does Shift Places the times automatically: the From is the moment the cashier opened the shift, the To (the cut-off) the moment it was closed, or now for a shift still open. The cashier and the site of the shift's terminal are filled in. To date and time The cut-off: the quantities are those on hand at that moment. Every sale, return, delivery, transfer and adjustment up to it counts; a POS sale at the moment it was rung up. For shifts of a 24-hour business, type the times (for example 2:00 PM for the 8:01 AM - 2:00 PM shift). Cashier The site becomes the outlet the cashier worked at. A cashier sees only their own name and shifts, and the report opens on their latest shift. Report type A. Item code & balance (the item code and the total, in item-code order) or B. Item description & balance (the description and the total, in description order). Exclude inventory with zero balance Leaves out the items with nothing on hand. Without it, every stocked item is listed, zeros included. Report type B, item description and total, with the zero balances left out The heading reads Quantity on hand by cashier, by item code (or by item description ), with the Cut-off , the Site and the Cashier . The TOTAL line adds up the quantities. At the foot are two signature lines, Inventory Turnovered by: and Inventory Received by: . Click a total to see the transactions that make it up. Beg. , In , Sold and Other out (from the From date and time) and the other description of the item can be added as columns with Modify Report . Printing on the POS printer Click Print to POS printer . The slip shows the company name, QUANTITY ON HAND BY CASHIER , By Item Code or By Item Description , Cut-off: To: with the date and time, Site: , Cashier: , the items with their totals, TOTAL , and the signature lines. Above it, choose the Report type to print : A. Item code & balance or B. Item description & balance , then click Print . The slip is sized to the roll paper set for the Bluetooth receipt printer (58 mm or 80 mm, System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date). When Bluetooth printing is on, a Bluetooth printer button sends it straight to the printer. The slip for the POS printer, report type A The same slip, report type B, without the zero balances The signature captions, the names above them and the foot text are customizable: in Modify Report , the heading and footer settings hold Caption under each signature line (Inventory Turnovered by: and Inventory Received by: as delivered), Names printed above the captions and Text at the foot of the report . Save the layout as the default and every user prints them, on the page and on the slip. A cashier's own ending inventory: the report opens on the cashier's latest shift Step by step: the ending inventory of a shift At the end of the shift, go to Point of Sale > Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings , open the shift and click Ending inventory (or open the report and choose the Shift ). Choose the Report type , A or B, and tick Exclude inventory with zero balance if the zeros are not to be counted. Click Print to POS printer , then Print . The outgoing cashier and the incoming cashier count the stock against the slip and sign it. The Ending inventory button of a shift

href="#pg-bank-write_checks" aria-label="Link to this section"> Write Checks records a payment made by check, or charged to a company credit card, that is not the payment of a bill already entered: rent paid on the spot, a purchase paid at once, a loan payment, a cash advance by check. To pay bills you have entered, use Pay Bills instead, so the bills are marked paid. Where to find it: Banking > Write Checks opens the list of checks. The Home page quick action Write Checks opens a blank check. Receipt Management can also open this form filled from a scanned receipt. Note A loan released by cheque on the Loan Release Form is a check of this list, numbered with the cheque no., with the member as the payee and the loan number as the reference. It prints as the Check Voucher of the loan release, it is never edited or deleted, and voiding it cancels the loan (only while the loan has no payment). Every voucher of a loan release is also listed on Loan Release Vouchers . The Checks list The list shows the checks of a date range (from 90 days back to 30 days ahead when it opens). Use From , To , Status , Class and Search (number, name or memo), then click Filter . A voided check is struck through. A check waiting to be printed has a to print tag in the Status column. Click a check number to open it. The columns Column What it shows Date The date of the check. No. The check number. Click it to open the check. Name The payee. Reference The reference, if any. Memo The memo of the check. Class The class of the check (shown when classes are in use). Total The amount of the check. Status Open for a posted check, Void for a voided one, with to print when it is queued for printing. By The user who entered it. A new check Fields Field What to enter / what it means Bank / credit card account The account the check is drawn on: a Bank or Credit Card account. It starts at 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking. Pay to the order of The payee: a supplier, customer, employee or other name. Type part of the name to search. Leave it at — other payee — to type a name below. Other payee name A payee who is on none of the lists, for a one-time payment. It is used only when Pay to the order of is blank. Date The date of the check. Check no. Leave blank to get the next check number (the grey text shows it, for example 1011). Type the number printed on the check if it is different. Print later Tick to put the check on the Checks to print list instead of printing it now. Default site for items The inventory site where the items on the Items tab are received, unless a line names another site. Class The class of the whole check. Memo What the check is for. It prints on the check voucher. The lines are on two tabs. Use Expenses for accounts and Items for items you buy with the check. Expenses tab: Column What to enter / what it means Account The account to charge, for example 6010 Rent Expense. Amount The amount before tax. Tax The tax code, for example VAT12. The tax is added to the total. Memo The description of the line. Customer:Job The customer or job the cost is for, if any. Billable Tick, with a Customer:Job, to bill the cost to that customer later. Items tab: Column What to enter / what it means Item The item bought. Its description and cost fill in. Description Changes the description of the line if needed. Qty The quantity (a U/M column appears when an item has several units). Cost The cost per unit. Amount Qty times Cost. Tax The tax code of the line. Site The site that receives the item. Default uses the site at the top. Customer:Job and Billable As on the Expenses tab. The Subtotal , Tax and Total of both tabs are added up at the bottom right. Add line adds a row to a tab and the red X removes one. Step by step To write a check: Open Banking > Write Checks and click New . Check the Bank / credit card account . Choose the payee in Pay to the order of , or type an Other payee name . Check the Date and the Check no. Choose the Class and type a Memo . On the Expenses tab, choose the Account , type the Amount and choose the Tax code if the payment includes VAT. If you are buying items, click the Items tab and enter them. Check the Total . If the check is above your limit, open Supervisor approval and let the supervisor type their username and password. Click Save , or Save & New to write another check. Example Check 1006 to Metro Property Leasing for ₱85,000.00, memo "Office and warehouse rent", with one expense line: 6010 Rent Expense, ₱85,000.00. To print a check voucher: Open the check. Click Print . Click Print above the page. To print later: Tick Print later when you write the check. When you are ready to print, open Banking > Write Checks and click Checks to print . The list shows only the checks marked to be printed. Open each check and click Print . Once printed, it leaves the list. The Checks list filtered to the checks to be printed To change a check: open it, click Edit , make the change and click Save . To void or delete a check: Open the check. Click Void (keeps the check with no effect on the ledger) or Delete (removes it; a full copy stays in the audit trail). Type the Reason . If the check is above your amount limit, a supervisor must approve in the same box. Confirm. To memorize a check you write every month: open it and click Memorize (see Memorized Transactions ). A voided check The saved check shows the date, number, status, payee, the account it was drawn on, the memo and who entered it, then its lines and, for a posted check, General ledger entries created automatically . A voided check has a grey VOID band with the reason and the time. Buttons New: a blank check. Checks to print: the checks marked Print later that are not printed yet. Export: the list as a spreadsheet file. On a saved check: Edit , Print , Email (when the payee is a supplier or customer; it opens your e-mail program with a link to the check), Memorize , Void , Delete , History ( Transaction History ) and Back to list . The check voucher A check prints as a CHECK VOUCHER with the company name, address and TIN (and the logo when it is switched on for checks in Company, Security & Closing Date ), the check number and the date. It shows Pay to with the supplier's or customer's address and TIN, the Amount in figures and in words (for example "Two thousand five hundred pesos and 00/100 only"), the memo, Paid from , the reference, site and class. The ledger entries follow in a table of Account , Memo , Class , Debit and Credit , debits first, with the totals, and the signature lines Prepared by , Checked by , Approved by and Received by . A voided check prints VOID and "No ledger entries (voided)." The check voucher of a voided check What it records Account Debit Credit Each expense line's account (for example 6010 Rent Expense) Line amount The inventory account of each stock item on the Items tab Line amount 1300 Input Tax (or the tax code's input tax account) Tax of the lines The bank or credit card account of the check (for example 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking) Total of the check Stock items on the Items tab go into stock at their site at the cost on the line. The class of the check, and the payee, go on every ledger line. Example An expense line of ₱10,000.00 with VAT12 posts Dr 6040 Office Supplies Expense ₱10,000.00, Dr 1300 Input Tax ₱1,200.00, Cr 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking ₱11,200.00. Good to know "Choose a payee or type a payee name." "Choose the bank account." "Add at least one expense or item line." "Choose an account for every expense line." and "Choose an item for every line that has a description or amount." "Supervisor approval is required: check above your amount limit (85,000.00). Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below." A user who has the approve permission on Write Checks approves their own checks. "You cannot approve your own transaction." appears when a user types their own name in the approval box. When an account on the check is marked With SL , the payee of the check counts as the name of every line, so a check always satisfies the rule when it has a payee from the lists. A typed Other payee name does not count. A check that debits 2000 Accounts Payable lowers the supplier's balance but does not mark any bill paid. Pay entered bills with Pay Bills . Expense lines marked Billable with a Customer:Job are offered as billable costs the next time you create an invoice for that customer (see Create Invoices ). Check numbers come from one series shared with the checks of Pay Bills and customer refunds. The program does not stop you from typing a number that was already used; the Check Register highlights duplicates and gaps. A check that has been cleared in a bank reconciliation, or that is dated on or before the closing date, can only be changed by a user with the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled . Changes to a cleared check are listed on the Reconciliation Discrepancy report. When you save a check with no class and classes are in use, the program asks No class selected first. Click Choose a class or Continue saving .

href="#pg-bank-cash_voucher" aria-label="Link to this section"> A cash voucher records cash paid out of a cash fund, such as the petty cash fund or a revolving fund: delivery fares, small purchases, cash advances to employees, government fees. The voucher is entered like a journal entry (the accounts debited and credited), and the cash account is credited for the cash amount. The same page lists the vouchers already saved. Where to find it: Banking > Cash Voucher. The Cash Voucher button on Employees & Other Names also opens it. Note A loan released in cash on the Loan Release Form is a cash voucher of this list, paid from the cash account chosen on the form, with "Loan release" and the loan number under the payee. It prints as the Cash Voucher of the loan release; Edit and Delete stay greyed on it, and voiding it cancels the loan (only while the loan has no payment). Every voucher of a loan release is also listed on Loan Release Vouchers . The Cash Voucher page: the entry form at the top and the voucher list below Fields Field What to enter / what it means CAV entry no. Leave blank to get the next number (the grey text shows it, for example CAV-00003). A number you type must not be used by another voucher. Paid to Who received the cash: an employee, customer, supplier or other name. Type part of the name to search. Cash account The cash fund the money comes out of, for example 1005 Petty Cash Fund. Only Bank accounts are listed. Transaction date The date of the payment. or a name that is not on the lists A payee who is on none of the lists. The box is locked while a Paid to name is chosen. Reference no. An outside reference, for example the receipt number. Particulars What the cash was for. It prints as the particulars of the voucher. Cash amount The cash paid out. Leave it blank and it adds up from the lines. The lines: Column What to enter / what it means Account The account charged, for example 6100 Freight and Delivery. Type part of the account name to search. Debit The amount charged to the account. Credit Use only when part of the voucher reduces an account, for example a refund of an earlier advance. Memo The description of the line. SL The subsidiary ledger name of the line: an employee, customer, supplier or other name. Required on lines to Accounts Receivable (a customer) and Accounts Payable (a supplier). On an account marked With SL, the Paid to name counts when the line has none. Class The class of the line. It follows the class at the bottom of the form. Under the lines, Totals adds the debits and credits, Cash account credited shows the cash amount and Difference shows what is still out of balance. It turns green when the voucher balances. At the bottom of the form: Field What to enter / what it means Class The class of the voucher. It fills the class of the lines and is the class of the cash line. Reason for the change Shown only when you edit a saved voucher. Recorded in the audit trail. Show print preview after saving Ticked, the printed voucher opens after Save . The program remembers your choice for the next voucher. Step by step To make a cash voucher: Open Banking > Cash Voucher . Choose the payee in Paid to , or type the name in or a name that is not on the lists . Choose the Cash account , for example 1005 Petty Cash Fund. Check the Transaction date . Type the Reference no. and the Particulars . On the first line, choose the Account and type the Debit . Add a Memo and, where needed, the SL name. Add more lines if the cash was spent on several things. Leave Cash amount blank, or type the amount on the receipt and check that Difference is 0.00. Choose the Class . Click Save , or Save & New to start another voucher. With Show print preview after saving ticked, Save opens the printed voucher. Example CAV-00002 pays ₱480.00 of delivery fares out of 1005 Petty Cash Fund to "Jeepney and tricycle fares", with one line: 6100 Freight and Delivery, debit ₱480.00, class Makati Store. To find a saved voucher: In Cash voucher list , choose the Date range ( Today , This week , This month , Last month , This quarter , This fiscal year , All dates or Custom ). For Custom , type the From and To dates; clicking in them switches to Custom. Choose a Class if you want only one. Click Query . To edit, void, delete or print a voucher from the list: Click any line of the voucher in the list. The footer shows "Selected: CAV-00002". Click Edit , Void , Delete or Print under the list. Edit and Void are not available for a voided voucher. For Void or Delete , type the reason and confirm. Double-click a line, or click its Entry no , to open the voucher. To clear the form without saving: click Clear . A saved cash voucher The saved voucher shows the date, number, status, Paid to , class, Cash account , memo and who entered it, the lines, and General ledger entries created automatically . Its buttons are Edit , Print , Memorize , Void , Delete , History and Back to list . The voucher list Column What it shows Date, Entry no, Paid to Shown on the first line of each voucher. Account Each account line, then the cash account (greyed). Subsidiary ledger The SL name of the line; the payee on the cash line. Memo The memo of the line; the particulars on the cash line. Class The class of the line. Debit/Credit (+/-) Debits as positive figures, credits (such as the cash line) in brackets. The footer gives the number of vouchers and the cash paid out by the vouchers that are not void. Export list downloads the list shown as a spreadsheet file. The printed voucher The voucher prints as CASH VOUCHER with the company heading, the number and the date; Paid to , Cash account , the Amount in figures and in words, and the Particulars ; the class; a table of Account , Description , Name , Class , Debit and Credit that includes the credit to the cash account, with the totals; and the signature lines Prepared by , Checked by , Approved by and Received by , so the payee signs for the cash. The printed cash voucher CAV-00002 What it records Account Debit Credit Each debit line's account (for example 6100 Freight and Delivery) Line amount Each credit line's account Line amount The cash account (for example 1005 Petty Cash Fund) Cash amount Each line carries its SL name and class to the ledger; the cash line carries the payee and the class of the voucher. Good to know "Enter at least one account line." "Choose the cash account the voucher is paid from." "The cash account is credited automatically for the cash amount. Do not enter it again in the account lines." "Debits less credits (480.00) must equal the cash amount (500.00)." Correct the lines or the cash amount. "The cash amount must be more than zero." "Choose who the cash is paid to, or type the name." "Lines posted to Accounts Receivable need a customer in the SL column." and "Lines posted to Accounts Payable need a supplier in the SL column." "CAV entry no. CAV-00002 is already used. Leave the number blank to get the next one." A voucher above your amount limit needs supervisor approval: "Supervisor approval is required: cash voucher above your amount limit (5,000.00)." When you save with the Class empty and classes are in use, the program asks No class selected first, even when every line has its own class, because the class at the bottom is the class of the cash line. To replenish the fund, move money into it with Transfer Funds or a check payable to the custodian.

href="#pg-bank-register" aria-label="Link to this section"> The register shows every transaction that touched one account, with a running balance, like a checkbook. For a bank account it also lets you record a simple check, deposit or transfer without leaving the page. Where to find it: Banking > Use Register. The Register link on the Chart of Accounts , and the accounts under Cash and bank accounts on the Home page, open the register of that account. The register of 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking The filters Filter What it does Account The account to show. Bank, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, Credit Card, Other Current Asset, Other Current Liability, Fixed Asset, Long Term Liability, Equity and Other Asset accounts can be chosen. The page reloads as soon as you choose. From The first date shown. It starts on the first day of the month two months back. To The last date shown. It starts 30 days after today. Search A word in the number, memo or name. Click Show after changing the dates or the search. The columns Column What it shows Date The date of the transaction. Number The document number. Click it to open the transaction. Type Check, Deposit, Bill Payment, Customer Payment, Transfer and so on. Payee / name The name on the transaction. Memo The memo. Payment / Deposit Money out and money in. For an account with a credit normal balance (a credit card or a liability) the columns are Decrease and Increase . ✓ A check mark when the transaction has been cleared in a bank reconciliation. Balance The running balance. The first line is the Opening balance at the From date and the last line is the Ending balance . Step by step To look at an account's register: Open Banking > Use Register . Choose the Account . Change From and To if needed and click Show . Choosing the account of the register To enter a simple transaction in the register (bank accounts only): In Enter a simple transaction in this register , choose the Type : Check / payment , Deposit or Transfer to another account . You see only the types you may create. Check the Date . Type the Number : the check number for a check (blank for the next number), or the deposit slip number for a deposit. A transfer does not use it. Type the Payee / received from name. Choose the Account (expense / income / transfer to) : the account charged by a check, the account credited by a deposit, or the account the money goes to in a transfer. Type the Amount , choose the Class and type a Memo . Click Record . The message "Entry recorded." appears and the entry is added to the register. To export the register: click Export . The file holds the date, type, number, payee, memo, payment, deposit, cleared mark and balance of the lines shown. Buttons Export: the register as a spreadsheet file. Reconcile: opens Reconcile for this account. What it records The register itself records nothing. A quick entry saves an ordinary transaction: Check / payment: a check on Write Checks : Dr the chosen account, Cr this bank account. Deposit: a deposit on Make Deposits : Dr this bank account, Cr the chosen account. Transfer to another account: a transfer on Transfer Funds : Dr the chosen account, Cr this bank account. You can open, print, edit or void them later on their own pages. Good to know "Enter the date, a positive amount and the other account." "Quick entry is available for bank and cash accounts only." The quick entry form appears only for Bank accounts. The quick check uses the typed payee name, has one expense line and no tax. For a check with several lines, VAT or a payee from the lists, use Write Checks. The quick entries do not check the With SL rule. For accounts that keep a subsidiary ledger, use Write Checks, Cash Voucher or Make Deposits so the name is recorded. A quick check above your amount limit needs supervisor approval, as on Write Checks. The register shows one line per transaction, even when the transaction posted several lines to the account.

href="#pg-bank-deposits" aria-label="Link to this section"> Make Deposits records money you put in the bank: customer payments and sales receipts waiting in Undeposited Funds, the cash of closed POS shifts, the settlement of card and e-wallet sales by the provider, and other money such as loan proceeds or an owner's contribution. One deposit matches one deposit slip. Where to find it: Banking > Make Deposits opens a new deposit. The Deposits list button shows the saved deposits. Edit on a saved deposit opens it again to change it (see Edit a deposit ). The Make Deposits form Fields Field What to enter / what it means Deposit to The bank account the money goes into. It starts at 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking. Date The date of the deposit slip. Deposit slip no. The number of the bank's deposit slip. Memo Starts as "Deposit". Class The class of the deposit. Payments waiting to be deposited (Undeposited Funds): the customer payments and sales receipts that were put in Undeposited Funds and are not in a deposit yet, and the journal entries that post to Undeposited Funds (see below). Tick the ones on your deposit slip; the box in the heading ticks them all. Column What it shows Date, Type, No. The payment, sales receipt or journal entry. Click the number to open it. Received from The customer. For a journal entry, its name, or else the description of its Undeposited Funds line (or its memo). Method The payment method, for example Check. For a journal entry: Debit, adds or Credit, deducts . Ref. The check or reference number. Amount The amount of the payment. For a journal entry, its net amount on Undeposited Funds: a credit shows in red in brackets and is taken off the deposit. Journal entries to Undeposited Funds A journal entry that debits or credits Undeposited Funds is usually an adjustment of what the POS or the collections bring to the bank: a cash overage, a shortage, a correction of a payment. Such entries (made on Make Journal Entries , opening balance entries included) are listed with the payments, with their net amount on Undeposited Funds. A debit to Undeposited Funds adds to the deposit; a credit deducts from it. Tick it with the payments or POS cash it adjusts: Items selected and Deposit total add the debits and take off the credits. Two journal entries crediting Undeposited Funds (120.00 in red, deducts) and one debiting it (500.00, adds) Once deposited, the entry leaves the list, as a payment does, and it cannot be voided or deleted until it is taken off the deposit ( Edit on the deposit) or the deposit is voided. If the entry is changed after it was deposited, editing the deposit shows its new amount with "was" and the old one under it; saving the deposit takes the new amount. Example JE-00007 debits Undeposited Funds ₱500.00 for a cash overage, and JE-00006 credits it ₱120.00 for a short collection. Ticked with customer payment PMT-00005 of ₱95,294.00, the deposit is ₱95,674.00: ₱95,294.00 + ₱500.00 − ₱120.00. POS cash from closed shifts (shown when there are some): the cash of each closed POS shift not deposited yet. To deposit is the Counted cash, less the opening float ( Less float : it stays in the drawer for the next shift), plus the cash drops ( Plus drops : cash taken out of the drawer during the shift). Tick the shifts you are depositing. The business date opens the shift, and a shift whose closing entries were corrected says so under its terminal; the figures are always the shift's figures as they are now. Example The cashier of POB1 Counter 2 opened with a float of ₱3,000.00 and closed the register with ₱9,170.48 counted, against ₱12,170.48 expected: a shortage of ₱3,000.00. The supervisor finds the drawer held ₱12,170.48 (the cashier had left out the float) and corrects Cash counted to 12,170.48. The shortage entry is voided, and Make Deposits now shows the shift with Counted 12,170.48, Less float 3,000.00 and To deposit 9,170.48: the cash sales of the day, while the ₱3,000.00 float stays in the drawer. Before the correction the shift showed 6,170.48 to deposit. Card and e-wallet settlements: the provider pays out card and e-wallet sales in one amount, less its fee. The table has one row for each clearing account: the account of every card or e-wallet payment method ( Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists > Payment Methods, POS clearing account ) and the module default accounts Card Clearing and E-wallet Clearing , used by a method that names no account. Each account is listed once, with the payment methods that use it under its name, so E-wallet Clearing shared by GCash and Maya is one row carrying the balance of both. Card and e-wallet settlements: each clearing account once, its payment methods, the unsettled balance and the Details button Column What to enter / what it means Clearing account For example 1060 Card Clearing or 1065 E-wallet Clearing. Unsettled What the provider has not paid out yet: the balance of the clearing account in the General Ledger on the deposit Date , its debits (card and e-wallet sales and payments) less its credits (settlements and refunds). It is the same figure as the Trial Balance for that date. Changing the Date changes it. A credit balance, in red, means more was settled than was received. Details Opens the Card and e-wallet balance details of the account (see below): what the unsettled balance is made of. Gross settled The sales amount the provider is settling. It cannot be more than Unsettled on the deposit date. Type it, or tick Settle on the receipts the provider paid in Details : their total goes into this box, which then shows "2 receipts ticked" under it and cannot be typed over. Clear takes the ticks off so the amount can be typed again. Fee deducted The provider's fee taken out of the settlement. Reference The provider's settlement reference. Card and e-wallet balance details Details beside an unsettled balance opens a window that explains it, as of the deposit date. Open as a page shows the same on a page of its own (Banking > Make Deposits, Details ), where you can choose another Clearing account or As of date and Print it. The balance details of 1065 E-wallet Clearing: the sources, the sales by payment method, the receipts not yet settled and the latest settlements Part What it shows The balance The unsettled amount, with the payment methods of the account, the total received (debits) and the total settled and refunded (credits). General Ledger and Trial Balance open those reports for the account and date. What the balance is made of The postings to the account by source: POS sales , POS returns refunded , Customer payments , Sales receipts , Settlements deposited to the bank , journal entries and others, each with the number of Documents , what was Received (debit) , what was Settled / refunded (credit) and the Net . The last line, Balance on the date, is the unsettled amount. Card and e-wallet sales by payment method For each payment method of the account (GCash and Maya on E-wallet Clearing): the POS sales paid with it, the POS refunds , the Payments and sales receipts and the Net received . Receipts not yet settled The sales the provider still owes. A settlement whose receipts were ticked settles those receipts; a settlement entered as an amount only is taken against the oldest receipts first. So the list holds the latest receipts that make up the balance, newest first: Date , Document (click to open it), Customer / terminal , Method , Reference (the approval or reference number typed at the counter), Amount and Unsettled , and, in the window opened from Make Deposits, Settle (see below). The oldest one may be partly settled. The total equals the balance. Latest settlements and other credits The last 25 deposits and other entries that took money out of the account, with their description (the provider's reference and, for a settlement whose receipts were ticked, how many). The General Ledger has all of them. Example E-wallet Clearing holds ₱16,113.44: a GCash sale of ₱1,564.64 and a Maya sale of ₱14,548.80. GCash and Maya settle ₱10,000.00. The balance becomes ₱6,113.44, and Receipts not yet settled shows the Maya sale of ₱14,548.80 with ₱6,113.44 unsettled: the ₱10,000.00 paid for the GCash sale and ₱8,435.36 of the Maya sale. The Trial Balance shows ₱6,113.44 on 1065 E-wallet Clearing too. Ticking the receipts a settlement pays The provider's settlement report lists the sales it pays. As the cash of the closed POS shifts is ticked for a deposit, those sales can be ticked: in the window opened by Details on Make Deposits, Receipts not yet settled has a Settle column with a tick box on every receipt and one in the heading that ticks them all. A click anywhere on the row ticks it too (not on its document link). The bar at the bottom of the window shows the Gross settled so far and how many receipts are ticked, and the same amount goes into Gross settled on the deposit at once. Done closes the window; opening Details again shows the ticks as they were. Details of 1060 Card Clearing with three receipts ticked under Settle and Gross settled 6,983.00 in the bar at the bottom Back on Make Deposits: Gross settled 6,983.00 with 3 receipts ticked and Clear under it When the deposit is saved, the ticked receipts are settled: they leave Receipts not yet settled , and the settlement line of the deposit says how many receipts were ticked ("Provider settlement BDO-77 (2 receipts ticked)"). The receipts that were not ticked stay on the list, whatever their date. Voiding or deleting the deposit makes its receipts unsettled again; editing it keeps them settled as long as the deposit still holds the settlement amount on that clearing account. Changing the deposit Date takes the ticks off, because what is unsettled depends on the date: tick them again. The Open as a page view has no tick boxes. Example The bank's card settlement report pays POS Sale MK1-00000012 (₱3,996.00), MK1-00000010 (₱1,998.00) and MK1-00000009 (₱989.00 still unsettled of ₱999.00). Tick the three under Settle : Gross settled becomes ₱6,983.00. Type the fee, save, and MK1-00000011 (₱2,997.00) is the only card sale left unsettled. Other receipts (loan proceeds, owner contributions, interest…): three rows for money that did not come through a customer payment. Column What to enter / what it means Received from Who gave the money. From account The account credited, for example a loan payable or 3000 Owner's Capital. Memo The description. Amount The amount. At the bottom: Field What to enter / what it means Cash back goes to The cash account that receives the cash you keep out of the deposit. It starts at 1005 Petty Cash Fund. Cash back amount The cash kept out of the deposit, if any. Items selected adds up what you ticked and typed, and Deposit total is what reaches the bank: the items less the fees and the cash back. It should equal your deposit slip. Step by step To deposit customer payments: Open Banking > Make Deposits . Check Deposit to and the Date . Type the Deposit slip no. Tick the payments on the slip under Payments waiting to be deposited . Check that Deposit total equals the deposit slip. Click Save deposit , or Save deposit & New to make another one. To deposit POS cash: tick the shifts under POS cash from closed shifts , then save as above. To record a card or e-wallet settlement: Find the clearing account under Card and e-wallet settlements . Type the Gross settled , the Fee deducted and the provider's Reference . Save. The bank receives the gross less the fee. To settle the receipts on the provider's report: Click Details beside the clearing account. Under Receipts not yet settled , tick Settle on each receipt the provider paid. Check the Gross settled at the bottom against the provider's report, and click Done . Type the Fee deducted and the Reference , and save. To see what an unsettled balance is made of: click Details beside it. Compare Receipts not yet settled with the provider's statement to find the sales still to be paid out. Example GCash settles ₱16,113.44 of e-wallet sales and deducts a fee of ₱322.27. Type 16,113.44 in Gross settled and 322.27 in Fee deducted on 1065 E-wallet Clearing; the deposit total is ₱15,791.17. To deposit other money: fill a row of Other receipts with Received from , From account , Memo and Amount , then save. To keep some cash out of the deposit: type the Cash back amount and choose where it goes in Cash back goes to . To find a saved deposit: click Deposits list . The list works like the other transaction lists: From , To , Status ( Posted or Void ), Class and Search , then Filter . The Deposits list To correct a deposit: open it from the list and click Edit (see below). To cancel a whole deposit, click Void , type the reason and confirm: its payments and shifts go back to the waiting lists. Edit a deposit Edit on a saved deposit opens Edit Deposit : the same page as Make Deposits, with what the deposit holds already ticked (and shaded), next to the payments and shifts still waiting. Edit Deposit: the payment and the POS shift on the deposit ticked, with the other payments still waiting Open the deposit (Banking > Make Deposits > Deposits list , then its number) and click Edit . Change what is wrong: - untick a payment or a POS shift to take it off the deposit: it goes back to the waiting list, to be deposited another day; - tick another payment or shift to add it; - change the Deposit to account, the Date , the Deposit slip no. , the Memo or the Class ; - change, add or clear the Other receipts (settlements and fees already on the deposit are listed there too), and the Cash back . Type the Reason for the change and click Save changes . The deposit keeps its number and is posted again with the new lines; the change, with the reason and every figure before and after, is in the audit trail. A POS shift always comes in at its figures as they are now ("was ..." under To deposit shows the amount the deposit held for it before). When the closing entries of a deposited shift are corrected later, the deposit follows on its own (see Correcting the closing entries ). Editing needs the Edit right on Make Deposits; a voided deposit cannot be edited. A deposit dated on or before the closing date, or one cleared in a bank reconciliation, is protected like every other transaction. "A deposit needs at least one line. To cancel the whole deposit, void it instead." "The cash back (...) is more than the items deposited (...)." What it records Account Debit Credit The Deposit to bank account Deposit total The Cash back goes to account Cash back amount 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges Fees deducted 1050 Undeposited Funds Each payment deposited The terminal's cash account (for example 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers) Each POS shift deposited The clearing account (1060 Card Clearing, 1065 E-wallet Clearing) Gross settled The From account of each other receipt Its amount The deposit prints as a DEPOSIT voucher with the account deposited to, the amount in figures and in words, and the ledger entries with their totals. Good to know "Choose the bank account and deposit date." "Select the payments to deposit or enter other receipts." A deposit needs at least one item. "A selected payment was already deposited or changed. Refresh and try again." Someone else deposited it, or it was changed, while you had the page open. "A selected POS shift was already deposited." "Settlement for 1060 - Card Clearing (50,000.00) is more than its unsettled balance on 10/21/2026 (43,556.24)." The settlement is checked against the balance on the deposit date; click Details to see it. "The fee deducted for Card Clearing is more than the gross settled." "Gross settled for Card Clearing (6,984.00) is not the total of the 3 receipt(s) ticked to settle (6,983.00). Open Details to change the ticks, or clear them to type the amount." "POS Sale MK1-00000012 is not unsettled on 10/30/2026 any more. Open Details again and tick the receipts once more." Another deposit settled it while you had the page open. "Enter the gross amount settled for E-wallet Clearing with its fee." A fee was typed without the gross amount. "Other receipts need both an account and an amount." "The items ticked add up to less than zero (-120.00): a journal entry that credits Undeposited Funds deducts from the payments or POS cash it adjusts. Tick them on the same deposit." A payment that is in a deposit cannot be voided or deleted: "It is included in deposit DEP-00001. Remove it from the deposit first." Take it off the deposit with Edit , or void the deposit. Payments that were deposited straight to a bank account on Receive Payments or Enter Sales Receipts do not pass through Undeposited Funds and do not appear here.

href="#pg-bank-transfers" aria-label="Link to this section"> Transfer Funds moves money from one account to another: from the checking account to the petty cash fund, from savings to checking, or a payment of the company credit card from the bank. A transfer does not affect income or expenses. Where to find it: Banking > Transfer Funds opens a new transfer. The Transfers list button shows the saved transfers. The Transfer Funds form Fields Field What to enter / what it means Date The date of the transfer. Reference The bank's reference, if any. Class The class of the transfer. Transfer funds from The account the money leaves: a Bank, Credit Card or Other Current Asset account. Transfer funds to The account the money goes into, from the same kinds of account. Amount The amount transferred. Memo Starts as "Funds transfer". Under the form, Current balances shows the balance of every account you can transfer between. It is shown to users who have the special permission View bank balances outside Banking or may open Use Register . Step by step To transfer funds: Open Banking > Transfer Funds . Check the Date and type the Reference . Choose Transfer funds from and Transfer funds to . Type the Amount and change the Memo if needed. Click Save transfer , or Save transfer & New to make another one. The message says "Transfer recorded. It appears in both registers and does not affect income or expenses." Example TRF-00001 moves ₱10,000.00 from 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking to 1005 Petty Cash Fund with the memo "Replenish petty cash". To change a transfer: open it from Transfers list , click Edit , change it and click Save transfer . To void or delete a transfer: open it, click Void or Delete , type the reason and confirm. The Fund Transfers list What it records Account Debit Credit Transfer funds to account Amount Transfer funds from account Amount The transfer prints as a FUND TRANSFER voucher with From , To , the amount in figures and in words, and the two ledger lines. Good to know "Choose two different accounts." "Enter an amount greater than zero." Other Current Asset accounts such as 1050 Undeposited Funds and the clearing accounts are listed too. Use Make Deposits for payments and settlements, so each payment is marked deposited.

href="#pg-bank-reconcile" aria-label="Link to this section"> Reconciling compares your records of a bank account with the bank statement. You tick the checks, payments and deposits that appear on the statement, add the bank's service charge and interest, and finish when the cleared balance equals the statement's ending balance. Reconcile every bank account every month. Where to find it: Banking > Reconcile, or the Reconcile button on the account's register. Reconciling 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking for the statement of 08/31/2026 Fields Field What to enter / what it means Account The bank account to reconcile. The page reloads when you choose. Statement date The ending date of the bank statement. It starts at the last day of last month. Only transactions dated on or before it are listed. Last reconciled The statement date and ending balance of the last completed reconciliation, or "never". Beginning balance The ending balance of the last completed reconciliation (0.00 the first time). You cannot change it. Ending balance (from statement) The ending balance printed on the bank statement. Service charge The bank's service charge on the statement, if any. Date and Account (service charge) The date of the charge and the expense account. The account starts at 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges. Class (service charge and interest) The class given to the service charge and interest entries. Interest earned The interest the bank paid, if any. Date and Account (interest) The date of the interest and the income account. The account starts at 4200 Interest Income. Below are two lists of the uncleared transactions: Checks and payments (money out) and Deposits and other credits (money in), each with a Mark all box. Each line shows the ✓ box, Date , No. with the transaction type, Payee and Amount . At the bottom, Cleared balance is the beginning balance plus the ticked lines, less the service charge, plus the interest. Ending balance repeats the statement's figure and Difference is what is still unexplained: red until it reaches 0.00, then green. Reconciling the same account for the statement of 09/30/2026, with September's deposits listed Step by step To reconcile a bank account: Open Banking > Reconcile . Choose the Account . Set the Statement date to the date of the bank statement. Type the Ending balance (from statement) . Type the Service charge and the Interest earned shown on the statement, if any, and check their dates and accounts. Tick each check and payment that appears on the statement. Tick each deposit and credit that appears on the statement. Watch Difference . When it is 0.00, click Reconcile now . The message "Reconciliation complete." appears. To stop and finish later: click Save for later . The ending balance, the ticks, and the service charge and interest with their dates, accounts and class are kept, and the message shows the difference. Nothing is posted yet. When you open Reconcile again for the account, they all come back. To see the result: in Reconciliation history , click Summary or Detail on the line of the statement. To undo the last reconciliation: In Reconciliation history , type the Reason . Click Undo last and confirm "Undo the last reconciliation?". The message "The last reconciliation was undone. Its items are uncleared, its service charge and interest entries are voided, and it is open for editing." appears. The reconciliation opens with its ending balance, ticks, service charge and interest as they were. Correct what is wrong and click Reconcile now : the service charge and interest are posted again, once. If a service charge or interest entry falls in a closed period and you may not change such entries, nothing is undone and the message says why. Buttons Discrepancy report: opens the Reconciliation Discrepancy report for this account. Save for later: keeps your work without finishing. Reconcile now: finishes the reconciliation. It is enabled only when the difference is 0.00. Undo last: reopens the most recent completed reconciliation. Needs the delete permission on this page. Reconciliation history The last twelve reconciliations of the account, with Statement date , Beginning , Ending , Status ( Completed or In Progress ), By and Reports ( Summary and Detail ). What it records When you click Reconcile now : Entry Debit Credit Service Charge (when a service charge is typed) The service charge account (6080 Bank and Merchant Charges) The bank account Interest Earned (when interest is typed) The bank account The interest account (4200 Interest Income) Both entries are dated on the dates you gave, numbered in the journal series (JE-) and marked cleared straight away. Every ticked transaction is marked cleared on this account: it shows a ✓ in the register and cleared in its ledger entries, and it no longer appears on the next reconciliation. Good to know "The difference must be zero to finish. Current difference: 1,500.00." Look for a deposit or check on the statement that you have not ticked, an amount typed differently from the bank, or a transaction not yet entered in the books. "An item changed while you were reconciling. Refresh and try again." Someone changed or deleted a listed transaction while you had the page open. "Enter the statement date." The first reconciliation of an account starts from 0.00, so every transaction up to the statement date is listed, including the opening balance entry. Tick the opening balance too. Save for later keeps the service charge and interest but posts nothing: they are posted only when you click Reconcile now . Undo last voids the service charge and interest entries the reconciliation made (the voided entries stay in the books with the reason, for the audit trail) and keeps their figures on the reopened reconciliation, so finishing it again posts them once. Once cleared, a transaction can only be changed or voided by a user with the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled . If its amount on the bank account changes, or it is voided or deleted, the cleared mark is removed and the change is listed on the Reconciliation Discrepancy report. The program asks No class selected only when a service charge or interest is typed and Class (service charge and interest) is empty. Reconciling is best done by someone who does not also receive customer payments.

href="#s-banking-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Banking reports are listed under Banking > Reports in the sidebar and in the Banking card of the Report Center . The common report tools ( Refresh , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize and clicking a number to open the transaction) are explained in Working with reports .

href="#pg-rpt-recon_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> A one-page summary of a completed reconciliation: what was cleared, what was still outstanding, and how the register balance compares with the statement. Print it and file it with the bank statement. Where to find it: Banking > Reports > Reconciliation Summary, or Summary in the reconciliation history on Reconcile . The Reconciliation Summary of the statement of 07/31/2026 Filter: Reconciliation lists every reconciliation as account, statement date and status. Leave it at All to see the most recent completed reconciliation. How to read it: the heading of the table names the account and the statement date. The lines are: Beginning balance. Cleared transactions: Checks and payments and Deposits and credits , with the number of items and their total (payments as negative figures), then Total cleared transactions and Cleared balance . Uncleared transactions (as of reconciliation): Outstanding checks and payments and Deposits in transit . Register balance as of the statement date: the balance in the books on that date. Statement ending balance. The note above gives the status, when and by whom it was completed, and a Detail link. Tip The register balance equals the statement ending balance plus the deposits in transit, less the outstanding checks. If it does not, a transaction dated on or before the statement date was entered or changed after the reconciliation.

href="#pg-rpt-recon_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists every transaction of a reconciliation, cleared and uncleared. Where to find it: Banking > Reports > Reconciliation Detail, or Detail in the reconciliation history. The Reconciliation Detail of the statement of 07/31/2026 Filter: Reconciliation , as on the summary. The columns: Type , Date , Num (click it to open the transaction), Name and Amount , in four groups: Cleared checks and payments , Cleared deposits and credits , Uncleared checks and payments and Uncleared deposits and credits , each with a Total . The note gives the account, statement date and ending balance. A transaction deleted since the reconciliation shows the type "(deleted)".

href="#pg-rpt-recon_discrepancy" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the cleared transactions that were changed, voided or deleted after they were reconciled. A clean report means the reconciled balances still stand. Where to find it: Banking > Reports > Reconciliation Discrepancy, or the Discrepancy report button on Reconcile . The Reconciliation Discrepancy report with no changes Filter: Account (a bank account, or blank for all). The columns: Column What it shows Changed When the change was made. Account and Reconciled statement The bank account and the statement date of the reconciliation that cleared it. Transaction The transaction, for example "Check 1004". Click it to open it. Change amount changed , voided or deleted . Cleared amount / New amount The amount on the account when it was cleared, and now. Effect New amount less cleared amount. Changed by The user who made the change. How to use it: check it before each reconciliation. Every line means the last reconciled balance no longer matches the books; ask the user who made the change why, and correct the entry or reconcile the difference.

href="#pg-rpt-check_register" aria-label="Link to this section"> Lists the checks, bill payments and customer refunds in check number order for each account, and highlights missing and duplicate numbers. Use it to account for every check in the checkbook. Where to find it: Banking > Reports > Check Register The Check Register for September 2026, with a gap in the numbers highlighted Filters: Dates (starts at This month ), From , To and Account (a bank account, or blank for all). The report can also be narrowed by Vendor and Class (see Filters on related records ). The columns: Column What it shows Check no. The number. Click it to open the check. Date, Account, Type The date, the account code, and Check, Bill Payment or Customer Refund. Payee and Memo The payee and the memo. Amount The amount. Status VOID , to print , printed , or blank. Exceptions duplicate number , or missing followed by the numbers skipped, for example "missing 1007–1009". How to read it: lines with an exception are highlighted. A voided check still holds its number, so it is not a gap. A number used on a date outside the range also shows as missing: in the picture, checks 1007 to 1009 were written in August, so widen the dates to the whole year before you look for a lost check. Note Checks made out to an employee or other name show a blank Payee on this report. Open the check to see the name.

href="#s-the-taxes-at-a-glance" aria-label="Link to this section"> Tax Who handles it Usual rate Where it goes Output VAT The VAT-registered seller 12% of the VAT-exclusive taxable sale BIR 2550Q: output VAT Input VAT The eligible VAT-registered buyer Normally 12% of the eligible VAT-exclusive purchase BIR 2550Q: allowable input VAT VAT withheld A qualifying government buyer / withholding agent Generally 5% of the VAT-exclusive payment Buyer: 1600-VT. Seller: a VAT credit on 2550Q (Item 16) Creditable withholding on goods Government buyers and BIR-notified top withholding agents Generally 1% of the income payment Buyer: 0619-E / 1601-EQ. Seller: an income-tax credit Creditable withholding on services Government buyers and BIR-notified top withholding agents Generally 2% of the income payment Buyer: 0619-E / 1601-EQ. Seller: an income-tax credit Important The 5% VAT withholding is not the VAT rate, and it is worked out on the amount net of VAT , never on the VAT itself. For a ₱112,000.00 invoice (₱100,000.00 plus ₱12,000.00 VAT) the 5% is ₱5,000.00 and the 1% ₱1,000.00; the supplier receives ₱106,000.00. The 1% / 2% are income tax, not VAT: they never reduce the VAT due and are never posted as input VAT. Who must withhold: government payors and the top withholding agents notified by the BIR withhold 1% on goods and 2% on services bought from their regular suppliers (RR 11-2018); government buyers also withhold 5% VAT on their qualifying VATable purchases. An ordinary private purchaser generally withholds neither. Check the thresholds (single purchases of ₱10,000.00 or less), the supplier's status and exemptions, and the special rates (0.5% under RR 24-2025, the rules of RR 9-2025 for registered business enterprises) before you withhold.

href="#s-the-accounts-used" aria-label="Link to this section"> Account (demo) Used for 2110 Withholding Tax Payable The 1% / 2% withheld from suppliers, until remitted with 0619-E and 1601-EQ 2115 VAT Withheld Payable The 5% VAT withheld from suppliers, until remitted with 1600-VT 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax The 1% / 2% customers withheld: a credit against the company's income tax 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld The 5% VAT government customers withheld: a credit on the 2550Q (Item 16) 2100 Output Tax, 1300 Input Tax The 12% VAT on sales and purchases, as before They are set in Module Default Accounts (Withholding Tax Payable (Expanded), VAT Withheld Payable, Creditable Withholding Tax, Creditable VAT Withheld). A tax of the Withholding Tax Table can have accounts of its own instead.

href="#pg-bir-wht_table" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Withholding Tax Table is the guide to how much is deducted: every tax that can be withheld from a payment, with its rate and the base it is worked out on. It is flexible: taxes can be added, changed, made inactive or deleted at any time. The same page says whether the company is a withholding agent and holds the payor details printed on BIR Form 2307. Where to find it: BIR Reports > Withholding Tax Table. Viewing it needs access to the page; adding, changing and deleting need the create, edit and delete permissions (by default the Administrator and the Accountant). The Withholding Tax Table with the company as withholding agent The withholding agent card Field What it means This company is a withholding agent On: the company deducts withholding taxes when it pays its suppliers. Pay Bills shows the Withholding column and BIR Form 2307 is printed for the suppliers. Off: Pay Bills has no Withholding column (a payment that already withheld taxes keeps them when it is edited). On as delivered. Payor on BIR Form 2307 The company name, TIN and address of System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date, printed in Part II of the form Payor zip code Printed in Item 8A of the form Authorized signatory , Title / designation , Signatory TIN Printed over the signature line of the payor on the form Click Save to keep them; the change goes to the audit trail. The table Column What it shows Type The name of the tax, its code and when it applies ATC The BIR alphanumeric tax code printed on Form 2307 (for example WC158) Rate The percentage withheld Kind Income tax withheld (the expanded withholding tax, 1% / 2%) or VAT withheld (the business tax, 5%). The kinds are kept apart in every report and on the form. Worked out on Amount net of VAT (as the BIR asks for these rates) or Gross amount (VAT included) Used on Payments to suppliers , Payments from customers or Both Accounts Where it posts: what is withheld from suppliers, and what customers withhold Used How many payment lines it was withheld on, and how many suppliers have it as a usual tax Status Active , or Inactive (no longer offered on new payments) As delivered, the table holds: Type (code) ATC Rate Kind WT on Goods (WT-GOODS) WC158 1% Income tax withheld WT on Services (WT-SERVICES) WC160 2% Income tax withheld WT on VAT (WT-VAT) WV010 5% VAT withheld All three are worked out on the amount net of VAT and used on both sides. Check the ATCs against the BIR's current list for your company (corporations and individuals have different codes). Step by step: add a tax Click Add a withholding tax . Type the Name , a short Code of your own (unique), the BIR ATC and the Rate (%) (0.5 for 0.5%). Choose the Kind of tax , what it is Worked out on and where it is Used on . Leave the two account boxes on their default, or choose an account of its own. Type When it applies , the Order on the list , and click Save . A new withholding tax Fields Field What to enter / what it means Name For example WT on Goods. Shown in Pay Bills, Receive Payments, the reports and on Form 2307 Code Your own short code, unique (WT-GOODS) BIR ATC The alphanumeric tax code (WC158, WC160, WV010 ...) Rate (%) Above 0 and up to 100 Kind of tax Income tax withheld (expanded) or Business tax withheld (VAT) Worked out on Amount net of VAT or Gross amount (VAT included) Used on Payments to suppliers , Payments from customers or Both Account for what is withheld from suppliers A liability account; blank = the default (Withholding Tax Payable, or VAT Withheld Payable for VAT) Account for what customers withhold An asset account; blank = the default (Creditable Withholding Tax, or Creditable VAT Withheld for VAT) When it applies A note shown on the table Order on the list Smaller numbers first Active Untick to stop offering it on new payments Reason for the change On an edit; kept in the audit trail Changing, deactivating and deleting Edit changes a tax. Payments already saved keep the rate and amount they were saved with; the new rate applies to payments from then on. Untick Active to stop offering a tax. A payment that used it still shows it. The bin button deletes a tax that has never been withheld on a payment (it is also taken off the suppliers and customers that had it as a usual tax). A tax already used stays on the table: "... has been used on ... payment line(s), so it stays on the table. Make it inactive instead." Messages: "Enter the code and the name of the withholding tax.", "The rate is a percentage above 0 and up to 100 (1 for 1%).", "Another withholding tax already has the code ...". How the table is used Vendor Center: each supplier's usual taxes ( Withholding taxes on the vendor form), one, two or more. Pay Bills: the Withholding column opens this table for each bill; tick one or more taxes (for example 1% and 5%). Each amount is worked out at once from the outstanding balance net of VAT and can be typed over. See The Withholding column . Receive Payments: the taxes a customer withheld are ticked the same way. Each payment keeps its taxes by bill (or invoice) and type, with the base, rate and ATC. BIR Form 2307 and the reports below are made from them.
