An asset with accumulated depreciation needs opening_through . Invoices, sales receipts and sales orders: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one document. Yes date Date. All lines of a document must carry the same date. Yes customer Customer, or Customer:Job. Yes terms Payment terms. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , rate Quantity and price per unit. Yes discount_pct Discount %. tax_code , site , class Tax code, inventory site and class of the line. memo Memo (header). deposit_to Sales receipts only: the bank or cash account. Blank = 1050 Undeposited Funds. Each invoice goes to 1100 Accounts Receivable with a due date from the terms. Each document posts exactly as one entered on Create Invoices or Enter Sales Receipts would. Sales orders are saved as open orders and do not post until invoiced (see Create Sales Orders ). The doc_no is kept as the document's reference number; the program gives the document its own next number. Purchase orders and receive items and enter bills: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one document. Yes date Date. Yes vendor Supplier. Yes ref_no Bills: the supplier's invoice number. Purchase orders: a reference number. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , rate Quantity and cost per unit. Yes tax_code , site , class Tax code, inventory site and class. memo Memo (header). Each Receive items and enter bills document becomes a bill with the vendor's terms: the items come into stock and 2000 Accounts Payable is credited, as on Receive Items and Enter Bills . A bill is refused as a duplicate when the supplier's invoice number (or the doc_no , if ref_no is blank) is already on a bill. Purchase orders are saved as open orders and do not post (see Create Purchase Orders ). Write checks: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Your own reference. Lines with the same one make one check. Yes date Date. Yes bank_account Bank account, code or name (1010). Yes payee A supplier's name, or any name. Yes check_no Check number. A check number already used on a check is refused. account Account charged, code or name (6020). Yes description Description of the line. amount Amount. Yes tax_code , class Tax code and class. memo Memo. Each check credits the bank account and debits the accounts charged, as on Write Checks . When the payee matches a supplier's name, the check is linked to that supplier. A check without a check_no cannot be recognised as a duplicate, so never import the same checks file twice. Cash vouchers: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Lines with the same one make one voucher. Yes date Date. Yes cash_account Cash account paid from, code or name (1005 Petty Cash Fund). Yes paid_to Employee, customer, supplier or any name. Yes account Account of the line, code or name. Yes debit , credit Amount of the line on one side. memo Memo of the line. class Class. particulars Particulars (header). ref_no Reference number. The cash account is credited with the debits less the credits, which must be more than zero. See Cash Voucher . Journal entries: the columns Column What goes in it Needed doc_no Lines with the same one make one entry. Yes date Date. Yes account Account, code or name. Yes debit , credit Amount of the line on one side. description Memo of the line. name Customer, supplier, employee or other name on the line. class Class. memo , ref_no Memo and reference number of the entry. The debits and the credits of each entry must be equal. See Make Journal Entries . POS transactions: the columns Column What goes in it Needed receipt_no Receipt number. Lines with the same one make one sale. Yes date Date. Yes terminal POS terminal, code or name (POS-01). Yes customer Customer. Blank = walk-in. item Item code, display name or barcode. Yes description Description. qty , price Quantity and price per unit. Yes discount_pct Discount %. tax_code Tax code. payment_method Cash, GCash, P.O. Card and so on. Blank = Cash. class Class. Each receipt becomes a completed POS sale at the terminal's site, paid in full with the payment method given. If the terminal has no open shift, one is opened for it. See Point of Sale . Good to know Checking and importing need Create on this page. Downloading a template needs Print/Export . Transactions are saved as if entered by hand, so the closing date applies. A transaction dated on or before it is refused unless you may change closed periods; such a problem is found while writing and shown at the top of the page, and nothing is written. Messages about the file itself: "Choose a CSV file (.csv). In Excel: File > Save As > CSV (Comma delimited).", "The file is empty.", "The file holds no data lines." and "The first line of the file must hold the column names. Download the template for "Inventory items" to see them." Typical line messages: "Line 5: "Net 45" is not in the terms list (column "terms").", "Line 7: the code LAP-001 is already on line 3 of the file.", "Document INV-IMP-001 is already in the books as INV-00012. Take it out of the file, or change its document number." and "Document JE-IMP-001: the debits (25,000.00) and the credits (24,000.00) are not equal."

href="#pg-admin-backup" aria-label="Link to this section"> A backup is one .sql file that holds every table and every row of the company's database. Make one before every month-end close, before a large price change, before every import and before a rebuild, and keep copies off the server. Restoring replaces what is in the database now with what is in the file. Where to find it: System Administration > Backup & Restore. The Backup & Restore button on Import from CSV also opens it. Backup & Restore with no backup made yet Make a backup The box shows the Database (in the demo, gsmart; for a company added later on a multi-company platform, the company's name), the number of Tables , the Size on disk and the Backups kept here . Field What to choose What is this backup for? (optional) A note, such as "Before the month-end close". It is kept in the backup history and the audit trail. What to save Everything: structure and data for a real backup, or Structure only (no rows) for empty tables. Backups to keep on the server Keep them all , The newest 5 , The newest 10 (the standard) or The newest 20 . After the backup, older files beyond this number are deleted from the server. Compress the file (.sql.gz, much smaller) Ticked: the file is compressed. Shown only when the server can compress. Type what the backup is for. Leave What to save on Everything: structure and data . Choose how many backups to keep. Click Make the backup now and leave the page open until it finishes. After a backup: the message with the file name and size, the file in Backups on the server, and a line in Backup history The message says "Backup written:" with the file name and size, and how many older backups were removed. The file is named after the database and the date and time, for example gsmart_20260927_141929.sql.gz . A structure-only backup ends in _structure . Backups on the server The table lists the files in the backups folder (shown beside the heading, for example storage/backups), newest first, with File , Made and Size . Download saves a copy to your computer. Do this at least weekly and keep the copy somewhere other than the server. The trash button deletes a file. In the box that opens, type the Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) and click Delete this backup . Files whose name starts with before_restore_ are the automatic backups made before a restore. Files marked uploaded came from From a file on my computer . Backup history lists the last 20 backups, restores and deletions: When , What ( Backup , Restore or Deleted ), File , Tables , Rows , By and Note . Restore from a backup Important A restore replaces every table of the database with what the file holds. Anything entered since that backup was made is lost. Ask everyone else to log out first. Open the tab From a backup kept here (or From a file on my computer to upload a .sql or .sql.gz file). Choose the Backup to restore (or choose the file). Type the Reason (recorded in the audit trail) . Type RESTORE in Type RESTORE to confirm . Click Restore (or Upload and restore ) and confirm. The message says how many statements were run. If some could not be run, a card Statements that could not be run lists them; check them before working in the books again. The upload tab tells you the largest file this server accepts. Copy a larger file into the backups folder instead and restore it from From a backup kept here . The safeguards Before it changes anything, the restore makes a fresh backup of what is there now ( before_restore_... ), so a restore can itself be undone by restoring that file. You must type RESTORE; otherwise "Type RESTORE in the box to confirm. Nothing has been changed." Only an administrator can restore (a user with the Administrator role, the Company Owner or the Super Admin), and only with Edit on this page. Others see "Only an administrator can restore the database." After the restore, the audit trail's protection is put back in place. With several companies, the list of users on the platform is brought in line with the restored users; a username that belongs to another company is reported, and that user cannot log in until the username is changed. If more than 25 statements fail, the restore stops. What is refused A file that does not end in .sql or .sql.gz ("A backup file ends in .sql or .sql.gz."). A single statement larger than 32 MB. Restore such a file with phpMyAdmin or Navicat. With several companies, only statements that rebuild the company's own tables are run (such as CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, INSERT INTO and SET). A statement that changes server settings or passwords, creates something other than a table, reads other data or names another database is listed as "not run". Good to know Making a backup needs Create , downloading needs Print/Export , and deleting needs Delete/Void on this page. The program does not make backups on a schedule. Make them yourself at the times listed above. A restore also brings back the audit trail and the backup history as they were in the file. Entries made after that backup remain in the automatic before_restore_ file. Backups to keep on the server also counts the before_restore_ and uploaded files, so a low number may remove them. Download any file you want to keep. A backup made here can be read back with phpMyAdmin (Import) or Navicat (Execute SQL File), and a file those programs wrote can be restored here. Compressed files are read back here directly. The backup file holds the tables and rows but not the two triggers that protect the audit trail. A restore on this page puts them back by itself. If you read a backup back with phpMyAdmin or Navicat instead, also run the program's database/triggers.sql file the same way, so the audit trail is protected again. If the backups folder cannot be written to, the page says so and Make the backup now is greyed out. Ask whoever manages the server to give the web server write permission on the storage folder. Backups, restores, downloads and deletions are all recorded in the audit trail.

href="#pg-admin-multi_company" aria-label="Link to this section"> This one-time step turns a single-company installation into a platform that can hold several companies, each in a database of its own. The present company is kept exactly as it is and becomes Company 1 . The step creates the platform (master) database, the first Super Admin account that manages every company, and the Company Code that new employees of Company 1 use to join. Where to find it: System Administration > Multi-Company Setup. The menu entry disappears once multi-company is running. The Multi-Company Setup form, with the company details filled in from the settings and the Super Admin account to create Fields Field What to enter Company name Required. Filled in from Company, Security & Closing Date. TIN , Phone , Address , E-mail Filled in from the settings; correct them if needed. Contact person Optional. Company Owner An active user of this company who will manage its employees, join requests and Company Code. Administrators are listed first. Employees who join with the Company Code wait for the Company Owner's approval Ticked by default. Clear it to let new employees in without approval. Username (Super Admin) 3 to 50 characters, different from every username of this company. Filled with superadmin. Full name (Super Admin) Filled with Platform Administrator. E-mail (Super Admin) Optional. Password and Password again At least 10 characters (or the company's minimum, if longer) with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol. A backup of this database was made (System Administration > Backup & Restore) Tick after you have made the backup. The What happens box lists the five things the step does: the platform database is created on the same MySQL server with the same user as config/config.php ; this database is registered as Company 1 without any record being moved, changed or deleted, and nobody's password changes; every user of the company is listed in the platform database so the log-in page knows where they belong; Company 1 gets its Company Code and owner; and the Super Admin account is created. Step by step: set up several companies Make a backup on Backup & Restore and download it. Read Before you start . The storage folder must be writable, and the MySQL user needs the right to create databases, tables, triggers and foreign keys. On shared hosting, create the platform database in the control panel first. Check the Company 1 details and choose the Company Owner . Fill in the Super Admin's username, full name and password twice. Tick the backup box. Click Set up and confirm. Multi-company set up: Company 1 got the Company Code STC-B8TJC, the Super Admin superadmin was created and 9 users were registered The result shows the Company Code (for example STC-B8TJC), the Super Admin username and the number of Company users registered . Everyone keeps logging in with the same username and password. From then on this page only says that multi-company is running, and names the company and its number. Good to know Only an administrator can run the setup, even if the page is allowed to other roles. Set up is greyed out when the storage folder cannot be written to. Messages you may see: "Tick the box to confirm that a backup of the database was made.", "The two Super Admin passwords do not match.", "The Super Admin needs a username of its own: admin is already a user of this company.", "Choose an active user of this company as its Company Owner." and "The master database gsmart_master already belongs to other companies." A company added later gets its own copy of this company's set-up (chart of accounts, tax codes, terms, roles and the other lists), never its customers, suppliers, items, users or transactions. Companies are created, switched on and off and given owners by the Super Admin; see Super Admin . The Company Code and the employees are managed under Company > Company Profile & Code ; see Company Owner .

href="#s-audit-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The audit trail is a permanent log of every action that creates, changes or removes information, and of every log-in, failed log-in and denied page. The audit reports read it in different ways. What is recorded. Each entry holds the date and time, the user and their roles at the time, the computer's IP address and browser, the POS terminal and site where there is one, the module and page, the action, the record (with its number), the amount, the fields that changed (before and after), a full copy of the record where useful, the reason typed and the supervisor who approved. Among the actions recorded are: create, edit, delete and void of every transaction; print, reprint, export and e-mail of documents and reports; log-in, log-out, session timeout, failed log-ins, account locks and unlocks, password changes and resets; denied pages and failed supervisor approvals; changes to users, roles, page access, overrides, settings and the closing date; segregation of duties and credit limit overrides; imports, backups, restores and data rebuilds; POS shifts, cash drops and readings; bank reconciliations; memorized transactions entered automatically. It cannot be changed. Nobody, not even an administrator, can edit or delete an audit entry. Two database triggers refuse any change or deletion, even when someone works on the database directly with another program. The audit trail cannot be switched off. The only way older entries are replaced is by restoring a backup, which brings back the audit trail as it was in the backup file. The last five reports below (Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary and Detail, User Activity, Login History, and User Access and Permission Changes) use the common report tools (dates, Refresh , Columns , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize and drill-down), explained in Working with reports .

href="#pg-admin-audit_trail" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Audit Trail lists every entry, newest first, and lets you filter them by date, user, module, page, action, record type and text. Use it to answer "who changed this, when, and what was it before?" Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Audit Trail, or Home > Report Center. The Audit Trail for the last seven days: 125 entries, most of them prints by admin The filters Filter What it does From and To The dates of the entries. The page opens from seven days ago to today. User One user's entries. Module One module, or Security for log-ins, lock-outs and denied pages. Page One page of the program. Action One kind of action, such as Void, Delete, Login Failed or Settings Change. Record type One kind of record, such as transaction, user, role or item. Record / text Words found in the record's name or number, the reason, the changes or the username. Click Filter to apply them. The number of entries found is shown above the table. The table shows 100 entries per page, with page numbers underneath. The columns Column What it shows Date / time When it happened, to the second. User Username, with the user's roles underneath. Where IP address, and the POS terminal and site when there is one. Module / page The module, with the page underneath. Action What was done: Create, Edit, Print, Void, Login and so on. Record The record. A transaction is a link to it (or marked deleted ); the clock icon opens its Transaction History ; [copy] opens the full copy saved with the entry. Amount The amount, when the action has one. Changes (before → after) Up to eight changed fields with old and new values, then "+N more". Reason / approval The reason typed and, if a supervisor approved, "Approved by" with their username. Rows for deletions, voids, failed log-ins, locked accounts, denied pages, failed approvals, segregation of duties overrides and credit limit overrides are highlighted. The terminal under Where is the POS counter the user last opened in the POS Register during that log-in session. It therefore also appears on entries the user made on other pages afterwards, as on the Banking prints in the screenshot. Export downloads the filtered entries (up to 50,000) as a CSV file for a spreadsheet; it needs Print/Export and is itself recorded in the audit trail. Print prints the page. Tip To see everything one clerk did yesterday, set From and To to yesterday, choose the clerk in User and click Filter . To find every change to one invoice, type its number in Record / text .

href="#pg-admin-txn_history" aria-label="Link to this section"> Transaction History shows every recorded version of one transaction, oldest first: who created it, each edit with the fields that changed, prints, voids and deletions, with the reasons and approvals. It works even for a transaction that was deleted, because the audit trail kept a copy. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Transaction History. You can also click History on a transaction form, the clock icon beside a transaction in the Audit Trail, or a number in the Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary . Transaction History before a document is looked up Type the document number, for example INV-00012, in the box. Click Find . The program opens the history of the latest transaction whose name contains what you typed, so type the whole number. The history of Invoice INV-00001, now Partial: one version, created by admin The heading shows the transaction and its present status (such as Partial , Paid or Void ), or deleted . Open current version at the top opens the transaction itself. Each entry is a card with: the action and, for saves, the version number ("Create, version 1"), the user and their roles, the date and time and the IP address; the Reason and Approved by , when there are any; a Field / Before / After table of what changed; Content after this action (or Content before this action for a void or delete), which opens the full header and lines as they were. A card for a void or a deletion has a red border. Good to know Someone who may not open the transaction's own page, and may not open the Audit Trail either, is refused the history of that transaction.

href="#pg-rpt-voided_deleted_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> This report lists every transaction voided or deleted in the period, with who did it, why and who approved. Voids and deletions are a common way to hide errors or theft, so review them regularly. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary, or Home > Report Center. Voided and Deleted Transactions Summary for September 2026: a voided check, a deleted estimate and a voided POS sale The filters are Dates (the date of the void or deletion; the report opens on This month ), User and Module . Column What it shows Voided / deleted When the transaction was voided or deleted. Action Voided or Deleted . Type and Num The kind of transaction and its number. Click the number for its Transaction History . Txn date The transaction's own date. Name The customer, vendor or payee. Original amount The transaction's total before it was voided or deleted. User Who voided or deleted it. Reason The reason typed. Approved by The supervisor who approved, if any. The last line gives the number of transactions and the total of the original amounts. Example In September 2026 the demo shows check 1010 to Office Snacks Co. (₱2,500.00) voided because it was "printed with wrong payee", estimate EST-00002 for Cebu Tech Hub deleted as a "Duplicate of an existing quotation", and POS sale POS-000004 (₱10,068.80) voided by the supervisor.

href="#pg-rpt-voided_deleted_detail" aria-label="Link to this section"> The same transactions as the summary, with the full content of each as it was just before it was voided or deleted: its date, name, memo and total, every line, and the documents it had been applied to. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Voided and Deleted Transactions Detail, or Home > Report Center. Voided and Deleted Transactions Detail: each voided or deleted transaction with its lines The filters are the same as the summary: Dates , User and Module . Each transaction starts with a shaded line that gives VOIDED or DELETED, the type and number, when and by whom, the approver if any, and the reason (for example VOIDED Check 1010 by admin, reason: Check printed with wrong payee). It is followed by a line with the date, name, memo and total, then its lines with Transaction / item (item code or account), Description , Qty , Rate and Amount . "Was applied to" lines show payments or credits it had been applied to. The rows cannot be sorted.

href="#pg-rpt-user_activity" aria-label="Link to this section"> User Activity counts what each user did in the period, by module and action, and flags work done outside business hours. Use it to spot unusual activity, such as voids late at night or a clerk working in a module outside their job. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > User Activity, or Home > Report Center. The Activity button on a user's page opens it for that user. User Activity for the week: admin's three log-ins and actions by module, all highlighted because 27 September 2026 is a Sunday The filters are Dates (the report opens on This week ), User and Module . Column What it shows User / module A shaded line per user with the number of log-ins in the period, then one line per module. Action The action, such as Create, Print, Void or Closing Date Change. Count How many times. Click it to open the Audit Trail filtered to those entries. First and Last The first and last time in the period. Outside business hours How many of them happened outside business hours. Business hours are taken as 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday. Lines with activity outside these hours are highlighted. A Total line closes each user.

href="#pg-rpt-login_history" aria-label="Link to this section"> Login History lists log-ins, log-outs, timeouts, failed log-ins, locked and unlocked accounts, password resets and denied pages. Check it for repeated failed log-ins, which can mean someone is guessing a password. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > Login History, or Home > Report Center. Login History for the week: three log-ins by admin, two failed log-ins by apclerk and one denied page for cashier1 The filters are Dates (the report opens on This week ) and User . The user filter finds both what the user did and what was done to their account, such as an unlock. Column What it shows Date / time When it happened, newest first. User The username. Event Login, Logout, Session Timeout, Login Failed, Account Locked, Account Unlocked, Password Change, Password Reset, Access Denied, Approval Failed and so on. Detail The reason, such as "Wrong password (attempt 2 of 5)", or the page and action for a denied page, such as "User Role Configuration (open)". IP address The computer's address. Workstation The browser and system used. The note above the table counts the failed log-ins and denied page access attempts in the period. Failed log-ins, locks, denied pages and failed approvals are highlighted. The report shows up to 5,000 events.

href="#pg-rpt-user_access" aria-label="Link to this section"> This report is made for periodic access reviews. The first part shows each user's current access; the second lists every change to users, roles, page access and security settings in the period. Where to find it: System Administration > Reports > User Access and Permission Changes, or Home > Report Center. User Access and Permission Changes for September 2026: each user's pages allowed and overrides, then the overrides and the closing date change made in the month The only filter is Dates (the report opens on This month ); it applies to the second part. Current access by user has one line per user: Column What it shows User / when Full name and username. Status / change active, inactive or locked. Roles / record The user's roles. Pages allowed / details Pages the user may open out of all pages (for example 31 / 168). Click it for Effective Access . Overrides Number of page overrides. Last login / reason Last successful log-in. Active users who have not logged in for 90 days are highlighted: confirm that departing employees were deactivated. A user who has never logged in is not highlighted, so look at blank Last login / reason cells as well. Changes to users, roles and page access lists, in order, each user created or edited, deactivated or activated, role created, edited or deleted, page access change and override, segregation of duties override, password reset, account lock and unlock, settings change and closing date change. Each line shows when and by whom, the change, the record, the details (old → new, up to six fields) and the reason. Tip Run this report every quarter, print it, and have the owner or the auditor sign it after checking that each person's access still fits their job.

href="#s-how-several-companies-work" aria-label="Link to this section"> A few facts explain almost everything on the Company pages: Each company has its own database. A database is the store where the program keeps its records. Every company on the platform has a separate one: its customers, suppliers, items, transactions, reports, users, audit trail, logo, uploaded receipts and backups are in it and nowhere else. When you log in, the program opens your company's database and no other. Nobody can see another company's records. There is no report, link, setting or search that reaches into another company. A Company Owner cannot even see another company's user list. Your company is decided on the server when you log in, from your username; nothing typed in the address bar, a form or a cookie can change it. Everybody logs in on the same page. There is no company to choose. You type your own username and password; the log-in page looks the username up, finds the company it belongs to, and checks the password, the lock-out and the approval in that company. Usernames are unique across all companies. Because the log-in page finds your company by your username, no two people on the platform can have the same one, whatever company they are in, and no company user can have a Super Admin's username. A username can therefore be refused as "already taken" even though nobody in your own company uses it: choose another. The Company Code is only for joining. Each company has a code, for example STC-B8TJC . A new employee types it once, on the join page, to say which company they belong to. It is not a password: it logs nobody in and opens nothing. After joining, the employee always logs in with their own username and password. A company can be switched off. The Super Admin can make a company inactive. Its users are logged out at their next click with the message "Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner.", nobody can log in or join, and everything in the company (database, users, records) is kept until it is switched on again. The checks are repeated on every click. Each time you open a page, the program checks again that your company is still active and that your account still belongs to it.

href="#s-who-is-who" aria-label="Link to this section"> Person What they do Super Admin Belongs to no company. Creates companies, gives each one its Company Owner, switches companies on and off, and can open any company to work inside it. Company Owner One per company. Has full access to every page of the company, approves the employees who join, manages the users and the Company Code. Administrators Users with a full-access role such as Administrator . They can use the Company pages but cannot change the Company Code, the joining rules or the owner's account. Employees Everyone else. They see the pages their roles and page access allow.

t: What makes the Company Owner different
x: href="#s-what-makes-the-company-owner-different" aria-label="Link to this section"> Full authority. The owner can always open every page of the company and do everything on it, whatever the roles, Page Access Configuration and user overrides say. Nothing can lock the owner out of their own company. Effective Access (View as User) gives Company Owner as the reason. A protected account. Only the owner (or the Super Admin) can change the owner's account. On Employees & Users the owner's row shows Company Owner instead of a Manage button to everybody else, and on User Accounts an administrator who tries gets "Only the Company Owner can change the Company Owner's account." Cannot be deactivated. "The Company Owner cannot be deactivated. The Super Admin can make someone else the owner first." Chosen by the Super Admin. The owner of a new company is set when the Super Admin creates it (or later on the company's page); the owner of Company 1 is chosen on Multi-Company Setup . To hand the company over to someone else, ask the Super Admin. Shown in the user menu. Click your name at the top right: the first line reads Company Owner followed by your roles, for example Company Owner, Administrator .

href="#s-the-company-owners-first-log-in" aria-label="Link to this section"> When the Super Admin creates a new company with its owner's account, they give the owner a username and a temporary password , a password that must be replaced at the first log-in. In the examples of this chapter the company is ABC Distribution Corp. and its owner is John Doe , username johndoe . Step by step Open the log-in page of the program. Type your username (for example johndoe ) in Username and the temporary password in Password . Click Log in . The Change password page opens with the message "Please replace your temporary password before continuing." You cannot open any other page until the password is changed. In Current password , type the temporary password. In New password , type the password you will use from now on. The line under the boxes gives your company's password rules. Type the new password again in Confirm new password . Click Change password . The message "Your password has been changed." appears and the Home page opens. Change password page asking the new owner to replace the temporary password The password rules come from the company's settings ( System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date ). A new company starts with the rules of the company its set-up was copied from, for example "at least 8 characters, upper- and lower-case letters, a number, a symbol. Passwords expire every 90 days." The new password must also not contain your username and must differ from the temporary one. If something is wrong you see one of these messages: "Your current password is incorrect.", "The new passwords do not match.", "Choose a password different from your current one." or "The new password must have ..." followed by what is missing. After the change, the Home page of your company opens. The company name appears in the top bar beside the program name, and the sidebar has every module, including Company at the bottom. Home page of the new company ABC Distribution Corp. seen by its owner John Doe, with every figure at zero

t: What a new company already has
x: href="#s-what-a-new-company-already-has" aria-label="Link to this section"> A company created by the Super Admin is not a blank database. It receives a copy of the set-up lists of another company (usually Company 1), so it can start work quickly: the company settings, with your company's own name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN (no logo, no closing date, and none of the other cooperative's registered name, CDA registration number and signatories); the modules and pages of the menu, the user roles with their page access and special permissions; the document numbering, with every counter starting again from 1; the chart of accounts with its account types (with the bank account numbers left blank) and the module default accounts; the terms, tax codes, payment methods, price level names, customer types, billing groups, item categories, units of measure, fixed asset categories with their accounts, the Withholding Tax Table and the business units; the cooperative's lists: member types, savings transaction codes, passbook types and their designs, ID types, documents, loan purposes, collateral types, account classes, the CDA report lines and calendar, address types, contact channels and cities; the water billing set-up: its settings, the organization units, the bill codes (an Inventory bill code without its item: link it again on Bill Codes), pipe sizes, rate codes and rates, meter discounts, discounts and their privileges and recurring billing plans, and the institution profile with your company's own name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN; one inventory site, Main . Nothing else is copied: no customers, suppliers, items, members, employees or other names, no savings or loan products, no classes, no report signatories, no users (you are the only user), no transactions, balances, budgets, fixed assets, POS records or audit trail. That is why every figure on the Home page is zero.

href="#s-getting-the-new-company-ready" aria-label="Link to this section"> A good order for the first day: Check the company details, the logo, the password rules and the closing date in System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date . Enter the bank account numbers in the Chart of Accounts, and add or remove accounts to suit the company. Add the other inventory sites you use ( Inventory > Inventory Site List ) and the POS terminals ( Point of Sale > POS Terminals ) if you sell over the counter. Enter or import your customers, suppliers and items (see System Administration for Import from CSV ), then your opening balances. Bring in your people: hand out the Company Code (see Company Profile & Code ) or create their accounts with New user .

href="#pg-company-profile" aria-label="Link to this section"> This page shows your company as the platform knows it, its Company Code, and the rules for employees who join with the code. Everybody who can open the page sees the code, so it can be handed out; only the Company Owner can change it. Where to find it: Company > Company Profile & Code. The Company Code button on Employees & Users opens it too. In the first picture the page belongs to Company 1, Sample Trading Company, whose owner is the System Administrator ( admin ). In the second it is seen by John Doe, owner of the new company ABC Distribution Corp.; two employees are waiting for his approval. Company Profile & Code of Sample Trading Company with the code STC-B8TJC Company Profile & Code of ABC Distribution Corp. seen by its owner, with the code AD-UW92E and two employees waiting What the page shows Part What it shows Company Code The code in large letters, and under it a line that says whether it can be used right now (see the next table). Copy code Copies the code, with its dash, so you can paste it into a message. The button reads Copied for a moment. Copy join link Copies the address of the join page with the code already filled in. An employee who opens the link only has to type their own details. Text under the code A reminder that the code only tells the system which company the employee is joining, and whether each registration waits for approval under Join Requests. A new code The owner's Regenerate code button. Joining The owner's switch Employees can join with the code , the Valid until (optional) date and Save . New employees Whether employees who join wait for approval, and the role they start with. Company Name , Address , Contact person , Phone , E-mail , TIN , Status , On the platform since and Company Owner . Users How many users are Active , Waiting , Inactive , Locked and Rejected . Click a number to open that tab of Employees & Users. The line under the code: Line Meaning Employees can join with this code. The code works. If an expiry date is set, the line ends with "until" and the date. Joining with the code is switched off. The owner turned the Employees can join with the code switch off. The code expired on ... The Valid until date has passed. The company is not active, so nobody can join. The Super Admin has switched the company off. Fields These fields are shown to the Company Owner (and to the Super Admin working inside the company). Other users see the code, the copy buttons, and one sentence under New employees saying whether employees who join wait for approval. Field What to enter / what it means Employees can join with the code On: new employees can use the code. Off: the code is refused on the join page until you switch it on again. The code itself stays the same. Valid until (optional) The last day the code can be used. It works until the end of that day. Leave it empty for no limit. The date cannot be in the past. Every employee who joins waits for approval (recommended) Ticked: a new account cannot log in until you approve it under Join Requests. Not ticked: employees can log in as soon as they have joined. Role to start with A role from your company's list (full-access roles are not offered). With approval, it is ticked for you when you approve someone; with the blank choice, Chosen when approving , you pick the role each time. Without approval, every employee who joins gets this role straight away, so a role is required. Step by step To hand out the code: Open Company > Company Profile & Code . Click Copy code and paste the code into a message to the new employee, or click Copy join link and send the link instead. Tell the employee to open the log-in page, click Join your company with its Company Code , and fill in the form (see "Joining your company with the Company Code" later in this chapter). To make a new code (for example when the code was shared with the wrong people): Click Regenerate code . Confirm the question "Make a new Company Code? The current code stops working immediately." The message "The new Company Code is ... The old one stopped working just now." shows the new code. Hand it out to the employees who still have to join. Employees who already joined keep their accounts and keep logging in as before: they never use the code again. To stop joining for a while, or to set an expiry date: Under Joining , turn Employees can join with the code off, or leave it on and pick a date in Valid until (optional) . Click Save . The message reads "Joining with the Company Code is switched off." or "Employees can join with the Company Code." To allow joining again, turn the switch back on (and clear or change the date), then click Save . To change whether new employees need approval, and the role they start with: Under New employees , tick or clear Every employee who joins waits for approval (recommended) . Choose a Role to start with , or leave Chosen when approving . Click Save . The message is "Joining rules saved." To change the company's name, address, phone, e-mail or TIN, click Edit company details at the top of the page. It opens System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date , and the platform's record of your company follows what you save there. The Contact person is kept by the Super Admin on the platform. Buttons Employees & Users : opens the list of the company's users. Edit company details : opens System Administration > Company, Security & Closing Date . It appears only for users who can open that page. Good to know Only the Company Owner, and the Super Admin working inside the company, can regenerate the code, switch joining on or off, set the expiry date and change the approval rule. Administrators see the line "Only the Company Owner can make a new code or switch joining off." If someone else tries anyway, the answer is "Only the Company Owner can change the Company Code and the joining rules." The code's format. The code is made of the initials of the company name (up to three letters; words such as The, And, Of, Inc, Corp, Co, Ltd and LLC are skipped), a dash, and five random characters. The random part never uses characters that are easy to confuse (0 and O, 1, I and L). "Sample Trading Company" gives codes like STC-B8TJC ; "ABC Distribution Corp." gives codes like AD-UW92E . Every code is unique on the platform, and a code that was replaced is never given out again. Typing the code. It can be typed with or without the dash, with spaces, in capitals or in small letters: AD-UW92E , aduw92e and AD UW92E are the same code. One message for every unusable code. A mistyped code, an old code, a code whose joining is switched off, an expired code and the code of an inactive company all get the same answer on the join page: "Invalid or inactive Company Code. Please verify the code with your Company Owner." This is on purpose: nobody can learn which companies exist by trying codes. Too many wrong codes. After 10 wrong codes from the same computer (the Super Admin can change the number) within 15 minutes, the join page refuses that computer for 15 minutes with "Too many attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." A full-access role is never given without approval. If you clear the approval box, the starting role must be an ordinary role. The messages are "Without approval, new employees need a role to start with: choose one." and "A full-access role cannot be given to employees who join without approval." Every change on this page is written to your company's audit trail (actions Company Code Changed and Company Join Rules ) and to the Super Admin's platform audit log.

href="#pg-company-users" aria-label="Link to this section"> This is the Company Owner's list of everybody who has an account in the company, with what each person can do and how the account was made. From here you approve or reject the employees who joined, change roles, reset passwords, unlock, deactivate and activate accounts. Where to find it: Company > Employees & Users. The Employees & Users button on Company Profile & Code, and the numbers under Users there, open it too. The first picture shows the nine users of Sample Trading Company. The second shows ABC Distribution Corp. seen by its owner: John Doe himself and two employees, Maria Reyes ( mreyes ) and Paolo Cruz ( pcruz ), who joined with the Company Code and are waiting for approval. Employees & Users of Sample Trading Company, all nine users active Employees & Users of ABC Distribution Corp. with two employees waiting for approval and the notice above the tabs When employees are waiting and you are not on the Join requests tab, a blue notice at the top says, for example, "2 employees are waiting for approval." with a Review the join requests link. The tabs and filters Tab or filter What it does All users Every user of the company. The number beside each tab is how many users it holds. Join requests Employees who joined with the Company Code and wait for approval. Active Approved accounts that can log in. Inactive Approved accounts that were deactivated. Locked Accounts locked after too many wrong passwords. Rejected Registrations that were rejected. Search Type part of a name, username, e-mail address or employee number and click Search . Role Shows only the users who have that role. The list changes as soon as you pick one. Waiting employees are always listed first; the others follow in order of name. The columns Column What it means Employee Full name. Under it: Company Owner for the owner, and No. with the employee number when there is one. Username The name the person logs in with, and their e-mail address under it. Roles The person's roles. None yet for an employee waiting for approval. Status Active , Inactive , Locked , Waiting for approval or Rejected (with the reason under it). For employees who joined with the code, it also shows who approved them ( Approved by ) or rejected them ( By ). Account made How the account came to be, and the date. Last log-in The date and time of the last log-in, or Never . Actions Approve and Reject for waiting employees, Approve for rejected ones, Manage for everybody else (see below). The Account made column reads: Created by an administrator : made on User Accounts (this includes every user who was there before the company joined the platform); Joined with the Company Code : the employee made the account on the join page; Created with the company : the owner's account, made by the Super Admin together with the company; Created by the Super Admin : an account the Super Admin made later, for example a new owner. The Manage menu Click Manage on a user's row to see what you can do with the account: Change roles : tick the roles the person should have. Reset password : give the person a temporary password. Unlock : shown only for a locked account. Activate : shown only for an inactive account. Deactivate : shown for active and locked accounts, except your own and the Company Owner's. All details, sites and POS terminals : opens the person's page on User Accounts , for the e-mail, employee number, sites, POS terminals and every other detail. It appears only if you may edit on User Accounts. For a user of another company working here ("User of ..." under Account made ), Reset password is not offered (their password is kept at their own company), and Deactivate and Activate read Remove access to this company and Give access back . Add user from another company at the top gives such access; see A user who works in two companies . A user of this company who also works elsewhere shows "Also works in" and the other company under their name. Step by step To change someone's roles: Click Manage on the person's row, then Change roles . In the Roles of ... window, tick the roles to give and clear the ones to take away. Full-access roles are marked (full access) . Click Save roles . The message lists the roles now held, for example "Roles of Ben Garcia saved: A/R Clerk." To reset a password (for someone who forgot theirs): Click Manage , then Reset password . Type a Temporary password that follows the company's password rules. Click Set temporary password . The message reads "Temporary password set. ... must change it at the next log-in." Give the temporary password to the person. At their next log-in they must replace it on the Change password page. A locked account is unlocked by the reset. To unlock an account: Open the Locked tab (or find the person on All users ). Click Manage , then Unlock . The message reads "... was unlocked." The person can log in again with their own password. To deactivate an account (for someone who has left): Click Manage , then Deactivate . Type a Reason (kept in the audit trail) if you wish. Click Deactivate . The message reads "... was deactivated and can no longer log in. Their name stays on everything they entered." If the person is working at that moment, they are sent to the log-in page at their next click. To activate an account again: Open the Inactive tab. Click Manage , then Activate . The message reads "... was activated and can log in again." To add a user yourself, without the Company Code: Click New user . The new-user form of User Accounts opens. Fill it in as described there. The username must be free on the whole platform. Approving and rejecting employees who joined with the code is described under Join Requests . Buttons New user : opens the new-user form on User Accounts . It appears only if you may create on that page. Roles : opens User Role Configuration , where the roles and what they may do are set. Company Code : opens Company Profile & Code . Good to know Users are never deleted , so their names stay on every record and audit entry they made. Deactivate a person who has left instead. The owner's row can only be changed by the owner (and the Super Admin). Other users see Company Owner in its Actions column instead of Manage . The owner's own Manage menu has no Deactivate . The Super Admin's account is never listed. When the Super Admin works inside your company, they use an account of their own that nobody can log into; it does not appear here or on User Accounts, but everything it does is in your audit trail. Permissions. Opening the page, like every page, is controlled by Page Access Configuration ; on a new installation it follows the access of User Accounts. Change roles , Reset password , Unlock , Activate and Deactivate need the edit permission on the page; Approve and Reject need the approve permission. The Company Owner and full-access roles have both. Messages you may see: "Keep at least one role." (a user must keep a role), "You cannot remove the Administrator role from your own account." (an administrator other than the owner), "You cannot deactivate your own account.", "The Company Owner cannot be deactivated. The Super Admin can make someone else the owner first.", "Approve the registration first." (activating or unlocking an account that was never approved), "That user cannot be changed here." (the owner's account, for anyone but the owner). Temporary passwords must follow the company's password rules and may not contain the username; otherwise the message says what is missing, for example "The temporary password must have at least 8 characters, a symbol." Every change is written to the company's audit trail with the old and new values (roles, status, approval) and the reason when one was typed.

t: Joining your company with the Company Code
x: href="#sec-joining" aria-label="Link to this section"> New employees can make their own account instead of waiting for an administrator to create one. All they need is the Company Code from their Company Owner. This section is written for the employee. Where to find it: on the log-in page, under the Log in button: New employee? Join your company with its Company Code . A join link sent by the owner opens the same page with the code already filled in. The empty join page, Join your company Fields Field What to enter Full name Your name as it should appear on the records you enter. Required. E-mail Your e-mail address. Required. Employee no. (if any) Your employee number, if your company uses them. Username The name you will log in with: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. It is saved in small letters. It must not be used by anybody on the platform. Password Your own password. It must follow your company's password rules and must not contain your username. Confirm password The same password again. Company Code The code your Company Owner gave you, for example AD-UW92E . The dash, spaces and capitals do not matter. It is not your password. Step by step Open the log-in page and click Join your company with its Company Code . Fill in Full name , E-mail and, if you have one, Employee no. Choose a Username , and type your Password twice. Type the Company Code . Click Create my account . The join page filled in by Maria Reyes, with the code of ABC Distribution Corp. The page then confirms which company the account was made in, for example "Your account for ABC Distribution Corp. was created". If your company wants to approve new employees, it adds "Your Company Owner has to approve it before you can log in. Once it is approved, log in with the username mreyes and the password you chose." If it does not, it says you can log in now. Click Go to log in to return to the log-in page. Confirmation that the account for ABC Distribution Corp. was created and waits for approval While you wait for approval If you try to log in before the owner has approved your account, and your password is right, the log-in page answers "Your registration is waiting for approval by your Company Owner. You can log in once it is approved." Wait until the owner tells you the account is approved, then log in with your username and the password you chose. You are not asked to change the password: it is already your own. Log-in refused with the message that the registration is waiting for approval If the owner rejected the registration, the answer is "Your registration was not approved. Please contact your Company Owner." With a wrong password you only see "Invalid username or password.", so nobody else can find out whether an account is waiting. Messages on the join page Message What to do Invalid or inactive Company Code. Please verify the code with your Company Owner. The code is wrong, old, switched off or expired, or the company is inactive. Ask the owner for the current code. That username is already taken. Please choose another. Somebody on the platform, in any company, has that username. Choose another. Your password must have ... Make the password longer or add what is listed (capital and small letters, a number, a symbol), and leave the username out of it. The two passwords do not match. Type the same password in both boxes. Enter your full name. / Enter a valid e-mail address. Fill in the box named. Choose a username of 3 to 50 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. Remove spaces and other characters from the username. Too many attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again. Too many wrong codes were typed from this computer. Wait, then try with the right code. You are logged in already. Joining is for new employees who do not have an account yet. Someone is logged in on this browser. Log out first, or use your existing account. Note The account is made in your company's database only. Joining does not give you any access by itself: the owner decides your role when approving you (or the company's starting role is given when approval is switched off).

href="#pg-company-join_requests" aria-label="Link to this section"> Join Requests lists the employees who made an account with the Company Code and wait for the Company Owner's approval. Approving lets the person log in with the role you choose; rejecting keeps them out, with a reason. Where to find it: Company > Join Requests. When employees are waiting, the menu shows how many, for example Join Requests (2) . The Join requests tab of Employees & Users, and the Review the join requests link in its blue notice, show the same list. Join Requests with Maria Reyes and Paolo Cruz waiting for approval The page has the same tabs, filters, columns and buttons as Employees & Users ; it simply opens on the Join requests tab. Clicking another tab takes you to Employees & Users. The employees who wait are also listed at the top of All users , above everybody else: The two join requests at the top of the user list, above the Company Owner John Doe Before approving, check that you know the person: the full name, username, e-mail address and employee number in the row are what they typed on the join page. Step by step To approve an employee: Click Approve on the employee's row. In the Approve ... window, tick the role or roles the person should have. If the company has a Role to start with , it is already ticked. Full-access roles are marked (full access) ; give them only to people who should see and change everything. Click Approve . The message reads, for example, "Maria Reyes is approved and can log in now." Tell the employee they can log in. If they must work only at certain sites or POS terminals, set these afterwards with Manage > All details, sites and POS terminals (see User Accounts ). To reject a registration: Click Reject on the employee's row. Type the reason in Reason (kept in the audit trail) . A reason is required. Click Reject . The message reads "The registration of ... was rejected. They cannot log in." The person moves to the Rejected tab, with the reason under the status. To approve a registration that was rejected earlier: Open the Rejected tab of Employees & Users. Click Approve on the row and continue as above. (A rejected registration cannot be rejected a second time.) What it records Approving sets the account to Active , gives it the roles you ticked, and records you as the approver (shown as Approved by in the Status column). The audit trail gets a User Approved entry with the roles given. Rejecting sets the account to Rejected and inactive, keeps the reason, and records who rejected it (shown as By ). The audit trail gets a User Rejected entry with the reason. The employee's own joining is in the audit trail too, as User Registered under the employee's username. Each of these is also written to the Super Admin's platform audit log. Good to know A role is required. Approving without a role gives "Give ... at least one role before approving." Approve and Reject need the approve permission on the page. The Company Owner and full-access roles have it. Users without it see the list but no buttons. Approval can be switched off on Company Profile & Code . Employees who join then become active at once with the starting role, and this list stays empty. Nothing is deleted. A rejected registration stays on the Rejected tab; the username stays taken. The Super Admin sees the number of employees waiting in each company, but the approval belongs to the company.

t: Logging in when there are several companies
x: href="#sec-multi-login" aria-label="Link to this section"> Everybody, owners and employees alike, logs in on the same page with their own username and password; the page subtitle reads Log in to your company . Besides the usual messages about wrong passwords and locked accounts (see Getting Started ), you may meet these: Message Meaning Your registration is waiting for approval by your Company Owner. You can log in once it is approved. You joined with the code and the owner has not approved you yet. Your registration was not approved. Please contact your Company Owner. The owner rejected your registration. Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner. The Super Admin has switched your company off. Your records are kept. Your account is no longer linked to this company. Please log in again. Your account was changed while you were working. Log in again; if it keeps happening, ask your Company Owner. Your account needs to be checked by your Company Owner before you can log in. The platform's record of your username did not match your account; the program corrects it. Try again. If the message comes back, the owner asks the Super Admin to rebuild the company's user list. Too many failed log-in attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again. Many log-ins with unknown usernames were tried from this computer. Wait 15 minutes. Tip If you forget your password, ask your Company Owner (or an administrator) to reset it on Employees & Users . The Company Code cannot be used to log in.

href="#sec-switch-company" aria-label="Link to this section"> A user who was given access to another company (see A user who works in two companies ) logs in at their own company as always. The company name at the top of the screen then becomes a switch. Click the company name at the top (on a phone, the building button beside the program name). The list Your companies shows your own company ("Your own company") and each company that gave you access ("Access given to you"). The one open now is ticked. Click the company to work in. Its Home page opens with "You are now working in ...". No password is asked. The company switch: your own company and the company that gave you access While you work in the other company, a blue strip under the top bar says so: "You are working in ABC Distribution Corp. with access given to you. Your own company is Sample Trading Company." Click Back to Sample Trading Company on the strip, or use the switch again, to go back. Working in the other company: the strip under the top bar, with the way back In the other company you see its menus, records and reports, and you can do only what its roles for you allow. You are not a Super Admin and have no rights over the platform or other companies. Your password belongs to your own company: Change password is offered there, not in the other company. Each switch is recorded in the audit trail of the company you open. When the other company removes your access, or your own account is deactivated, the switch disappears; if you were working in the other company you are taken back to your own. Message Meaning Your access to ... has ended. You are back in your own company. The other company (or yours) removed the access while you were working there. You have no access to that company. The access was removed, or the company is not open. Your access to ... is switched off there. Please ask its administrator. The other company switched your account off. The database of ... needs the latest update first. Please ask the platform administrator (Super Admin). The other company's database is waiting for an update.

href="#s-coop-how" aria-label="Link to this section"> One ledger. An official receipt, a disbursement, a loan release or a cooperative journal voucher is a transaction of the general ledger. At the same moment the program writes the member's own ledger: the savings or share capital account, the time deposit, the loan. Each member ledger line carries the number of the voucher that posted it. The Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation proves that the member ledgers add up to the control accounts. Members in the general ledger. Every member is also a name in Employees & Other Names . The ledger lines of a member carry that name, so the existing Subsidiary Ledger report shows a member's lines under each account. Branches are classes. Each branch has a class, and every voucher of the branch carries it, so the Income Statement and Balance Sheet by Class give branch statements. A user tied to a branch sees and works on that branch's members only. Nothing posted is edited or deleted. A wrong voucher is voided with a reason, which reverses the general ledger and the member ledgers together, or corrected with an adjusting entry. The program refuses a void that would leave the books wrong (for example the release of a loan that already has payments) and says why. Approvals. What needs a second person (large receipts, withdrawals above a limit, share capital withdrawals, loan approvals, waivers, distribution batches, settlement of a member who has left) asks for a supervisor's username and password on the same form, unless the user has the Approve right on the page. The approver is recorded on the voucher and in the audit trail. Posted once. Each form can be posted only once: a double click, a refresh or the browser's back button cannot post a receipt twice. Interest, accrual and penalty runs are posted once for each period or date. Printed documents are controlled. The first print of a promissory note, a certificate or a voucher is the original; each later print is a numbered copy that asks for a reason. Every print is listed in the Document Print History . Exact amounts. Money is computed as exact decimals and rounded to the centavo where a document shows it, so the totals of a report always equal the sum of its lines.

href="#s-coop-setup" aria-label="Link to this section"> An administrator sets the cooperative up once, in this order. Each page is described in this chapter. Cooperative Profile & Policies : the registered name, CDA registration number, signatories, the membership, teller and loan policies, the alert windows and the year-end allocation percentages. Check the percentages against your bylaws. Module Default Accounts , Cooperative group: check that each cooperative account points at the right account of your chart. Branches : the head office and each branch, with its class and official receipt prefix. User Accounts : give each teller and branch user their branch and cash drawer, and give users their roles (see the next section). Document Numbering , Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists and Passbook Types . Savings & Deposit Products : at least one share capital product, the savings products and the time deposit products, with their rates. Then Savings Transaction Codes if you need codes of your own. Loan Charges , Loan Products and the Loan Approval Matrix . Document Templates , if your documents use wording of your own. Report Field Mappings , the Regulatory Calendar and the officers . When moving from another system: Opening Balances Import of the members, then the savings and share capital balances, the time deposits and the loans, all as of the cut-off date. Or Consolidated Import : the members with their savings, loans, water-service accounts and bill balances from one file. Run the Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation . It must show no difference before you go live.

href="#s-coop-roles" aria-label="Link to this section"> The module adds eight roles. Like every role, they can be changed on User Role Configuration . Role What it can do General Manager Every cooperative, savings, loan, teller, distribution and compliance page with every right, including Approve, and the main accounting reports. Bookkeeper Cooperative vouchers, interest and penalty runs, the distribution pages and every cooperative report, without the profile, branches, numbering, products and approval matrix set-up. Loan Officer Loan applications, credit investigation, release, collection, loan accounts, documents, waiver requests and renewals, and the loan reports. Credit Committee Reviews and approves loan applications and waivers, and reads the loan reports. Teller The teller shift, official receipts, member disbursements, deposits and withdrawals, loan collection, passbook printing, check clearing and time deposits. Membership Officer Member records and statements, savings account opening and the member reports. Collector Loan collection and the collection, due and aging reports. Branch Manager Everything of the branch with the Approve right, except the set-up pages. The special permissions of a role (on User Role Configuration) set the limits: "Cooperative: max savings withdrawal without supervisor approval", "Cooperative: max loan release amount without supervisor approval", "Cooperative: can waive loan interest and penalties, and adjust loan balances", "Cooperative: can record back-dated member transactions", "Cooperative: can override the payment allocation (penalty, interest, principal) on a loan collection" and "Cooperative: sees every branch regardless of the branch on the user account".

href="#s-coop-routines" aria-label="Link to this section"> When What Where Every business day Open the shift with the beginning cash; post the savings transactions, loan collections and receipts (all on the Teller menu); close the shift with the cash count and print the cash count sheet and the Daily Collection & Disbursement Summary. Teller Shift & Cash Count , Savings Transaction Center , Loan Collection , Official Receipt , Daily Collection & Disbursement Summary Every business day Clear the checks the bank has cleared; record returned checks. Check Clearing Month end (or the product's interest period) Post savings interest for each product; run dormancy. Post Savings Interest Month end Accrue time deposit interest; settle the placements that matured. Time Deposit Center Month end Post loan penalties, accrue loan interest and refresh the loan statuses. Post Loan Penalties & Interest Accrual Month end Check that the member ledgers agree with the general ledger. Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation After the fiscal year Allocate the net surplus as the General Assembly approved, then compute, approve and post the ISC and PR batches. Net Surplus Allocation , Interest on Share Capital and Patronage Refund As scheduled Prepare the CAPR data, file the compliance requirements and watch the calendar. CAPR Data Preparation & Export , Compliance Tracking , Regulatory Calendar The runs are made by a user on their pages; nothing runs by itself at night. Each run is safe to repeat for the same date or period: it adds nothing the second time. The Home page and the alert count in the top bar list what needs attention: amortizations due, past due loans, maturing time deposits, accounts about to turn dormant, documents expiring, approvals waiting, regulatory deadlines and teller shifts left open.

href="#pg-coop-members" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Member Center is the list of the cooperative's members and the place to start any work on a member. The counts at the top show how many members are in each membership status; click a count to list those members. Click a member's name to open Member Information . Where to find it: Members & Others > Member Center. The Member Center with the counts by status and the active members of the sample cooperative The counts are Active members , Applicants , Suspended , Resigned , Terminated and Deceased . Under them are the filters: Field What to enter / what it means Find Part of the member's name or mobile number, the first digits of the member number, or the whole passbook number, TIN, savings account number or loan number. Status One membership status, or Any status . Member type One member type, or Any type . Branch One branch, or All branches . Shown only to users who see every branch, when the cooperative has more than one branch. Show only Everyone , On hold , With an alert , No share capital yet (the share capital balance is zero) or Subscription not fully paid (the subscribed capital is more than the paid-up capital). Click Show to apply the filters, or Clear to remove them. The member list Column What it shows Member The name (click it to open the member), with the member number and the city under it. A red circle with a slash means the member is on hold; a warning triangle means the member has an alert note. Point at the mark to read the reason or the note. Type, Status, Branch The member type, the membership status and the branch of the member. Member since The membership date. Share capital The balance of the member's share capital accounts that are not closed. Savings The balance of the member's ordinary and special savings accounts. Time deposits are not included. Loans The principal balance of the member's open loans (current, past due or restructured). "past due" in red under the amount means one of the loans is past due. The list is in name order, 50 members to a page; the page numbers and the number of members found are under the list. The buttons at the top are New member , with an arrow beside it for Joint account and Institution (they need the Create right on Member Information), and Masterlist report , which opens the Member Master List report. Import Member (beside them, with the Create right on Member Information) brings the members of the former system in from a CSV file: see Importing members . A user whose account is tied to a branch sees only the members of that branch, in the list and in the counts. To find a member: Open Members & Others > Member Center . Type part of the name, or a member, passbook, account or loan number, in Find . Choose a Status , Member type or Show only if you want fewer members. Click Show , then click the member's name. To list the members on hold: choose On hold in Show only and click Show . Importing members (Import Member) For the move from the former system, the individual members are brought in from a CSV file instead of being typed one by one. Each member is created with the status Active . Import the members first, then their savings ( Import Savings ) and time deposits ( Import Time Deposit ). To bring the members with their savings, loans and bill balances in one file, use Consolidated Import . Where to find it: Import Member on the title bar of the Member Center. Reading and checking a file needs the Create right on Member Information; uploading it needs the Approve right there. Import members: a file with columns of the full template read for review; the two rows with a problem are in red The file. Download the CSV template gives the columns with two sample rows; open it in Excel, replace the samples with the members, and save it as CSV (Comma delimited) . The first line holds the column names (the template's, or the headings in words, for example "Last Name" or "Date of Birth"); one member per line after it. The card The columns on the page lists every column with what goes in it; the required ones are in bold. Column What to enter Member no. The member number of the former system. Blank: the next member number of this system. Last name , First name , Middle name Required. Write - in Middle name for a member who has none. Suffix Jr., Sr., III and the like. Date of birth Required. YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY. Sex, Civil status M or F (or Male, Female); Single, Married, Widowed, Separated or Annulled. Member type Required. The code or the name, as on Member Types, for example REG or Regular. Membership date Required. YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY. Street The house number and street of the residence address. Barangay , Municipality / City , Province Required: the residence address. Branch The branch code or name. Blank: the branch of the user. Mobile, E-mail, TIN As on Member Information. The full template. Full template (every detail) , beside Download the CSV template , gives a template with a column for every other detail of Member Information as well: 53 more columns. Which of them to fill is up to you: keep only the columns you have and delete the others; a column left out, or a cell left blank, is simply not filled in. The page lists them under The full template: 53 more columns at the end of The columns (click it to open the list), by group: Group Columns Personal Salutation (Mr., Ms., Mrs., Dr., Engr., Atty. or Hon.), place of birth, nationality (blank: Filipino), passbook no. Residence, provincial and office address The house / unit no. and ZIP code of the residence; the house no., street / barangay, municipality / city, province and ZIP code of the provincial and of the office address. Education and work Highest education, year completed, course, occupation, employment (Employed, Self-employed, Business owner, OFW, Retired, Student, Unemployed, Other), employer or business name, its contact and address, other organizations. Membership and grouping PMES attended (date), subscribed shares (a whole number), par value per share (blank: the par value of Cooperative Profile & Policies), cluster, segmentation, account officer (the username or the name of a user), account class, account group, address sub-group and savings group (each a name on its list of Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists). Contacts and notes The alert shown at the counter, notes, landline (saved with the mobile number on the member's contact numbers). Spouse Last, first and middle name, date of birth, contact no. A spouse needs the last and the first name. Beneficiaries Two beneficiaries, each with the name, relationship, date of birth, contact no. and share % (0 to 100; the shares add up to 100 at most). A beneficiary's details need the name. The review grid shows only the columns of the full template that the file fills. A row's line says which details it brings, for example "Becomes Pascual, Ramil S., member no. 200111, Active, with details on education and work; membership and grouping; spouse; beneficiaries". The review. Choose the file and click Read the file for review . Nothing is saved yet: every row of the file is shown in a grid, one row per member, and each row is checked at once. A row with a problem is in red : a red ground and a red bar on its left, a red dot, and its messages in red under it, for example "Enter the barangay.", "The date of birth "1979-13-40" is not a date.", "Member type "XYZ" is not on Member Types." or "... is already a member: 200101." (the same member number, or the same name and date of birth, already on file or earlier in the file). The cells a message names are outlined in red. A row without a problem has a green dot and shows what it will become. The bar above the grid counts the rows and those with a problem; Find in the rows narrows the grid, and Only rows with a problem leaves those alone. The line under the grid says how many rows are still in red. Correct a row by typing in its cells. The row is checked again by itself a moment after you stop typing (Enter in a cell checks it at once): while it is being checked it is marked in blue, then it turns red again with the problems left, or loses its red when there is none. The columns beyond the first ones are under … at the end of the row; they open by themselves when a message names one of them. Remove a row with × at the end of it.
