Remove the rows with a problem , above the grid, removes every row in red at once. Put back the last brings back the last row, or the last rows, removed. Check again checks every row as it now is. Start over leaves the file and opens the page again. Upload (for example Upload 5 members ) asks to confirm, checks every row once more and saves them all, or none if a row still has a problem. The same review, with its rows in red and its automatic check, is on Import Savings , Import Time Deposit , the batch deposits and withdrawals, Import Loans and Import Items. On a phone each row of the grid shows as a card with its cells under one another, and the buttons stay at the bottom of the screen. Note The upload is all or nothing: one row with a problem saves nothing, and the grid comes back with the rows as you left them. The import is kept on the audit trail with the file name and the number of rows. An upload is sent once: refreshing the page, going Back or a second tab does not upload the same rows again.

href="#pg-coop-member" aria-label="Link to this section"> Member Information holds everything about one member: the profile from the membership application, the accounts and loans, the documents on file, the membership status and its history, holds and notes. A new member is also entered here. Where to find it: click a member's name on the Member Center , or click New member there. Member names on the cooperative reports also open this page. The page is not in the sidebar menu. Member Information of Mendoza, Ramon, open on the Personal part of the Profile tab Note Every member belongs to a party of the Party Master, which also holds the member's customer and supplier records. On a new member, Already on file as a customer or supplier chooses a customer, supplier or other name already in the program, so the person joins as a member on that same party instead of being recorded twice; a new member that looks like one on file is stopped with the possible matches. A saved member shows its Party ID beside Kind of member . The member's date of birth, TIN, contact numbers and addresses are masked for users without the permission to see confidential member details. See Member Information in chapter 14. The top of the page The buttons in the title bar of a saved member are: Statement : the member's Member Statement of Account . Receive payment : an official receipt for the member on Official Receipt (Member Collection) . Loan application : a new loan application for the member. Open account : opens a new account for the member on the Savings Account Center . ID card : prints the member's ID card (see The ID card ). Member Center : back to the list. Each button appears only for users with the right it needs. Under the title is the member panel: the photo (or the initials), the name, the member number, the member type, the status and the branch, an On hold line and the alert note when there are any, and the balances Share capital , Savings , Time deposits and Loans (with the number of open loans). Note The Loans figure on the member panel is the principal, interest and penalty still to be paid on the open loans. The Loans column of the Member Center shows the principal only, so the two can differ. The page has four tabs: Profile , Accounts and loans , Documents and History and notes . A new member shows the profile form only. The Profile tab The profile of an individual is in parts: Personal , Family and beneficiaries , Financial , Membership and Loan and savings grouping , then Water Defaults , Customer Defaults and Vendor Defaults for the users who may change those (see below). A joint account or an institution has its own form, in the format of the former program: Joint/Institution Details and Membership Information , then the defaults tabs (see Joint accounts and institutions ). All are saved together with Save member (or Add member for a new member). Users without the Edit right see the profile but cannot change it. Personal Field What to enter / what it means Kind of member Individual , Joint account or Institutional . Choosing Joint account or Institutional changes the form to the joint account and institution form (see Joint accounts and institutions ); choosing Individual brings back the individual's. Member no. (blank = next number) Shown for a new member only. Leave it blank to get the next member number (the grey text shows it). A number you type must not be used by another member. The member number cannot be changed after the member is saved. Salutation, Last name, First name, Middle name, Suffix Last name and first name are required for an individual. The program writes the member's name as last name, first name and middle initial, for example "Mendoza, Ramon" or "Lopez, Teresa R.". Date of birth, Place of birth, Sex, Civil status, Nationality The date of birth is used by the duplicate check and for the age on the Member Master List. Nationality starts as Filipino. TIN, Mobile, E-mail The e-mail address must be valid. When Mobile is left blank, the first mobile number under Contact numbers fills it. Residence address House / unit no. , Street , Barangay , City / municipality , Province and ZIP . The address prints on the statement and the ID card. Provincial and office addresses Click the line to open the provincial and office address boxes. Contact numbers One row per number: Type (Mobile, Landline, Office, Other), Country , Area , Number and Primary . Add a number adds a row; the x at the end of a row removes it. Education and work Highest education , Year completed , Course , Occupation , Employment (Employed, Self-employed, Business owner, OFW, Retired, Student, Unemployed, Other), Employer / business name , Employer contact , Employer address and Other organizations . Photo (JPG / PNG), Specimen signature A picture file (JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP) of up to 8 MB. A new file replaces the one on file. The photo shows on the member panel and the ID card; the signature on file shows beside these boxes and prints on the ID card. Family and beneficiaries Field What to enter / what it means Spouse, children and other dependents One row per person: Kind (Spouse, Child, Other dependent), Last name , First name , Middle name , Relationship , Birth date , Contact , and Dependent ticked for a person who depends on the member. Click Add a person for another row. Beneficiaries Name , Relationship , Birth date , Contact , Address , Share % and Primary . The shares of all the beneficiaries must not add up to more than 100 %. Click Add a beneficiary for another row. Relatives who are members The Member and the Relationship . Financial Field What to enter / what it means Income, Expenses, Other cash outlay (amortizations elsewhere) One row per item: the Item , the Member (monthly) amount and the Spouse (monthly) amount. Monthly income, Expenses and outlay, Net disposable income Shown after the member is saved: the income less the expenses and the other cash outlay. The net disposable income is checked against the NDI requirement of the loan products. Assets and liabilities Kind (Asset, Liability), Description and Amount . Membership Field What to enter / what it means Branch Required. The branch the member belongs to. A user tied to a branch can file members under that branch only. Member type Required. The types are set up on Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists . PMES attended The date the member attended the Pre-Membership Education Seminar. Membership date The date the member was admitted. When it is blank, activating the member fills it with the activation date. Status Shown for a saved member, with the date of the last change. The status is changed on the History and notes tab. Subscribed shares, Par value per share The number of shares the member subscribed and the par value of one share. The par value starts at the Par value per share of Cooperative Profile & Policies . The subscribed capital is the shares times the par value. Subscribed / paid-up capital Shown for a saved member: the subscribed capital, the paid-up capital (the balance of the share capital accounts) and the percentage paid. Cluster, Segmentation, Account officer The cluster and segmentation (from Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists) and the user who looks after the member. Attendance (general assembly, PMES, seminars) One row per meeting: Meeting (General assembly, PMES, Seminar / training, District meeting), Date , Attended and Remarks . Click Add a meeting for another row. Loan and savings grouping Field What to enter / what it means Account class, Account group, Address sub-group, Savings group Groupings the cooperative keeps for its members. The account classes come from the Account classes list. Passbook number The member's passbook number. Get passbook number puts the next number of Document Numbering (Passbook) that no member has in the box; it is taken from the series when the member is saved (if another member was given it in the meantime, the next free one is given and the message says so). A number typed by hand must not belong to another member. Find on the Member Center finds the member by it. Alert shown at the counter A short warning for the staff, for example "Verify ID before withdrawals". It shows on the member panel of the teller, savings and loan pages, and as a mark on the Member Center. Notes Any other remarks about the member. One name: Water Defaults, Customer Defaults and Vendor Defaults A member is entered once, on this form, and is the same name in every line of business: the member is the cooperative's customer (sales, the POS, statements) and its supplier (bills, checks, cash vouchers) on records kept with the member, and the member's water service is set here too. There is no separate customer, supplier or water consumer form for a member. The name, TIN, e-mail and contact numbers of those records follow the member when the member is saved; a member renamed is renamed everywhere. The Water Defaults tab of Santos, Maria with her water-service account Water Defaults (users who may change Water Billing's water-service accounts): Field What it means Zone, Address sub-group, Sequence The zone, the address sub-group and the meter reading sequence of the member's water service. The address sub-group is kept right in its box: the pencil renames the sub-group chosen (every member and water-service account that has it takes the new name) and + adds a new one to the list and chooses it, each saved at once with Save or Enter (Cancel or Escape leaves it). All sub-groups: order, switch off, delete under the box opens the whole list. Rate code / classification, Pipe size The tariff of the service. Both are needed, and the two must have a complete tariff on Water Meter Rates. Connection date The date the connection started. Disconnection date A date makes the connection Inactive: the water-service account is marked disconnected in Water Billing, with the date. Connection status Active or Inactive . To reconnect, clear the disconnection date and choose Active. Water-service account these defaults are for Shown when the member has more than one water-service account: the one the defaults are applied to. Saving the member applies the defaults to the member's water-service account; a member without one gets a new account when a rate code and a pipe size are given (the Create right on Water Billing's water-service accounts is needed). The table under the boxes lists the member's water-service accounts with their rate code, zone, connection and status. A disconnection made in Water Billing shows here too. Customer Defaults (users with the Edit right on the Customer Center): Payment terms , Credit limit (0 = none) , Tax code , Preferred payment method , Customer type , Sales representative , Billing group (batch invoicing) , Taxes this customer withholds and Price level . A credit limit change by a user who may not approve on the Customer Center needs the Reason for a credit limit change . Price level decides what the member pays for the items, as the price level of a customer does: on invoices, sales receipts, sales orders, estimates, statement charges and batch invoices (with each customer's price level) the item's price comes from it when the member is chosen, and at the POS when the member is the sale's customer (the POS shows the level under the customer). A level with a price of its own for an item gives that price; otherwise its percentage is applied to the item's sales price. Left blank, the member pays the members' price level of the line of business (Business Units), or of the cooperative, when one is set (the blank choice then reads Members' price level ), else the standard prices ( Standard ). Only an active level can be chosen; a level the member already has keeps working until it is changed, shown with "(inactive)" if it was made inactive since (an inactive level gives the standard prices). Water bills are not affected: a material on a water bill is priced from its bill code. Vendor Defaults (users with the Edit right on the Vendor Center): Payment terms , Credit limit with vendor , Our account no. with this vendor , Default expense account , Tax code and Withholding taxes . On the name lists of every form the member appears once, by member type ("Regular Member: Santos, Maria"). An entry with the member is recorded on the record of the role the member plays: on Accounts Receivable (an invoice, a receivable line of a journal entry) the member's customer record, on Accounts Payable or as the payee of a check or cash voucher its supplier record, elsewhere its member name. The Subsidiary Ledger, the schedules and Find show the member once, with all of them. On the Customer Center and the Vendor Center the member's record carries a line that leads to these tabs. Joint accounts and institutions A joint account (two or more people saving together, for example a husband, a wife and a son) and an institution (a hospital, a school, an association) are filed on the form of the former program. Choosing Joint account or Institutional as the Kind of member shows it. It has no Family and beneficiaries , Financial or Loan and savings grouping : those are for an individual. On the right of the form the status and the type are shown in large letters, for example NEW and ASSOCIATE - JOINT for a joint account not saved yet, with the Member ID once it is saved. Joint/Institution Details Field What to enter / what it means Member ID (blank = next number) Shown for a new member only, as for an individual. Membership name Required. The name the account goes by, which becomes the member's name: for a joint account the holders, for example "Santos, Ana or Ramon or Miguel"; for an institution its registered name. When a save is refused (an e-mail that is not valid, a passbook number already given), the form comes back with everything as typed. Authorized representatives One row per person who may act for the account: Authorized representative name , Position / relation (Wife, Husband, Son; President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary) and Member (if a member) . Click Add a representative for another row. Residence address House / bldg no. , Postal code , Street , Barangay , City / municipality and Province . Water Billing uses this address for the member's water-service account. Office / business address House / bldg no. , Postal code , Street , City / municipality and Province . Contact details The Contact list , one row per number: Type , Country , Area code , Number and Primary ; then the E-mail address and the TIN (optional) . The first mobile of the list is the member's mobile (Find on the Member Center finds the member by it). Specimen signatures of the representatives A picture of the representatives' signatures (JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP, up to 8 MB). The signatures on file show beside the box and print on the ID card, as an individual's specimen signature does. Membership Information Field What to enter / what it means Passbook number As for an individual: type it, or click Get passbook number for the next number of the series that no member has. Membership date, PMES date The date the member was admitted and the date of the pre-membership seminar. Type Required. The member types of the kind ( Associate - Joint and Regular - Joint for a joint account, Associate - Institutional for an institution on a new installation; see Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists ). A new joint account or institution starts with the first one. A member type of another kind is refused. Status New for a member not saved yet (it is saved as an Applicant); for a saved member the status and the date of the last change. The status is changed on the History and notes tab. Cluster, Segmentation From Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists. Branch, Subscribed shares, Par value per share, Account officer As for an individual: the branch is required. Alert shown at the counter, Notes As for an individual, for example "Two of the representatives sign every withdrawal". To add a joint account or an institution: Open Members & Others > Member Center , click the arrow beside New member and choose Joint account or Institution . On Joint/Institution Details , type the Membership name and the authorized representatives with their position or relation, then the addresses and the contact details. On Membership Information , click Get passbook number (or type the number), check the Type , type the Membership date and the PMES date , and choose the Branch . Click Add member . It is saved as an Applicant , as an individual is. Adding a member To add a member: Open Members & Others > Member Center and click New member . For a joint account or an institution, click the arrow beside it and choose Joint account or Institution . On Personal , leave Member no. (blank = next number) blank, or type the number from the membership application. Type the name, date of birth and the other personal details, the residence address and the contact numbers. Choose the photo and the specimen signature if you have them. On Family and beneficiaries , enter the dependents and the beneficiaries with their shares. On Membership , choose the Branch and the Member type , and type the PMES attended date and the Subscribed shares . Fill the other parts as needed. Click Add member , or Add member & New to start another one. The member is saved as an Applicant , and the program says: "Member added as an applicant. Activate the membership when the Board has approved it and the share capital is paid." The member's name is also added to Employees & Other Names as a member, so that ledger lines can carry it. To make the member active, see Membership status . The duplicate check. When another member already has the same name and the same date of birth, the program does not save and says, for example: "A member with the same name and date of birth already exists (member no. 100006). Tick "This is a different person" to save anyway." Open that member first to make sure it is not the same person. If it is a different person, tick This is a different person beside the save button and save again. To change a member's profile: open the member, change the fields on any part of the Profile tab and click Save member . The changes are kept in the audit trail of the member record. The Accounts and loans tab The tab lists, with links to each account and loan: Savings, share capital and time deposits : Account , Product , Opened , Balance , Available (what can be withdrawn now) and Status , with "restricted" beside a restricted account. Closed accounts are greyed at the end. Loans : Loan , Product , Released , Maturity , Principal , Balance (principal), Penalty and Status . Loan applications in process , when there are any. Loans guaranteed as co-maker : the open loans of other members that this member signed for, with the borrower and the principal balance. The Documents tab The documents on file for the member, such as IDs, the membership application form or the PMES certificate, with a scan or photo of each. The list shows Document (the kind and the notes), No. , Issued , Expires and File . An expiry date that has passed is shown in red with "(expired)". Click the file name to open the file in a new tab. To add a document: Open the member and click the Documents tab. In Add a document , choose the Kind . The kinds are the Member document types list of Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists . Type the Document / ID no. and the Issued and Expires dates. Choose the File (picture or PDF, up to 8 MB) and type any Notes . Click Save document . To remove a document from the list: click Remove on its row, type the reason and confirm. Removing needs the Delete/Void right on Member Information; the removal and the document's details are kept in the audit trail. Documents that expire within the number of days set in Documents, collateral and insurance expiring within (days) on Cooperative Profile & Policies , or have already expired, are counted in the cooperative alerts on the Home page (for active members and applicants). The photo, the signature and the document files can be opened by users who may open Member Information, the Member Center, the Official Receipt page, the Savings Account Center or the Loan Application Center, for the members of their own branch. Each time a document file is opened, it is recorded in the audit trail. Membership status The History and notes tab shows the Membership status history: each status, the status it came from, the reason and reference, the date and the user. The Change status button needs the Approve right on the Member Center. A status can only move as follows: From May change to Applicant Active, Terminated Active Suspended, Resigned, Terminated, Deceased Suspended Active, Resigned, Terminated, Deceased Resigned Active Terminated Active Deceased No further change The Change the membership status form: Field What to enter / what it means New status Only the statuses the member may move to are listed. Effective date The date the change takes effect. It starts as today. Reason (kept in the member's history and the audit trail) Required. For example "Approved by the Board (membership committee)". Board resolution / reference The resolution or other reference, for example BR-2024-01. Activate even if the paid-up share capital is below the minimum Tick to activate a member whose paid-up share capital is below the minimum. The waiver is noted in the audit trail. Allow resignation / termination with open loans (to be offset) Tick to let a member with open loans resign or be terminated, so the loans can be offset against the member's deposits and share capital. What the program checks and does: Active. The paid-up share capital must reach the minimum: the higher of Minimum paid-up share capital to activate a member on Cooperative Profile & Policies and the Minimum share capital to activate of the member type. A blank membership date is filled with the effective date, and a hold on the member is released. Resigned and Terminated. A member with open loans is refused unless the open-loans box is ticked. Deceased. The date of death is recorded and the member is put on hold with the reason "Deceased: claims by the beneficiaries only". For a resigned, terminated or deceased member, the member's name in Employees & Other Names is made inactive; it is active again when the member is reactivated. Deposits, loan releases and time deposit placements are refused for a suspended, resigned, terminated or deceased member. An applicant can already pay at the teller (for example the membership fee and the first share capital); a loan release or a time deposit needs an active member. A member who has resigned, been terminated or died is settled: the teller still receives loan payments, the loans can be paid from the member's own deposits on Loan Collection (paid by savings, with a supervisor's approval), and the share capital and deposits are paid out in full with Settle the accounts on the member's page ( Member Disbursement ), always with a supervisor's approval. A deceased member's claim is paid to the beneficiary or the estate named in Received by . To activate an applicant: Receive the membership fee and the share capital on Official Receipt (Member Collection) . Open the member and click the History and notes tab. Click Change status . Choose Active in New status and check the Effective date . Type the Reason and the Board resolution / reference . Click Change status . The program says "Status changed to Active." Hold and alert note A hold stops the member's transactions until it is released: "No deposit, withdrawal, payment or loan can be recorded." The Hold card on the History and notes tab shows "Not on hold." or the reason of the hold. To put a member on hold: click Put on hold on the Hold card, type the Reason (required) and click Save . To release the hold: click Release the hold , type the reason if you want, and click Save . Both need the Edit right on Member Information and are recorded in the audit trail. An alert note does not stop anything: it is a warning shown to the staff. Type it in Alert shown at the counter on Loan and savings grouping and save the member. Notes and the audit trail To add a note: on the History and notes tab, choose the Kind (Note, Phone call, Visit, Complaint), type the Note and click Add . The Notes list shows each note with its kind, date and time, and the user. Notes cannot be changed or removed. Audit trail of the member record shows the last 40 entries for the member: when, by whom, and what was done (created, changed, status changes, holds, notes, photo and signature uploads, prints) with the reason. Good to know Adding a member needs the Create right on Member Information; changing the profile, holds, notes and adding documents need the Edit right; removing a document needs Delete/Void; changing the status needs Approve on the Member Center. "Choose the member type." "Enter the last name and first name." or, for a joint account or an institution, "Enter the name of the joint account or institution." "The e-mail address is not valid." "Member number 100013 is already used." Leave the number blank to get the next one. "The beneficiaries' shares add up to more than 100 %" with the total. Correct the Share % of the beneficiaries. "You may only file members under your own branch." "The file is larger than 8 MB." and "Upload a JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP picture." for the photo and the signature. "Paid-up share capital is 500.00, below the minimum of 1,000.00 for activation. Collect the share capital first, or tick the waiver (recorded in the audit trail)." "The member still has 1 open loan(s) with a balance of 7,334.40. Settle them, or tick "allow with open loans" (for offsetting against deposits and share capital)." "Enter the reason for the hold." A user tied to a branch cannot open a member of another branch.

href="#pg-coop-member_statement" aria-label="Link to this section"> The statement of account shows a member's savings, share capital and time deposit accounts with their movements in a period, the loans with their payments, and the interest on share capital and patronage refund received. From the same page you print the statement, the member's ID card, the share capital certificate and a certificate of balances. Where to find it: Members & Others > Member Statement of Account, or the Statement button on Member Information . The statement of account of Mendoza, Ramon from 01/01/2026 to 10/11/2026 Showing a statement Field What to enter / what it means Member Type part of the name, the member number, or an account or loan number, and pick the member from the list. The statement shows at once. From, To The period. It starts as January 1 of this year to today. Change the dates and click Show . The statement shows the member panel, then: One table per savings, share capital and time deposit account , headed by the product and the account number: Date , Code (the transaction code), Particulars , OR / ref. , Withdrawals , Deposits and the running Balance . The first line is the Balance forwarded on the From date and the last line the balance on the To date. A deposit still clearing is marked "clearing". A time deposit account also lists its certificates (amount, rate, term, maturity value and status). A closed account with no balance and no movement is left out. One table per loan , headed by the product, the loan number, the amount released, the maturity date and the status: Date , Entry (with the OR number of a payment), Principal , Interest , Penalty and Principal balance . The release shows in brackets. The last line gives what is outstanding on the loan now: principal, interest and penalties. A paid, renewed, cancelled or written-off loan with no movement in the period is left out. Interest on share capital and patronage refund , when the member received any from a posted distribution whose period ends within the statement period: Batch , Kind , Period ending , Basis and Amount . The buttons Print , Share certificate , ID card and Certificate of balances appear when a member is shown and you have the Print/Export right on this page. Printing the statement Click Print . The statement opens as a printed page and the print dialog opens. It has the cooperative's heading, the title STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT , today's date and the period; the member's name, number and address; the accounts, loans and distributions as on the screen; the note "Please examine this statement and report any discrepancy to the cooperative within fifteen (15) days; otherwise it will be considered correct."; and the signature lines Prepared by (your name) and Certified correct (the bookkeeper named on Cooperative Profile & Policies). Each print of a statement is recorded in the audit trail. The ID card Click ID card (here or on Member Information). The card prints in two parts. The front has the cooperative's name, "Member identification", the photo (or the initials), the member's name, member number, member type and membership date, and the branch. The back has the date of birth, the address, the mobile number, "In case of emergency, contact the cooperative office.", the line for the member's signature with the specimen signature on file, and the name of the General Manager. The ID card is a controlled document: the first print is the original, and a reprint needs a reason and prints "Reissued (copy 1)" and so on (see Reprints of controlled documents ). The share capital certificate Click Share certificate . The certificate prints with the heading SHARE CAPITAL CERTIFICATE , its number and today's date; the wording of the Share capital certificate template (see Document Templates ), which states the member, the number of fully paid-up shares, the par value and the amount in words and figures as of today; the amount in large figures; and the signature lines Chairperson , Secretary / Treasurer and General Manager with the names from Cooperative Profile & Policies. The number of shares is the paid-up share capital divided by the par value per share, in whole shares. The par value is the member's own; if the member has none, the Par value per share of the share capital product; if that is blank too, the one on Cooperative Profile & Policies . The first print of a member's certificate takes the next Share capital certificate number of Document Numbering (SC-000001 in the sample data). Every later print for the same member keeps that number. A reprint needs a reason and is marked "COPY 1 (reprint)" and so on. It shows the paid-up share capital on the day it is printed. Certificate of balances A certificate of balances certifies a member's share capital and deposit balances, and the loans, on a date the member asks for, for example for a visa or a loan with another lender. Each certificate is a new document with its own number. Field What to enter / what it means Balances as of The date of the balances. It starts as today and cannot be a future date. Purpose Required. What the member needs the certificate for, for example "loan application with another lender". It prints on the certificate. To issue a certificate of balances: Show the member's statement. Click Certificate of balances . Check the Balances as of date and type the Purpose . Click Issue and print . The certificate opens with the print dialog. Back to the statement above it returns to the statement. The certificate has: The heading CERTIFICATE OF BALANCES , the next number of the Certificate of balances series (BC-000003 is next in the sample data) and the date of issue. The wording of the Certificate of balances template: the member, member number, member type, membership date and status, and the as-of date. A table of the share capital and deposit accounts (savings and time deposits) open on that date, with Account , Account no. and Balance on that date, and the lines Total paid-up share capital and Total deposits . A table of the loans released by that date that still had a principal balance: Loan , Released , Maturity and Principal balance , with Total loan principal outstanding , or "No outstanding loan.". The Past due today column, only when the date is today: what is due and unpaid on each open loan today. The note then says "Past due amounts include the interest and penalties due today." For an earlier date the column is left out and the note says "Loan balances are principal; interest is charged by the schedule and is not included." "This certification is issued on (date) upon the request of the member for (purpose).", "Not valid without the seal of the Cooperative or with erasures or alterations.", and the signature lines Prepared by (your name), Certified correct (the bookkeeper) and Noted (the General Manager). Each certificate is recorded in the Document Print History report with its number, the as-of date and the purpose, and in the audit trail. To give the member another copy later, issue a new certificate: it takes a new number. Reprints of controlled documents The ID card, the share capital certificate and the vouchers and receipts printed from the cooperative pages are controlled documents. Every print is recorded in the Document Print History report: The first print is the Original . It prints without asking anything. Any later print is a reprint. The program first shows Reprint ... : "This share capital certificate was already printed 1 time. A reprint is marked as a copy and recorded in the audit trail." Type the Reason for the reprint and click Reprint , or Cancel . The reprint is marked as a numbered copy ("COPY 1 (reprint)" on certificates and vouchers, "Reissued (copy 1)" on the ID card), and the reason is kept with it. Printing a controlled document needs the Print/Export right on the page it is printed from. Good to know "Enter an as-of date that is not in the future." "Enter the purpose the member asked the certificate for." "Issue a new certificate of balances from the member statement." appears when a certificate page is opened again outside the session that issued it. "That member belongs to another branch." A user tied to a branch sees the statements of that branch's members only.

href="#pg-coop-vouchers" aria-label="Link to this section"> A cooperative journal voucher records an adjustment between the members' accounts and the general ledger, with the member on each line: for example moving an amount posted to the wrong member's savings, or a charge to a member's share capital. A line on a member's savings or share capital account changes that account's ledger as well as the general ledger. The page also lists the cooperative journal vouchers and loan release vouchers already posted, so they can be opened, printed and voided. Where to find it: no longer in the menu: the cooperative asked for it to be taken out in version 39, as not needed. The page stays for the vouchers already on file: the number of a cooperative journal voucher (CJV) opens it from Find , the General Ledger, a member's ledger or the reports, to be viewed, printed or voided. A correction between members' accounts is made with a debit or credit memo on Savings Account Transaction , and any other entry on Make Journal Entries . Cooperative Vouchers from 10/01/2026 to 10/11/2026 The voucher list The list shows the cooperative journal vouchers (CJV numbers) and the loan release vouchers (LR numbers) of the period. Besides the vouchers made on this page, it has the cooperative journal vouchers the other cooperative pages post, for example loan adjustments, waivers and write-offs, interest postings and accruals, batch deductions, year-end distributions, the net surplus allocation, the cash over or short of a closed teller shift, and opening balance imports. Type the From and To dates (this month to today at first), and in Find part of a voucher number, a member's name or number, or the memo, then click Show . The columns are Date , No. , Member , Memo , Mode , Amount and Status (Posted or Void). The footer gives the number of vouchers and their total, voids excluded. Up to 500 vouchers are listed. Click the number to open a voucher. A loan release voucher opens on Loan Release . From version 33 a loan is released through Banking (a Cash Voucher or a Check Voucher): those vouchers are on Loan Release Vouchers . A saved voucher The voucher shows Voucher (type and number), Date , Member , Branch / class , Reference , Memo , Approved by , Recorded (when and by whom), Status and the Total ; the General ledger entry ( Account , Name , Memo , Debit , Credit ); and Member ledgers , the rows it wrote to the members' savings accounts and loans with the balance after each. A voided voucher shows when, by whom and why it was voided. The buttons are Print , Void and Back . Print prints the JOURNAL VOUCHER with the cooperative's heading, the number and date, the member and reference, the account lines, the memo, and the signature lines Prepared by , Checked by (the bookkeeper), Approved by (the approver, or the General Manager) and Received by . A voided voucher prints with VOID across it. The voucher is a controlled document: a reprint needs a reason (see Reprints of controlled documents ). Making a journal voucher Click New journal voucher (it needs the Create right). The form New cooperative journal voucher has: Field What to enter / what it means Date The date of the voucher. A past date is allowed only within the back-dating days of Cooperative Profile & Policies, or with the permission to back-date; a future date is refused. Reference An outside reference, for example a memo number. Branch The branch of the voucher. Its class goes on every ledger line. Explanation Required. What the voucher is for. It is the memo of the voucher and of every line that has no memo of its own. The lines (at least two): Column What to enter / what it means Member savings / share capital account A member's savings or share capital account (number, member and product). The line posts to the general ledger account of the account's product, and to the member's account as a credit memo (CM) for a credit or a debit memo (DM) for a debit. or GL account Any other account of the chart of accounts, when the line is not on a member's savings or share capital account. Member (for a member ledger account) The member, for a GL account that keeps a member ledger (an account marked With SL). It is required on those accounts. Memo The description of the line. Debit, Credit The amount, on one side only. Add a line adds a row. Under the lines, Debits and Credits add up the lines; they must be equal before you post. To make a cooperative journal voucher: On the voucher list (open a cooperative journal voucher and click Vouchers ), click New journal voucher . Check the Date , type the Reference , choose the Branch and type the Explanation . On each line, choose the member's account in Member savings / share capital account , or a GL account (with the Member where needed), and type the Debit or the Credit . Check that Debits equals Credits . If you do not have the Approve right on this page, open Supervisor approval and let the supervisor type their username and password, or type an approval code (see Supervisor approval ). Click Post voucher and confirm Post this journal voucher? . The saved voucher opens. Example A deposit of ₱1,000.00 was posted to the savings account of the wrong member. The voucher has two lines: the wrong member's savings account, debit ₱1,000.00 (a DM on that account), and the right member's savings account, credit ₱1,000.00 (a CM on that account). The general ledger lines cancel out on the savings deposits account, each with the member's name. What it records Account Debit Credit Each debit line: the product account of the member's savings or share capital account (for example 2300 Savings Deposits), or the GL account of the line Line amount Each credit line: the product account of the member's savings or share capital account, or the GL account of the line Line amount The voucher is a Cooperative Journal Voucher numbered from the Cooperative journal voucher series of Document Numbering (CJV-000009 is next in the sample data). Each line carries the member's name and the class of the branch. A line on a member's account also writes a CM or DM entry to that account's ledger, with the line's memo. Voiding a voucher A void keeps the voucher on file marked VOID and reverses the general ledger and the member ledgers together. Open the voucher, click Void , type the Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) and click Void with the voucher number. A supervisor approves in the same form unless you have the Approve right on Cooperative Vouchers. The Void button needs the Delete/Void right. When a voucher cannot be voided, the Void button is greyed and the voucher shows "This voucher cannot be voided now:" with the reason. A void is refused when: the voucher brought opening balances over from the previous system: "Correct an opening balance with an adjusting entry (Loan Adjustments, a debit / credit memo), not by voiding the import."; it posted a year-end distribution batch, or the net surplus allocation of a fiscal year: these are reversed with an adjusting entry; it released a loan that already has payments or adjustments ("Void those first, or restructure the loan."), or a loan that is paid, written off or renewed; voiding it would overdraw a member's savings account: "Void the later withdrawals first."; it placed a time deposit that has since matured or been paid, or that has interest accruals posted; it is a receipt of a teller shift that is already closed, and you do not have the Approve right on Teller Shift & Cash Count ; a check deposited or received on it was cleared or returned since: "Its check was cleared or returned on voucher ... Void that voucher first."; it is dated on or before the closing date, unless you may change closed periods (see The closing date ). Good to know "Enter the explanation of the voucher." "A voucher has at least two lines." "The voucher does not balance: debits ..., credits ..., difference ...." Correct the amounts so the debits equal the credits. "A line is either a debit or a credit, not both." "Choose the account of each line." "Account ... keeps a member ledger: choose the member on its line." The line is on an account marked With SL and has no member. Choose the member, or use the member's account in the first column. "Loan balances are changed on Loans > Loan Adjustments, so the loan ledger and the schedule follow." A loans receivable account cannot be used on this voucher; use Loan Adjustments . "A member on the voucher belongs to another branch." A debit on a member's savings account cannot take more than the available balance: "Insufficient available balance on ...". "Back-dated entries beyond 0 day(s) need the "can record back-dated member transactions" permission." and "The transaction date cannot be in the future." "Supervisor approval is required: cooperative journal voucher. Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below, or type a one-time approval code."

href="#pg-coop-import" aria-label="Link to this section"> When the cooperative starts using the program, this page brings over the members and their balances from the previous system as of a cut-off date: the members, the savings and share capital balances, the time deposit placements and the loan balances. Each file is checked first, row by row, without saving anything. The import then saves every row in one go, with one journal voucher that puts the same totals on the general ledger control accounts, so the member ledgers and the general ledger agree from the first day. Where to find it: Members & Others > Opening Balances Import. The Opening Balances Import page with the four imports of the sample data as of 09/30/2026 What can be imported Import in this order: members, then savings and share capital, time deposits and loans. The Columns card on the page lists the columns of each kind, the required ones in bold, and has a sample link that downloads a CSV file with the header and one example row. Import Required columns What it creates Members member_no, last_name, first_name One individual member per row. member_type and branch are codes; status is active (the default) or applicant; membership_date is the cut-off date when blank. No voucher is posted. Savings and share capital balances member_no, product, balance One account per row of the savings or share capital product (its code), with an opening balance entry (code OB) dated on the cut-off date. An empty account of the same product is used if the member has one; otherwise a new account is opened. account_no, opened_on and passbook_no are optional. Time deposit placements member_no, product, principal, rate, placement_date, term_days One placement per row. rate is in % a year; maturity_action is payout (the default), renew_principal, renew_all or credit_savings; accrued_interest is the interest already booked as payable at the cut-off. Loan balances member_no, product, principal_balance, first_due, remaining_term One loan per row with a new schedule: the principal balance over the remaining term (months, or days when term_unit is days) from the first_due date. A first_due before the cut-off makes those amortizations past due. mode and rate default to the loan product's. interest_balance replaces the scheduled interest of add-on loans; accrued_interest is interest receivable already in the general ledger. The file is a CSV file (comma, semicolon or tab separated) whose first line is the header. Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD. Step by step Field What to enter / what it means Import What the file holds: Members , Savings and share capital balances , Time deposit placements or Loan balances . Cut-off date The date of the balances. It starts as the last day of last month. The opening entries and the voucher are dated on it. Offset account Shown for balances, placements and loans: the account that takes the other side of the voucher. "Normally Opening Balance Equity, cleared when the opening trial balance is entered." CSV file The file to check (CSV, TXT or TSV, up to 10 MB). or paste the rows (first line is the header) Instead of a file, paste the rows copied from a spreadsheet. To import opening balances: Open Members & Others > Opening Balances Import . Choose what to Import , type the Cut-off date , and for balances check the Offset account . Choose the CSV file , or paste the rows. Click Check . Nothing is saved by checking. Read the result: the heading gives the number of rows and how many have errors. Each row shows its line number, its first columns and, under Check , "ok" or what is wrong. Rows with errors are red. For balances, General ledger effect shows the debit or credit each control account will receive. If any row has an error, correct the file and check it again: "Correct the rows marked in red in the file and check it again. Nothing has been saved." When every row is ok, click Import with the number of rows and confirm. All the rows are saved together, or none. Run the Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation (the SL vs GL reconciliation button) to check that the ledgers agree. The Imports done list shows each import: When (and by whom), What (and the file name), Cut-off , Rows , Amount and the Voucher with the offset account. Click the voucher number to open it. What it records Each import of balances, placements or loans posts one Cooperative Journal Voucher dated on the cut-off date, with the memo "Opening balances:" and the kind. Each member row is a line with the member's name: Account Debit Credit The account of the savings, share capital or time deposit product Balance or principal The accrued interest account of the time deposit product (or the default interest payable on deposits) Accrued interest The receivable account of the loan product (or the default loans receivable) Principal balance The default interest receivable on loans Accrued interest The offset account (for example 3900 Opening Balance Equity) The difference, on the side that balances the voucher A loan's interest_balance and penalty_balance go to the loan's own ledger; the general ledger receives only the principal balance and the accrued interest. Important An import cannot be voided. Correct an opening balance with an adjusting entry, for example on Loan Adjustments or with a debit or credit memo on the member's account. Good to know Checking a file needs the Create right on this page. Importing needs the Approve right on this page (or the Administrator role): "The file is ready. Importing needs the Approve right on this page." Every row is checked again when you click Import . If the checked file is no longer in your session: "The checked file is no longer in your session. Check it again." "Missing column(s): ..." The header lacks a required column. Typical row errors: "member no. 100101 already exists", "member no. 100101 is not on file (import the members first)", "product 01 is not a savings / deposit product", "time deposits are imported as placements (choose Time deposit placements)", "opened after the cut-off date", "the member already has a Regular Savings account with transactions". Balances can only be imported for active, applicant or suspended members. The voucher is refused when the books are closed through the cut-off date, unless you may change closed periods.

href="#pg-coop-consolidated_import" aria-label="Link to this section"> One file for the members and everything they have: the members, their savings and share capital accounts with their balances, their loans with what was paid on them, their water-service account and the unpaid balances of their water bills. It does in one file what Import Member , Import Savings , Import Loans and Upload Bill Balances do one at a time, with the same checks and the same entries. A member may have only savings, savings and loans, savings and bill balances, or all of them. Where to find it: Members & Others > Consolidated Import, after Opening Balances Import. A Consolidated Import button is also on the Member Center, Import members, Import savings, Import loans and Water Billing > Upload Bill Balances. Reading, checking and correcting a file needs the Create right on Consolidated Import. Saving it needs, besides, the rights of each part it holds: Approve on Member Information (the members are made Active), Approve on the Savings Account Center, Approve on the Loan Accounts Center, Create on Upload Bill Balances, Create on Water Service Accounts (accounts opened) and Create on Fixed Share Capital Billing. Consolidated Import: a file under review, with the line in red and its cell The file: no fixed format The file is a CSV file (comma, semicolon or tab separated) or an Excel workbook (.xlsx). Its first row names the columns, in any order and with your own names; only the columns of what you import are needed and the others may be left out. The page recognises the names of the four imports (member_no, last_name, savings_code, principal, billing_type ...), the headings in words ("Member No", "Date of Birth", "Savings Balance", "Release Date", "One-Time Balance") and the usual other names (Surname, Principal, Rate Code, Water Account, Name ...). A column with a whole name ("Dela Cruz, Juan S." or "Juan S. Dela Cruz") is split into the last, first and middle name when those columns are not in the file. A member's accounts may be in either layout, or both in one file: One row per member. The member and the member's accounts across the row. A second account of the same kind has the columns numbered: savings2_code , savings2_balance , loan2_principal ... (or savings_code_2 , "Savings Code 2"); a column name written twice is the next account. The bill balances may be given as in Upload Bill Balances, a column for each billing type ( recurring_balance , installment_balance , one_time_balance , share_capital_balance with their charge categories). Rows under the member. The member on its row, then one row per account with the member's columns left blank: a row with no member name and no member no. adds its accounts to the member above it. A row with the same member no., or the same name and date of birth, is the same member (its details fill what the first row left blank). Part Columns What it makes Member The columns of Import Member (member_no, last_name, first_name, middle_name, birth_date, member_type, membership_date, barangay, city, province and the other details). A member, Active. A member no. already on file is that member: only the accounts and balances of the file are added and the member's details on file are not changed. Water service water_account_no; or water_rate_code and water_pipe_size (with water_zone, water_sequence, water_connection_date). The member becomes the same person as the holder of the water-service account named (the names must match), or a water-service account is opened for the member. The member's bill balances go to it. Fixed share capital billing fsc_amount (with fsc_frequency, fsc_posting_day, fsc_start_date, fsc_term_days). The member on Fixed Share Capital Billing for that amount, on the member's share capital account of the file, from the day after the cut-off date unless a start date is given. Needed for a fixed share capital balance of a new member. Savings (any number) savings_code and savings_balance; savings_account_no, savings_passbook_no, savings_opened_on, savings_cut_off_date, savings_txn_code. A savings or share capital account, Active, its balance entered on the cut-off date with the savings transaction code (as Import Savings). Loans (any number) loan_name, loan_principal, loan_term, loan_mode, loan_amort_type, loan_rate, loan_release_date, loan_principal_paid, loan_interest_paid, loan_penalties_paid; loan_no, loan_pn_no, loan_first_due and the others of Import Loans. A loan, Active, with its schedule and what was paid up to the cut-off date (as Import Loans). Bill balances (any number) bill_type, bill_charge_code, bill_balance; bill_date, bill_due_date, bill_installments, bill_payment_mode, bill_share_capital_account. A recurring, installment, one-time or fixed share capital bill on the member's water-service account, with its invoice (as Upload Bill Balances). The card The format on the page lists every column by part, the ones a part needs in bold, and has the Excel and CSV templates of both layouts (the Excel template has a second sheet explaining every column). A file may have up to 60,000 rows and 150 MB. Reading, reviewing and saving a file Open Members & Others > Consolidated Import , choose the file and click Read the file for review . The file is sent in pieces and its rows are kept in the database (a bar shows the progress); nothing is saved to the members, savings, loans or bills yet. The page of the file opens. Columns of the file says how many columns were recognised. Open it to see what each column holds, with an example from the file, and change it: choose what a column holds (or Not imported ) and, for a savings, loan or bill column, which account of the member it is (1st, 2nd ...). Make the lines again with these columns makes the lines again from the rows of the file. The choice is remembered: the next file with the same column names is read the same way. Check Values for the blank cells : the Cut-off date (the date of the savings balances, the loans' totals paid and the bill balances), the Savings transaction code , the Loan balancing account , the Class of the bill balances (their journal entries need one), the Installments left and the Installment payment mode . A cell of the file overrides them. Use these values and check again keeps them and checks every line again. Every line is checked, in steps, with a bar: each member, savings account, loan and bill balance is a line of the review. The four boxes above the lines give the number of lines of each kind, how many have a problem and their totals; click one (or its tab) to see its lines, 50 a page, with the member of each account and the row of the file it came from. A line with a problem is in red: the reason in red under it and the cell it names in red. Correct the cell by typing in it or choosing from its list: the member is checked again at once with all its lines. Remove a line with (a member line takes its savings, loans and bill balances with it); Put back the last brings it back, and Removed in the list on the right shows the lines removed, each with Put back . Only lines with a problem and Find in the lines narrow the list. shows the other columns of a line. When no line is in red, click Save N members to the database and confirm. The members are saved a few at a time, each member with all its lines in one transaction, every line checked again first: the members, their water-service accounts, their savings accounts with their balances, their fixed share capital billings, their loans and their bill balances. Keep the page open until it ends. If saving stops (a member no. taken in the meantime, a lost connection), the members saved stay saved, nothing of the member that stopped it is saved, its line shows the reason in red: correct it or remove it and click Go on saving . The page of the file then says what was saved, and each line what it became (the member no., the account no., the loan no., the upload of the bill balances). Run the Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation afterwards. The Files read list on the first page shows each file with its number (CI-00001), the rows, its state (Under review, Being saved, Saved), who read it and when; Open goes back to it. A file under review stays until it is saved or closed ( Close the file : nothing of it is saved). What is checked Each member with the checks of Import Member (the required details, the dates, the member type, the branch, the same member no. or the same person on file); each savings account with those of Import Savings, each loan with those of Import Loans and each bill balance with those of Upload Bill Balances, as of a member not on file yet when the file makes it. The file as a whole: the same member no. on two member lines, the same person (name and date of birth) under two member nos., the same savings account no. or loan no. on two members, the same water-service account for two members. The water-service account: it exists and is active, it is not another member's, its holder's name is the member's; or the rate code and pipe size of the account to open are known and have a complete tariff on Water Meter Rates ("Rate code "A" is 2 rate codes ...: write its name"). A bill balance needs the member's water-service account. The fixed share capital billing: its amount, frequency, posting day, start date and term, the member's one share capital account it bills; a fixed share capital balance of a new member needs fsc_amount ("... is not on Fixed Share Capital Billing: give the fixed share capital amount (fsc_amount) on the member's line") and a date before the start of the billing. Above the lines: a missing savings transaction code, balancing account or cut-off date, a cut-off date after today, and the class when there are recurring, installment or one-time balances. Good to know Accounts in a row before any member, or member details with no name, make a member line in red so nothing of the file is lost: remove it, or complete it. An existing member is named by its member no. on the line; a person on file under another number is in red with that number ("... is already a member: 100201. To add the accounts to that member, enter member no. 100201 on this line."). The entries are those of the four imports: the savings balances with the savings transaction code against its GL account (one voucher per cut-off date and code in each group of members saved), the loans against the balancing account, the recurring, installment and one-time balances each with its invoice against 39999 Legacy Water Balances Clearing, a fixed share capital balance with no journal entry. A file is saved once. Reading the same file again shows every account already on file in red. On a phone each line of the review is a card with its cells as fields.

href="#pg-coop-profile" aria-label="Link to this section"> The cooperative's registration details, the names of the signatories that print on documents, and the policies the cooperative pages follow: the minimum share capital, back-dating, approval thresholds, teller rules, account number formats, loan payment rules, alerts and the year-end distribution percentages. Where to find it: Members & Others > Cooperative Profile & Policies. Cooperative Profile & Policies of the sample cooperative The settings Registration Setting What it means and where it is used Registered name (as in the CDA certificate) Printed at the top of every cooperative document and on the ID card. Blank uses the company name. CDA registration number Printed under the name on the cooperative documents as "CDA Registration No.". Type of cooperative Credit, Multi-Purpose, Consumers, Producers, Marketing, Service, Agrarian Reform, Cooperative Bank, Electric, Transport, Workers, Housing or Other. Category Primary, Secondary or Tertiary, as registered. Fiscal year ends (MM-DD) Usually 12-31. Used for the fiscal year on Net Surplus Allocation, CAPR Data Preparation & Export and Compliance Tracking. Division name printed under the cooperative name on documents Printed under the cooperative's name at the top of every cooperative document, for example Savings and Credit Division. Leave it blank to print nothing. Signatories Setting What it means and where it is used General Manager Prints on the ID card, the share capital and time deposit certificates, as Noted on the certificate of balances, and as Approved by on vouchers that have no approver. Chairperson of the Board Prints on the share capital certificate and the CDA reports. Treasurer Prints on the share capital and time deposit certificates and on the teller's cash count. Credit Committee chair / Loans officer Prints as Noted by (Credit Committee) on the credit investigation. Bookkeeper / Accountant Prints as Checked by on vouchers and as Certified correct on the statement of account and the certificate of balances. Membership and share capital Setting What it means and where it is used Minimum paid-up share capital to activate a member Checked when a member is made active on Member Information. The member type can set a higher minimum; the higher one applies. Zero means no minimum. Par value per share The par value a new member starts with (subscribed shares times par value is the subscribed capital). On the share capital certificate it is used for a member with no par value of their own when the share capital product has none either. Membership fee When an applicant has not paid a membership fee yet, the official receipt for the applicant starts with a Membership fee line of this amount. Teller and transactions Setting What it means and where it is used Cash transactions need an open teller shift Yes: official receipts and member disbursements (savings deposits and withdrawals and loan collections included) and loan releases in cash are refused until the user opens a teller shift on Teller Shift & Cash Count : "Open your teller shift first (Teller > Teller Shift & Cash Count)." Days a transaction may be back-dated without the special permission Checked on every member transaction: official receipts and disbursements, savings transfers, time deposits, loan releases, adjustments, waivers, restructures and write-offs, interest and dormancy postings, batch deductions, distributions and cooperative journal vouchers. A date further back needs the special permission Cooperative: can record back-dated member transactions . Zero: only users with that permission may back-date. A receipt above this needs supervisor approval An official receipt or a deposit (on Official Receipt, Savings Account Transaction or Loan Collection) above this total needs a supervisor's approval, unless the user has the Approve right on that page. Zero = no limit. A withdrawal above this needs supervisor approval A member disbursement or savings withdrawal above this total needs a supervisor's approval, unless the user has the Approve right on that page. This is on top of each role's own limit, the special permission Cooperative: max savings withdrawal without supervisor approval . Zero = only the role limits apply. Cash over/short a teller may post without approval When a teller shift is closed on Teller Shift & Cash Count, a difference between the cash counted and the cash expected that is larger than this needs a supervisor's approval, unless the user has the Approve right on that page. Zero: every difference needs a supervisor. Savings account number format How new savings account numbers are built: {BRANCH} the 2-digit branch, {BRANCHC} the branch code as written, {MEMBER} the member number, {PRODUCT} the 2-digit product code, {PRODUCTC} the product code as written, {SEQ} the next Savings account number of Document Numbering. Reference layout: {BRANCH}{MEMBER}{PRODUCT}1. When the number is already used (a second account of the same product), -2, -3 and so on is added. Loan account number format How new loan numbers are built: {BRANCH}, {BRANCHC}, {PRODUCT} (the product code), {SEQ} (the next Loan account number) and {YEAR}. Reference layout: {BRANCH}-{PRODUCT}-{SEQ}, for example 02-6-0000005. Loans Setting What it means and where it is used Payment allocation order How a loan payment is split when no one splits it by hand: Penalty, interest, then principal , Interest, penalty, then principal , Interest, principal, then penalty or Principal, interest, then penalty . Users with the special permission Cooperative: can override the payment allocation (penalty, interest, principal) on a loan collection may split a payment themselves. Compute penalties when a payment is received Yes: the penalty up to the payment date is worked out when a payment is received. No: only the penalties posted by the batch run (Post Loan Penalties & Interest Accrual) are collected. Remind of amortizations due within (days) The cooperative alerts on the Home page count the loans with an amortization due within this many days. Alerts Setting What it means and where it is used Time deposits maturing within (days) The Home page alert counts the time deposits maturing within this many days, or already matured. Accounts turning dormant within (days) The Home page alert counts the savings accounts that become dormant within this many days. Documents, collateral and insurance expiring within (days) The Home page alerts count the member documents, and the loan collateral documents and insurance, expiring within this many days or already expired. Year-end distribution (defaults; confirm against your bylaws and the General Assembly resolution) Setting What it means and where it is used Reserve fund (% of net surplus), Education and training fund (%), Part of the education fund due to the union / federation (%), Community development fund (%), Optional fund (%) The percentages a new year starts with on Net Surplus Allocation , where they can be changed for that year. The Statement of Operations also shows the reserve, education and training, community development and optional funds at these percentages, for information. Each is from 0 to 100, and the reserve, education, community development and optional funds together may not be more than 100 %. Interest on share capital basis Average daily balance or Ending balance : the basis a new interest on share capital batch starts with. To change the settings: change the boxes and click Save settings . The program says how many settings were saved, and each change is recorded in the audit trail with the old and new value. Changing the settings needs the Edit right on this page; other users see them greyed. Good to know "Enter the fiscal year end as MM-DD, for example 12-31." "Reserve fund (% of net surplus): enter a percentage from 0 to 100." and "The statutory percentages add up to more than 100 %." The company address, TIN and logo are set on Company, Security & Closing Date ; the wording of the promissory notes, certificates and letters on Document Templates .

href="#pg-coop-branches" aria-label="Link to this section"> The cooperative's head office and branches. Every member belongs to a branch, every branch posts under its own class (so the reports by class are the branch reports), and each branch can have its own series of official receipt numbers. Where to find it: Members & Others > Branches. The Branches page with the head office and the Poblacion branch, and the form for a new branch The list shows Code , Branch (with "head office" beside the head office, and the address), Class (reports) , OR prefix ("(none)" when there is none), Members , Users and Edit . An inactive branch is greyed. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Code Required, up to 10 letters, numbers or dashes, for example 01. It must not be used by another branch. It is part of the savings and loan account numbers ({BRANCH} uses its digits). Name Required, for example Poblacion Branch. Address, Phone, Email The branch's contact details. Class used on its postings The class every posting of the branch carries. Leave it at Make a class with the branch name and the program uses the class with the branch's name, or creates it. Official receipt prefix Starts every official receipt number of the branch, for example P for P000123, so each branch keeps its own series. No two branches may have the same prefix. Head office Tick for the head office. Only one branch is the head office: ticking it on one branch takes it off the others. Active Untick for a branch that is no longer used. An inactive branch is not offered for new members and vouchers. To add a branch: fill the New branch form and click Save branch , or Save branch & New to add another. To change a branch: click Edit on its row, change the fields and click Save branch . Branches cannot be deleted. Each change is recorded in the audit trail. Good to know Users are given a branch in Cooperative branch on User Accounts , with their teller cash account. A user with a branch works only with the members of that branch, their accounts and vouchers, and sees that branch only on the member reports. Administrators, and roles with the special permission Cooperative: sees every branch regardless of the branch on the user account , see every branch. "Enter the branch code and name." "The branch code uses letters, numbers and dashes only (it is part of the account numbers)." "Branch code 01 is already used." and "Another branch already uses the official receipt prefix P."

href="#pg-coop-lists" aria-label="Link to this section"> The pick lists of the cooperative pages: the member types with their minimum share capital, the clusters and segmentation of members, the member groupings (account classes, account groups, address sub-groups and savings groups), and the lists of loan purposes, collateral types, member document types and ID types. Every entry can be added, renamed, switched off and deleted; an entry still used by a member (or a water-service account) is not deleted: the page says how many use it, and switching it off stops offering it. Where to find it: Members & Others > Member Types, Clusters & Other Lists. The Member types tab with the regular and associate member types of the sample cooperative The tabs Tab What it holds and where it is used Member types The Member type of each member, for example Regular or Associate - Individual. The list shows Code , Member type , Kind , Regular , Min. share capital and Members . Clusters The Cluster on a member's Membership tab, also a filter of the Member Master List and of the distribution batches. A cluster can belong to one branch or to Any branch . Segmentation The Segmentation on a member's Membership tab. A loan product can be limited to the members of one segmentation, and distribution batches can be limited to one. Loan purposes The Purpose of a loan application. Collateral types The Type of a collateral on a loan application. Account classes, Account groups, Address sub-groups, Savings groups The member groupings on the Grouping tab of Member Information, and the Grouping filter of the Member Master List. Renaming an entry renames it on the members that have it. The Address sub-group is also shown, filtered and set (for selected accounts at once) on Water Billing > Water Service Accounts, and its list is kept on Water Billing > Service & Materials > Address Sub-groups too, or from the link Add, edit or delete sub-groups under every Address sub-group box (Member Information and Water Service Accounts): a renamed sub-group is changed on the members and the water-service accounts that have it; one in use cannot be deleted, but it can be switched off. Member document types The Kind of a document on a member's Documents tab. ID types The kinds of identification documents the cooperative accepts. Fields A member type has: Field What to enter / what it means Code Required and not used by another type, for example REG. The code is what the Members import uses in its member_type column. Name Required, for example Regular. Kind Individual , Joint account or Institutional : the kind of member the type is for. Minimum share capital to activate The paid-up share capital a member of this type needs before being made active. When the minimum on Cooperative Profile & Policies is higher, that one applies. Regular member (votes, may be elected) Ticked for regular members, unticked for associate members. The CDA report figures count regular and associate members by this tick. Order The position of the type in the lists. Active Untick to stop using the type. A cluster has a Name and a Branch ; a segmentation a Name ; an entry of the other lists a Name (not used twice on the same list), a Note and an Order . All have Active . To add an entry: click the tab, fill the form on the right and click Save . To change one: click Edit on its row, change it and click Save . Adding needs the Create right, changing the Edit right. Nothing is deleted on this page: an entry in use is switched off (not active) rather than deleted, so old records keep their names. Each change is recorded in the audit trail. Messages: "Enter the name.", "Enter the code.", "That code is already used." and "That name is already on the list."

href="#pg-coop-passbooks" aria-label="Link to this section"> This is the Passbook Type Setup of the former program, with the design of each passbook. A passbook type is either a savings passbook or a loan passbook : each kind has its own design, its own header and its own columns. The savings and share capital products choose a savings passbook type, the loan products a loan passbook type, and Passbook Printing prints with it. Where to find it: Members & Others > Passbook Types (Setup). Passbook Types on Passbook Printing opens the type of the passbook shown. The Loan Passbook on Passbook Types: the Passbook Type Setup (margins in tups, Start Line Skip 13, No. of Line Skip 2, Max Lines 29) and the design of the body, lines 13 and 14 skipped The list of Passbook types shows the Type ID , the Name and description, the Kind (Savings or Loan) and Used by (the products that use it). Click a type to open it; New savings passbook and New loan passbook start a type of that kind with the set-up and the design of the former program. Passbook Type Setup Every measurement is in tups (twips), as in the former program: 1 inch = 1,440 tups (1 cm = 567). Each is a whole number from 0 to 30,000. Field What to enter / what it means Passbook Information: Type ID, Name, Description, Kind, Active The name is required and must not be used by another type. Kind : Savings passbook or Loan passbook ; it cannot change once a product or an account uses the type. Untick Active for a type no longer used. Cover: Top, Left Where the inside cover starts printing (Print Passbook Cover). The fields of the cover are placed from here. Header: Top, Left The top margin and the left margin of the passbook header: where the header starts printing on a page. Footer: Top, Left Where the footer prints (Print Passbook Footer, and the foot of a full page when the footer is set to print there). Passbook Body: Top, Left The top margin and the left margin of the passbook body: where line 1 prints. Interval The distance from one entry to the next (275 tups is about 1/5 inch). Line 5, for example, prints at Body Top plus 4 intervals. Start Line Skip The first line never printed on (the centre fold of the passbook), or 0 when no line is skipped. Printing always starts on line 1, so it is 2 or more. No. of Line Skip How many lines are skipped from Start Line Skip. With 13 and 2, lines 13 and 14 are left blank: after line 12 the next entry prints on line 15. With 12 and 1, line 12 is left blank and printing resumes on line 13. Max Lines The last line of a page. The entry after it goes to line 1 of the next page, after the header. Passbook size, Page width, Page height The size of an open passbook page: choose one of the sizes (4.5 x 7, 4.75 x 6.75, 5 x 7, 6 x 8 inches, 8.5 x 6 inches, or letter paper for a test on plain paper) or type the width and height. One design fits any size: every field is placed in tups. Font, Characters per inch, Font size (pt) Dot matrix (Courier New) or Arial ; the characters per inch of the dot-matrix printer (10, 12, 15, 17 or 20; 17 and 20 are the condensed print of the passbooks of the former program), or As the font size ; the size from 6 to 16 points. Header prints On a new page, before line 1 (as the former program), With every printing , or Never (preprinted) . Footer at the foot of a full page Ticked, when a page is full and entries continue on the next page, the footer prints at the foot of the full page. Under the Passbook Body, a line in words says which lines of a page print, for example "Printing starts on line 1. A page prints lines 1 to 12 and 15 to 29; lines 13 and 14 are skipped (after line 12 the next entry prints on line 15). After line 29, the next entry goes to line 1 of the next page, after the header." It follows the numbers as you type them. The design: cover, header, body and footer Design of the savings passbook (or of the loan passbook) replaces the cover, header, body and footer templates of the former program.
