The Official Receipt List of 10/01/2026 to 10/19/2026: the official receipts and a member disbursement made before version 39 (MCV-000001) To find a receipt: type the From and To dates (the first of the month to today by default), type part of the number, the member's name, the member no. or the memo in Find , and click Show . The columns are Date , No. (the OR or voucher number), Member (with the member no.), Memo , Mode (Cash, Check, Bank or Savings), Amount and Status (Posted or Void; a void line is greyed). The footer counts the vouchers and totals the amounts: "4 voucher(s), voids excluded from the total". Up to 500 lines are shown; a user limited to a branch sees that branch only. New official receipt and New disbursement start a new one.

href="#s-teller-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Teller reports are listed under Teller > Reports in the sidebar and in the Teller card of the Report Center . The common report tools ( Refresh , Print / PDF , Export to spreadsheet , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize and clicking a number to open the transaction) are explained in Working with reports .

href="#pg-rpt-teller_journal" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every official receipt and member disbursement of a period, one line each, in the order they were made. Use it to go over a teller's day. Where to find it: Teller > Reports > Teller Transaction Journal. Filters: Dates ( Today by default), From , To , Teller , Kind (Official receipts or Disbursements) and Branch . The columns: Date , Time , Teller , Receipt / voucher (click it to open the voucher), Kind (OR or CV), Member , Mode , Received , Paid out and Status ("VOID", or "Back entry" for a back-dated receipt). Voided receipts stay on the list marked VOID and are left out of the totals. The report also offers the columns Drawer and Shift , hidden at first; see Modifying a report .

href="#pg-rpt-teller_daily" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every transaction of the teller by day, with the money collected and paid out by payment mode and the net cash: the Loan Collection payslips and their error corrections, every transaction of the Savings Transaction Center (cash and check slips, memo codes, transfers and GL-opposite codes, with their error corrections), the official receipts of other items, the member disbursements and the loans released from the drawer. Voided transactions are left out. Where to find it: Teller > Reports > Daily Collection & Disbursement Summary. Filters: Dates ( This week by default), From , To , Teller , Show ( By transaction source , or One line per day and teller ) and Branch . The columns: Date , Teller , Transactions (the source), Documents , Collected, cash , Collected, checks , Collected, bank / savings / memo , Paid out, cash , Paid out, cheque / other and Net cash (cash collected less cash paid out). By transaction source each teller's day has one line per source, then a subtotal "Total teller1, 10/20/2026"; the grand total adds up the sources. Transactions What it counts Loan Collection The loan payments of the official receipts (Teller > Loan Collection), by cash, check, or bank and savings. Loan Collection: error corrections An error-corrected payslip, negative in the column of the payment it negates: the cash paid back from the drawer, or the check or bank payment taken back by its journal voucher. Savings Transaction Center: deposits, withdrawals Every transaction of the center: cash and check slips in the cash and check columns, memo codes, transfers and GL-opposite codes in the bank / savings / memo and cheque / other columns. Savings Transaction Center: error corrections A corrected deposit taken back from what was collected, a corrected withdrawal from what was paid out. Official receipts: savings and deposits, fees and other items The other lines of the official receipts (Teller > Official Receipt). Loan releases from the drawer, Member disbursements The cash vouchers paid from the teller's drawer.

href="#pg-rpt-teller_over_short" aria-label="Link to this section"> The closed teller shifts of a period with their cash count and the over or short found. Where to find it: Teller > Reports > Teller Over / Short. Filters: Dates , From , To (the business date of the shift), Teller , and Show : All closed shifts or Only shifts with a difference . The columns: Business date , Teller , Shift , Drawer , Beginning cash , Cash received , Cash paid out , Expected , Counted , Over , Short , Closed by and Voucher (the over/short voucher; click it to open it), with the totals of the cash received and paid out, the overs and the shorts.

href="#pg-rpt-teller_or_list" aria-label="Link to this section"> The official receipts (or the disbursement vouchers) of a period in number order, with the numbers that were skipped. Use it to account for every pre-printed receipt. Where to find it: Teller > Reports > Official Receipt Register. Filters: Dates , From , To , Branch and Series ( Official receipts or Disbursement vouchers ). How to read it: the numbers are sorted within each series; each branch prefix, such as P, is a series of its own. Where numbers are missing, an amber line gives them, for example "P000164 to P000165" and "2 number(s) not used in this period". The columns are Number (click it to open the receipt), Date , Member , Mode , Amount (blank for a voided receipt), Status ("VOID:" and the reason), Teller and Prints (how many times it was printed). The note under the title gives the number of missing numbers, or "The series has no gap in this period." Tip A gap is not always an error: the number may have been used just before or after the period, or the receipt was spoiled. Account for each one and keep the spoiled receipts.

href="#pg-rpt-teller_cash_position" aria-label="Link to this section"> The cash in the teller drawers and the bank balances on a date, against the savings members can withdraw: a quick liquidity check. Where to find it: Teller > Reports > Cash Position. Filter: As of . How to read it: Teller cash and cash items lists the drawer accounts (those used by shifts or set on user accounts, the Teller Cash on Hand default) and Checks and Other Cash Items, with their general ledger balance and "open shift 3 (admin)" beside a drawer in use; click an account for its general ledger. Banks lists the other bank and cash accounts. TOTAL CASH POSITION adds them. The last line, Deposits that can be withdrawn on demand (savings, net of holds) , is the ordinary and special savings of active and dormant accounts less holds and uncleared checks, at their current balance. The Balance column is shown only to users with the permission "View bank balances outside Banking".

href="#pg-dist-surplus" aria-label="Link to this section"> After the fiscal year, the net surplus is divided as the cooperative's bylaws and the General Assembly decide: first the statutory funds (reserve fund, education and training fund, community development fund, optional fund), then interest on share capital (ISC) and patronage refund (PR). This page records that division for each fiscal year, has it approved with the resolution, and posts it once. The ISC and PR amounts it sets aside are then shared among the members with Interest on Share Capital and Patronage Refund batches. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Net Surplus Allocation. The Net surplus allocation button on Distribution Batches also opens it, and each year on the Net Surplus Allocation Summary opens its allocation. The posted net surplus allocation of 2025, its ISC batch, and the Reverse box Fiscal years on the left lists each allocation with its net surplus and status (Draft, Approved or Posted); click one to open it. With no year chosen, the page shows the form for a new allocation. New year in the title bar starts one; Edit opens a draft. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Fiscal year The year being divided. Last year by default. One allocation per fiscal year. From, To The fiscal period, worked out from Fiscal year ends (MM-DD) on Cooperative Profile & Policies . Net surplus The net surplus to divide. A new allocation starts with the figure in the ledger. The line under it reads "Net surplus in the ledger for the period: ... (income less expenses). Use the audited figure when it differs." Reserve fund %, Education fund %, Community development %, Optional fund % The share of the net surplus for each statutory fund. They start from the percentages on Cooperative Profile & Policies (10, 10, 3 and 7 when installed). The help on the policies page gives the usual limits: reserve fund at least 10 % (RA 9520 Art. 86), education fund not more than 10 %, community development fund at least 3 %, optional fund not more than 7 %. Confirm the percentages against your bylaws and the General Assembly resolution. of which to the federation % The part of the education and training fund due to the union or federation (CETF). 50 when installed. Interest on share capital The amount set aside for interest on share capital. "The patronage refund is what remains after the statutory funds and the interest on share capital." Notes Any remark. A reversal adds its date and reason here. The Allocation table shows the division: Net surplus ; each fund with its percentage and amount, and the education fund split into "retained by the cooperative / due to the federation"; Statutory funds ; Interest on share capital ; Patronage refund . While you edit, it is worked out from the figures the page was opened with; save the draft to see new figures. A saved allocation also shows Period , Resolution , Approving officers , Approved and Allocation voucher , and Member batches : the ISC and PR batches of the year with their amount and status, ISC used / set aside and PR used / set aside (batches approved or posted), and the buttons ISC batch and PR batch to start one for the year. Step by step To prepare the allocation: Open Year-end Distribution > Net Surplus Allocation . Check the Fiscal year , From and To . Type the Net surplus of the audited financial statements if it differs from the ledger. Check the percentages and type the Interest on share capital approved. Click Save the draft . The message "Allocation saved as a draft. The General Assembly approves it before it is posted." appears. To approve it (users with the Approve right): Open the year. In Approve (General Assembly resolution) , type the Resolution no. , its Date and the Approving officers . Click Approve and confirm. The message "Allocation approved and locked." appears. An approved allocation can no longer be edited. To post it (users with the Create right), after the end of the fiscal year: In Post the allocation , type the Posting date . It must be after the last day of the fiscal year. Click Post and confirm "Post the allocation? Retained earnings are debited and the funds and payables credited, once." The message "Allocation posted (voucher CJV-000003). The ISC and PR batches of the year can now be computed." appears. To reverse a posted allocation (users with the Approve right): in Reverse , type the Date and the Reason , click Reverse the allocation and confirm. "Allowed only while no ISC or PR batch of the year is posted. The original voucher stays; an adjusting entry reverses it." The allocation goes back to approved and can be posted again. What it records Posting makes one Cooperative Journal Voucher, memo "Allocation of net surplus 2025 (resolution GA-2026-03)", with the resolution number as reference: Account Debit Credit Retained Earnings (where the year's net surplus is once the year has ended) Net surplus Reserve Fund Reserve fund amount Education and Training Fund Part retained Due to Union / Federation (CETF) Part due to the federation Community Development Fund Amount Optional Fund Amount Interest on Share Capital Payable ISC set aside Patronage Refund Payable PR set aside The accounts are those set on Module Default Accounts . A reversal is a Cooperative Journal Voucher "Reversal of ..." that turns every line around. Example The 2025 net surplus of ₱200,000.00 gives the reserve fund ₱20,000.00 (10 %), the education and training fund ₱20,000.00 (10 %, of which ₱10,000.00 is due to the federation), the community development fund ₱6,000.00 (3 %) and the optional fund ₱14,000.00 (7 %): ₱60,000.00 of statutory funds. With ₱60,000.00 of interest on share capital, the patronage refund is ₱80,000.00. Good to know "There is no net surplus to allocate (...)." "Interest on share capital (...) cannot exceed the net surplus left after the statutory funds (...)." The Allocation table warns: "The interest on share capital is more than what is left after the statutory funds." "An allocation for fiscal year 2025 already exists." Open that year instead. "Enter the General Assembly / Board resolution number and date." "Post the allocation after the end of the fiscal year (12/31/2025), when its net surplus is in Retained Earnings." "ISC or PR batches of this year are posted. Reverse them first." The allocation voucher cannot be voided: "It posted the net surplus allocation of a fiscal year. Reverse it with an adjusting entry."

t: Interest on Share Capital and Patronage Refund
x: href="#pg-dist-isc" aria-label="Link to this section"> A distribution batch shares an amount among the members. An interest on share capital (ISC) batch shares it by each member's share capital, on the average daily balance or the ending balance of the period. A patronage refund (PR) batch shares it by the income the cooperative earned from each member. The program computes the batch for your review: computing posts nothing and asks nothing. You see the list of the members with their amounts and what each one owes the cooperative, remove the members who should not receive it (for example a member with a past-due loan or another obligation to the cooperative) with the reason, or adjust an amount, and finish the review; another user approves it with the resolution; then it is posted once, crediting each member's savings or share capital, or keeping the amount as payable to be paid out later. Both menu items open the same page, for its own kind of batch. What is specific to a patronage refund is summed up under Patronage Refund . Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Interest on Share Capital, or Year-end Distribution > Patronage Refund; each opens a new batch. ISC batch and PR batch on Net Surplus Allocation start a batch for that year, and New ISC batch and New PR batch on Distribution Batches start one too. Click a batch number on Distribution Batches or Net Surplus Allocation to open it. A new patronage refund batch for 2025 sharing the ₱80,000.00 set aside by the income earned on 4400 Interest Income on Loans Fields: Computation Field What to enter / what it means Fiscal year allocation The approved or posted net surplus allocation the batch draws on, for example "Fiscal year 2025 (ISC 60,000.00)". The line under it gives the amount set aside and what approved or posted batches already used. None (not limited by an allocation) leaves the batch without that limit. Description For example "Interest on Share Capital 2025". It shows on the batch lists. Balances from, to (ISC); Income earned from, to (PR) The period measured. The fiscal period of the allocation by default. Basis (ISC only) Average daily balance or Ending balance of share capital. It starts from Interest on share capital basis on Cooperative Profile & Policies. Method Share an amount in proportion : the amount is shared by each member's basis over the total basis. Apply a rate : each member gets the rate times their basis. Amount to distribute For Share an amount in proportion . A new batch starts with what the allocation set aside less what other batches used. The rounding difference goes to the member with the largest basis, so the amount is distributed exactly. Rate % For Apply a rate : the dividend (ISC) or refund (PR) rate, in percent. Credit to Credit to a savings account ; Credit to share capital ; Share capital until the subscription is fully paid, the rest to savings ; or Keep as payable (paid out in cash / cheque later) . Savings product For the savings and share-capital-then-savings choices: the savings product whose account is credited. Memo A remark on the batch. Fields: Members covered Active and suspended members are covered. These filters narrow the list: Field What to enter / what it means Branch, Cluster, Segment Only the members of one branch, cluster or segment. All by default. Share capital product (ISC only) The share capital product measured. Every share capital product by default. Member types Choose one or more types. "None selected: every type." Income accounts (patronage) (PR only) See Patronage Refund . Basis from, to Only the members whose basis (balance or income) is within this range. Leave blank for all. Leave out members with a past-due loan Ticked, a member with a past-due loan is put on the list already removed, with the reason "Past due loan" ( Put back brings the member back). Unticked, such a member is on the list and stands out in red during the review. The batch: the computation for review The sample ISC batch DIST-00001 in review: 10,000.00 shared by 10 members, the two members with a past-due loan removed with the reason, and the totals under the list The steps at the top show where the batch is: Review the list , Reviewed , Approved , Posted (and Reversed ). While the batch is not approved, the note under them says "Nothing is posted yet", with the number of members and the amount, and has Finish the review . The tiles give the Members on the list (and how many were removed), the total basis ( Average daily balances , Ending balances or Income earned ), To distribute (with the rate, or the pool and any rounding) and how many members on the list have a past-due loan or are on hold . The list of Members has, for each member: the name (click it to open the member) with the member no., the account credited and any reason; Basis (underlined with dashes: point at it to see where it comes from, see Where the basis comes from ); Computed ; Adjustment ; Net ("removed" for a member removed); and Owes the cooperative : Past due and the amount, in red, with the loan nos.: the amortizations of the open loans that fell due before today and are unpaid, with the penalties; On hold and the reason, in red, for a member put on hold (Members); Loans : the principal balance of the member's open loans; Subscription unpaid : the share capital subscribed and not yet paid; None when the member owes nothing of these. A member with a past-due amount or on hold is marked with a red edge. Find a member narrows the list by name, member no. or account, and Only those with a past-due loan or on hold shows only them. The members removed stay on the list, greyed, with "Removed:" and the reason, and Put back . The totals under the list: Total , "of the 10 member(s) on the list": the Basis , Computed , Adjustment and Net of the members who receive the amount. The total Net is what is posted; with an amount shared in proportion it equals the amount to distribute. Removed , "2 member(s), not given any amount": the basis of the members removed from the list (shown when there are any). Shown , for example "3 of the 10 member(s) on the list": while Find a member or Only those with a past-due loan or on hold narrows the list, the totals of the members on the list that are shown. On a phone each member is a card, and each total is a card under them. Under the list are the box of the next step ( 1. Finish the review , 2. Approve or 3. Post ) and the card with Batch , Description , Period , Fiscal year , Status ("In review, not posted", "Reviewed, not posted", Approved, Posted), Resolution , Approved , Voucher and Memo . The title bar has Recompute (a batch not yet approved), Print register , CSV , Delete (a batch not yet posted, see Deleting a computation ) and Batches . Where the basis comes from Pointing at the basis of Cruz, Ana: her share capital balance stood at 8,000.00 for 293 days and 8,600.00 for 9 days, 2,421,400.00 balance-days divided by 302 days give the average daily balance of 8,017.88, and her share of the 10,000.00 Point at a member's amount in the Basis column and, after a moment, a window shows how the amount is worked out, so you can see where it comes from. Move the pointer away and it closes; move it into the window to read it or to click a document in it. Click the amount instead to keep the window open until you click elsewhere, press Esc or click its X. With the keyboard, Tab onto the amount opens it, and Enter moves into the window so that Tab reaches its documents and its X. On a phone, tap the amount: the window opens from the bottom of the screen; tap X or outside it to close it. The window is worked out from the records when it opens, with the same arithmetic as the batch. Interest on share capital, average daily balance (the window is titled Average daily balance ): the member, the share capital account and its product, and the period with its number of days; then a table of each stretch of days the balance stood the same: Dates : from the first to the last day of the stretch; Days : the number of days; Balance : the balance on those days, with what changed it on the first day under it (a deposit in green, for example +600.00, a withdrawal in red), or "brought forward" for the balance the period started with (when money moved on the first day of the period, a first line "Before 01/01/2026" gives that balance); Balance × days : the balance times the days. The Total row adds up the days (the days of the period) and the balance-days, and the line under it divides them: "2,421,400.00 ÷ 302 days = 8,017.88", the Average daily balance . An entry counts from its value date when it has one. Voided entries do not count. Interest on share capital, ending balance (titled Ending balance ): the balance brought forward on the first day of the period, each day the balance changed with what came in or went out and the balance after it, and "the balance at the end of 10/29/2026 = 8,600.00". Patronage refund (titled for example Patronage: income earned ): what the patronage is measured by and the period, then the documents behind the amount, grouped by income account (for example 4400 - Interest Income on Loans , with its total): the date, the document no. (click it to open the document) with its kind, and the amount. For purchases or deliveries, the sales or purchase documents of the member that count, returns and debit memos negative. The line under them gives the total, the member's basis. With more than 40 documents in a group, the rest is summed on one line. Pointing at the basis of Mendoza, Ramon on a patronage refund batch: the official receipts that earned interest income from him, 1,842.22 in all, and his share of the 5,000.00 Then, for every batch, how the member's amount comes from the basis: Computed : with a rate, the basis × the rate, for example "8,600.00 × 5.0000 % = 430.00"; with an amount shared in proportion, the amount to distribute × the member's basis ÷ the basis of the members on the list, for example "10,000.00 × 8,017.88 ÷ 96,971.52 = 826.83"; Rounding , for the member with the largest basis when the shares did not add up to the amount to the centavo: the difference given to that member; Adjustment with its reason, when the amount was adjusted; Net : what the member receives. For a member removed from the list: "Removed from the list" with the reason, and no amount. If an entry dated in the period was recorded or voided after the batch was computed (a deposit entered late, for example), the figures worked out now no longer give the basis on the batch. The window then says so in yellow: "Worked out again now, the basis is 8,167.72; the batch has 8,017.88. An entry dated in the period was recorded or voided after the batch was computed. Recompute takes it." Click Recompute on a batch not yet approved to take it in; an approved or posted batch keeps its figures. Reviewing the list: removing a member Two members ticked: the bar above the list removes them together, with the reason To remove one member (a batch not yet approved, users with the Edit right): Click Remove beside the member. Choose the reason: Delinquent: past-due loan , Has another obligation to the cooperative , Not a member in good standing or Other reason , and type the details if you like (they are needed for Other reason ). Click Remove . "1 member(s) removed from the list." With an amount shared in proportion, "The amount is shared again among the members left."; with a rate, "The others keep their amounts." To remove several members together: tick them in the first column (the box in the heading ticks every member shown, so Only those with a past-due loan or on hold then ticks all of those). A bar appears above the list with the number ticked: choose the reason, type the details if needed and click Remove from the list . To put a member back: click Put back on the member's line. "The member is back on the list." To adjust a member's amount: click Adjust , type the amount to add or take off (for example -250.00) and the reason, and click Save . "The adjustment is saved; the list is back in review." Every removal, put-back and adjustment is written to the audit trail, and puts a reviewed batch back in review. The printed register lists the members removed under Not included , with the reasons. Step by step To compute a batch: Open Year-end Distribution > Interest on Share Capital (or click ISC batch on the year's net surplus allocation). Check the Fiscal year allocation , the period and the Basis . Choose the Method and check the Amount to distribute , or type the Rate % . Choose Credit to and, where asked, the Savings product . Set the filters under Members covered . Click Compute . Nothing is posted, so nothing is asked: the batch opens for review with "Computed: 12 member(s), 10,000.00. Nothing is posted yet: review the list below." To review it: go through the list, remove the members who should not receive it and adjust any amount (see above). To recompute: click Recompute , change the fields and click Recompute , then confirm "Recompute the batch? Members removed by hand stay removed." with Recompute . Adjustments are not kept; enter them again. To finish the review: when the list is right, click Finish the review (in the note at the top or in 1. Finish the review ). It checks that every member left on the list has the account to credit and that the year's amount set aside is not exceeded. The message "The review is finished. An approver records the resolution next, then the batch is posted." appears, or "The batch cannot be validated yet: ..." with the problems. A user who may not approve sees in 2. Approve who approves next. To approve (a user with the Approve right who did not prepare the batch): in 2. Approve , type the Board / General Assembly resolution , click Approve and confirm "Approve and lock the batch of 10,000.00 for 10 member(s)?" with Approve . "Approved and locked." From then on the list cannot change. To post (users with the Create right): In 3. Post , type the Posting date . Check Charged to : "Normally the payable set up by the net surplus allocation" (Interest on Share Capital Payable, or Patronage Refund Payable). Click Post to members and confirm "Post 10,000.00 to 10 member(s)? This is done once." with Post . Only the members on the list are credited; the members removed get nothing. The message "Posted (voucher CJV-000004). Each member's account was credited." appears (with Keep as payable : "Each member's amount is payable to the member, paid out from the report Unclaimed Distributions (click the member)."). To reverse a posted batch (users with the Approve right): in Reverse , type the Date and the Reason , click Reverse the batch and confirm "Reverse the posted batch? Each member credit comes back out." The message "Reversed by voucher ..." appears and the batch shows Reversed . Deleting a computation Delete the computation: the batch DIST-00001, in review and not posted, with the reason typed A batch that was never posted (in review, reviewed or approved) can be deleted, for example a computation made on the wrong period or with the wrong amount, or one computed twice. Nothing of it was posted, so no member account, voucher or payable changes. Click Delete in the title bar of the batch (or Delete beside it on Distribution Batches ). The window Delete the computation shows the batch no., its kind, members, amount and status, for example "Interest on share capital, 10 member(s), 10,000.00, in review, not posted". Type the Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail). Click Delete the batch (or Keep it to leave it). The batch and its list of members are removed and Distribution Batches opens with "Batch DIST-00001 deleted with its list of 12 member(s). Nothing had been posted; the batch as it was is kept in the audit trail." It cannot be undone: compute a new batch to start over. The audit trail keeps the batch as it was, with each member's basis, computed amount, adjustment and net, those removed and why, and the reason of the deletion. The batch number is not used again. A posted batch is not deleted: it is reversed (see To reverse a posted batch above), and a reversed batch stays on file with its vouchers. Deleting needs the Delete right on the page (Interest on Share Capital or Patronage Refund); an approved batch also needs the Approve right. Example The sample batch DIST-00001 shares ₱10,000.00 of interest on share capital by the average daily balances of 2026. Ramos, Danilo and Torres, Edgar have a past-due loan and were removed with the reason "Delinquent: past-due loan", so the 10 members left share the whole ₱10,000.00: Aquino, Rosa, with an average daily balance of ₱11,000.00, receives ₱1,134.35. The rounding difference of (0.01) was applied to the member with the largest balance, so exactly ₱10,000.00 is distributed. Nothing is posted until the batch is reviewed, approved and posted. The register and the CSV file Print register prints the INTEREST ON SHARE CAPITAL REGISTER (or PATRONAGE REFUND REGISTER ) with the batch number, the status, the period, the method and basis, how the amounts are credited and the resolution; the members included with Member , Account , Basis , Computed , Adjustment and Net , and the totals; Not included with each reason; and the signature lines Prepared by , Checked by and Approved by . A reprint asks for the reason and is marked as a copy. CSV downloads the lines ( Member no. , Member , Account , the basis, Computed , Adjustment , Net , Excluded , Reason ) as a file for a spreadsheet. Both need the Print/Export right. What it records Posting makes one Cooperative Journal Voucher with the batch number as reference: Account Debit Credit The Charged to account (Interest on Share Capital Payable or Patronage Refund Payable) Total to distribute Each member: the ledger account of the savings or share capital product credited Member's net Each member, when kept as payable: Interest on Share Capital Payable or Patronage Refund Payable, under the member's name Member's net Each member's account gets an entry with code ISC (Interest on Share Capital) or PR (Patronage Refund), for example "Interest on share capital 2025". With Share capital until the subscription is fully paid, the rest to savings , the share capital account takes what is still unpaid on the member's subscription and the savings account the rest. An amount kept as payable is paid on Member Disbursement and listed until then on Unclaimed Distributions . A reversal is a Cooperative Journal Voucher "Reversal of ..." that turns every line around and takes each credit back out of the member's account with code DM. Good to know The batches of a fiscal year cannot use more than its allocation set aside: "The batches of fiscal year 2025 (...) would exceed the ISC set aside by its allocation (...)." "Santos, Maria (100001) has no savings account to credit." Open the account first, or choose another Credit to . "There is nothing to distribute." "Enter the dividend (ISC) rate in percent.", "Enter the amount to distribute.", "Choose the savings product the amounts are credited to." and "No share capital product is set up." "Enter the reason the member is removed from the list." (an Other reason without details), "Tick the members to remove from the list first." and "Enter the reason for the adjustment." "The batch is locked: it is approved." Once approved, the list no longer changes; a posted batch is corrected by reversing it. "The batch is approved by someone other than the user who prepared it." An administrator may approve their own. "Validate the batch first." and "Only an approved batch is posted, and only once." "Some members have already been paid. Reverse those payments first." A credit that the member has already withdrawn cannot come back out until the account holds it again. A posted batch is never voided: "It posted a year-end distribution batch. A distribution is corrected with an adjusting entry, not voided." Users who may approve see "Distribution batches waiting for approval" in the alerts. Deleting: "Enter the reason for deleting the batch."; "Batch DIST-00001 is posted: it is not deleted. Reverse it instead."; "Batch DIST-00001 was posted and reversed: it stays on file with its vouchers."; "Batch DIST-00001 is approved: deleting it needs the Approve right as well." Rights: Create computes a new batch and posts; Edit recomputes, removes and puts back members, adjusts amounts and finishes the review; Approve approves and reverses; Delete deletes a batch not yet posted (an approved one with Approve as well); Print/Export prints the register and downloads the CSV. Seeing where a basis comes from needs only access to the page. By default the General Manager and the Branch Manager have Delete; the Bookkeeper and the Accountant do not.

href="#pg-dist-pr" aria-label="Link to this section"> Year-end Distribution > Patronage Refund opens the batch page described under Interest on Share Capital and Patronage Refund , for a patronage refund. The computation for review (nothing posted on Compute ), the list with what each member owes the cooperative and its totals, where each basis comes from (the documents behind it, see Where the basis comes from ), removing members with the reason, the approval, posting, reversal, deleting a batch not yet posted, register and CSV are the same. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Patronage Refund (a new batch, titled "New patronage refund batch"), PR batch on Net Surplus Allocation , or New PR batch on Distribution Batches . What differs from an ISC batch: Patronage measured by chooses what each member's share is based on: Income earned from the member (the income accounts chosen) : the credits less the debits, in the period, on the Income accounts (patronage) you choose, on the lines that carry the member's name or are made out to one of the member's customer records. "The member's share is the income these accounts earned from them in the period, in lines of business whose member transactions count, on the goods and services that count." The loan interest income account is chosen at first; choose all the income accounts your bylaws count as patronage. If none is chosen the program says "Choose the income accounts (income codes) the patronage refund is based on." Member's purchases of goods and services that count : the invoices, sales receipts, POS sales and statement charges made out to any customer record of the member, less credit memos and POS returns. Member's deliveries (produce sold to the cooperative) that count : the bills, item receipts and checks for items from any supplier record of the member, less supplier debit memos. For purchases and deliveries only item lines count, and only items marked Counts for patronage refund . For every basis, documents of a line of business whose member transactions do not count are left out. The member is recognized through the Party Master, so a purchase on the member's customer record counts even though the member's ledger name is not on it. See Lines of Business . Members with nothing on the chosen basis are not listed. The period boxes read Patronage from and to . There is no Basis and no Share capital product . The amount comes from the PR set aside by the allocation, Rate % is a refund rate on the chosen basis ("Enter the refund rate in percent."), Charged to starts at Patronage Refund Payable, and the member ledgers get code PR.

href="#pg-dist-batches" aria-label="Link to this section"> The list of the interest on share capital and patronage refund batches, latest first, with their status. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Distribution Batches. Batches on a batch page and Back on a new batch also return here. Distribution Batches with a patronage refund batch and the sample ISC batch, both in review and not posted, each with Delete Filters: Kind ( Both , Interest on share capital, Patronage refund) and Status ( Any , In review (not posted), Reviewed (not posted), Approved, Posted, Reversed). The list changes as soon as you choose. The columns: Batch (click it to open the batch; the description under it), Kind , Year (the fiscal year of its allocation), Period , Members , Amount , Credit , Prepared by and Status (a computed batch shows as In review and a finished review as Reviewed, both with "not posted"; a reversed one as Voided). Up to 300 batches are listed. On a phone each batch is a card. Delete beside a batch not yet posted (in review, reviewed or approved) deletes the computation: the window Delete the computation names the batch, asks the Reason and has Delete the batch ; "Batch DIST-00002 deleted. Nothing had been posted; the batch as it was is kept in the audit trail." It shows to users with the Delete right on Interest on Share Capital or Patronage Refund (for an approved batch, with Approve as well). A posted batch has no Delete: it is reversed on its page. See Deleting a computation . When amounts kept as payable are not yet paid out, a note above the list gives their number and total: "... are payable and not yet paid out. They are paid from the report Unclaimed Distributions (click the member)." The title bar has Net surplus allocation , New ISC batch and New PR batch .

href="#s-dist-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Year-end Distribution reports are listed under Year-end Distribution > Reports in the sidebar and in the Year-end Distribution card of the Report Center . The common report tools are explained in Working with reports .

href="#pg-rpt-dist_register" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every member line of one distribution batch, included or left out, with when it was credited or paid. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Reports > Distribution Register. Filters: Batch (number, kind and status; the latest batch at first) and Search (part of the member's name, or the member no.). The columns: Member (click it to open the member), Member no. , Account , Basis , Computed , Adjustment , Net , Note ("Removed:" and the reason, or the reason for an adjustment) and Credited / paid , with totals. The members removed from the list are listed last, without a computed or net amount. The note under the title gives the batch, its period and status (for example "in review, not posted"), how the amounts are credited and the resolution.

href="#pg-rpt-dist_unclaimed" aria-label="Link to this section"> The interest on share capital and patronage refund kept as payable and not yet paid out, member by member. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Reports > Unclaimed Distributions. Filter: As of , the date the days unclaimed are counted to. The columns: Member , Member no. , Batch , Kind , Year , Posted , Days unclaimed and Amount , with the total. Click a member to pay them on Member Disbursement .

href="#pg-rpt-dist_summary" aria-label="Link to this section"> One line per fiscal year: how the net surplus was divided, and how much of the ISC and PR set aside has been distributed. Where to find it: Year-end Distribution > Reports > Net Surplus Allocation Summary. The columns: Fiscal year (click it to open the allocation), Net surplus , Reserve , Education , Community development , Optional , ISC set aside , ISC distributed , PR set aside , PR distributed (posted batches) and Status (with the resolution number). The report has no filter.

href="#pg-cda-officers" aria-label="Link to this section"> The register of the cooperative's officers: the Board of Directors, the committees and management, with each person's position, term and the trainings attended. "CDA rules require officers to complete the mandatory trainings for their position; the list printed here goes with the annual reports." The number of active officers whose term had not ended by the end of the year is also a figure of the CAPR data . Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Officers, Committees & Trainings. The officers by board and committee, with a term that has ended shown in red, and the New officer form The officers are listed by board or committee: the name (with the member no. for a member), the position, the term ("term ended" in red, "term ends soon" in amber within 60 days), the number of trainings or "no training recorded", and Edit . Only active officers are listed; Include past officers shows the others greyed, and Active only hides them again. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Member The officer, when a member. Type part of the name or the member no. and choose. or name (not a member) The name of an officer who is not a member, for example a hired general manager. Board / committee Board of Directors, Audit Committee, Election Committee, Credit Committee, Education and Training Committee, Ethics Committee, Mediation and Conciliation Committee, Gender and Development Committee, Management (General Manager, Treasurer, Secretary, Bookkeeper) or Other committees. Position Required. For example Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Member. Term from, to The term of office. Trainings attended (one a line: title, date, provider) Each training on its own line. Active Untick it when the person leaves office. Officers are not deleted. To add an officer: fill in New officer and click Save . To change one: click Edit , change the fields and click Save , or Cancel . Print the list prints the LIST OF OFFICERS AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS of the active officers with today's date, by board and committee ( Name , Position , Term , Trainings attended ), with the signature lines Certified correct (Secretary) and Chairperson . A second print on the same day asks for the reason for the reprint. Messages: "Enter the officer (a member, or the name) and the position." and "The term ends before it starts."

href="#pg-cda-compliance" aria-label="Link to this section"> A checklist of the reports and requirements the cooperative submits for each year, with the due date, the date submitted, the receiving reference and a copy of what was filed. Overdue items stand out here and in the alerts. Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Compliance Tracking. Compliance tracking on Regulatory Calendar and a requirement on the Compliance Status report also open it. The requirements of report year 2025: three submitted and five overdue, with the New requirement form Type the Report year and click Show ; last year is shown at first, and "On file:" links to each year recorded. The tiles count the Items of the year, those Done (submitted, accepted, submitted late or not applicable) and those Overdue . The list has Report / requirement (with the notes and a link to the attached file), Due , Submitted , Reference , Status and Update . The title bar has Regulatory calendar and CAPR data . Fields Field What to enter / what it means Report year The year the requirement is for. Report / requirement Required. For example Social audit report. Due The deadline. Submitted on The date it was filed. Reference / receiving no. The receiving or reference number given by the office. Status From the dates : without a submitted date the item is to submit ("To submit", or "Overdue" in red once the due date has passed); with one it is "Submitted", or "Submitted late" when filed after the due date. Accepted by CDA : accepted (it needs the submitted date). Not applicable : the requirement does not apply this year. Notes A short remark, for example "Submitted online". Copy of the submission (PDF or picture) A PDF, JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP file of up to 8 MB. A new file replaces the one on file. Step by step To start the checklist of a year: Type the Report year and click Show . When nothing is recorded for that year, click Add the standard annual requirements . The program adds Cooperative Annual Progress Report (CAPR), Audited financial statements, Social audit report, Performance audit report, List of officers and trainings attended, Certificate of Compliance, Annual tax incentives / benefits report (BIR) and General Assembly minutes and resolutions, each due 120 days after the end of the fiscal year: "8 item(s) added for 2025. Check each due date against the current CDA issuances." Correct the due dates with Update , and add any other requirement with New requirement . To record a submission: Click Update on the item. Type Submitted on and the Reference / receiving no. Choose the file of what was filed in Copy of the submission (PDF or picture) . Click Save . Later, when the CDA accepts it, set Status to Accepted by CDA . "The standard list and the 120-day due date are a starting point; follow the current CDA memorandum circulars for your cooperative's type and category." Items are not deleted; mark one that does not apply as Not applicable . Overdue items count in the alerts as "Regulatory submissions overdue". Message: "Enter the report or requirement."

href="#pg-cda-calendar" aria-label="Link to this section"> The cooperative's own list of recurring deadlines (CDA, BIR, local government and internal ones such as the General Assembly) with a reminder before each. "Deadlines within their reminder period appear on the dashboard and in the alert count at the top of every page." Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Regulatory Calendar. Regulatory calendar on Compliance Tracking also opens it. Four yearly deadlines with their next due date and reminder, and the New deadline form The list has Deadline (with the notes), For , Next due (the date and "in 171 day(s)", "today" or "passed"), Repeats (with the reminder) and Edit , the nearest first. A deadline within its reminder period is shown in amber, a passed one in red. Inactive deadlines are greyed at the end. The program comes with a few common deadlines to start from. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Title Required. Two deadlines cannot have the same title. For CDA, BIR, Local government, Internal (General Assembly, Board) or Other. Due date Required. The first (or next) due date. Repeats Once , Every month , Every quarter or Every year (the default). A repeating deadline rolls forward by itself: Next due is the first date on or after today counted from the due date. Remind days before How many days before the next due date the reminder starts. 30 by default, up to 365. Notes A short remark. Active Untick it to stop a deadline without deleting it. Untick a one-time deadline once it is done, since it keeps showing as passed. To add a deadline: fill in New deadline and click Save . To change one: click Edit , change it and click Save . Saving refreshes the alert count. "The dates set here are your own: confirm them against the current CDA, BIR and local government issuances." Messages: "Enter the title and the due date." and "There is already an item with that title."

href="#pg-cda-capr" aria-label="Link to this section"> This page gathers the figures the Cooperative Annual Progress Report (CAPR) asks for, from the general ledger and the member ledgers, for a fiscal year: membership, capital, deposits, loans, results, statutory funds and distributions. Print them or export them, then transcribe them into the current CDA form. The page gives the data for the form; it is not the official CAPR layout. Which figures appear, and how each is computed, is set on Report Field Mappings . Where to find it: CDA Compliance > CAPR Data Preparation & Export. CAPR data on Compliance Tracking and Compute the report on Report Field Mappings also open it. The CAPR figures of fiscal year 2025 computed from the books To compute the figures: type the Fiscal year (last year at first) and click Compute . The line beside the button gives the period, worked out from the fiscal year end of Cooperative Profile & Policies: "Period 01/01/2025 to 12/31/2025 (fiscal year end 12-31)." When more than one report is mapped, choose it in Report . For a year that is not over, "Fiscal year 2026 is not over: the figures are as of today." How to read it: the lines are grouped in sections (General, Membership, Capital, Deposits, Loans and so on). Each line gives the item with its field code under it, its source (for example metric:members_total ) and the value: amounts with two decimals, counts as whole numbers, text as it is. A line whose source cannot be computed shows the error in red, and a note above the list says "1 line(s) cannot be computed; correct their source in Report Field Mappings." Print prints the COOPERATIVE ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT DATA of the year with the period, the sections and values, the note "Figures from the books of the cooperative as of ... Transcribe them into the current CDA form; the line definitions are kept in Report Field Mappings.", and the signature lines Prepared by , Certified correct and Chairperson (the Bookkeeper / Accountant, General Manager and Chairperson of Cooperative Profile & Policies). A reprint of the same year asks for the reason. Export CSV downloads Section , Field code , Item , Value and Source for a spreadsheet, numbers without thousands separators, an error as "ERROR:" and the message. Both need the Print/Export right. Field mappings opens Report Field Mappings. Tip Before submitting, check the Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation and the Trial Balance for the same date. The member figures come from the member ledgers and the totals from the general ledger; they should agree.

href="#pg-cda-mappings" aria-label="Link to this section"> The definition of each line of the CAPR data (and of any other report you map): its section, code, label and where its value comes from. "When the CDA revises the CAPR form, change the lines in Report Field Mappings: each line takes a named figure, a list of account codes or a fixed text, so no program change is needed." The program comes with a CAPR mapping to start from. Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Report Field Mappings. Field mappings on CAPR Data Preparation & Export also opens it. The CAPR lines with their sources, the New line form and the list of sources The list has Order , Section , Field (the label, with the field code under it), Source , Edit and Remove . When more than one report is mapped, a tab opens each one. Compute the report opens the CAPR page for the report shown. Fields Field What to enter / what it means Report The report the line belongs to: capr by default. Lower-case letters, digits and the underscore. A new name starts another report, which then gets its own tab and appears in Report on the CAPR page. Section The heading the line is grouped under, for example Loans. Field code Required. The code of the line in the form; letters, digits, underscore, point and hyphen. It must be unique in the report. Order The position of the line. Lines are listed by it. Label Required. The item as it prints. Source Required. Where the value comes from (see below). The Sources card lists what a source can be: account: account codes separated by commas; a code ending in * takes every code that starts with it, for example account:4* . Balance-sheet accounts give the balance at the end of the year, income and expense accounts the year's activity, in their normal direction. text: a fixed text. setting: a cooperative setting, such as setting:cda_reg_no . metric: one of the figures listed with their meaning, for example metric:members_total ("Members (active and suspended) at the end of the period"), metric:loans_outstanding , metric:par_ratio or metric:net_surplus . To add a line: fill in New line and click Save . To change one: click Edit , change it and click Save . To remove one: click Remove and confirm "Remove this line from the report?" (the Delete/Void right). When you save, the program computes the source for the last year to check it works. Messages: "Enter the field code, the label and the source.", "That field code is already used in this report." and "The source does not work: Unknown source "...": use metric:, account:, text: or setting:."

href="#s-cda-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The CDA Compliance reports are listed under CDA Compliance > Reports in the sidebar and in the CDA Compliance card of the Report Center . The common report tools are explained in Working with reports .

href="#pg-rpt-cda_officers" aria-label="Link to this section"> The officers of Officers, Committees & Trainings as a report, grouped by board and committee, with their trainings written out. Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Reports > List of Officers and Committees. Filter: Show : Active officers or Including past officers . The columns: Name , Member no. , Position , Term from , to , Trainings attended (separated by semicolons, or "none recorded") and a last column with "past" for an officer no longer active.

href="#pg-rpt-cda_compliance" aria-label="Link to this section"> The requirements of Compliance Tracking with their status, for one year or every year. Where to find it: CDA Compliance > Reports > Compliance Status. Filter: Year ( Every year by default). The columns: Year , Report / requirement (click it to update the item), Due , Submitted , Reference , Status (OVERDUE, To Submit, Submitted, Late, Accepted or Not Applicable) and Notes .

href="#s-party-how" aria-label="Link to this section"> Each person or organization the cooperative deals with has one party record in the Party Master, with a Party ID that never changes: P-000001, P-000002 and so on. The party holds the legal name printed on documents, the name shown in lists, the TIN, the contact details, the address and the home branch. What the party does for the cooperative is a role. Each role keeps its own record, with its own number, terms, limits, status and history, and that record points at its party: Role The role record Number shown on the Party Center Member The member on the Member Center The member no., for example 100001 Customer The customer on the Customer Center C- and the record number, for example C-10 Supplier The vendor on the Vendor Center V- and the record number, for example V-9 Employee An employee on Employees & Other Names The employee no. when one is entered, otherwise N- and the record number, for example N-18 Other name Another name (a payee) on Employees & Other Names N- and the record number A customer's jobs belong to the customer's party and are not roles of their own. A member's own ledger name on Employees & Other Names belongs to the member's party and is not listed as a separate role. The rules the program keeps Nothing is joined by name alone. A new member, customer, supplier or other name gets a new party unless you choose an existing one. When its details look like a party already on file, the program warns you before saving (see The party on member, customer, supplier and other-name forms ). Possible duplicates already on file are listed on Identity Review , where a person decides. Nothing is deleted. Giving, taking away, restoring or moving a role never deletes the role record or its documents. Taking a role away makes its record inactive; its number, open balance, documents and history stay. Old numbers keep pointing to the party. The program keeps a crosswalk of every member, customer, supplier and other-name record and the party it belongs to. When two parties are linked, the party that is merged keeps its Party ID, which then points to the party kept. Role history. Every role given, taken away, restored, linked or moved, every link of two parties and every change of the party's name is written to the party's role history, with the date, the user and the reason, and to the audit trail. The Party Role History report lists it. One membership. A person or organization holds one membership. Membership starts on Member Information and ends or is restored through the member's status (resignation, termination, reinstatement), not on the Party Center. A change of membership status is also written to the role history. Which record leads the details The party and its role records share details. Which one leads depends on the roles the party holds: A member leads its party. Saving the member on Member Information writes its details to the party: the kind of party, the legal name, the name in lists, the last, first and middle name and suffix, the date of birth, TIN, e-mail, mobile, address and home branch. A blank on the member does not erase a TIN, e-mail, mobile, address, date of birth or branch the party already has. On the Party Center these details of a member's party are read-only. A party that is not a member and has one role follows that role record. When you change the customer, supplier or other name on its own page, the changes you make are written to the party. A party with several roles is edited on the Party Center. The role records then only fill in details the party does not have yet: TIN, e-mail, mobile, phone, address, date of birth and home branch. For a member who is a person, the legal name is the first name, the middle initial, the last name and the suffix, for example "Maria R. Santos Jr.", while the lists keep the member's name as "Santos, Maria R.". For an institution or a joint account, the legal name is the member's name. Editing a party does not rename its customer, supplier or other-name records: each keeps the name it has in its own list. Documents print the party's legal name (see Names on documents, posted documents and reissues ). Kinds of party A party is a Person or an Organization . An individual member or a joint account belongs to a person's party, and an institutional member to an organization's. The program refuses to attach a member to a party of the other kind, for example: "ABC Trading Corp. is an organization, and this member is an individual. Choose the party of the same kind, or none." Customers, suppliers and other names may belong to either kind. A party's status is Active , Inactive (no longer dealt with, set with Edit party on the Party Center) or Merged (linked into another party on Identity Review). See Making a party inactive . At the upgrade to this version Every existing member, customer, supplier, employee and other name got a party of its own, numbered from P-000001. Nothing was merged, not even records with the same name. A customer's jobs took the customer's party, and a member's ledger name the member's party. Institutional members became organizations and the other members persons. A customer or supplier with a company name became an organization, with the company name as its legal name; the others became persons. The crosswalk records each record and the party it was given. The role history shows each role as "Granted" with the reason "Held at the upgrade". Every existing document was given its party and the name, address and TIN to print, taken from its record at the upgrade and marked as coming from the upgrade. Two lines of business were made, SC Savings and Credit and TR Consumer Store. The existing cooperative vouchers were given SC, and the sales, purchasing, POS and inventory documents TR; the other documents were left without a line of business (see Lines of Business ). Because nothing was merged, a member who was also a store customer now has two parties. After the upgrade, click Look for duplicates now on Identity Review and link the pairs that are the same person or organization.

href="#pg-party-center" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Party Center lists every person and organization on file and shows everything about one of them: the details, what it owes and is owed, its roles, its documents and its role history. Here you create a party, give it a role, take a role away or restore it, and move a role that was attached to the wrong party. Where to find it: Parties > Party Center. The Party ID shown on a customer, supplier or other-name record, on Member Information and on a saved document also opens it. The Party Center with party P-000001 Maria Santos, a member who is also a customer, a supplier and an employee Finding a party The list on the left shows each party's name in lists, its Party ID and its roles. "(inactive)" follows a role whose record is inactive, and "No role" marks a party without roles. A party that is not active shows its status after the roles, for example "Inactive". Type in the search box ( Name, party no., member no., TIN, mobile ) to narrow the list as you type. Press Enter to search the whole list: the search looks at the Party ID, the legal name and the name in lists, the TIN, mobile and e-mail, the member no. and member name, and the customer and supplier names. Every role narrows the list to one role (Member, Customer, Supplier, Employee or Other name), to More than one role or to No role . The status choice shows the Active parties at first. Choose Inactive , Merged or All to see the others. Every branch , shown when the cooperative has branches, narrows the list to the parties whose home branch, or whose member's branch, is the branch chosen. The line under the filters, for example "34 of 34 parties", counts the parties shown. The list shows 100 parties at a time, with Previous and Next . Click a party to open it on the right. The selected party The top of the right side shows the name in lists, the Party ID and the kind of party, for example "P-000001, person", and the line "Printed on documents as Maria Santos, with member no. 100001". Under it are the details on file: TIN , Date of birth , Registration no. , Mobile , Phone , E-mail , Address and Home branch . Only the details that are filled in are shown. Three tiles give the party's position over all dates up to today, taken from the Consolidated Party Statement : Party owes the cooperative: its accounts receivable and loans. Cooperative owes the party: its accounts payable, savings deposits, time deposits, and interest on share capital and patronage refund still payable. Member equity interest: its share capital. Shown for a member only. The tiles are shown to users who may open the Consolidated Party Statement. In the screenshot, Maria Santos owes the cooperative ₱500.00, the cooperative owes her ₱4,130.31, and her share capital is ₱9,000.00. The buttons under the tiles: Edit party opens the party form (see New party and Edit party ). Consolidated statement opens the party's statement. Enroll as member , for a party that is not a member, opens a new member on Member Information with the party chosen and its details filled in. It is shown to users who may add members. Give a role makes a customer, supplier, employee or other-name record for the party. For an inactive party the line under the name ends with ", inactive". Enroll as member and Give a role are shown for it too; giving it a role, or enrolling it as a member, makes it active again (see Making a party inactive ). A party that was linked into another shows "This party was merged into" and the party kept, with a link: its records and documents are there now. A merged party cannot be edited or given roles. Roles Column What it shows Role Member, Customer, Supplier, Employee or Other name. Number The member no., C-10, V-9, N-18 or the employee no. Record The name of the role record. Click it to open the record on its own page. Status The member's status and branch, or Active or Inactive. Details For a member, "Member since" and the date, and ", on hold" when the member is on hold. For a customer, the terms, credit limit, price level and number of jobs. For a supplier, the terms and "Our account no.". For an employee or other name, the position. At the end of each row: Take away (on an active record) or Restore (on an inactive one), for users with the Edit right on the page. Not on the member row. Move , for users who also have the special permission "Parties: can link records found to be the same person or organization, and move a role to another party". Not on the member row. Membership status on the member row opens the member's history on Member Information, where the status is changed. Documents, role history and possible matches Documents lists the party's latest 25 documents, whatever role they were made in; the heading gives the count, for example "latest 22 of 22". The columns: Column What it shows Date The date of the document. Document The kind and number of the document. Click the number to open it. A voided document is greyed and marked "(void)". As What the party was on the document: Bill to, Customer, Received from, Supplier, Pay to or Name. Name printed The name the document prints. "(reissued 1)" follows it when the printed name was corrected. Unit The code of the document's line of business, for example SC or TR. Amount The total of the document. Role history shows the latest 30 entries: what happened (Granted, Revoked, Restored, Moved in, Moved out, Merged, Edited or Linked), the role, the other party when there is one, the date and time, the user and the reason. "Revoked" is a role taken away. May be the same as , for an active party, lists up to six other parties, active or inactive, that share a TIN, e-mail, mobile or phone number, name and date of birth, or name with this party, with what they share and their roles. Click a name to open it. Review and link on Identity Review , shown to users who may open Identity Review, records these possible pairs for review (pairs already on Identity Review are left as they are) and opens Identity Review on the pairs of this party, where they are decided. When nothing matches, the box reads "No other party with the same TIN, e-mail, mobile or name." New party and Edit party New party at the top of the page opens an empty party form; Edit party opens the selected party. The New party form Field What to enter / what it means Kind of party Person or Organization. For an organization, the name boxes and the date of birth are hidden. Legal name (printed on documents) The full legal name, for example "Maria R. Santos" or "ABC Trading Corporation". For a person you may leave it blank and type the names below: the program then builds it from the first name, middle initial, last name and suffix. Name in lists How the party is listed and searched, for example "Santos, Maria". Leave it blank to use the legal name. Last name, First name, Middle name, Suffix The names of a person. Date of birth For a person. TIN The taxpayer identification number. SEC / CDA / DTI registration no. The registration number of an organization. E-mail Must be a valid e-mail address. Mobile, Phone The contact numbers. Address The address. Documents print it when the role record and the document have none. Home branch Shown when the cooperative has branches. Notes Anything worth keeping about the party. Status On Edit party only. Active , or Inactive (no longer dealt with) ; see Making a party inactive . Reason for the change (required when the legal name or the status changes) On Edit party only. A change of the legal name or the name in lists is written to the role history with the old name and this reason; a change of status with "Made inactive" or "Made active" and this reason. Click Create party (or Save party ), or Cancel . Edit party for a member: the details that come from the member record are read-only For a member's party, the form says "This party is member no. 100001. Its name, date of birth, TIN, mobile number, e-mail, address and branch come from the member record; change them on the Member Information page." The kind of party, the names, date of birth, TIN, e-mail, mobile, address and home branch are read-only; the phone, the registration no., the notes and the status can be changed here. A new legal name is printed on new documents. Documents already issued keep the name they were issued with; to change it on one of them, see Correcting the printed name . Making a party inactive A party the cooperative no longer deals with can be made inactive: on Edit party , choose Inactive (no longer dealt with) in Status , type the reason and click Save party . This is allowed only when none of its roles is active. Take its customer, supplier, employee and other-name roles away first, and end a membership through the member's status; otherwise the program says, for example, "Party P-000035 still has an active role. Take its roles away first (a membership ends through its status on the Member Center)." Without a reason it says "Enter the reason for making the party inactive." An inactive party is left out of the pick lists: Person or organization already on file , On file as , the Party of the Consolidated Party Statement, and the party lists of Move and Link two parties found another way . The one exception is Enroll as member , which opens On file as with the inactive party chosen. The party stays on the Party Center under Inactive or All , with its roles, documents and history. The possible-match warning and Identity Review still find it (see The possible-match warning ). The party becomes active again, with an entry in its role history, when: its Status is set back to Active on Edit party, with a reason; it is given a role with Give a role , or one of its roles is restored with Restore ; it is enrolled as a member with Enroll as member and the new member is saved; one of its role records is saved as active on its own page, or its member is saved with an active, applicant or suspended membership; it is the party kept on Identity Review and has an active role after the link. Step by step To create a party and give it its roles: Search the list first: the person or organization may already be on file. Click New party . Choose the Kind of party , then type the legal name (or, for a person, the names) and the details you have. Click Create party . If the details look like a party already on file, the program does not save and lists the possible parties. Open the existing party from the list instead, or, when it is really a different person or organization, tick This is a different person or organization and click Create party again. The new party opens with "Party created. Give it its roles below." Click Give a role , fill in the dialog (below) and click Give the role . The program names the record, for example "Supplier role given (V-12, Bright Minds Academy)." To make the party a member, click Enroll as member instead. The Give a role dialog: Field What to enter / what it means Role Customer (buys from the cooperative), Supplier (sells or delivers to the cooperative), Employee, or Other name (payee). Terms, Credit limit (0 = none), Price level, Can charge purchases at the POS For a customer. Leave Price level at its blank choice, Member prices of the line of business (follows the membership) for a member's party or Nonmember prices of the line of business for others, and the customer gets no price level of its own: each sale then takes the member or nonmember prices of its line of business, according to the party's membership at the time (see Member and nonmember prices ). Choose a level only for a customer who should always have it. Employee no., Position / relationship For an employee or other name. Reason or reference (recorded with the role) Optional, for example "Member buying on credit at the store". It goes to the role history. The role record is made from the party: its name is the party's name in lists, an organization's legal name becomes its company name, and it takes the party's phone, mobile, e-mail, address and TIN. Its own number, terms and history start then. If the party had the same role before and it was taken away, the old record is restored instead, so its number and history continue. To give the customer role you also need the Create right on the Customer Center; for a supplier, on the Vendor Center; for an employee or other name, on Employees & Other Names. To take a role away, or restore it: Click Take away (or Restore ) on the role's row. Type the reason, which is required and goes to the role history and the audit trail. Click Confirm . The record becomes inactive (or active again); its number, open balance, documents and history stay. A customer's jobs follow the customer. To move a role that was attached to the wrong party: Click Move on the role's row. In To party , choose the party the record belongs to, or leave A new party made from the record . Type the reason, for example what shows the record belongs to the other party. Click Move . The record and its documents go to the other party (a customer with its jobs); the names printed on the documents stay as issued. The program opens the party the role went to. The role history of both parties shows "Moved out" and "Moved in". Confidential member details For a party that is a member, users without the special permission "Cooperative: can see confidential member details (birth date, TIN, contact numbers, home address)" see the TIN, date of birth, e-mail, mobile, phone, address and registration no. with all but the last three characters replaced by asterisks (a value of four characters or fewer is all asterisks), and the line "Confidential member details are partly hidden." On Edit party those details are not shown at all: "The member's contact details and TIN are confidential and are not shown to you." The details of parties that are not members are shown in full. Identity Review, the Consolidated Party Statement and the Party List hide them the same way. The same permission applies on Member Information . For an existing member, a user without it sees the date of birth, TIN, mobile, e-mail and the residence and provincial addresses partly hidden in locked boxes, and instead of the contact numbers the line "Hidden: you need the special permission to see confidential member details. Saving this page keeps the member's numbers as they are." When that user saves the member, these details stay as they were. The form of a new member is not hidden. The Customer Center and the Vendor Center show the contact details, billing address and TIN of the customer or supplier record itself. They belong to the role record and are shown to anyone who may open those pages: the hiding applies to the details of the member and of its party, not to these records. Good to know "Enter the legal name (or the first and last name of a person)." "The e-mail address is not valid." and "Enter a valid date of birth." "Enter the reason for changing the legal name (new documents print it; documents already issued keep the name they were issued with)." "Santos, Maria is already a customer (Maria Santos)." The party already has an active record of that role; open it from the Roles table. The same message is given for a supplier, and "is already on Employees & Other Names" for an employee or other name. "You are not allowed to add customers." (or suppliers, or employees and other names): you have no Create right on the page of that role. "You are not allowed to move roles between parties (special permission: link or move parties)." "Party P-000035 still has an active role. Take its roles away first (a membership ends through its status on the Member Center)." and "Enter the reason for making the party inactive." (see Making a party inactive ). "The role is already on that party." The member row has no Take away or Move : a membership is ended or restored through the member's status (resignation, termination, reinstatement), and a membership is never moved. If two parties are the same member, link them on Identity Review.

t: The party on member, customer, supplier and other-name forms
x: href="#s-party-forms" aria-label="Link to this section"> The forms that add a member, a customer, a supplier or an employee or other name ask whom the new record belongs to. A member who starts buying at the store, or a supplier who joins the cooperative, then stays one party with two roles. Person or organization already on file On a new customer ( Customer Center ), a new supplier ( Vendor Center ) and a new employee or other name ( Employees & Other Names ), the first field is Person or organization already on file . Type part of a name to search. Each active party is listed with its name in lists, Party ID and roles, for example "Santos, Maria (P-000001), Member, Customer, Supplier, Employee". The New customer or job form, with Person or organization already on file as its first field Choose the party when the person or organization is already on file. The new record becomes a role of that party, and details the party does not have yet are filled in from the record. The role history shows "Linked" with "Linked to an existing party". Leave it at "Not on file: a new party made from this customer" (or supplier, or name) for someone new. A new party is made from the record. The role history shows "Granted" with "New record". The field is on new records only. A job takes the party of the customer it belongs to, whatever is chosen. The possible-match warning When no party is chosen, the program compares the new record's TIN, e-mail, mobile and phone numbers and name with the active and inactive parties before saving. If any look the same, the record is not saved and the form shows up to four of them, the closest first, for example: "This customer may already be on file: Cruz, Ana (P-000003, Member; same mobile number, same name). Choose the existing party, or tick "This is a different person or organization" to make a new one." The tick box This is a different person or organization then appears next to the field. An inactive party is marked ", inactive" after its Party ID, and the message adds after "Choose the existing party": "(an inactive party is made active again on the Party Center first, or by giving it the role there)". An inactive party is not in the pick list, so open it on the Party Center and either give it the role there with Give a role (for a new member, Enroll as member ), or make it active with Edit party and then choose it on the form. To answer the warning: Check the parties named in the message, on the Party Center if you need to. If one of them is the same person or organization, choose it in Person or organization already on file and save again. If none is, tick This is a different person or organization and save again. A new party is made. The party line on saved records On the edit form and the detail panel of a customer or supplier, and on the edit form of an employee or other name, a line names the party, for example: "Party P-000001, printed on documents as Maria Santos (member no. 100001). Also member, supplier, employee." The Party ID opens the Party Center for users who may open it. A saved record is not moved to another party from its own form; use Move on the Party Center . Member Information On a new member, the field above the tabs is On file as (a customer, supplier or other name joining the cooperative) . It lists the active parties that are not members yet.
