Choose the party when the new member is already on file, for example a store customer joining the cooperative; otherwise leave it at Not on file: a new party . Enroll as member on the Party Center opens the form with the party chosen and fills in the names, TIN, e-mail, mobile, date of birth and branch from the party. The party is chosen even when it is inactive; it is then listed with ", inactive" after its Party ID, for example "(P-000012, inactive)", and saving the member makes it active again. An organization is filled in as an institutional member, with its legal name as the name of the institution. When no party is chosen and the details look like a party that is not a member, the member is not saved and the form says, for example: "This person may already be on file: Ana M. Cruz (P-000035, Customer; same mobile number, same name). Choose the existing party, or tick "This is a different person" to make a new one. To use it, choose it under "On file as"." The tick box This is a different person appears next to Add member . Parties that are already members are left out of this check; the member check for the same name and date of birth covers them. The chosen party must be of the same kind as the member (see Kinds of party ). Once the member is saved, the member record leads the party's details. On a saved member, the line next to Kind of member reads "Party P-000001: documents print the member's registered name." The Party ID opens the Party Center. Member Information of member 100001, with the line naming its party P-000001 To enroll a store customer as a member: Open Parties > Party Center and find the customer's party. Click Enroll as member . Member Information opens with the party chosen in On file as and its details filled in. Complete the member's details and membership on the tabs, as for any new member. Click Add member . The member joins the party; the role history shows "Linked" with "Enrolled as a member". The customer record, its number and its documents stay as they were.

href="#pg-party-review" aria-label="Link to this section"> Identity Review lists pairs of parties that may be the same person or organization, and records what a person decides: the two are the same and are linked into one party, or they are different. The program never links parties on its own. As the page says: "Records are never joined by name alone." Where to find it: Parties > Identity Review. The Identity Review button on the Party Center also opens it and shows the number of pairs waiting, for example "Identity Review (2)". Review and link on Identity Review under May be the same as on the Party Center records that party's possible pairs and opens Identity Review on them. Identity Review with two pairs to review and the form to link two parties found another way How possible pairs are found Look for duplicates now compares every party that is not merged. Two parties become a pair when they share at least one of the following. The pair's score is the sum of what they share; the higher the score, the more likely they are the same. Basis What is compared Score Same TIN The first nine digits of the TIN, without dashes or spaces. A TIN of zeros does not count. 60 Same name and date of birth The name, as compared below, together with the date of birth. 50 Same e-mail The e-mail address, without regard to capitals. 30 Same mobile number, Same phone number The last ten digits of the mobile and phone numbers, with spaces, dashes, brackets and other characters left out. A phone number and a mobile number match each other, so a mobile number typed in the phone box of a customer or supplier is found. Numbers shorter than ten digits are not compared. 30 Same name The legal name or the name in lists, without capitals, punctuation, initials or word order: "Santos, Maria R." and "Maria Santos" are the same name. 20 A value shared by more than 40 parties, such as a placeholder TIN or e-mail, is not used. Pairs already decided stay decided; pairs still to review get their basis and score brought up to date. The program says how many new pairs it found: "2 new possible duplicates found." or "No new possible duplicates." The pairs The tabs To review , Linked , Different and All show the pairs by decision, with their counts. The pairs to review come first, the highest score first. Each pair's heading says what the two share, for example "Same mobile number, Same name", with "Score 50" on the right; a decided pair shows instead "Linked" or "Different", the date and time, the user and the reason. Each side shows the party's name (click it to open the Party Center), the Party ID and kind, the roles, and the Legal name , TIN , Date of birth , Mobile , Phone (when it differs from the mobile), E-mail and Address . Under a pair to review, when neither party is merged, are the buttons Same: keep P-000003 , Same: keep P-000035 (one for each party) and Different . This includes pairs with an inactive party. When the page was opened for one party, the line "Showing pairs with party" names it, and Show every pair shows them all again. What linking does Every role record of the other party (its membership, customers with their jobs, suppliers, employees and other names) and every one of its documents moves to the party kept. Details the party kept does not have (TIN, e-mail, mobile, phone, address, date of birth, home branch) are filled in from the other party. When the membership came from the other party, the member's details then lead the party kept. The other party stays, with the status Merged, pointing to the party kept. Its Party ID still opens it on the Party Center, with the link to the party kept. When the party kept was inactive and now has an active role, it becomes active again. The names already printed on documents stay as issued. The role history of both parties shows "Merged" with the reason and who approved it, and the link is written to the audit trail. Pairs still to review that involve the merged party are removed; the next Look for duplicates now finds them again against the party kept. Two members are never linked: "Both parties are members (100003 and 100013). A person holds one membership: settle and close one membership first." Step by step To decide a pair: Open Parties > Identity Review . After adding or importing records, click Look for duplicates now . On To review , compare the two sides. Open a name to see the party's roles and documents on the Party Center. If they are different people or organizations, click Different , type the reason (what shows they are different) and click Record . The program says "Recorded as two different parties." The pair moves to Different and is not proposed again. If they are the same, click Same: keep on the party to keep, usually the member. In Link the parties , check the line that says which party is kept and which is moved into it, and type the reason (what shows they are the same). If you do not have the Approve right on the page, open Supervisor approval and have a supervisor type their username and password, or type a one-time approval code. Click Link . The program says "The parties were linked. The party kept has every role and document now." and opens the party kept on the Party Center. To link two parties that were not proposed: under Link two parties found another way , choose the Party to keep and the Party to move into it (both lists hold the active parties), type the Reason (what shows they are the same) , have a supervisor approve if needed, and click Link the parties . Example Ana M. Cruz (P-000035), a store customer, has the same mobile number as the member Cruz, Ana (P-000003). The membership officer confirms that they are the same person and clicks Same: keep P-000003 with the reason "Same person, mobile number and address confirmed by phone on 10/12/2026". The customer record and its invoices move to P-000003, and P-000035 stays as a merged party pointing to it. Who may do what Look for duplicates now: the Create right on Identity Review. Review and link on Identity Review on the Party Center: any user who may open Identity Review. It only records possible pairs; nothing is linked. Different: the Edit right on Identity Review. Same: keep and Link two parties found another way: the Edit right and the special permission "Parties: can link records found to be the same person or organization, and move a role to another party", and the Approve right on Identity Review. A user without the Approve right needs a supervisor who has it to approve on the form, with their username and password or a one-time approval code from Approval Codes . The approver is recorded in the role history. Messages you may meet: "Supervisor approval is required: link two parties into one. Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below, or type a one-time approval code." "You are not allowed to link parties (special permission: link or move parties)." "Choose the two parties." and "Choose two different parties." "One of the parties was already merged." "This pair was already decided."

href="#pg-party-statement" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Consolidated Party Statement puts together everything one party has with the cooperative, in whatever role: receivables, loans, payables, savings, time deposits, distributions payable and share capital. Each balance keeps its own opening balance, activity and closing balance, taken from the subsidiary ledger of its role, and each line leads to its document. Nothing is offset: a member's savings are not used to pay a store account on the statement. Where to find it: Parties > Reports > Consolidated Party Statement, or Consolidated statement on the Party Center. It is also in the Parties card of the Report Center . The Consolidated Party Statement of Maria Santos for 01/01/2026 to 10/12/2026 Filters Field What to enter / what it means Party Type part of the name to search. The active parties are listed with their Party ID and roles. Choosing one shows its statement. From, To The period. At first, January 1 of this year to today. Line of business Shown when there are active lines of business. All , or one line: only the entries of that line are counted. Branch / class Shown when classes are in use. All , or one class: only the entries of that class are counted. Show Balances and activity lists every line; Balances only gives the opening and closing balance of each account. Click Show after changing the dates or filters. How to read it The heading gives the period, when the statement was prepared and the filters used. On the left are the legal name, the Party ID ("Party ID P-000001, listed as Santos, Maria"), the address and the TIN; on the right, each role with its number, record name and status. Three tiles give the closing totals: Party owes the cooperative ("Receivables: what the party is to pay the cooperative."), Cooperative owes the party ("Payables, deposits and distributions due: what the cooperative is to pay or return to the party.") and Member equity interest ("Paid-up share capital: the member's equity in the cooperative, not a debt."). The equity tile is left out for a party that is not a member and has no share capital. The line under the tiles gives the net position, what the party owes less what it is owed, for information only. In the screenshot: "Net position for information only: (3,630.31) (the cooperative owes the party more than the party owes it). Nothing is offset: each balance is settled through its own documents, and share capital is equity, not part of this figure." The sections follow, under the three headings: Section What it holds Party owes the cooperative Accounts receivable One group for each customer record of the party, with its jobs, from the accounts receivable lines of the general ledger. Loans receivable One group for each loan of the party's membership, with its status: the principal, interest and penalties owed. Its closing line gives the principal and the interest and penalties separately when there are charges. Cooperative owes the party Accounts payable One group for each supplier record of the party. Savings deposits Each savings account of the member. Time deposits Each time deposit of the member. Interest on share capital and patronage refund payable The amounts of distribution batches posted as payable, less what was paid out. Member equity interest Share capital Each share capital account of the member. Each section heading gives its totals, for example "Opening 13,752.00, increase 0.00, decrease 13,752.00, closing 0.00". Under it, each account starts with its name and opening balance, then its lines with the columns Date , Document (click it to open the document), Description , Unit , Increase , Decrease and Balance , and ends with Closing balance . An account with no activity and a zero balance is left out when its record is inactive, the account is closed or the loan is paid, renewed or written off, and whenever a line of business or class is chosen. Last comes Interest on share capital and patronage refund allocated in the period , with the columns Posted , Batch , Kind , Period , Basis , Amount and Settled (Credited to savings, Credited to share capital, or Payable with the date paid or "not yet paid"). Printing and exporting Print / PDF opens the statement with the company heading and the button Print or save as PDF ; Back returns to the page. Excel downloads the statement as a spreadsheet file: the summary, the net position, then each section and account with its lines. CSV downloads the same as a CSV file. The three buttons need the Print right on the page. Each print and each export is written to the audit trail with the party and the period. Party Center returns to the party. Tip Before settling a member who is leaving, print the statement with From set to the date the member joined: it shows the store account, the supplier account, the loans, the deposits and the share capital together, each with its own balance to settle.

t: Names on documents, posted documents and reissues
x: href="#s-party-documents" aria-label="Link to this section"> The name printed on a document When a document is saved, the program takes what it will print about the counterparty from the party master at that moment, and keeps it on the document: Name: the party's legal name. Address: the address typed on the document, otherwise the address of the role record (the customer's billing address, or the customer's for a job; the supplier's or the other name's address), otherwise the party's address. TIN: the TIN of the role record (or of the customer, for a job), otherwise the party's. Member no.: the member no. of the party's membership, when it has one. These are taken again only when the customer, supplier, name or payee on the document is changed; any other edit keeps them. Renaming a member, customer or supplier later therefore does not change the documents already issued. A document made out to a name that is on no list prints that name. Documents saved before the upgrade print what was taken at the upgrade. The document's page shows what it prints as, for example, Bill to (printed) : the name, "Member no. 100001", "Reissued 1 time" after a correction, and a link to the party, such as "Party P-000001". It also shows the Line of business . Labels and the member number The label in front of the name follows the kind of document: Label Documents Bill to Invoices, statement charges, finance charges, estimates and sales orders Customer Sales receipts, credit memos, POS sales and returns Received from Customer payments and official receipts Supplier Purchase orders, bills, supplier debit memos and item receipts Pay to Checks, bill payments, customer refunds, advances to suppliers, cash vouchers, member disbursements and loan releases Name Other documents, such as journal entries With Print the member no. under the name of a member on invoices, receipts, checks and vouchers ticked on Lines of Business , the document of a member shows the member no. with the name, for example "Member no. 100001" under the name of an invoice, or "(member no. 100001)" after the payee on a check or voucher. Untick it and the number is not shown. Posted documents are locked With Lock posted documents ticked on Lines of Business (the upgrade turns it on), the amounts, accounts, names, dates and lines of a posted document can be changed only by a user with the special permission "Can change or delete a posted document while posted documents are locked (with a reason)", and only with a reason. Nobody else can delete a posted document: they void it, or record a correcting document such as a credit memo, a supplier debit memo or a journal entry. A document is posted when it has general ledger entries and is not void, pending or suspended. Estimates, sales orders and purchase orders do not post and are not locked. The memo, the reference and similar details can still be changed by anyone with the Edit right. The page of a locked document shows "Posted. Changes to amounts, accounts, names, dates or lines need a reason and are kept in the audit trail." to users with the permission, and "Posted. Only the memo, reference and similar details can be changed; correct amounts with a void or a correcting document." to the others. Delete is not offered to users without the permission. On the form of a locked document, users with the permission get the box Reason for changing this posted document : "Needed when amounts, accounts, names, dates or lines change. The document as it was stays in the audit trail." Messages: "This document is posted, and posted documents are locked: amounts, accounts, names, dates and lines cannot be changed. Void it and record it again, record a correcting document (credit memo, vendor credit, journal entry), or ask a user who may change posted documents." "Enter the reason for changing this posted document (it is kept in the audit trail with the document as it was)." "Posted documents are locked and cannot be deleted. Void it instead: the document stays, marked void, with the reason." Cooperative vouchers (official receipts, member disbursements, loan releases and cooperative journal vouchers) are never edited or deleted in any case; they are voided. Correcting the printed name When a document was issued with a wrong name, address or TIN, for example with the middle initial missing, Correct printed name on the document's page corrects only what is printed. The amounts, the accounts and the ledger do not change, and the document keeps its number. The correction is a reissue: it is numbered (Reissue no. 1, 2 and so on), kept with the old and new name, address and TIN, the reason and who approved it, listed in Reissued Documents and written to the audit trail. The print-out then shows "Reissue no. 1 of this document" with the date. The button is shown to users with the special permission "Can correct the name, address or TIN printed on an issued document (a reissue, with a reason)" and the Print right on the document's page. It is not offered on a voided document or on a document with no printed name. Each correction is approved. A user with the Approve right on the document's page approves their own correction. Anyone else needs a supervisor who has that right, who types their username and password under Supervisor approval in the dialog, or a one-time approval code from Approval Codes . The dialog says so: "A user without the Approve right on this page needs a supervisor's approval." The approver is shown in the Approved by column of Reissued Documents. Invoice INV-00015 after its printed name was corrected to Maria R. Santos To correct the name printed on a document: If the name is wrong at its source, correct it there first: on Member Information for a member, otherwise with Edit party on the Party Center (or on the role record, for a party with one role). Open the document and click Correct printed name . The boxes Name to print , Address and TIN hold the party master's current details; the line under them gives the name printed now. Change them if needed. An address or TIN box left empty takes the party master's current detail. Type the reason, which is required and goes to the audit trail. If you do not have the Approve right on the document's page, open Supervisor approval and have a supervisor type their username and password, or type a one-time approval code. Click Correct printed name . The program says, for example, "Invoice INV-00015 reissued with the corrected name. The correction is kept in the audit trail." Example Invoice INV-00015 of ₱500.00 was issued to Maria Santos. Her legal name is corrected to Maria R. Santos, then the invoice is reissued with the reason "Middle initial missing on the issued invoice". The invoice still owes ₱500.00 and posts the same entries; it now prints "Maria R. Santos" and "Reissue no. 1 of this document, 10/12/2026". When the correction is refused, the document's page shows the message and the dialog opens again by itself with the name, address, TIN and reason as you typed them; when a supervisor's approval is needed, Supervisor approval is open. Correct what the message asks and click Correct printed name again. The messages: "The name, address and TIN are the same as on the document." "Enter the reason for the correction." "Supervisor approval is required: correction of the name printed on Invoice INV-00015. Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below, or type a one-time approval code." "Approval failed: the supervisor username or password is wrong." "You are not allowed to correct the name printed on an issued document (special permission: reissue documents)."

href="#pg-coop-business_units" aria-label="Link to this section"> A multipurpose cooperative runs several lines of business: savings and credit, a consumer store, wholesale or member purchasing, marketing of members' produce, production, services. Each document carries one line of business, and so do its ledger lines, so the one general ledger can be reported for the whole cooperative or for one line at a time. A line sets who may transact in it, the price levels of members and nonmembers, and whether its member transactions count for patronage refund. The same page holds the default line of each kind of document, the lines of the program the cooperative runs, the member and nonmember prices, the document rules (the lock on posted documents and the member no. on documents), the goods and services that count for patronage refund, and the inter-unit accounts. Where to find it: Members & Others > Lines of Business. Lines of Business with three lines: SC Savings and Credit, TR Consumer Store and MK Marketing of Produce The lines of business The list shows each line with its Code , Line of business (the name and kind), Who may transact , Patronage (Counts or Does not count), Prices (member / nonmember) (the price levels that apply in the line: its own, otherwise the level set under Prices when the line of business has none followed by "(general)", otherwise "Standard") and the number of Documents . An inactive line is greyed. Edit opens a line in the form on the right. The form New line of business (or Edit and the line): Field What to enter / what it means Code A short code of up to 10 letters, numbers and dashes, for example MK. It is saved in capitals and shown in lists and in the Unit column of documents. Name For example Marketing of Produce. Kind Savings and credit, Consumer store / retail, Wholesale / member purchasing, Marketing of members' produce, Production / processing, Services, or Other. Who may transact Members and nonmembers ; Nonmembers need approval (a supervisor approves each sale to a nonmember); or Members only (sales to nonmembers and walk-in customers are refused). A marketing line applies the same rule to the suppliers of produce. See The Line of business field on documents . Price level of members, Price level of nonmembers The price levels used in this line for customers who have no price level of their own. "The general one" uses the prices set under Prices when the line of business has none . Usual site The inventory site where the line usually works, for example the store's warehouse. A new document whose default line of business is this line starts at this site, and choosing this line on a form moves the form's site to it (see The Line of business field on documents ). Order in lists The lines are listed by this number, then by code. Description What the line does. Member transactions here count for patronage refund Ticked, the member transactions of this line can count for patronage refund (see The patronage refund basis ). Active Untick to stop using the line. New documents can no longer choose it; its documents keep it. Click Save . When editing, New returns to an empty form. A line of business cannot be deleted. Defaults, lines run and document rules "The line of business a new document takes when its form does not choose one. Forms show the choice while two or more lines are active." Choose a line, or None , for each kind of document: Cooperative vouchers (receipts, disbursements, loan releases, journal vouchers) Sales (estimates, orders, invoices, sales receipts, payments, credit memos, refunds) Purchasing (purchase orders, receipts, bills, bill payments, vendor credits, advances) Point of sale (sales, returns, over and short) Inventory (adjustments, transfers, builds, processing) Banking (checks, deposits, transfers, cash vouchers, bank charges and interest) General journal, depreciation, asset disposals and opening balances The upgrade set SC Savings and Credit for the cooperative vouchers, TR Consumer Store for sales, purchasing, point of sale and inventory, and None for banking and the general journal. While only one line is active, every new document takes that line. Lines the cooperative runs lists the parts of the program that can be switched off: Point of Sale, Inventory, Savings & Deposits, Loans, Teller and Fixed Assets. Untick one the cooperative does not run. "A line switched off closes its entry pages for everybody. Its reports stay, so its history can be read." Its entry pages leave the menu for every user, administrators included. Prices when the line of business has none : the price level of Members and of Nonmembers and walk-in customers , or Standard prices (see Member and nonmember prices ). Documents : Lock posted documents (see Posted documents are locked ). Turning it on or off needs the Approve right on this page: "Turning the lock of posted documents on or off needs the Approve right on this page." Print the member no. under the name of a member on invoices, receipts, checks and vouchers (see Labels and the member number ). Click Save settings . It needs the Edit right on the page; the changes are written to the audit trail. Member and nonmember prices When a sale is entered, the price of an item comes from the first price level found in this order: The customer's own price level, on the customer record. "A customer's own price level always comes first." The line of business's price level of members, when the customer's party is an active member (an applicant or a suspended member counts as a member), or its price level of nonmembers otherwise. A walk-in sale with no customer uses the nonmember level. The level set under Prices when the line of business has none , for members or for nonmembers and walk-in customers. Otherwise, the standard price of the item. A price level can have dates. On Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists , the Price levels list has Valid from and Valid until : a level with dates applies only to documents dated within them, for example a promotion for one month; a level without dates always applies. Outside its dates, or when it is inactive, the level is not used and the standard price applies. Documents without a line of business This box is shown to users with the Edit right while some documents have no line of business. It counts them by kind, for example "General journal, depreciation, asset disposals and opening balances: 3". To give older documents a line of business: In Documents , choose the kind of documents. In Give them , choose the line of business. Type the Reason . Click Assign . Every document of that kind without a line of business gets it, for example "3 document(s) given SC Savings and Credit." "Only the line of business is recorded on the documents and their ledger lines; amounts, numbers and dates do not change." The assignment is written to the audit trail. Goods and services that count for patronage refund "Not every member sale qualifies: only these items, in lines of business that count." The goods and services are the items of the types Inventory part, Non-inventory part, Inventory assembly and Service. The box says how many of the active ones count, for example "19 of 19 active goods and services count." To mark many items at once, choose a Category (or Every good and service ), choose Count or Do not count in They , and click Apply . Only the goods and services of the category are changed; other charges, discounts and the other item types are left as they are. The program says how many items were updated. One item at a time, tick Counts for patronage refund on the item in Item List . New items do not count until they are marked. Inter-unit accounts When one line of business lends to, sells to or charges another, the books use accounts kept only for these dealings: a due-to and due-from account between the lines, and, for sales and charges between them, an inter-unit sales account and the matching cost account. In Due to / due from, inter-unit sales and charges, and their cost , tick these accounts among the asset, liability, income and expense accounts, and click Save . The program says "Inter-unit accounts saved." "Accounts used only for dealings between lines of business, such as Due from Consumer Store and Due to Savings and Credit, or Inter-unit Sales and Inter-unit Purchases. They show on each unit's statements and are eliminated (left out) when the whole cooperative is reported: what the units owe each other nets out, and what they sold or charged each other nets out against its cost, so nothing is counted twice." Elimination means that, on the statements of the whole cooperative, the inter-unit accounts are left out, because what one line owes, sells or charges another is not a dealing with anyone outside the cooperative. The asset and liability accounts are netted together, and the income and expense accounts together, each group on its own. See Eliminations . The Line of business field on documents While two or more lines are active, the document forms of Customers and Vendors (estimates, orders, invoices, sales receipts, payments, credit memos, purchase orders, item receipts, bills, bill payments, advances), and Write Checks, Make Deposits, Cash Voucher and Make Journal Entries show a Line of business field. It starts with the default line for that kind of document; a saved document shows its own line. Leave it blank and the document has no line of business. Documents entered without the field, such as cooperative vouchers, POS sales and inventory documents, take the default of their kind. The forms with an inventory site follow the usual site of the line of business. A new sales order, invoice, sales receipt, credit memo, purchase order, bill, supplier debit memo or check, and a new receipt on Receive Items (when it does not come from a purchase order), starts at the usual site of its default line of business, or at the first site when the line has none. Choosing on the form a line of business that has a usual site moves the form's site to it; you can still change the site afterwards. When a sale (an invoice, sales receipt, sales order, statement charge or POS sale) is saved for the first time, and again when an edit changes its customer or its line of business, the program checks who may transact in its line of business. The customer counts as a member when its party has an active membership; an applicant or a suspended member counts too. In a marketing line, the same check applies to the supplier of a purchase order, item receipt or bill, when it is first saved and when an edit changes the supplier or the line of business. Members only: a document made out to a nonmember or a walk-in customer is refused, for example "Savings and Credit serves members only, and this invoice is made out to a nonmember. Choose a member, or record it under another line of business." Nonmembers need approval: a user with the Approve right on the document's page saves the document as usual; others need a supervisor's approval on the form, for example "Supervisor approval is required: buy from a nonmember in Marketing of Produce. Ask a supervisor to enter their username and password below, or type a one-time approval code." The supervisor is recorded as the approver of the document. Members and nonmembers: nothing is checked. Step by step To add a line of business: Open Members & Others > Lines of Business . In New line of business , type the Code , for example MK, and the Name , for example Marketing of Produce. Choose the Kind , for example Marketing of members' produce, and Who may transact , for example Nonmembers need approval. Choose the price levels of members and nonmembers, if the line has its own. Tick or untick Member transactions here count for patronage refund . Click Save . The program says "Line of business saved." If the line should be the default for a kind of document, choose it under Defaults, lines run and document rules and click Save settings . Good to know "Enter the code and the name of the line of business." "The code uses letters, numbers and dashes only." "Code MK is already used." A line that is the default of a kind of document cannot be made inactive: "This line of business is the default of Sales (estimates, orders, invoices, sales receipts, payments, credit memos, refunds). Choose another default first." Adding or changing a line needs the Create or Edit right on the page; the settings, the assignment of older documents, the patronage items and the inter-unit accounts need the Edit right. Every change is written to the audit trail. Statement of Operations by Line of Business at the top of the page opens that report .

href="#s-bu-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Line of business filter Every report with a Class filter gets a Line of business filter next to it while two or more lines of business are active, for example the Trial Balance , the Balance Sheet , the Income Statement and the General Ledger . The cooperative Statement of Financial Condition and Statement of Operations always have it. Choose a line and the report counts only the ledger lines of that line's documents; the note above the report reads, for example, "Line of business: SC Savings and Credit only." Leave it at All for the whole cooperative. Eliminations When the whole cooperative is reported and inter-unit accounts are marked on Lines of Business, the financial statements eliminate the dealings between lines of business: the Trial Balance , the Balance Sheet , the Income Statement , the Statement of Cash Flows , and the cooperative Statement of Financial Condition and Statement of Operations . Their note reads "Whole cooperative; balances and charges between lines of business are eliminated." The inter-unit asset and liability accounts are netted together: what the lines owe each other. The inter-unit income and expense accounts are netted together: what the lines sold or charged each other, against its cost. Only a difference that does not net to zero, such as an entry recorded on one side only, stays, on the first account of its group that has a balance, so the statements still balance and show it. The General Ledger , the Journal , the Trial Balance by Date Range , the Trial Balance of Totals and the Balance Sheet by Date Range show every entry as it was booked, and their note reads "Whole cooperative; entries between lines of business are listed as booked (they are eliminated only on the financial statements)." Run for one line of business, every report shows the inter-unit accounts as they are. The Statement of Operations by Line of Business shows each line side by side, with the elimination of the inter-unit income and expense accounts in a column of its own. Accounts receivable and payable in the reconciliation The Subsidiary vs General Ledger Reconciliation now also has the lines Accounts receivable (customers) and Accounts payable (suppliers) . Each compares the open balances of the documents on the date (invoices, statement charges and finance charges less unapplied payments and credit memos; bills less supplier debit memos) with the accounts receivable or accounts payable control accounts. When they differ, the customers or suppliers whose open documents differ from their ledger balance are listed under the line, with their C- or V- number; click one to open it on the Customer Center or Vendor Center. "(no name on the ledger line)" collects entries made to a control account with no customer or supplier. A journal entry posted to a control account without a document shows as a difference. The patronage refund basis On a Patronage Refund batch, Patronage measured by chooses the basis of each member's share, between the dates in Patronage from and to : Choice What is counted for each member Income earned from the member (the income accounts chosen) The credits less the debits on the Income accounts (patronage) you choose, on ledger lines that carry the member's name or are made out to a customer record of the member's party. A line of an item counts only when the item counts for patronage refund. Member's purchases of goods and services that count The item lines of the invoices, sales receipts, POS sales and statement charges made out to a customer record of the member's party, less credit memos and POS returns, for the items that count. Voided, pending and suspended documents are left out. Member's deliveries (produce sold to the cooperative) that count The item lines of the bills, item receipts and checks from a supplier record of the member's party, less supplier debit memos, for the items that count. Voided and pending documents are left out. With each basis, only documents in lines of business whose member transactions count (or with no line of business) are taken. "A member is recognized through the party, also when buying or selling as a customer or supplier." The rest of the batch (method, credit, approval, posting) is as described under Interest on Share Capital and Patronage Refund .

href="#s-party-reports" aria-label="Link to this section"> The party reports are listed under Parties > Reports in the sidebar and in the Parties card of the Report Center ; the Statement of Operations by Line of Business is under Members & Others > Reports . The common report tools ( Refresh , Print / PDF , Excel , CSV , Email link , Modify Report , Memorize and Columns ) are explained in Working with reports .

Where to find it: Parties > Reports > Party List. The Party List of the sample cooperative Filters: Role (Member, Customer, Supplier, Employee, Other name, More than one role or No role), Status (Active, Inactive or Merged), Kind (Person or Organization), Home branch (the party's home branch, or its member's branch) and Search (Party ID, legal name, name in lists or TIN). The columns: Party ID and Name (click either to open the Party Center), Legal name (printed) , Roles , Member no. , TIN and Status . Kind , Mobile , E-mail , Home branch and On file since can be added with Columns . The note gives the number of parties. For users without the permission to see confidential member details, the TIN, mobile and e-mail of members are partly hidden, and the note says "Members' TIN and contact details are partly hidden."

href="#pg-rpt-party_role_history" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every role given, taken away, restored, linked and moved, every link of two parties and every change of a party's name, with the reason and the user: the full history behind the Role history box of the Party Center. The Party Role History for this fiscal year, starting with the roles held at the upgrade Filters: Dates (this fiscal year at first), Role (Member, Customer, Supplier, Employee, Other name, or The party itself), What happened (Granted, Revoked, Restored, Moved in, Moved out, Merged, Edited or Linked) and Search (Party ID, party name or reason). Record and Approved by can be added with Columns . The entries made by the upgrade show "Held at the upgrade" and no user. "Membership status changes are also on the member's status history."

href="#pg-rpt-doc_reissues" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every correction of the name, address or TIN printed on an issued document (see Correcting the printed name ). "Amounts and the ledger did not change." Where to find it: Parties > Reports > Reissued Documents. Reissued Documents with the correction of invoice INV-00015 Filters: Dates of the correction (this fiscal year at first) and Search (document number, name before or name now). The columns: When the correction was made, Document (click it to open the document), Dated (the date of the document), Reissue no. , Name before , Name now , Reason and By . Address before , Address now , TIN before , TIN now and Approved by can be added with Columns .

t: Statement of Operations by Line of Business
x: href="#pg-rpt-sop_business_unit" aria-label="Link to this section"> The income and expenses of each line of business side by side, with the whole cooperative in the last column, from the one general ledger. Each line of business is the ledger lines of its documents. Where to find it: Members & Others > Reports > Statement of Operations by Line of Business, or the button at the top of Lines of Business . The Statement of Operations by Line of Business, fiscal year to date Filters: Dates (fiscal year to date at first) and Class . There is no Line of business filter: every line is a column. How to read it: there is a column for each active line of business, and for an inactive line with activity in the period, then No line of business when some ledger lines have none, Eliminations when inter-unit income or expense accounts are marked, and Whole cooperative . The rows are the income accounts under REVENUES with Total revenues , the expense accounts under EXPENSES with Total expenses , and NET SURPLUS (LOSS) . Expenses are shown as positive amounts; sales returns and discounts show as negative revenues. Click an account to open its General Ledger for the period. The note above the table says how the lines are taken from the one general ledger. With inter-unit income or expense accounts marked it reads "Sales and charges between lines of business (the inter-unit income and expense accounts) net out in the Eliminations column; a difference that does not net shows on the whole-cooperative column."; without them, "No inter-unit income or expense accounts are set, so nothing is eliminated (set them on Members & Others > Lines of Business)." When some documents have no line of business, it adds "Documents without a line of business are shown apart; give them one on Members & Others > Lines of Business." Tip In the sample cooperative, the depreciation expense of ₱113,950.00 falls under No line of business because the default line for the general journal and depreciation is None. Assign those documents on Documents without a line of business , or set a default for them, so that each line carries its own costs.

href="#s-party-rights" aria-label="Link to this section"> The new pages are given to roles on User Role Configuration or Page Access Configuration like any other page. The Administrator role and the Company Owner have every right and every special permission. The upgrade gave the standard roles this access: Role Pages Rights General Manager Party Center, Identity Review, Consolidated Party Statement, Party List, Party Role History, Reissued Documents, Statement of Operations by Line of Business, Lines of Business Create, Edit, Print/Export and Approve Branch Manager The same pages, except Lines of Business Create, Edit, Print/Export and Approve Bookkeeper, Accountant The same pages, except Lines of Business Create and Edit on the Party Center only; Print/Export on all Membership Officer, Loan Officer, A/R Clerk, A/P Clerk Party Center, Consolidated Party Statement, Party List Create and Edit on the Party Center; Print/Export on all Teller, Credit Committee, Collector Party Center, Consolidated Party Statement Print/Export (they read the pages) Auditor Every page above, Lines of Business included Print/Export (reads them) The four special permissions of this version, set for each role on User Role Configuration: Special permission What it allows Given by the upgrade to Cooperative: can see confidential member details (birth date, TIN, contact numbers, home address) See in full the TIN, date of birth, contact numbers, e-mail, address and registration no. of a member's party on the party pages and the Party List; the date of birth, TIN, mobile, e-mail, addresses and contact numbers of an existing member on Member Information; and the age, mobile and address on the Member Master List. Without it they are partly hidden or left out (see Confidential member details ). General Manager, Branch Manager, Membership Officer, Loan Officer, Credit Committee Parties: can link records found to be the same person or organization, and move a role to another party Same: keep and Link two parties found another way on Identity Review, and Move on the Party Center. General Manager, Branch Manager Can correct the name, address or TIN printed on an issued document (a reissue, with a reason) Correct printed name on a document, together with the Print right on the document's page. Each correction is also approved (see below). General Manager, Bookkeeper, Accountant Can change or delete a posted document while posted documents are locked (with a reason) Change the amounts, accounts, names, dates and lines of a posted document, with a reason, and delete it, while Lock posted documents is on. General Manager, Accountant The Approve right is used on these pages: Identity Review: linking two parties needs the Approve right on the page, or a supervisor who has it approves on the form. Correct printed name: a correction is approved by the user's own Approve right on the document's page, or by a supervisor who has it. Lines of Business: turning Lock posted documents on or off needs the Approve right on the page. There is no supervisor approval for this. Documents in a line of business with "Nonmembers need approval": a sale to a nonmember (or, in a marketing line, a purchase from a nonmember), when it is first saved or when an edit changes the customer, supplier or line of business, needs the Approve right on the document's page, or a supervisor who has it approves on the form.

href="#s-how-the-platform-works" aria-label="Link to this section"> Read this once before you create the first company. It explains the words used on every platform page. One database per company. A database is the store where the program keeps its records. Each company has a database of its own, holding all of its customers, suppliers, items, transactions, users and audit trail. The database the program was installed with is Company 1 ; every company you add gets a new database, made and named by the program (in the pictures, gsmart_company_002 for the second company). Nobody ever types a database name. The platform database. One more database, the platform database (in the pictures gsmart_master ), holds the list of companies, which database each one uses, the Company Codes, which company every username belongs to, the Super Admin accounts and the platform audit log. It holds no accounting records. Nobody can see another company's records. A company user only ever works in their own company's database. The company is decided on the server when they log in, from the platform database, and is checked again on every click. Nothing in the address bar, a form or a cookie can move a session to another company. Each company's logo, pictures, receipts and backups are also kept in a folder of its own. The Super Admin belongs to no company. Your account lives in the platform database only. The platform pages never open a company's records. To work inside a company, you Open it: you then work through an account of your own in that company, and everything you do there is written in that company's audit trail. One log-in page, unique usernames. Company users, Company Owners and Super Admins all log in on the same page. The page finds where a username belongs, so a username can exist only once on the whole platform, across every company and the Super Admins. The Company Code is only for joining. Each company has a code, for example AD-UW92E , that its new employees type once on the join page. It says which company they are joining; it is not a password and opens nothing. See Company Profile & Code . The Company Owner. Each company has one owner, chosen by you. The owner has full authority inside the company, approves the employees who join, and manages its users and its Company Code. Inactive companies. A company you switch off keeps its database, users and records, but its users are logged out at their next click, nobody can log in to it or join it, and its scheduled report e-mails stop. You can still open it, and switch it on again at any time.

href="#s-turning-on-several-companies" aria-label="Link to this section"> Several companies are switched on once, by an administrator of the existing company, on Multi-Company Setup (System Administration). That page: creates the platform database; registers the existing database as Company 1 , without moving, changing or deleting any record in it; lists every existing user on the platform, so all of them keep logging in with the same username and password; gives Company 1 its Company Code and the Company Owner chosen from its users; creates the first Super Admin with the username and password typed on that page. There is no default Super Admin password. After the set-up, Multi-Company Setup leaves the menu, and the Super Admin logs in as described below.

t: Logging in as the Super Admin
x: href="#sec-sa-login" aria-label="Link to this section"> The Super Admin logs in on the ordinary log-in page, which reads Log in to your company once several companies are running. Open the log-in page of the program. Type your Super Admin username (for example superadmin ) in Username and your password in Password . Click Log in . The Companies page of the platform opens. If your password is a temporary one, My account opens first and asks you to replace it. The log-in page used by company users and the Super Admin alike The platform pages have a sidebar of their own, in two groups: Companies : Companies , New company , Database updates ; Platform : Super Admins , Platform settings , Platform audit log , My account . The top bar reads Platform administration . The button at the top right shows your full name; it opens a menu with Change password and Log out . Good to know A wrong password gives "Invalid username or password." with the number of attempts left. After 5 wrong passwords in a row (see Platform settings ) the account locks: "Too many failed attempts. The account is now locked." A locked account answers "This account is locked. Another Super Admin can unlock it (or run tools/platform.php)." and an inactive one "This account is inactive." See "When something goes wrong" at the end of this chapter. Your session ends after 30 minutes without activity (see Platform settings ): "You were logged out after a period of inactivity." Working inside a company keeps it alive. After 30 failed log-ins with unknown usernames (or wrong Super Admin passwords) from one computer within 15 minutes, that computer is stopped for 15 minutes: "Too many failed log-in attempts from this computer. Please wait 15 minutes and try again." Every log-in, failed log-in and log-out of a Super Admin is in the Platform audit log .

href="#pf-companies" aria-label="Link to this section"> The list of every company on the platform, with its Company Code, owner, status, number of users and database. It is the page you see after logging in and the place where you Open a company to work inside it. Where to find it: Companies > Companies. It opens after you log in, and the program name at the top left leads back to it. Right after multi-company is switched on, the list has one company, Sample Trading Company, whose owner is the System Administrator ( admin ): Companies right after the first log-in of the Super Admin, with Company 1 only With a second company, ABC Distribution Corp., created: Companies with Sample Trading Company and ABC Distribution Corp., each with its own database The figures at the top Figure What it counts Active companies Companies that are switched on. The line under it gives the number of companies in all. Inactive Companies that are switched off. Their users cannot log in. Company users Every user account listed on the platform, across every company, including those waiting for approval. Waiting for approval Employees who joined with a Company Code and wait for their Company Owner. Each owner approves their own. When a company's set-up failed or is still running, a yellow notice says so, for example "1 company set-up failed. Open the company to see the steps and set it up again." The columns Column What it means # The company's number on the platform. Company 1 is the original database. Company The name (click it to open the company's details page), and under it the contact person and e-mail. Company Code The current code. joining off under it means the code is switched off. Company Owner The owner's full name and username, or Not assigned . Status Active , Inactive , Being set up or Set-up failed . Users How many accounts the company has, and how many are waiting (for example 2 waiting ). Database The company's database, and under it original database for Company 1 or since and the date it was created. Last column Open for an active or inactive company; Details for a company that is being set up or whose set-up failed. Buttons New company : opens New company . Database updates : opens Database updates . Open : works inside the company as the Super Admin (see "Working inside a company" below).

href="#pf-new" aria-label="Link to this section"> Creates a company with a database of its own, copies the set-up lists of an existing company into it, and (if you wish) creates the owner's account, all in one step. Where to find it: Companies > New company, or the New company button on the Companies page. The empty New company form, with the list of what is set up on the right Fields The Company box: Field What to enter / what it means Company name The company's name, as it will appear on its reports and vouchers. Required. Two companies cannot have the same name. TIN The company's Tax Identification Number. Address The company's address. Contact person The person to contact about the company. Shown on the platform and on the company's profile. Phone The company's phone number. E-mail The company's e-mail address. Notes (platform only) Your own notes. Only Super Admins see them. Copy the set-up of The company whose set-up lists are copied (the active companies are listed; Company 1 is chosen at first). Employees who join wait for the owner's approval Ticked: employees who join with the Company Code wait for the owner's approval. The starting value comes from Platform settings . The Company Owner box: Field What to enter / what it means Create the owner's account now (otherwise assign one later) Ticked: the owner's account is made with the company. Cleared: the fields below are hidden and you assign an owner later on the company's page. Full name The owner's full name. Required when the box is ticked. E-mail The owner's e-mail address. Optional. Username The owner's log-in name: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore, saved in small letters. It must be free across every company and the Super Admins. Temporary password A password the owner will replace at the first log-in. It must follow the password rules of the company whose set-up is copied, and must not contain the username. Password again The same temporary password. The What is set up box on the right lists the steps, the set-up lists that are copied and what is never copied. It is a summary of what happens when you press Create company ; you do not fill anything in there. Step by step Click New company . Type the Company name and the other details of the company. Check Copy the set-up of . Choose the company whose chart of accounts, tax codes, roles and other lists are closest to what the new company needs. Tick or clear Employees who join wait for the owner's approval . Leave Create the owner's account now ticked and fill in the owner's Full name , E-mail , Username , Temporary password and Password again ; or clear it to assign the owner later. Click Create company and confirm the question "Create the company and its database now?". It takes a few moments. The company's page opens with the result. Give the owner their username and temporary password, and tell them to change the password at the first log-in. The New company form filled in for ABC Distribution Corp. and its owner John Doe What happens when you press Create company The company gets a Company Code, unique on the platform (for ABC Distribution Corp., AD-UW92E ). A database name is chosen: the prefix from Platform settings followed by the company number in three digits, for example gsmart_company_002 . A database that already exists on the server is never used or touched: the program adds a letter instead ( gsmart_company_002_b , _c ...). The database is created, with the same character set as the copied company's. Every table is created exactly as the copied company has it today, with all its columns, keys, indexes and links between tables, and every counter starting from 1. The set-up lists are copied: the company settings (with the new company's name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN; no logo, no closing date, and none of the cooperative's registered name, CDA registration number and signatories), the modules, the pages, the roles with their page access and special permissions (every role allowed on every site), the document numbering (starting again from 1), the chart of accounts with its account types (bank account numbers left blank, no balances), the module default accounts, terms, tax codes, payment methods, price level names, customer types, billing groups, item categories, units of measure, fixed asset categories with their accounts, the Withholding Tax Table and the business units (without their usual site). Of the cooperative: the member types, the savings transaction codes, the passbook types and their designs, the lists of ID types, documents, loan purposes, collateral types and account classes, the CDA report lines and calendar, the address types, contact channels and cities. Of the water billing: its settings, the organization units (branches without their class, divisions, segments), the bill codes, pipe sizes, rate codes and rates, the meter discounts, the discounts and their privileges, and the recurring billing plans. An Inventory bill code comes without its item, since items are not copied: link it again on Bill Codes. The water module's institution profile is made with the new company's name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN. One inventory site, Main , is added. The audit trail protection is put in place: database triggers that stop anybody from changing or deleting audit trail entries, even directly in the database. The water module's two views ( chartofaccntstbl and operator ) are made in the new database. The database user of the program needs the CREATE VIEW right for this. The owner's account is created with the company's full-access role ( Administrator ), and must change the temporary password at the first log-in. The new database is checked: every table is there, its structure matches the program, and no customer, supplier, item or transaction is in it. The company, its database and its users are registered on the platform, its file folder is made ( storage/companies/c002/ for company 2), and the first line of its audit trail is written. Only then is the company switched on. Nothing else is copied: no customers, suppliers, items, members, employees or other names, no savings or loan products, no classes, no users, transactions, sales, payments, bills, journals, balances, budgets, fixed assets, POS records, audit trail or other history. When everything worked, the message reads, for example, "ABC Distribution Corp. is set up with a database of its own. Company Code: AD-UW92E. The owner logs in as johndoe and must change the temporary password." The company's page shows each step with a green tick under Set-up steps : The page of ABC Distribution Corp. just after it was created, with its set-up steps Good to know If a step fails , the company is marked Set-up failed , the database that attempt made is removed again, and nobody can log in to the company or join it. The message reads "The set-up of ... did not finish:" followed by the step and the reason, and "Nothing half-made was left behind." The company's page shows where it stopped and lets you set it up again or delete the failed record (see Company Details ). Bring the copied company up to date first. If the company whose set-up is copied still needs a program update (see Database updates ), Create company (and Set it up again ) is refused with "... needs a database update first (Database updates): ... A company copied from it would not match the program." and nothing is made. Audit trail protection. On some servers the triggers cannot be created. The set-up then carries on (the company works), the Triggers step shows a red cross with the reason, and the company's page shows Missing beside Audit trail protection , with a button to try again. Messages before anything is created: "Enter the company name.", "There is already a company named ...", "The company e-mail address does not look right.", "Choose the company whose set-up is copied.", "The two owner passwords do not match.", "The owner's username: 3 to 50 characters, letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore.", "The username ... is already taken on this platform.", "Enter the owner's full name.", "The owner's e-mail address does not look right." and "The owner's temporary password must have ..." followed by what is missing. Nothing is created until all of these are right. The database user needs rights. The program creates the database with the MySQL user in config/config.php , which needs the right to create and drop databases and to create tables, keys and triggers in them. XAMPP's root user has them. On shared hosting, set the Name of new company databases: prefix in Platform settings to the prefix the host requires (for example cpuser_company_ ). The MySQL user must still be allowed to create databases with that prefix, because the program never uses a database that already exists. What the new owner sees at the first log-in, and what to do first in a new company, is in Your Company: Company Owner and Employees .

href="#pf-company" aria-label="Link to this section"> Everything about one company on a single page: its details, owner, users, Company Code, joining rules, database, status, set-up steps and recent activity. From here you change the owner, regenerate the code, switch the company off or on, and repair a failed set-up. Where to find it: Companies > Companies, then click the company's name (or Details for a company whose set-up did not finish). The page opens by itself after Create company . The page's title is the company's name; under it are the status and "Company #1, created ..." (with "set-up copied from ..." for a company made on the platform). The details page of Sample Trading Company, Company 1 The parts of the page Part What it holds Company information Company name , TIN , Address , Contact person , Phone , E-mail , Notes (platform only) and Save . Company Owner The current owner with e-mail and last log-in (or "This company has no Company Owner yet."), and the form to set a new owner. Users Every user of the company with Name , Username , Roles , Status , Account made and Last log-in , and the Sync user list button. Company Code The code, whether joining is on, Regenerate , the switch Employees can join with the code with a date, and New employees wait for the owner's approval with a starting role. Database Database , Origin , Tables , Checked , Program updates , Audit trail protection and Files . Deactivate or Activate Switches the company off (with a reason) or on. Set-up steps Each attempt at setting the company up, step by step, with a tick or a cross and the details. Recent platform activity The last 25 entries of the platform audit log for this company. The Database box, line by line: Line What it means Database The name of the company's database. Origin The original database (Company 1) or Created by the platform . Tables and Checked How many tables the database had when it was last checked, and when. Program updates Up to date , or how many updates still have to be run (see Database updates ). Audit trail protection In place , or Missing in red with a Put the protection back button. Files The company's own folder for its logo, pictures, receipts and backups: storage/ (the original folders) for Company 1, storage/companies/c002/ for company 2, and so on. Step by step To change the company's details: Change the fields under Company information . Click Save . The message is "Company details saved." The name, address, phone, e-mail and TIN are also written to the company's own settings, so they appear on its reports and vouchers; the change is recorded in the company's audit trail. To make one of the company's users the Company Owner: Under Company Owner , leave One of its users chosen. Pick the person in the list. Only active, approved users are listed. Click Set owner and confirm "Make this person the Company Owner?". The message is "Company Owner saved." The new owner has full authority in the company from their next click, whatever their roles. The previous owner stays a user with the roles they had. To give the company an owner with a new account: Under Company Owner , choose A new account . Fill in Username , Full name , E-mail and Temporary password . The same rules apply as on New company . Click Set owner and confirm. The message is "Company Owner saved. They must change the temporary password at the first log-in." The account gets the company's full-access role. To give the company a new Company Code: Under Company Code , click Regenerate . Confirm "Make a new code? The current one stops working at once; people who already joined stay." The message gives the new code: "New Company Code: ... The old one no longer works." Send it to the Company Owner. To stop joining, or to set the last day the code can be used: Turn Employees can join with the code off, or pick a date in the date box beside Save . Click Save . The message is "Company Code saved." The date counts to the end of that day. To change whether new employees need approval, and the role they start with: Tick or clear New employees wait for the owner's approval . Pick a role in the list, or leave Role chosen when approving . Full-access roles are not offered. Click Save . The message is "Joining rules saved." Without approval a role is required: "Without approval, new employees need a role to start with." To switch a company off: Under Deactivate , type the Reason . It is required. Click Deactivate and confirm. The message reads "... is deactivated. Its users cannot log in and nobody can join it; all of its data is kept." Users who are working at that moment are logged out at their next click with "Your company's access is currently suspended. Please contact your Company Owner." You can still open the company. To switch it on again: Under Activate , type a reason if you wish. Click Activate . The message reads "... is active again. Its users can log in." The users log in with their accounts as they were. A company whose database still needs updates cannot be switched on: "Bring the company database up to date first (Database updates)." To rebuild the platform's list of the company's usernames: Click Sync user list above the Users table. The message says how many users are listed on the platform, for example "9 user(s) listed on the platform." Use it when a user of the company cannot log in although their account is there, or after the company database was restored outside the program. If a username is also used in another company, the message names it: "These usernames belong to another company and cannot log in until they are renamed: ..." Rename that user on the company's User Accounts page and sync again. To put the audit trail protection back (when it shows Missing ): Click Put the protection back in the Database box. The message is "The audit trail protection is in place.", or "The triggers could not be created:" with the reason given by the database server. A company whose set-up did not finish A company that is Set-up failed (or still Being set up after 15 minutes) shows a red box at the top: "The set-up did not finish" (or "has not finished"), with the step and the reason, and "The company is not active, nobody can log in to it or join it, and any database this attempt created was removed again." To set it up again, once the cause is fixed (for example the database rights): If the company needs an owner's account, fill in Username , Full name , E-mail and Temporary password in the red box. Passwords are never kept, so they must be typed again. You can also leave them empty and assign the owner later. Click Set it up again . The steps run again as a new attempt, listed under Set-up steps . The message is "The company is set up and active." or "The set-up failed again. The steps below say where." To delete the failed record instead: Type the company's name exactly in Or delete this failed record: type the company name . Click Delete record and confirm. The message is "The failed company record was deleted." Its Company Code is retired. Good to know Active companies are never deleted. Only the record of a company whose set-up failed can be deleted; for any other company the answer is "Only a company whose set-up failed can be deleted. Deactivate an active company instead." Changes reach the company's audit trail. Changing the details or the owner, regenerating the code, and switching the company off or on are written in the company's own audit trail under the name platform: followed by your username, with the role Super Admin , as well as in the platform audit log. The company's users see it there. Two companies cannot share a name. "Another company already has that name." The Users list here is for reading. Users are approved, changed and deactivated inside the company, by its owner or by you after Open company (see Employees & Users ). If the company's database cannot be reached, a red line says so ("The company database cannot be reached: ..."). The company information and the Company Code can still be changed on the platform; the owner, the joining rules, the status and the user list wait until the database answers again. Open company at the top of the page works as Open on the Companies page. All companies goes back to the list.

href="#sec-inside-company" aria-label="Link to this section"> To look at a company's books, fix a setting, approve an employee or help a user, you open the company and work inside it as its Super Admin. Where to find it: Open on the Companies page, or Open company on the company's details page . The Super Admin working inside ABC Distribution Corp., with the yellow strip at the top While you work inside a company: A yellow strip at the top reads "Super Admin: you are working inside ABC Distribution Corp.. Everything you do here is recorded in its audit trail." with a Back to the platform link. For an inactive company it adds "(inactive: its users cannot log in)". You see the company exactly as its users do: its menu, its Home page, its records. You have full authority, like the Company Owner: every page opens and every action is allowed, including the owner's actions on Company Profile & Code and Employees & Users . You work through an account of your own in that company, named @platform- followed by your Super Admin number (for example @platform-1 ) and shown as "Super Admin:" followed by your name. The program makes this account the first time you open the company. Nobody can log in with it (its password is random and never shown), and it never appears in the company's user lists. Every change you make is in the company's audit trail under that name. The menu under your name at the top right reads Super Admin, managing this company and offers Back to the platform and Log out . Step by step On Companies , click Open on the company's row. The company's Home page opens with the yellow strip. Work as you would in any company. Click Back to the platform in the strip (or in the menu under your name). You return to the Companies page. Good to know Log out in the company's menu ends your Super Admin session as well and takes you to the log-in page. Use Back to the platform to leave the company only. Opening any platform page while you are inside a company (for example with the browser's Back button) takes you out of the company first. A company whose database needs an update cannot be opened: "The database of ... needs the latest update first. Use "Update databases" on the Companies page." Run the update on Database updates and open it again. Inactive companies can be opened, for example to check something before switching them on again. Every opening and closing of a company is in the Platform audit log ( company opened , company closed ).

href="#pf-updates" aria-label="Link to this section"> When a new version of the program is installed, it may bring upgrade scripts : files that add the new tables and columns the new version needs. Every company database has to receive them. This page shows which companies still need which scripts and runs them for you. Where to find it: Companies > Database updates, or the Database updates button on the Companies page. A company's details page also warns "This company's database needs ... update(s)." with a link here. Database updates with both company databases up to date The line at the top says how many upgrade scripts the program knows ( 9 in the picture). A company database is up to date when every one of them has been run on it. New companies are created up to date. The columns Column What it means Company The company (click to open its details page) and its status. Database The company's database. Updates to run The names of the scripts still to run, oldest first, or Up to date . A red message means the database could not be read. Last column Run , for a company with scripts to run. Step by step After copying the files of a new version of the program onto the server: Back up the company databases and the platform database (see "When something goes wrong" below). Log in as the Super Admin and open Database updates . Click Update all companies (shown only when something is waiting) and confirm "Run every pending update on every company database? Back the databases up first." To update one company only, click Run on its row. Read the message: "... update(s) run. Every company database is up to date.", "Every company database was already up to date.", or "Some updates could not be run." followed by the company and the reason. Good to know The scripts run oldest first. For each company, the program stops at the first script that fails and leaves the later ones for the next attempt. The scripts keep every record and can safely be run again. Until its database is updated, a company cannot be opened by the Super Admin or switched on again, and no new company can be copied from it. Its users see a Database update needed page after log-in instead of their work: users of the other companies are asked to contact the Super Admin, while administrators of Company 1 also see the files to run by hand. Each update run is recorded in the Platform audit log as database updated , with the names of the scripts. The server administrator can also run every pending update from the command line: php tools/platform.php update-all .

href="#pf-admins" aria-label="Link to this section"> The accounts that manage the platform. A Super Admin can open and change every company, so keep this list short, and keep at least two active Super Admins so one can help the other. Where to find it: Platform > Super Admins. Super Admins with one account and the New Super Admin form The columns Column What it means Name Full name, You for your own account, and the e-mail address. Username The log-in name. Status Active , Inactive or Locked . temporary password under it means the person has not yet replaced a temporary password. Last log-in Date and time of the last log-in. The buttons at the end of each row, for the other Super Admins: Unlock (for a locked account), Deactivate or Activate , and a Temporary password box with Reset . On your own row there is Change my password , which opens My account . Fields The New Super Admin box: Field What to enter Full name The person's full name. Required. Username 3 to 50 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore. Saved in small letters. It must not be used by any Super Admin or any company user. E-mail Optional. Temporary password At least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol, not containing the username. Step by step To add a Super Admin: Fill in the New Super Admin box. Click Create . The message reads "Super Admin ... created. They must change the temporary password at the first log-in." Give the new Super Admin their username and temporary password. At their first log-in My account opens and they cannot use any other platform page until they have chosen their own password. To reset another Super Admin's password: Type a temporary password in the Temporary password box on their row. Click Reset . The message is "Temporary password set for ..." A locked account is unlocked at the same time, and the person must change the password at the next log-in. To unlock, deactivate or activate another Super Admin, click Unlock , Deactivate (and confirm) or Activate on their row. Good to know "You cannot deactivate your own account." and "This is the last active Super Admin." protect the platform from being left without anyone to manage it. "That username is already used on the platform (by a Super Admin or a company user)." means the username is taken somewhere on the platform. Super Admin passwords follow their own rule (at least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol), whatever the companies' password rules are. Every change here is in the Platform audit log .

href="#pf-settings" aria-label="Link to this section"> The few settings that belong to the platform as a whole rather than to one company. Where to find it: Platform > Platform settings. Platform settings with the database prefix, the approval default and the log-in limits Fields Field What it means Name of new company databases: prefix The start of the name of each new company database; the company number follows it ( 002 , 003 ...).
