Letters, digits and underscores, at most 50. Left empty, the program uses the first company's database name followed by _company_ (shown in grey in the box). On shared hosting, use the prefix your control panel requires (for example cpuser_ ). New companies: employees who join wait for approval The starting value of the approval box on New company . Each company can change it afterwards on its own page. Super Admin session ends after (minutes without activity) How long a Super Admin can be idle before being logged out. At least 5. Super Admin failed log-ins before the account locks How many wrong passwords in a row lock a Super Admin account. Wrong Company Codes allowed from one address in 15 minutes How many wrong codes one computer may type on the join page. After that, the join page stops that computer for 15 minutes. Step by step Change the values you need. Click Save . The message says how many settings were changed, for example "1 setting(s) changed." Good to know The box under the settings, Platform database , names the platform database (for example gsmart_master ) and reminds you that the MySQL user of config/config.php needs the right to create and drop databases and to create tables, keys and triggers in them. It also explains the emergency switch described in "When something goes wrong" below. Changing the prefix affects only companies created afterwards; existing databases keep their names. Messages: "The database prefix may only have letters, digits and underscores (at most 50)." and "The Super Admin session needs at least 5 minutes." Every change is in the Platform audit log as platform settings , with the new values.

href="#pf-audit" aria-label="Link to this section"> A permanent record of what happened on the platform and to which company: log-ins of Super Admins, companies created, opened, changed, switched off and on, codes regenerated, employees who joined, were approved or rejected, database updates and settings changes. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Where to find it: Platform > Platform audit log. Platform audit log showing the creation of ABC Distribution Corp. and the set-up of Company 1 The filters Filter What it does Company One company, or All companies . The list changes as soon as you pick one. What happened One kind of entry, or Everything . Only the kinds recorded so far are listed. From and To The period. It starts as the last 30 days. Click Show after changing the dates. The columns Column What it means When Date and time. Who The username, and under it what kind of person: super admin , owner , user , guest (someone on the join page) or system (the command-line tool). Company The company concerned, when there is one. What happened The kind of entry (see below). Details What exactly was done, for example "Set-up finished: database gsmart_company_002, 70 tables". From The address of the computer it came from. Some of the entries you will see: What happened Meaning platform setup Multi-company was switched on and Company 1 registered. login, login failed, logout, session timeout A Super Admin logged in, failed, logged out or timed out; login failed is also written for unknown usernames on the log-in page. login refused A user of an inactive company tried to log in. company created, company activated A company record was made; its set-up finished (or it was switched on again). company setup failed, company setup retried, company deleted A set-up failed, was run again, or a failed record was deleted. company opened, company closed A Super Admin opened a company or went back to the platform. company edited, company deactivated, owner changed The company's details, status or owner were changed. company code regenerated, company code state, company join rules The Company Code or the joining rules were changed, by the owner or a Super Admin. employee joined, join refused An employee made an account with a code; someone typed a code that was refused. employee approved, employee rejected A Company Owner decided on a join request. database updated, restore Upgrade scripts were run; a company database was restored from a backup. super admin created, super admin password reset, platform settings Changes to Super Admins or to the platform settings. Good to know The page shows the latest 500 entries of the period. Narrow the period or pick a company to see older ones. What happens inside a company is also in that company's own audit trail ( System Administration > Audit Trail ), in much more detail. The platform audit log records the platform's view: who did what to which company.

href="#pf-account" aria-label="Link to this section"> Where a Super Admin changes their own password. Where to find it: Platform > My account; also Change password in the menu under your name, and Change my password on Super Admins. It opens by itself when you log in with a temporary password. My account, with the boxes to change the Super Admin's password The line at the top gives your full name, username and last log-in. When you have a temporary password, a yellow line asks "Please replace your temporary password before continuing." Step by step Type your Current password . Type the new password in New password and again in Confirm new password . It needs at least 10 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, a number and a symbol, must not contain your username and must differ from the current one. Click Change password . The message is "Your password has been changed." and the Companies page opens. Messages: "Your current password is incorrect.", "The new passwords do not match.", "Choose a password different from your current one." and "The new password must have ..." followed by what is missing.

href="#s-when-something-goes-wrong" aria-label="Link to this section"> A Super Admin is locked out Another active Super Admin can unlock the account or reset its password on Super Admins . If there is no other Super Admin (or all are locked out), the server administrator can give the account a new temporary password from the command line, in the program folder: php tools/platform.php reset-superadmin USERNAME "NEWPASSWORD" Replace USERNAME with the Super Admin's username and NEWPASSWORD with the temporary password to give; keep the quotes, because the password contains a symbol. The password must follow the Super Admin rule. The account is unlocked and made active, and the Super Admin must choose a new password at the next log-in. The reset is written in the platform audit log. The same tool has three more commands for the server administrator: php tools/platform.php list : lists the companies with their status, database and Company Code; php tools/platform.php sync 2 : rebuilds the platform's list of the usernames of company 2 (or the number you type), like Sync user list ; php tools/platform.php update-all : runs the pending upgrade scripts on every company database, like Update all companies . A user cannot log in although the account exists Open the company's details page and click Sync user list . If a username is used in two companies (this can happen after restoring an old backup), the message names it; rename the user in one of the companies and sync again. Backups Each company backs up and restores its own database only, on its own Backup & Restore page. The files are kept in the company's own folder, and the files of companies other than Company 1 are named after the company number ( company_002_... ), not after the database. A restore can only rebuild the company's own tables. Statements in a backup file that switch to or name another database, create databases, users, triggers, routines or views, read files or copy data with a SELECT are refused and listed. The audit trail protection is put back afterwards, and the company's list of usernames on the platform is rebuilt; a username that now clashes with another company is reported. The platform database (for example gsmart_master ) is in no company's backup. Back it up yourself, for example with phpMyAdmin > Export, at the same time as the company databases, and keep a copy off the server. Switching multi-company off in an emergency If the platform database cannot be reached, no company can be opened. In an emergency the server administrator can move the file storage/platform/multi_company.json out of its folder: the program then runs as Company 1 alone, with Company 1's users only, and the other companies cannot be reached. Put the file back (or run Multi-Company Setup again) to return to several companies. Nothing is lost either way. Before going live with several companies Keep the Super Admin password safe, and create a second Super Admin. Check on Companies that every company has a Company Owner. Back up the platform database together with the company databases, and do it before every database update. Scheduled report e-mails are sent for every active company from the same daily task; nothing extra is needed per company.

t: Appendix A. What each transaction records
x: href="#app-posting" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every transaction you save is turned into general ledger lines and, for stocked items, into inventory movements. The rules are fixed in the program: you choose the accounts (through Module Default Accounts, items, tax codes and asset categories), but you never type the posting of an invoice or a bill yourself. This appendix lists, for every kind of transaction, the accounts it debits and credits, what it does to stock and to customer or vendor balances, and the page where you enter it.

href="#s-how-to-read-this-appendix" aria-label="Link to this section"> The account names are those of the demo chart of accounts of Sample Trading Company. Your company posts to the accounts chosen under Module Default Accounts , on each item in the Item List , on each tax code in Terms, Tax Codes & Other Lists and on each asset category. Prices and amounts on sales and purchase forms are VAT-exclusive. VAT is worked out on each line and posted to the account of the line's tax code (in the demo, 2100 Output Tax on sales and 1300 Input Tax on purchases). Stocked items are items of the types Inventory part and Inventory assembly . Only they have a quantity on hand and a value. Non-inventory parts, services and other charges post to accounts only. A stocked item leaves stock at its weighted-average cost : the book value of the item divided by the quantity on hand, over all sites. A sale that brings the quantity to zero takes all the value that is left. A customer balance is what 1100 Accounts Receivable holds for that customer and its jobs. A vendor balance is what 2000 Accounts Payable holds for that vendor. Every ledger line carries the class of the transaction (see The class on a transaction, at the end of this appendix). Tip To see the entry of any saved transaction, open it. The box General ledger entries created automatically lists every line with its account, memo, class, debit and credit. On sales documents (invoices, sales receipts, statement and finance charges, credit memos, POS sales and returns) the box is shown only to users who have the special permission View costs and margins , because it shows the cost of goods sold.

href="#s-where-the-accounts-come-from" aria-label="Link to this section"> The table lists every setting of Module Default Accounts , the account it points to in the demo company, and what uses it. Default account Demo account Used for Accounts Receivable 1100 Accounts Receivable Invoices, statement and finance charges, credit memos, payments, refunds Undeposited Funds 1050 Undeposited Funds Payments and sales receipts waiting to be deposited Default Sales Income 4000 Sales Sales lines whose item has no income account Sales Returns and Allowances 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances Credit memos and POS returns Sales Discounts 4060 Sales Discounts Early-payment discounts in Receive Payments Finance Charge Income 4100 Finance Charge Income Finance charges Reimbursable Expense Income 4110 Reimbursable Expense Income Billable costs added to an invoice Creditable Withholding Tax 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax Tax a customer withholds from a payment Output Tax 2100 Output Tax Sales VAT when the tax code names no account Accounts Payable 2000 Accounts Payable Bills, item receipts, debit memos, bill payments Input Tax 1300 Input Tax Purchase VAT when the tax code names no account Purchase Discounts 5050 Purchase Discounts Discounts taken in Pay Bills Default Purchases / Expense 6110 Purchases - Non-inventory Purchase lines whose item has no expense or cost account Inventory Asset 1200 Inventory Stocked items with no asset account of their own Cost of Goods Sold 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Cost of stocked items sold, when the item names none Inventory Adjustment (Shrinkage) 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage Adjustments and physical counts Processing / Disassembly Variance 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage Differences on processing orders Item Group Price Variance 4070 Item Group Price Variance Group price less the prices of the items, on item groups sold Processing Labor & Overhead Absorbed 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed Listed on the page; no posting rule reads it Cash on Hand (Register) 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers Proposed as the cash account of new POS terminals Cash Over and Short 6200 Cash Over and Short Drawer differences when a register is closed Card Clearing 1060 Card Clearing Card and other non-cash tenders whose payment method names no account E-wallet Clearing 1065 E-wallet Clearing E-wallet tenders whose method names no account Bank / Merchant Charges 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges Service charges, merchant fees on settlements Interest Income 4200 Interest Income Interest earned entered in Reconcile Retained Earnings 3200 Retained Earnings Earlier years' profit on the balance sheet Opening Balance Equity 3900 Opening Balance Equity Opening stock and opening asset balances Gain / Loss on Disposal of Assets 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets Asset disposals Important If a default account the transaction needs is not set, saving stops with the message The default account "..." is not set. Set it under Financial > Module Default Accounts. Nothing is saved until the account is chosen. There is no year-end closing entry to make. The balance sheet shows the net income of earlier fiscal years inside Retained Earnings, and the income statement starts again at the beginning of each fiscal year.

href="#s-overview" aria-label="Link to this section"> Transaction Entered on Number Posts to the ledger Estimate Create Estimates EST- No Sales Order Create Sales Orders SO- No Invoice Create Invoices INV- Yes, unless pending Sales Receipt Enter Sales Receipts SR- Yes, unless pending Statement Charge Enter Statement Charges SC- Yes Finance Charge Assess Finance Charges FC- Yes Customer Payment Receive Payments PMT- Yes Credit Memo Create Credit Memos/Refunds CM- Yes Customer Refund Create Credit Memos/Refunds Check series Yes Purchase Order Create Purchase Orders PO- No Item Receipt Receive Items IR- Yes Bill Enter Bills BILL- Yes Supplier Debit Memo Supplier Debit Memos DM- Yes Bill Payment Pay Bills Check series (AAP- when it applies an advance) Yes Advance to Supplier Advances to Suppliers ADV- Yes Check Write Checks Check series Yes Cash Voucher Cash Voucher CAV- Yes Deposit Make Deposits DEP- Yes Transfer Transfer Funds TRF- Yes Journal Entry Make Journal Entries JE- Yes Opening Balance Make Journal Entries JE- Yes Inventory Adjustment Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand ADJ- Yes Inventory Transfer Transfer Inventory IT- Stock only Build Assembly Build Assemblies BLD- Yes, unless pending Processing Order Disassemble / Process Items PRC- Yes, unless pending Depreciation Run Depreciation JE- Yes Asset Disposal Dispose of Assets JE- Yes POS Sale POS Register POS- Yes, unless suspended POS Return POS Receipts, Returns & Voids POS- Yes Cash Over/Short Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings JE- Yes Service Charge Reconcile JE- Yes Interest Earned Reconcile JE- Yes The names in the first column are the ones the program shows in lists, in Find and in the Type column of reports. Numbering is explained in Appendix C .

href="#s-sales-and-receivables" aria-label="Link to this section"> Estimate and Sales Order Entered on Create Estimates and Create Sales Orders . Ledger: nothing. The view of the document says Non-posting document: it records a commitment and does not affect the ledger. Stock: nothing moves. The quantities of an open sales order that are not yet invoiced count as on sales order in the stock status reports and the Inventory Center. Balances: no effect on the customer's balance. Status: an estimate is Pending , becomes Accepted when it is turned into a sales order or partly invoiced, and Closed when it is fully invoiced or closed with Close . A sales order is Open , then Partially filled , then Closed when every line is invoiced or closed. Invoice Entered on Create Invoices . Invoices are also made by Create Batch Invoices and by a charge sale on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit 1100 Accounts Receivable Invoice total, VAT included Income account of each item (for example 4000 Sales, 4010 Service Income) Line amount 2100 Output Tax (the tax code's account) VAT of the lines 5000 Cost of Goods Sold (the item's cost account) Average cost of stocked items 1200 Inventory (the item's asset account) Average cost of stocked items Stock: stocked items leave the Inventory site of the invoice (or the site of the line) at their average cost. The cost is stored on the line and shows in the Cost column for users who may view costs. Balances: the customer's balance goes up by the invoice total. The invoice stays open until payments or credits are applied to it. Special lines: a discount item is posted as a debit to its own income account (4060 Sales Discounts for DISC-10 and DISC-AMT); a payment item such as DOWNPMT (Down Payment Received) debits 1050 Undeposited Funds and lowers the amount charged to Accounts Receivable; billable costs added from bills and checks credit 4110 Reimbursable Expense Income; a subtotal line posts nothing; a group item is entered as the separate items it holds. Pending: an invoice saved with Pending (non-posting until marked final) ticked posts nothing (see Pending transactions, later in this appendix). Example ABC Trading Corp. is invoiced for one LAP-001 Laptop 14-inch i5 16GB at ₱39,990.00 plus 12% VAT, and the laptop's average cost is ₱32,000.00. The invoice debits 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱44,788.80, credits 4000 Sales ₱39,990.00 and 2100 Output Tax ₱4,798.80, and debits 5000 Cost of Goods Sold and credits 1200 Inventory ₱32,000.00. One laptop leaves the Main Warehouse, and ABC Trading Corp.'s balance goes up by ₱44,788.80. Sales Receipt Entered on Enter Sales Receipts . Ledger: the same as an invoice, except that the total is debited to the Deposit to account instead of Accounts Receivable. The default is 1050 Undeposited Funds; you can also choose a bank account or another current asset. Stock: stocked items leave the Inventory site at average cost. Balances: no effect on the customer's balance: the sale is paid on the spot. Later: a sales receipt deposited to 1050 Undeposited Funds waits in Make Deposits until you deposit it. Statement Charge Entered on Enter Statement Charges . Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit the income account of each item (for example 4100 Finance Charge Income for LATE-FEE Late Payment Fee, 4020 Delivery Income for DEL-FEE Delivery Fee), and credit Output Tax for any VAT. Stock: statement charges are meant for services and other charges. A stocked item on one would leave stock like on an invoice. Balances: the customer's balance goes up. The charge appears on the next statement and can be paid in Receive Payments. Finance Charge Made on Assess Finance Charges , one for each customer you select. Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit 4100 Finance Charge Income. No VAT. Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes up. The charge is due on the assessment date. Customer Payment Entered on Receive Payments , or as a payment at the counter on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit Deposit to account (default 1050 Undeposited Funds) Amount received 4060 Sales Discounts Early-payment discount 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax (or the tax's own account) Income tax withheld by the customer (1% / 2%) 1315 Creditable VAT Withheld (or the tax's own account) VAT withheld by the customer (5%) 1100 Accounts Receivable Amount received plus discount plus withholding Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes down by the amount received plus the discount and withholding. The invoices the payment is applied to become Partially paid or Paid . An amount received but not applied stays on the payment as an unapplied credit. Taxes withheld: each type ticked in the Withholding box is kept with its base, rate and ATC; the 1% / 2% and the 5% go to different accounts, as the BIR requires (an income-tax credit, and a VAT credit for 2550Q Item 16). A payment saved before the types were kept posts its withholding to 1310. Applying credits: using an existing credit memo or unapplied payment on the same screen posts nothing new; it only records which invoice the credit pays. At the POS: a payment taken at the counter debits the terminal's cash account for cash, or the clearing account of the payment method, and is applied to the customer's oldest open invoices first. Example ABC Trading Corp. pays the ₱44,788.80 invoice by check and withholds 1% of the VAT-exclusive amount, ₱399.90. You enter Amount received ₱44,388.90, and on the invoice line Withholding ₱399.90 and Payment ₱44,388.90. The payment debits 1050 Undeposited Funds ₱44,388.90 and 1310 Creditable Withholding Tax ₱399.90, and credits 1100 Accounts Receivable ₱44,788.80. The invoice is paid in full. Credit Memo Entered on Create Credit Memos/Refunds . Account Debit Credit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances Line amounts 2100 Output Tax VAT of the lines 1100 Accounts Receivable Credit memo total 1200 Inventory Average cost of goods returned to stock 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Average cost of goods returned to stock Stock: only when Return goods to stock is ticked: stocked items come back into the Return to site (or the inventory site of the credit memo) at the item's current average cost. Without the tick, only the first three lines are posted. Balances: the customer's balance goes down. What happens to the credit depends on the choice under What to do with this credit : keep it as an available credit, apply it to an invoice now, or give a refund. Customer Refund Recorded with the Refund button of a credit memo or of a payment that has an unapplied credit, on Create Credit Memos/Refunds . Ledger: debit 1100 Accounts Receivable, credit the Pay from account (a bank or cash account). Stock: none. Balances: the customer's balance goes back up by the refund, which uses up the credit. Rules: the refund cannot be more than the available credit. A refund cannot be edited: void it and record a new one. A refund above your amount limit needs supervisor approval.

href="#s-purchases-and-payables" aria-label="Link to this section"> Purchase Order Entered on Create Purchase Orders . Ledger: nothing. It is a non-posting document. Stock: nothing moves. The quantities not yet received count as on purchase order in the stock status reports. Balances: no effect on the vendor's balance. Status: Open , Partially filled as items are received, Closed when every line is received or closed. Item Receipt Entered on Receive Items , when goods arrive before the vendor's bill. Ledger: debit 1200 Inventory (the item's asset account) for stocked items, or the item's expense account for other items, and credit 2000 Accounts Payable. An item receipt carries no VAT. Stock: stocked items come into the receiving site at the cost on the receipt, and the average cost is worked out again. Balances: the vendor's balance goes up at once: open item receipts are part of Accounts Payable and of the A/P aging. Editing: an item receipt not billed yet can be edited; it is posted again (stock, Inventory and Accounts Payable) and the purchase order follows the new quantities received. Later: Enter Bill for Received Items turns the same record into a bill with a new BILL- number. The quantities stay as received; the cost and the VAT can change, and inventory value and the payable are adjusted to the billed cost. Bill Entered on Enter Bills , Receive Items and Enter Bills or Enter Bill for Received Items . Receipt Management , the Fixed Asset Register and Asset Maintenance can also create bills. Account Debit Credit Account of each line on the Expenses tab Line amount 1200 Inventory, for stocked items on the Items tab Line amount Expense account of other items (else their cost account, else 6110) Line amount 1300 Input Tax VAT of the lines 2000 Accounts Payable Bill total Stock: stocked items come into the site of the line (or the Default site for items ) at the bill's cost, and the item's average cost is worked out again. Balances: the vendor's balance goes up. The bill stays open until it is paid in Pay Bills or a debit memo is applied to it. Billable costs: a line marked billable to a Customer:Job is offered on that customer's next invoice. Example TechDistributors Inc. bills 5 MOU-001 Wireless Mouse at ₱350.00. The bill debits 1200 Inventory ₱1,750.00 and 1300 Input Tax ₱210.00, and credits 2000 Accounts Payable ₱1,960.00. Five mice come into stock, and the vendor's balance goes up by ₱1,960.00. Supplier Debit Memo Entered on Supplier Debit Memos , for goods returned to a supplier, price or billing corrections and allowances. Ledger: debit 2000 Accounts Payable for the total; credit the account of each expense line, 1200 Inventory for stocked items returned, and 1300 Input Tax for the VAT. Stock: stocked items leave the site of the line at the amount on the debit memo. Balances: the vendor's balance goes down. The available amount is applied to the supplier's bills on the debit memo's own page or under Credits in Pay Bills; applying it posts nothing further. Bill Payment Made on Pay Bills . One bill payment is recorded for each vendor. Account Debit Credit 2000 Accounts Payable Payment plus discount plus taxes withheld Payment account (bank or credit card, default 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking) Payment 5050 Purchase Discounts Discount taken 2110 Withholding Tax Payable (or the tax's own account) Income tax withheld (1% / 2%) 2115 VAT Withheld Payable (or the tax's own account) VAT withheld (5%) Stock: none. Balances: the vendor's balance goes down, and the bills paid become Partially paid or Paid . Supplier credits used on the same screen only link the credit to the bill. Rules: a bill payment can be edited (date, account, check number, the bills it pays, the amounts and the taxes withheld); the vendor stays the same. A payment above your amount limit needs supervisor approval. Taxes withheld: each type ticked in the Withholding column is kept with the bill, its base (net of VAT), rate and ATC, for BIR Form 2307 and the BIR Reports . Advance applied: when Use advance is used, the advance is applied as a bill payment of its own (AAP-00001 ...): debit 2000 Accounts Payable, credit 1410 Advances to Suppliers. Example a ₱112,000.00 bill (₱100,000.00 plus VAT) paid less 1% and 5% withheld: debit 2000 Accounts Payable ₱112,000.00; credit 1010 Cash in Bank ₱106,000.00, 2110 Withholding Tax Payable ₱1,000.00 and 2115 VAT Withheld Payable ₱5,000.00. Advance to Supplier Entered on Advances to Suppliers . Account Debit Credit Advance account (default 1410 Advances to Suppliers) Amount paid Paid from (bank or credit card) Amount paid Balances: not part of Accounts Payable: the vendor's balance and the A/P aging do not change until the advance is applied to a bill in Pay Bills. Rules: it can be edited, but not below what was applied; it is voided only after its applications are voided. Check Entered on Write Checks or as a quick entry in Use Register . Receipt Management , the Fixed Asset Register and Asset Maintenance can also write checks. Ledger: debit the lines exactly as on a bill (expense accounts, 1200 Inventory for stocked items, the expense account of other items) and 1300 Input Tax; credit the Bank / credit card account the check is drawn on. A "check" drawn on 2050 Company Credit Card records a card charge. Stock: stocked items on the Items tab come into stock like on a bill. Balances: a check does not go through Accounts Payable, so the vendor's balance does not change. Pay open bills with Pay Bills instead. Rules: a check above your amount limit needs supervisor approval. Lines to accounts marked With SL need a name, or a payee on the check. Cash Voucher Entered on Cash Voucher , for petty cash, revolving fund and other cash payments. Asset Maintenance can also make one. Ledger: the account lines exactly as entered (debit or credit), plus one credit to the Cash account (for example 1005 Petty Cash Fund) for the cash amount. The debits less the credits of the lines must equal the cash amount. Stock: none. Balances: a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable must name a customer and changes that customer's balance; a line to 2000 Accounts Payable must name a supplier and changes that supplier's balance.

href="#s-banking" aria-label="Link to this section"> Deposit Entered on Make Deposits or as a quick entry in Use Register . Account Debit Credit Deposit to bank account Total less cash back Cash back goes to account Cash back amount 1050 Undeposited Funds Each payment and sales receipt deposited Terminal cash account (1001) Cash of each POS shift deposited Clearing account (1060, 1065, 1070) Card or e-wallet settlement 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges Merchant fee deducted Account of each other receipt Amount of the receipt Stock: none. Balances: no effect on customer balances: the payments deposited already lowered them. POS cash: the amount of a closed POS shift is the counted cash, less the opening float (which stays in the drawer), plus the cash drops. When the shift's closing entries are corrected later, the deposit's line for the shift follows. Later: a deposit can be edited (payments and shifts taken off or added, other receipts, date, account); it is posted again. Transfer Entered on Transfer Funds or as a quick entry in Use Register . Ledger: debit the Transfer funds to account, credit the Transfer funds from account. It does not touch income or expenses. Stock and balances: none. Service Charge and Interest Earned Recorded by Reconcile when you finish a reconciliation with a Service charge or Interest earned amount. Service Charge: debit the account chosen beside it (default 6080 Bank and Merchant Charges), credit the bank account. Interest Earned: debit the bank account, credit the account chosen beside it (default 4200 Interest Income). Both are dated on the dates you enter beside them, take their numbers from the JE- series, and are marked cleared in the reconciliation straight away. A reconciliation saved for later keeps the two amounts but posts nothing. Undo last voids the two entries and keeps their amounts on the reopened reconciliation, so they are posted once more when it is finished.

href="#s-general-ledger" aria-label="Link to this section"> Journal Entry Entered on Make Journal Entries . Ledger: every line exactly as entered, debit or credit. The debits must equal the credits, and an entry needs at least two lines. Names: a line to 1100 Accounts Receivable needs a customer and changes that customer's balance; a line to 2000 Accounts Payable needs a vendor and changes that vendor's balance; a line to an account marked With SL needs a customer, supplier, employee or other name. Stock: none. A journal entry to 1200 Inventory changes the ledger but not the quantities or values of items, so the inventory valuation reports will no longer agree with the ledger. Use Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand for stock. Opening Balance Entered on Make Journal Entries with Opening balance entry ticked. It posts like a journal entry and is listed with the journal entries. The Fixed Asset Register also makes one when a new asset is saved with Record the purchase set to Existing asset (opening balance) : debit the category's asset account for the cost, credit 3900 Opening Balance Equity for the cost less the opening accumulated depreciation, and credit the accumulated depreciation account for the opening accumulated depreciation. Import from CSV does the same for imported fixed assets. Opening stock is not an opening balance entry: it is an inventory adjustment against 3900 Opening Balance Equity (see below). Tip For customers' and vendors' opening balances, enter one line per customer to 1100 Accounts Receivable (or per vendor to 2000 Accounts Payable) with the name on the line, balanced against 3900 Opening Balance Equity. The names are required on those lines.

href="#s-inventory" aria-label="Link to this section"> Inventory Adjustment Entered on Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand . Physical Inventory Count posts its differences as an inventory adjustment, and the Item List posts one when a new stocked item is saved with a Quantity on hand . Quantity added: debit 1200 Inventory, credit the Adjustment account (default 5100 Inventory Adjustments and Shrinkage), at the item's average cost. Quantity removed: debit the adjustment account, credit 1200 Inventory, at the item's average cost. Value changed (Total value): debit or credit 1200 Inventory against the adjustment account for the difference, with no change in quantity. Only users who may view costs can adjust values. Opening quantity from the Item List: debit 1200 Inventory for the Total value entered, credit 3900 Opening Balance Equity. Stock: the quantity changes at the site of the adjustment, and the average cost is worked out again. Editing: an adjustment can be edited; it is taken off the books, worked out again against the stock without it, and posted again under the same number. Inventory Transfer Entered on Transfer Inventory . Ledger: nothing, because both sites use the same inventory account. The page confirms Quantities moved without changing total inventory value. Stock: the quantity leaves the from site at the item's average cost and arrives at the to site with the same value. Editing: a transfer can be edited (date, sites, lines); the stock moves again. Build Assembly Entered on Build Assemblies . Account Debit Credit 1200 Inventory, assembly item Total cost of the components 1200 Inventory, stocked components Average cost of each component Expense account of non-stock components Quantity times the item's cost Stock: the components leave the build site and the assembly comes in at their total cost. Example: building one SET-OFFICE Office Monitor Set takes one each of MON-024, KEY-001, MOU-001 and CAB-HDMI out of stock at average cost, and credits 5200 Direct Labor Absorbed ₱150.00 for LAB-ASM Assembly Labor (per set). Pending: a build saved with Save as pending build posts nothing until Complete build . Editing: a build can be edited (assembly, site, quantity, date); a completed build is posted again, a pending one stays pending unless it is completed on the same save. Processing Order Entered on Disassemble / Process Items , for disassembly, de-kitting and co-product processing. Account Debit Credit Asset account of each input item Average cost of the inputs Expense account of non-stock inputs Quantity times the item's cost Account of each additional cost line (for example 5200) Amount of the cost Asset account of each output item Cost allocated to the output Processing variance account (default 5100) Difference, if any Difference, if any Stock: the inputs leave the processing site and the outputs come in at their allocated cost. Variance: only the valuation methods (current average cost, manual amounts) leave a difference between the total cost and the value of the outputs. Pending: an order saved with Save as pending posts nothing until Complete and post .

href="#s-fixed-assets" aria-label="Link to this section"> Depreciation Posted by Run Depreciation , dated the last day of the month. Ledger: for each asset category and class, debit the category's depreciation expense account (6090 Depreciation Expense in the demo) and credit its accumulated depreciation account (for example 1555 Accumulated Depreciation - Computer and POS). Assets: the month is marked as run for each asset. An asset whose net book value reaches its salvage value becomes fully depreciated. Undoing: voiding or deleting the entry frees the month, so it can be run again. Asset Disposal Posted by Dispose of Assets . Account Debit Credit Accumulated depreciation account All depreciation to date Asset account Cost of the asset Received into account (default 1050) Proceeds received 4300 Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Assets Loss Gain Assets: the asset is marked disposed. When asked, the page first runs the missing months of depreciation up to the disposal date. Undoing: voiding or deleting the disposal makes the asset active again. Asset purchases and maintenance A new asset in the Fixed Asset Register is recorded as a check ( Paid now (Write Checks) ), a bill ( On account (Enter Bills) ) or an opening balance, each debiting the category's asset account; or nothing, with Already recorded elsewhere . A record in Asset Maintenance is paid through a bill, a check or a cash voucher that debits the Parts charged to and Labor charged to accounts (proposed: the account whose name contains "Repair", 6030 Repairs and Maintenance in the demo) and, with VAT, 1300 Input Tax.

href="#s-point-of-sale" aria-label="Link to this section"> POS Sale Completed on the POS Register . Account Debit Credit Account of each tender Amount paid with it Income account of each item Line amount 2100 Output Tax VAT of the lines 5000 Cost of Goods Sold Average cost of stocked items 1200 Inventory Average cost of stocked items Tenders: cash is debited to the terminal's cash account (1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers for both demo counters). Other payment methods debit their own clearing account: in the demo, Credit/Debit Card to 1060 Card Clearing, GCash and Maya to 1065 E-wallet Clearing, Gift Voucher to 2120 Gift Vouchers Outstanding, P.O. Card to 1070 P.O. Card Clearing and Bank to 1010 Cash in Bank - BDO Checking. Stock: stocked items leave the site of the terminal at average cost. Balances: no effect on customer balances, even when a customer is named on the sale. Suspended sales ( Suspend ) post nothing until they are recalled and completed. A sale completed with Charge to account is saved as an invoice instead (see Invoice), and a payment at the counter as a customer payment. POS Return Processed on POS Receipts, Returns & Voids , always with supervisor approval. Ledger: debit 4050 Sales Returns and Allowances and 2100 Output Tax; credit the account of the refund method (cash: the terminal's cash account). Stock: when Goods can be resold (back to store stock) is ticked, the items come back into the store's site; when it is not, they go to the damaged-goods site. Either way they come back at the current average cost: debit 1200 Inventory, credit 5000 Cost of Goods Sold. If no damaged-goods site exists, items that cannot be resold do not come back into stock. Cash Over/Short Posted by Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings when a register is closed and the cash counted differs from the expected cash. Short: debit 6200 Cash Over and Short, credit the terminal's cash account. Over: debit the terminal's cash account, credit 6200 Cash Over and Short. Example: Makati Counter 1 is ₱50.00 short: 6200 Cash Over and Short is debited and 1001 Cash on Hand - Store Registers credited ₱50.00.

href="#s-voiding-versus-deleting" aria-label="Link to this section"> Both are done from the view of a saved transaction with the Void and Delete buttons. Both need the Delete/Void right on the page, a reason ( Reason (required, recorded in the audit trail) ), and a date after the closing date. What happens Void Delete The document Stays, marked VOID with the reason, date and user Is removed Ledger and stock Everything it posted is taken out Everything it posted is taken out Its number Stays in use Is not given out again Available for Posting transactions only All, except POS sales, returns and over/short Audit trail Full copy with the reason Full copy with the reason A voided transaction cannot be edited or voided again. It still appears in lists and reports as void, and in Voided and Deleted Transactions Detail . Estimates, sales orders and purchase orders cannot be voided (they post nothing); delete them, or use Close to stop expecting the rest. Voiding or deleting is refused while: payments or credits are applied to the invoice, statement charge, finance charge or bill (remove them first by editing the payment or credit); the payment or sales receipt is included in a deposit (void the deposit first); the credit memo or payment has been refunded (void the refund first); the estimate, sales order or purchase order has been converted or received in part (close it instead). Voiding or deleting a payment or credit releases the invoices it paid, which become open again. Voiding or deleting a check, bill payment or customer refund above your amount limit, and voiding any POS sale or return, needs supervisor approval. A transaction cleared in a bank reconciliation can be changed, voided or deleted only by a user with the closed-period permission. The change is listed on the Reconciliation Discrepancy report. Note Item receipts, inventory adjustments, inventory transfers, builds and finance charges cannot be changed after they are saved, so they have no Edit button. To correct one, void it and enter it again. Deposits and bill payments can be edited.

href="#s-pending-transactions" aria-label="Link to this section"> Some transactions can be saved first and posted later. While they wait they are pending : they post nothing to the ledger and move no stock. Transaction How to save as pending How to post it Invoice, sales receipt Tick Pending (non-posting until marked final) Mark as final , then save Build assembly Save as pending build Complete build Processing order Save as pending Complete and post POS sale Suspend Recall , then Complete sale A pending invoice is not part of the customer's balance or the A/R aging, is not offered in Receive Payments, and is not checked against the credit limit until it is marked final. A pending sales receipt is not offered in Make Deposits. The view of a pending invoice or sales receipt says This transaction is pending. It does not affect the books or inventory until it is marked final. Pending invoices and sales receipts are listed on the Pending Sales report and counted on the Home dashboard; pending builds on the Pending Builds reports; pending processing orders on the Processing & Disassembly Register. A pending build or processing order can be saved even when the components or inputs are short; completing it checks the stock again. Pending documents take their number when they are first saved.

href="#s-the-closing-date" aria-label="Link to this section"> The closing date protects the periods you have finished. It is set in Company, Security & Closing Date in the box Books closed through (blank = open) . Once a closing date is set, a user without the special permission Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled cannot: save a transaction dated on or before the closing date; edit, void or delete a transaction dated on or before it, or move it to a later date; import transactions or opening stock dated on or before it. The messages are The books are closed through 07/08/2026. You do not have permission to record transactions dated on or before the closing date. and This transaction is dated on or before the closing date (07/08/2026) and cannot be changed. Administrators, the Company Owner and the Super Admin always have the permission; of the installed roles, no other role has it. A memorized transaction set to be entered automatically on a date in the closed period stops, and is set back to Remind me when it is due . The same permission is needed to change a transaction cleared in a bank reconciliation, whatever its date. Tip After each month-end close, make a backup, check the reports, and then move the closing date to the last day of that month.

href="#s-the-class-on-a-transaction" aria-label="Link to this section"> A class is your own way of splitting the books (branches, departments, projects). The classes are kept in the Class List . Every transaction form has a Class box. The class is copied to every ledger line the transaction posts, so every financial report can be filtered by class and the "by Class" statements show one column per class. On journal entries and cash vouchers a line can have its own class; a line without one takes the class at the top. When you save a transaction without a class, a window No class selected warns that it will be saved as Unclassified . Choose Choose a class to go back, or Continue saving . The window does not appear while the Class List is empty. On the POS Register a sale starts with the user's default class (set in Company, Security & Closing Date) or else the terminal's default class, and the class is kept for the next sale. Run Depreciation posts each asset under its own default class when no class is chosen on the run. A class already used on transactions cannot be deleted; make it inactive instead. Reports list entries without a class as (Unclassified) .

t: Appendix B. Default roles and what they can do
x: href="#app-roles" aria-label="Link to this section"> A new installation starts with nine roles, and a company created on the platform copies the roles of the company it is copied from. Administrators can change their page access in Page Access Configuration and their rights and special permissions in User Role Configuration , but the installed roles cannot be deleted. Effective Access (View as User) shows what one user can really do and why.

href="#s-the-rights-on-a-page" aria-label="Link to this section"> Open: the user can open the page and see its records (the page is allowed for the role). Create , Edit , Delete/Void , Print/Export , Approve: what the user can do on a page they can open. Approve lets the user approve other users' actions that need supervisor approval, and their own. A user with several roles gets everything any of the roles gives. A user override set for one user and one page always wins over the roles.

href="#s-the-installed-roles" aria-label="Link to this section"> Role What it is for Demo user Administrator Everything in every module, including user accounts, roles, page access, the closing date and the audit trail admin (System Administrator) Accountant Financial, Fixed Assets, Banking and reconciliation, all module reports and the financial statements accountant (Ana Cruz) A/R Clerk Customers module transactions and the Customer and Receivables reports arclerk (Ben Garcia) A/P Clerk Vendors module transactions, Pay Bills and the Vendors and Payables reports apclerk (Carla Lim) Inventory Clerk Items, sites, receiving, adjustments, builds, processing, stock counts and quantity reports invclerk (Dan Villanueva) Sales Representative Estimates, sales orders, invoices and the Sales reports salesrep (Maria Santos) Cashier POS sales, returns and cash drops at the assigned terminal only cashier1 (Ella Ramos) POS Supervisor Everything a cashier can do, plus approvals and X- and Z-readings supervisor (Fred Tan) Auditor View-only access to all transactions, reports and the audit trail auditor (Grace Uy) In the demo company the admin user logs in with the password Admin@12345 (and must change it at once) and the other demo users with Demo@12345. Change these passwords, or deactivate the users you do not need, before real use.

href="#s-administrator" aria-label="Link to this section"> Pages: every page of every module, with every right, including Approve. Special permissions: all of them, without limits. Sites: all sites. The Company Owner and a Super Admin working inside the company have the same full authority whatever their roles say, and no role or user override can lock them out.

href="#s-accountant" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Home All Home pages (Dashboard, Report Center, Memorized Reports, Saved Report Layouts, Search, Find) Open, Print/Export Financial Every page and report, including Make Journal Entries and Module Default Accounts Open, Create, Edit, Delete/Void, Print/Export Fixed Assets Every page and report Open, Create, Edit, Delete/Void, Print/Export Banking Every page and report, including Reconcile Open, Create, Edit, Delete/Void, Print/Export Customers Customer Center, Create Invoices, Receive Payments, every report Open, Print/Export Vendors Vendor Center, Bill Tracker, Enter Bills, Pay Bills, Advances to Suppliers, every report Open, Print/Export BIR Reports Withholding Tax Table, Print BIR Form 2307 and every BIR report Open, Create, Edit, Delete/Void, Print/Export Inventory Inventory Center, Item List, Category List, U/M Set List, Processing Formulas, Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand, Disassemble / Process Items, every report Open, Print/Export Point of Sale Every POS report Open, Print/Export System Administration Utilities: Verify & Rebuild Data Open, Print/Export The Accountant can run the checks on the Utilities page but not Rebuild data , which needs Edit.

href="#s-ap-clerk" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Home All Home pages Open, Print/Export Vendors Vendor Center, Bill Tracker, Enter Bills, Supplier Debit Memos, Pay Bills, Receipt Management, Create Purchase Orders, Receive Items and Enter Bills, Receive Items, Enter Bill for Received Items Open, Create, Edit, Print/Export Vendors Advances to Suppliers Open, Create, Edit, Print/Export Vendors The Vendors and Payables Reports Open, Print/Export Inventory Item List Open BIR Reports Print BIR Form 2307, Summary of Taxes Withheld from Vendors/Suppliers, Expanded Withholding Tax Register, VAT Withholding Register, Withholding Tax Remittances Open, Print/Export BIR Reports Withholding Tax Table Open The A/P Clerk cannot void or delete.

href="#s-inventory-clerk" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Home All Home pages Open, Print/Export Inventory Item List, Inventory Site List, U/M Set List, Processing Formulas, Transfer Inventory, Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand, Build Assemblies, Disassemble / Process Items Open, Create, Edit, Print/Export Inventory Category List Open, Create, Edit, Delete, Print/Export Inventory Inventory Center, Physical Inventory Count Open, Print/Export Vendors Receive Items Open, Create, Edit, Print/Export Vendors Create Purchase Orders Open, Print/Export Inventory reports Quantity on Hand by Site, the three Stock Status reports, Physical Inventory Worksheet, Pending Builds, Pending Builds by Site, Processing & Disassembly Register, Processing Yield Analysis, Negative Inventory Listing, No. of Days Inventory Has No Movement, Inventory Movement Summary Report, Inventory Movement Detailed Report (and the Inventory Movement Transactions they open) Open, Print/Export The Inventory Clerk can print count sheets but cannot post a physical count, because adjusting stock and counting it are kept apart. The valuation reports are not included.

href="#s-cashier" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Home Home Dashboard Open Point of Sale POS Register; Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings Open, Create, Print/Export Point of Sale POS Receipts, Returns & Voids Open, Create, Delete/Void, Print/Export Point of Sale Ending Inventory - POS Cashier (their own shifts) Open, Print/Export Sites: the role is limited to the Makati Store (ST1) and the Cebu Store (ST2). The demo user cashier1 is limited further to the Makati Store and the terminal POS-01 Makati Counter 1. Voids, returns, X-readings and closing the register always need a supervisor's approval.

href="#s-pos-supervisor" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Home Home Dashboard, Report Center Open Point of Sale POS Register; Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings; POS Receipts, Returns & Voids; Approval Codes Open, Create, Edit, Delete/Void, Print/Export, Approve Point of Sale POS Terminals Open, Print/Export Point of Sale The 9 POS reports Open, Print/Export The role itself covers all sites; the demo user supervisor is limited to the Makati Store and POS-01.

href="#s-auditor" aria-label="Link to this section"> Area Pages Rights Every module Every page and report, including Audit Trail, Transaction History and the audit reports Open, Print/Export Not included POS Register; Shifts, Cash Drops & Readings; the setup pages of System Administration; the Company pages None The pages left out are User Accounts, User Role Configuration, Page Access Configuration, Effective Access, Company, Security & Closing Date, Utilities, Import from CSV, Backup & Restore, Multi-Company Setup, Company Profile & Code, Employees & Users and Join Requests. Note A few pages open on a new entry when you click them in the menu: Receive Payments, Pay Bills, Make Deposits, Transfer Funds and Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand. A user who may only view them (the Accountant, the Auditor) sees Access denied there. Open those transactions from the Customer Center, the Vendor Center, a report or Find instead.

href="#s-special-permissions" aria-label="Link to this section"> Special permissions are set per role in User Role Configuration . The labels are the ones shown there. Special permission What it allows View costs and margins See item costs, average costs, cost of goods sold and margins in reports, the Inventory Center, the Item List, the price pages and processing orders; adjust inventory values; see the ledger entries of sales documents View bank balances outside Banking See bank balances on the Home dashboard, in the Chart of Accounts, on Transfer Funds and in the bank-balance columns of reports Max discount % without approval The largest discount a user may give on a line (or with a percentage discount item) on estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts and at the POS Max price change % without approval How far a line's price may differ from the item's standard or price-level price on the same documents Max check / bill payment / adjustment amount without approval The largest check, cash voucher, bill payment, customer refund, inventory adjustment, count difference or processing order a user may save alone, and the largest check, bill payment or refund they may void or delete Can exceed customer credit limits Save an invoice (with a reason) or a POS charge sale that takes a customer over the credit limit Can change the Chart of Accounts and default accounts Add, change and delete accounts, and change Module Default Accounts (with Edit on that page) Can change transactions on/before the closing date or already reconciled Work in the closed period and change transactions cleared in a bank reconciliation Can design report layouts (fonts, headings and footers, columns and rows) and save or share them Use the Modify Report button on reports, save and share layouts, and choose the layout a report opens with How the values work: A Yes/No permission is granted when any of the user's roles grants it. A limit is the highest value among the user's roles. A blank limit in any role means no limit. A limit that none of the user's roles sets counts as 0: every discount, price change or amount then needs approval. Going over a limit does not stop the user: the form asks for Supervisor approval , and a user who has Approve on that page types their username and password. A user who has Approve on the page approves their own action. Nobody can approve with their own password otherwise ( You cannot approve your own transaction. ). Of the installed roles only the Administrator and the POS Supervisor (on the POS pages) have Approve . Approvals for the clerks therefore come from an Administrator, unless you give Approve to another role. Administrators, the Company Owner and the Super Admin have every special permission with no limits. The values each role is installed with: Role Granted Limits Accountant View costs, View bank balances, Chart of Accounts changes, Design report layouts Amount: no limit; discount 0%; price change 0% A/R Clerk None Amount ₱50,000.00; discount 10%; price change 5% A/P Clerk View costs Amount ₱100,000.00 Inventory Clerk None Amount ₱20,000.00 Sales Representative None Discount 5%; price change 0% Cashier None Discount 5%; price change 0%; amount 0 POS Supervisor None Discount 30%; price change 20%; amount ₱20,000.00 Auditor View costs, View bank balances None set

href="#s-duties-kept-apart" aria-label="Link to this section"> When a user (or a role) would be able to create or edit on both pages of one of these pairs, User Accounts and User Role Configuration show a segregation-of-duties warning, and you must tick a box to save anyway: Vendor Center and Pay Bills (creating vendors and paying bills); Receive Payments and Reconcile (receiving customer payments and reconciling the bank account); Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand and Physical Inventory Count (adjusting inventory and counting it); Enter Bills and Write Checks (entering bills and writing checks); POS Register and Make Deposits (selling at the POS and depositing the cash).

href="#s-sites" aria-label="Link to this section"> A role can cover all sites or only the sites ticked for it, and a user can be limited to certain sites and POS terminals in User Accounts . When both are set, the user works only in the sites that both allow. Users limited to sites see only those sites in lists, site pickers and site-based reports, and saving a transaction for another site is refused.

t: Appendix C. Number series and document numbers
x: href="#app-numbers" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every transaction and a few records get a number from a series : a prefix, then a running number filled with zeros. Each company has its own series.

href="#s-the-series" aria-label="Link to this section"> Series First number Used by EST- EST-00001 Estimates SO- SO-00001 Sales orders INV- INV-00001 Invoices, including batch invoices and POS charge sales SR- SR-00001 Sales receipts SC- SC-00001 Statement charges FC- FC-00001 Finance charges PMT- PMT-00001 Customer payments CM- CM-00001 Credit memos PO- PO-00001 Purchase orders IR- IR-00001 Item receipts BILL- BILL-00001 Bills DM- DM-00001 Supplier debit memos ADV- ADV-00001 Advances to suppliers AAP- AAP-00001 Advances applied to bills (bill payments made out of an advance) (none) 1001 Checks, bill payments and customer refunds CAV- CAV-00001 Cash vouchers DEP- DEP-00001 Deposits TRF- TRF-00001 Fund transfers JE- JE-00001 Journal entries, opening balances, depreciation, asset disposals, cash over/short, service charges, interest earned ADJ- ADJ-00001 Inventory adjustments, physical counts, opening stock IT- IT-00001 Inventory transfers BLD- BLD-00001 Assembly builds PRC- PRC-00001 Processing orders POS- POS-000001 POS sales and returns FA- FA-00001 Fixed asset numbers MNT- MNT-00001 Asset maintenance records

href="#s-how-numbers-are-given" aria-label="Link to this section"> A number is taken when the transaction is first saved, never when the form is opened. The form shows the next number as a hint, for example INV-00024 (auto) in the Number box. If saving fails (a message in red), no number is used up. The counter only goes forward. A voided transaction keeps its number; a deleted one leaves a gap, and the number is not given out again. A suspended POS sale removed with Cancel suspended sale is deleted, so it also leaves a gap in the POS- series. Because checks, bill payments and customer refunds share one series, a bill payment made by bank transfer or card also takes the next check number. Changing a transaction's date does not change its number. When an item receipt is turned into a bill with Enter Bill for Received Items , the record gets the next BILL- number in place of its IR- number. A new company created on the platform starts every series again from 1.

href="#s-typing-your-own-number" aria-label="Link to this section"> On these forms you can type a number instead of taking the automatic one, both when entering and when editing: Number on estimates, sales orders, invoices, sales receipts, statement charges, credit memos, purchase orders, bills and supplier debit memos; Check no. on Write Checks; Entry no. on Make Journal Entries; CAV entry no. on Cash Voucher. Leave the box blank to get the next number. A number you type does not move the counter. Important Only the cash voucher checks that a typed number is not used already ( CAV entry no. ... is already used. Leave the number blank to get the next one. ). On the other forms the program accepts a number that is already in use, and a typed number that is ahead of the counter will be given out again later. Type your own numbers only when you must match a pre-printed form, and check the list first. All other transactions (payments, bill payments, deposits, transfers, item receipts, adjustments, transfers of stock, builds, processing orders, POS transactions and the entries the program makes) are always numbered automatically.

t: POS receipt numbers and Z-reading numbers
x: href="#s-pos-receipt-numbers-and-z-reading-numbers" aria-label="Link to this section"> Every POS terminal has its own receipt series: the Receipt prefix set in POS Terminals followed by an 8-digit number, for example MK1-00000001 for Makati Counter 1 and CB1-00000001 for Cebu Counter 1. New terminals are offered the prefix OR-. Sales, returns, charge sales and payments taken at the counter each take the next receipt number of the terminal, in addition to their own transaction number. Z-readings are numbered per terminal (#1, #2 ...) when the register is closed. The prefix can be changed on the POS Terminals page. The running number cannot be reset there ( Receipt numbers are sequential per terminal and cannot be reset here. ).

href="#s-can-the-series-be-changed" aria-label="Link to this section"> Not from within the program. There is no page for the prefixes or the next numbers of the series; they are kept in the sequences table of the company database. A system administrator with access to the database (phpMyAdmin or Navicat) can change a prefix or the next number there, for example to start at the next number of your pre-printed invoices. Important Make a backup before changing the table, and never set a next number at or below a number already used: the program would give out duplicate numbers.

href="#s-other-codes" aria-label="Link to this section"> Company Code: with several companies, each company has a code such as ABD-7K2QX (see Appendix F ). It is not a document number and cannot be chosen; the Company Owner or the Super Admin can only regenerate it. Codes you choose yourself: account codes, item codes, customer and vendor names, site codes and terminal codes are typed by you and must be unique.
